- Cancels any pending `loadAsync()` operation. Matching resolved paths, faces, physical sizes, oversampling settings, and mipmap settings share an atlas; changing any of these selects a separate cache entry. Glyphs are rasterized lazily.

```cpp
// tcApp.h (inside class tcApp : public App)
Font font;

// tcApp.cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!font.load(TC_FONT_SANS, 24)) return;
}
```

## Font::resetLineHeight

- Clears the custom line height so `getLineHeight()` uses the loaded font's default, or returns 0 when no font is loaded.
- This spacing separates baselines in horizontal text and columns in vertical text; see `Font::setLineHeight`.

## Font::setAlign

- `setAlign(h, v)` stores both `Direction` values; `setAlign(h)` changes only the horizontal value. The stored defaults are `Direction::Left` and `Direction::Top`.
- `getAlignH()` and `getAlignV()` return these values, but the default `drawString()`, `forEachGlyph()`, and `getStringPath()` overloads use global `setTextAlign()` settings. Pass explicit alignment arguments to those functions to choose alignment per call.

## Font::setHangingPunctuation

- When enabled, an overflowing character prohibited at line start, together with consecutive prohibited characters, stays at the end of the current horizontal line or vertical column. The default is `false`.
- Requires active wrapping and a kinsoku level other than `KinsokuLevel::Off`; the selected table determines which characters can hang. See `Font::setMaxLineLength` and `Font::setKinsoku`.

## Font::setKinsoku

- `KinsokuLevel::Off` is the default and disables the prohibition tables. `PunctuationOnly` prohibits selected commas, periods, colons, semicolons, question marks, exclamation marks, and ellipses at line start, including their supported CJK and fullwidth forms.
- `Standard` additionally prohibits closing brackets, small kana, sound marks, and iteration marks at line start, and opening brackets at line end. The selected table also controls hanging punctuation.
- Applies to automatic wrapping in both writing modes; see `Font::setMaxLineLength`. If no permitted break is available, wrapping can still force a break at a prohibited boundary.

## Font::setLatinHyphenation

- When enabled, horizontal wrapping appends `-` before a forced break when no earlier break opportunity is available. The default is `false`; vertical wrapping does not use this setting.
- This check is not limited to Latin characters, and the inserted hyphen's width is not reserved within the maximum line length.
- Wrapping requirements are described in `Font::setMaxLineLength`.

## Font::setLineHeight

- A positive `pixels` value specifies spacing in logical pixels: baseline spacing in horizontal writing and column spacing in vertical writing. Vertical character cells still use the font size.
- A value of 0 or less selects the font's default line height, as does `resetLineHeight()`.
- The value is stored directly and persists across font loads; `getLineHeight()` returns the effective spacing.

## Font::setLineHeightEm

- Stores `getDefaultLineHeight() * multiplier` as a fixed logical-pixel value: `1.0f` uses the current default and `1.5f` uses 1.5 times that height. This is a multiple of default line height, not font size.
- The multiplier is not retained or reapplied after loading another font. Calling before a font is loaded stores 0; a nonpositive result uses the default.
- Horizontal and vertical spacing behavior is described in `Font::setLineHeight`.

## Font::setMaxLineLength

- `length` is in logical pixels: line width for horizontal writing and column height for vertical writing. The default is 0.
- Wrapping requires `enableWrap(true)`, a positive length, and a loaded font. Drawing, glyph iteration, string paths, and text measurements use the resulting inserted newlines; explicit newlines remain effective.
- This is a wrapping threshold rather than a clipping boundary. A single oversized character or indivisible vertical Latin or digit run can exceed it, as can hanging punctuation and inserted hyphens.

## Font::setTcyDigits

- `setTcyDigits(maxDigits, inMode, overflowMode)` applies `inMode` to runs of at most `maxDigits` ASCII digits (`0`–`9`) and `overflowMode` to longer runs. With `maxDigits <= 0`, every run uses `overflowMode`.
- `TcyMode::Rotate` rotates the entire run clockwise by `TAU / 4`; `Upright` gives each digit its own upright cell; `Combine` centers the run in one font-size cell and compresses it horizontally only if needed.
- The defaults are 0, `TcyMode::Combine`, and `TcyMode::Rotate`. This setting affects vertical placement and wrapping, but has no effect in horizontal writing.

## Font::setTcyLatin

- Applies one `TcyMode` to consecutive ASCII letters (`A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`); the default is `TcyMode::Rotate`, which rotates the whole run clockwise by `TAU / 4`.
- `Upright` and `Combine` use the same cell and compression rules described in `Font::setTcyDigits`. This affects vertical placement and wrapping, but has no effect in horizontal writing.

## Font::setWritingMode

- The default `WritingMode::Horizontal` places text left to right. `WritingMode::VerticalRL` places characters top to bottom and columns right to left; newlines start a new column.
- Applies to `drawString()`, `forEachGlyph()`, `getStringPath()`, and wrapping. Vertical layout uses supported Unicode vertical-form glyphs when available, with rotation or positional fallbacks.
- This does not switch `getWidth()` and `getHeight()` to vertical block measurements; they retain horizontal advance and line-count calculations after wrapping.

## Font::stringWidth

- Calls `getWidth(text)` and returns the greatest line advance in logical pixels after automatic wrapping, or 0 if no font is loaded. Tabs count as four space advances.
- This measures horizontal advances even in vertical writing; see `Font::getWidth` for the measurement contract.

## FpsSettings

- `getFpsSettings()` returns the main loop configuration. `updateFps` and `drawFps` contain `VSYNC` (-1), `EVENT_DRIVEN` (0), or a positive target rate in frames per second.
- `synced` is true when updates and draws run together in a 1:1 relationship through `setFps`; `setIndependentFps` sets it to false.
- `actualVsyncFps` estimates the display callback rate from the frame duration when either configured rate is `VSYNC`. It is 0 when neither rate uses `VSYNC` or no positive frame duration is available.

## FpsSettings::actualVsyncFps

- When either target rate is `VSYNC`, this `float` is the reciprocal of the platform frame duration in seconds, expressed in frames per second; it is an estimate rather than a direct monitor refresh-rate query.
- It is 0 if neither target rate is `VSYNC`, or if the frame duration is not positive.
- See `FpsSettings::drawFps` for how settings are read and changed.

## FpsSettings::drawFps

- This `float` is `VSYNC` (-1) for drawing on each platform frame, `EVENT_DRIVEN` (0) for drawing on `redraw()` requests, or a positive target in frames per second. The initial main-loop setting is `VSYNC`.
- A positive rate is implemented by skipping platform frames, with at most one draw per platform frame.
- `getFpsSettings()` returns a snapshot of the main-loop settings, including when called from a secondary window. Editing its fields does not change the loop; in the main-window context, use `setFps()` for synchronized rates or `setIndependentFps()` for separate update and drawing rates.
- In a secondary-window context, `setFps()` changes only that window's throttle, and `setIndependentFps()` is ignored; neither changes the reported main-loop settings.

## FpsSettings::synced

- This `bool` is `true` when one update runs for each drawn frame. The initial main-loop setting is `true`, and `setFps()` selects this mode when called in the main-window context.
- `setIndependentFps()` sets it to `false` when called in the main-window context, even when the two target rates are equal.
- See `FpsSettings::drawFps` for how settings are read and changed, including the different setter behavior in a secondary-window context.

## FpsSettings::updateFps

- This `float` is `VSYNC` (-1), `EVENT_DRIVEN` (0), or a positive target in updates per second. The initial main-loop setting is `VSYNC`.
- When `synced` is `true`, updates run once per drawn frame, including frames requested by `redraw()`. In independent mode, `VSYNC` updates once per platform frame, a positive rate uses fixed steps of `1 / updateFps` seconds, and `EVENT_DRIVEN` runs no updates, even after `redraw()`.
- See `FpsSettings::drawFps` for how settings are read and changed.

## FullscreenShader

- Inherits `Shader` loading and texture binding, but uses a fullscreen quad with two-component position and two-component texture coordinates.
- Call `setParams()` before `draw()` to copy a parameter structure; `draw()` uploads those bytes to uniform block slot 0. Stored `setUniform()` values are not applied by this draw method.
- Use inherited `setTexture()` to bind source textures; `draw()` applies these bindings without requiring a subclass.
- Call `draw()` directly to render the quad into the current window or FBO; it flushes preceding recorded layers and issues its GPU draw immediately. An unloaded shader performs no drawing.
- The default pipeline disables blending and overwrites covered pixels; after drawing, the current target's drawing state is reapplied.
- Threading and GPU resource lifetime rules are described under `Shader`.

## FullscreenShader::draw

- Draws directly into the current window or Fbo render target, opening its render pass if necessary; `begin()` and `end()` are not required.
- Flushes preceding drawing commands before drawing the quad; the default pipeline disables blending and overwrites the covered pixels.
- Applies textures configured with `setTexture()` and the uniform block configured with `setParams()`, then draws two triangles and restores the target drawing state.
- Does nothing if the shader is not loaded; also returns without drawing if a compatible pipeline cannot be selected.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    // shader is a FullscreenShader member loaded in setup().
    shader.draw();
}
```

## FullscreenShader::setParams

- This C++ template copies `sizeof(T)` bytes from `params` into internal storage; provide a structure whose size and memory layout match the shader uniform block.
- Call before `draw()`; each call replaces the stored block, which remains available for subsequent draws without retaining a reference to `params`.
- `draw()` applies this block at uniform slot `0`; it does not apply the blocks stored by the inherited `Shader::setUniform()`.

## GraphicsBackend

- Static methods query the active sokol graphics backend. Use them after graphics initialization, such as in the windowed app’s `setup()` or later.
- Boolean queries include `isWebGPU()`, `isWebGL2()`, `isMetal()`, `isD3D11()`, `isVulkan()`, and `isOpenGL()`. `isOpenGL()` includes desktop OpenGL and GLES3, including WebGL2; `isWebGL2()` additionally requires the Web platform.
- `name()` returns `"opengl"`, `"gles3"`, `"webgl2"`, `"d3d11"`, `"metal"`, `"webgpu"`, `"vulkan"`, `"dummy"`, or `"unknown"`.

## GraphicsBackend::isD3D11

- Returns `true` for the Direct3D 11 backend and `false` for other backends.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::isMetal

- Returns `true` for the macOS, iOS, and simulator Metal backends, and `false` for other backends.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::isOpenGL

- Returns `true` for OpenGL core or OpenGL ES 3, including WebGL2 on the Web, and `false` for other backends.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::isVulkan

- Returns `true` for the Vulkan backend and `false` for other backends.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::isWebGL2

- Returns `true` only when `Platform::isWeb()` is `true` and the backend is OpenGL ES 3; this corresponds to GLES3 under Emscripten. Returns `false` otherwise, including native OpenGL ES 3.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::isWebGPU

- Returns `true` for the WebGPU backend and `false` for other backends; it does not additionally check `Platform::isWeb()`.
- See `GraphicsBackend::name` for initialization requirements shared by these queries.

## GraphicsBackend::name

- Returns a `const char*` string literal: `"opengl"`, `"gles3"`, `"webgl2"`, `"d3d11"`, `"metal"`, `"webgpu"`, `"vulkan"`, or `"dummy"`; an unrecognized backend returns `"unknown"`.
- OpenGL ES 3 is named `"webgl2"` on the Web and `"gles3"` elsewhere. All Metal variants are named `"metal"`.
- Except for `isWebGL2()` on native platforms, `GraphicsBackend` queries require initialized graphics; call them from the windowed app's `setup()` or later, while graphics remain initialized. These queries assert before graphics initialization, and `runHeadlessApp()` does not initialize graphics.
- On native platforms, `isWebGL2()` returns `false` without querying the graphics backend and does not require graphics initialization.

## HALF_TAU

- This constexpr float is `TAU / 2.0f`, approximately 3.1415927 radians, equivalent to π or 180 degrees.

## HasTexture::getTexture

- A pure virtual interface returning `Texture&` for a mutable object and `const Texture&` for a const object. Derived classes provide the texture; ownership is not transferred.
- The default `hasTexture()` checks `getTexture().isAllocated()`, and the default drawing and filter/wrap methods use this texture.
- See `Image` for CPU pixels and GPU texture updates, `Fbo::getTexture` for framebuffer texture access, and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## HeadlessSettings

- Pass this type to `runHeadlessApp` to run without a window or graphics context. Its only setting is `targetFps`, the target update rate in updates per second, which defaults to 60.
- `setFps(fps)` assigns `targetFps` and returns the settings by reference for chaining. Use a positive rate; the runner computes its fixed timestep as `1.0 / targetFps` and does not interpret `VSYNC` or `EVENT_DRIVEN`.
- Known issue: [#906](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/906) (the headless loop calls only `App::update()` and does not update the scene graph).

## HeadlessSettings::setFps

- Assigns `fps` directly to `targetFps` and returns `HeadlessSettings&` referring to the same object, allowing chained calls.
- See `HeadlessSettings::targetFps` for units, defaults, valid values, and when the setting takes effect.

```cpp
HeadlessSettings settings;
settings.setFps(120.0f);
```

## HeadlessSettings::targetFps

- This `float` is measured in updates per second and defaults to `60.0f`. `runHeadlessApp()` uses fixed update steps of `1 / targetFps` seconds, which is also the value reported by `getDeltaTime()` during updates.
- Set it before calling `runHeadlessApp()`. The runner copies the value at startup, so later changes to this settings object do not change the running update rate.
- Use a finite positive value. Values are not validated or clamped; zero, negative, or non-finite values result in no update steps, and `VSYNC` and `EVENT_DRIVEN` have no special meaning here.

## Node::HitResult

- `Node::findHitNode()` and `Node::findHitNodeFromScreen()` return this structure; call `result.hit()` before using its hit data.
- `node` holds the hit node, `distance` is the parameter along the normalized local ray, and `localPoint` is the hit position in that node's coordinates.
- A search with no hit returns a null `node`, zero `distance`, and a zero `localPoint`; a local declaration without braces does not initialize `distance`, so use `Node::HitResult result{};` when creating an empty result.

## Node::HitResult::distance

- This `float` is the value written by the successful ray hit test; the search computes the hit position as `localRay.at(distance)`.
- The transformed ray is normalized, so this is a distance from its origin in local units, which can differ from global units under scaling; it is not used to rank hits.
- Check `hit()` before using it; see `Node::HitResult` for empty-result initialization.

## Node::HitResult::hit

- `bool hit() const` returns `node != nullptr`.
- It does not rerun hit testing or check the node's current state; it only tests the stored pointer.

## Node::HitResult::localPoint

- This `Vec3` is calculated as `localRay.at(distance)` using the ray passed to the successful hit test.
- Check `hit()` before using it; see `Node::localToGlobal` for converting the point to global coordinates.

## Node::HitResult::node

- This field is a `Node::Ptr`, equivalent to `shared_ptr<Node>`; `hit()` returns whether it is non-null.
- Keeping the result keeps the referenced node alive, even if it is removed from the tree; the stored pointer does not establish that the node is still attached or currently hit.

## IVec2

- Public `int` components `x` and `y` default to zero; `IVec2(x, y)` sets them individually, and explicit `IVec2(v)` sets both to `v`.
- Supports addition, subtraction, negation, integer scalar multiplication in either order, and component-wise equality; `+=`, `-=`, and `*=` modify the vector.
- `toVec2()` returns a `Vec2` with both components converted to `float`.

## IVec2::operator!=

- `a != b` returns `true` if either corresponding `int` component differs, and `false` if both components match.

## IVec2::operator*

- `a * s` multiplies both components by the `int` scalar `s` and returns a new `IVec2`, leaving `a` unchanged.
- `s * a` is also supported and returns the same result.

## IVec2::operator*=

- `a *= s` multiplies both components of `a` by the `int` scalar `s`.
- Returns an `IVec2&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec2::operator+

- `a + b` returns a new `IVec2` containing `a.x + b.x` and `a.y + b.y`, leaving both operands unchanged.

## IVec2::operator+=

- `a += b` adds each component of `b` to the corresponding component of `a`.
- Returns an `IVec2&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec2::operator-

- `a - b` returns a new `IVec2` containing `a.x - b.x` and `a.y - b.y`, leaving both operands unchanged.
- Unary `-a` returns a new `IVec2` containing `-a.x` and `-a.y`, leaving `a` unchanged.

## IVec2::operator-=

- `a -= b` subtracts each component of `b` from the corresponding component of `a`.
- Returns an `IVec2&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec2::operator==

- `a == b` returns `true` if both corresponding `int` components match, and `false` otherwise.

## IVec2::toVec2

- `a.toVec2()` casts `x` and `y` to `float` and returns a new `Vec2`, leaving `a` unchanged.

## IVec2::x

- This public `int` member can be read and assigned directly. It is initialized to `0` when the vector is default-constructed.

## IVec2::y

- This public `int` member can be read and assigned directly. It is initialized to `0` when the vector is default-constructed.

## IVec3

- Public `int` components `x`, `y`, and `z` default to zero; `IVec3(x, y, z)` sets them individually, and explicit `IVec3(v)` sets all three to `v`.
- `IVec3(ivec2, z)` copies `x` and `y` from an `IVec2`; `z` defaults to zero.
- Supports addition, subtraction, negation, integer scalar multiplication in either order, and component-wise equality; `+=`, `-=`, and `*=` modify the vector.
- `toVec3()` converts all components to `float`, and `xy()` returns the first two components as an `IVec2`.

## IVec3::operator!=

- `a != b` returns `true` if any corresponding `int` component differs, and `false` if all three components match.

## IVec3::operator*

- `a * s` multiplies all three components by the `int` scalar `s` and returns a new `IVec3`, leaving `a` unchanged.
- `s * a` is also supported and returns the same result.

## IVec3::operator*=

- `a *= s` multiplies all three components of `a` by the `int` scalar `s`.
- Returns an `IVec3&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec3::operator+

- `a + b` returns a new `IVec3` containing `a.x + b.x`, `a.y + b.y`, and `a.z + b.z`, leaving both operands unchanged.

## IVec3::operator+=

- `a += b` adds each component of `b` to the corresponding component of `a`.
- Returns an `IVec3&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec3::operator-

- `a - b` returns a new `IVec3` containing `a.x - b.x`, `a.y - b.y`, and `a.z - b.z`, leaving both operands unchanged.
- Unary `-a` returns a new `IVec3` containing `-a.x`, `-a.y`, and `-a.z`, leaving `a` unchanged.

## IVec3::operator-=

- `a -= b` subtracts each component of `b` from the corresponding component of `a`.
- Returns an `IVec3&` reference to the modified vector.

## IVec3::operator==

- `a == b` returns `true` if all three corresponding `int` components match, and `false` otherwise.

## IVec3::toVec3

- `a.toVec3()` casts `x`, `y`, and `z` to `float` and returns a new `Vec3`, leaving `a` unchanged.

## IVec3::x

- This public `int` member can be read and assigned directly. It is initialized to `0` when the vector is default-constructed.

## IVec3::xy

- `a.xy()` returns a new `IVec2` containing `a.x` and `a.y`; `z` is omitted.
- The result is an independent copy, so changing it does not modify `a`.

## IVec3::y

- This public `int` member can be read and assigned directly. It is initialized to `0` when the vector is default-constructed.

## IVec3::z

- This public `int` member can be read and assigned directly. It is initialized to `0` when the vector is default-constructed.

## IesProfile

- Loads photometric data from a file or string for attachment to a light with `light.setIesProfile(&profile)`; GPU PBR uses the profile to modulate point or spot light intensity.
- Always averages the candela samples across horizontal angles and linearly interpolates vertically into a 256×1 RGBA8 texture; the RGB channels store intensity normalized by the profile peak, and alpha is `1`.
- Loading parses data on the calling thread and immediately creates GPU resources; load on the main rendering thread after graphics initialization.
- Owns its GPU image, view, and sampler, supports moving, and prohibits copying. Returned GPU handles are borrowed; do not destroy them or retain them across replacement of the profile resources.
- A light stores only a pointer to the profile. Keep the profile alive at the same address while attached; before destroying or moving it, detach it with `light.setIesProfile(nullptr)` or update the light's pointer.
- Replacing or destroying the profile queues its GPU resources for deferred destruction so recorded draws can retain them. Failed reloads preserve the previous profile, including its loading state, metadata and handles. Moving clears the source loading state but can leave numeric metadata; use `isLoaded()` to check it.

## IesProfile::getMaxCandela

- Returns the peak after applying the file's candela multiplier, before horizontal averaging and texture normalization; the stored peak never falls below `0`.
- The initial value is `0`; for loading-state and metadata lifetime rules, see `IesProfile`.

## IesProfile::getMaxVerticalAngle

- Returns the last vertical-angle entry from the loaded data, converted from degrees to radians; the initial value is approximately `TAU / 2`.
- For loading-state and metadata lifetime rules, see `IesProfile`.

## IesProfile::getTextureWidth

- Returns the number of vertical-angle samples in the texture: initially `0`, and `256` after texture generation; the texture height is `1`.
- For loading-state and metadata lifetime rules, see `IesProfile`.

## IesProfile::isLoaded

- Initially `false`; becomes `true` only after parsed tables, pixels and valid GPU resources have been prepared and installed.
- A failed `load()` or `loadFromString()` preserves the previous loading state and profile. Moving clears the source object's flag.

## IesProfile::load

- Accepts an `fs::path`; relative paths are resolved through `getDataPath()`, and absolute paths are used directly.
- Reads the file synchronously and passes its contents to `loadFromString()`; returns that function's result.
- Returns `false` and reports an error if the file is missing, is not a regular file, or cannot be opened; these failures preserve the existing profile. Once parsing starts, the replacement and failure behavior follows `loadFromString()`.
- For supported data, threading, GPU resource ownership, and attachment lifetime, see `IesProfile` and `IesProfile::loadFromString`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    // ies and light are IesProfile and Light members.
    if (ies.load("spot.ies")) {
        light.setPoint(0, 100, 0);
        light.setIesProfile(&ies);
        addLight(light);
    }
}
```

## IesProfile::loadFromString

- Accepts IES text as a `const string&`; requires a `TILT=` line followed by the numeric header, vertical and horizontal angles in degrees, and the candela table.
- Applies the header's candela multiplier. Embedded `TILT=INCLUDE` data is skipped without applying its factors; external tilt files are not loaded, and the photometric-type header does not change the angle interpretation.
- Prepares parsed tables, pixels and GPU resources before replacing the profile. Parsing, allocation or GPU creation failure logs an Error, returns `false`, and preserves the previous profile, including metadata and handles. Allocation recovery requires standard-library configurations without iterator debugging; MSVC Debug iterator-proxy allocations in noexcept container operations are outside this guarantee.
- On success, installs the lookup texture, defers retirement of previous resources without allocating, marks the profile loaded, and returns `true`.
- For texture averaging, threading, ownership, and attachment lifetime, see `IesProfile`.

## Image

- Pixel access and `save()` use the CPU `Pixels`; drawing uses the GPU `Texture`. Changes to the texture do not update the CPU pixels.
- Loading uploads pixels into an Immutable texture. `allocate()` creates a Dynamic texture without uploading the zero-filled CPU pixels.
- `setColor()` marks the image as dirty. After editing through `getPixels()` or `getPixelsData()`, call `setDirty()` yourself, then call `update()` to upload changes to a Dynamic texture. Drawing and `getTexture()` do not upload changes automatically.
- `crop()`, `resize()`, `halve()` and the mirror methods rebuild the texture while preserving its usage and mipmap setting. Immutable textures receive the changed pixels immediately; Dynamic textures require `update()`.
- Direct edits through the returned pixel reference or pointer do not cancel a pending asynchronous load; its result can replace those edits. See `Image::loadAsync` for cancellation and delivery rules.
- Images cannot be copied. Moving transfers committed pixels and texture resources; see `Image::loadAsync` for the effect on pending requests and listeners.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and upload costs, and `TextureFormat` for pixel and texture formats.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.load("photo.png");
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Image::allocate

- `allocate(width, height, channels = 4, mipmaps = false)` replaces the image with a zero-filled U8 pixel buffer and a Dynamic texture. Width and height are in pixels.
- CPU channel counts from 1 to 4 are accepted. The current GPU allocation selects RGBA8 for four channels and R8 otherwise; see `TextureFormat` for format details.
- Edit the pixels and call `update()` to upload them; allocation alone does not upload the CPU buffer or mark it as dirty. See `Image` for CPU and GPU synchronization.
- With `mipmaps = true`, each upload rebuilds and uploads the mip chain using CPU 2×2 averaging.
- Negative dimensions, invalid channel counts and byte-count overflow log an error and leave the CPU buffer empty. Zero dimensions are accepted by the CPU allocator; GPU allocation is separate. `isAllocated()` reports CPU allocation even if GPU allocation fails.
- Cancels pending asynchronous loading before releasing the previous image. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.allocate(256, 256);
    image.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    image.update();
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Image::clear

- Cancels pending asynchronous loading without waiting or sending `onLoad`, then releases the CPU pixels and GPU texture.
- Resets dimensions and channel count to zero, clears the dirty flag and disables mipmaps. The debug name and registered listeners remain.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Image::crop

- `crop(x, y, w, h)` copies a region starting at the top-left-based pixel coordinate `(x, y)` into a new `w × h` buffer. Samples outside the source repeat the nearest edge pixel.
- An unallocated image or nonpositive `w` or `h` leaves the pixels unchanged. Pending asynchronous loading is cancelled even for invalid or unchanged requests.
- Preserves the pixel format and channel count, then rebuilds the texture. See `Image` for when `update()` is required and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Image::getChannels

- Returns the channel count of the internal `Pixels`, or zero after construction or `clear()`. Successful image loading produces four channels.
- See `TextureFormat` for channel and format details.

## Image::getColor

- `getColor(x, y)` delegates to the internal `Pixels` and returns a `Color` without reading the GPU texture.
- See `Pixels::getColor` for coordinates, bounds, channel handling and color ranges, and `Image` for CPU and GPU synchronization.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!image.load("photo.png")) return;
    Color color = image.getColor(0, 0);
    image.setColor(1, 0, color);
}
```

## Image::getHeight

- Returns the internal CPU pixel height in pixels, or zero after construction or `clear()`.

## Image::getPixels

- Returns `Pixels&`, or `const Pixels&` for a const image, without copying pixels or reading the GPU texture.
- Direct edits do not mark the image as dirty or cancel asynchronous loading. See `Image` for synchronization and `setDirty()` usage.
- The reference belongs to the Image; replacing or clearing its pixel storage invalidates pointers into that storage.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.allocate(64, 64);
    image.getPixels().setColor(0, 0, Color(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    image.setDirty();
    image.update();
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Image::getPixelsData

- Returns the internal `Pixels::getData()` pointer as `unsigned char*`, or `const unsigned char*` for a const image; it is null after construction or `clear()`. For F32 pixels, use `getPixels().getDataF32()` instead of treating the storage as U8 values.
- For U8 pixels, channels are interleaved in row order; channel zero of `(x, y)` starts at `((size_t)y * getWidth() + x) * getChannels()`. See `TextureFormat` for formats.
- The pointer is borrowed and becomes invalid when its storage is replaced or released. Direct edits neither mark the image as dirty nor cancel asynchronous loading; see `Image` for synchronization.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.allocate(64, 64);
    image.getPixelsData()[0] = 255;
    image.getPixelsData()[3] = 255;
    image.setDirty();
    image.update();
}
void tcApp::draw() { image.draw(0, 0); }
```

## Image::getTexture

- Returns `Texture&`, or `const Texture&` for a const image, without uploading dirty CPU pixels. The returned texture can be unallocated even when `Image::isAllocated()` is true.
- The texture belongs to the Image and can be rebuilt by image operations. See `Image` for CPU and GPU synchronization and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Image::getWidth

- Returns the internal CPU pixel width in pixels, or zero after construction or `clear()`.

## Image::halve

- Replaces the pixels with 2×2 box averages at `max(width / 2, 1) × max(height / 2, 1)`, using integer division. An unmatched final row or column of an odd dimension is omitted; a dimension of one repeats its only sample.
- U8 RGB channels in three- or four-channel buffers use a gamma 2.2 conversion for averaging in linear light. Alpha, one- and two-channel buffers and F32 values are averaged directly.
- An unallocated image is unchanged. Pending asynchronous loading is cancelled before this check, including for unchanged requests.
- Preserves the pixel format and channel count, then rebuilds the texture. See `Image` for when `update()` is required and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Image::isAllocated

- Returns the allocation state of the internal `Pixels`, independently of GPU texture allocation. Use `getTexture().isAllocated()` to check the texture.
- During asynchronous loading, reports the committed image state rather than whether loading is in progress; use `isLoading()` for the request state.

## Image::load

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- `load(path, mipmaps = false)` decodes the file into four-channel U8 RGBA pixels and uploads an Immutable texture. Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`; absolute paths are used as given.
- The decoder supports JPEG, PNG, TGA, BMP, PSD, GIF, Radiance HDR, Softimage PIC and binary PPM/PGM, subject to each decoder's supported variants. This method produces U8 pixels even for HDR or higher-bit-depth input; use `Pixels::loadHDR()` for floating-point HDR pixels.
- On macOS and iOS, files rejected by the first decoder are tried with ImageIO, including HEIC/HEIF, TIFF and JPEG 2000 where supported by the OS. This fallback sets alpha to 1.
- Returns a `LoadResult` that is true on success. An unavailable file returns `FileNotFound`, rejected image data returns `DecodeFailed`, dimensions above the active GPU texture limit return `TooLarge`, and texture upload failure returns `Unknown`.
- Clears the previous image and cancels pending asynchronous loading before decoding. Failure leaves the image empty. Without an active GPU, successful loading retains CPU pixels and leaves the texture unallocated.
- `mipmaps = true` builds a mip chain for sampling at varying scales, such as on a 3D surface. See `Image` for subsequent CPU and GPU synchronization.
- Call on the main thread; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules. Use `loadAsync()` for deferred loading, or `Pixels::load()` for CPU decoding on a worker.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto result = image.load("photo.png", true);
    if (!result) logError("Image") << result.message;
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Image::loadFromMemory

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- `loadFromMemory(buffer, len, mipmaps = false)` decodes `len` bytes of encoded image data into four-channel U8 RGBA pixels and uploads an Immutable texture. It copies the decoded pixels and does not retain the input buffer.
- Uses the same primary decoder as `Image::load`, without the platform file-loading fallback. `mipmaps = true` builds a mip chain.
- Returns `LoadResult`: `DecodeFailed` for rejected data, `TooLarge` for dimensions above the active GPU texture limit, or `Unknown` for texture upload failure. Clears the previous image and cancels asynchronous loading before decoding; failure leaves the image empty.
- Without an active GPU, successful decoding keeps CPU pixels and leaves the texture unallocated. Call on the main thread; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules. For worker decoding, use `Pixels::loadFromMemory()`.

## Image::mirror

- `mirror(horizontal, vertical)` flips left to right when `horizontal` is true and top to bottom when `vertical` is true. Both true produce a half-turn; dimensions, channels and pixel format are unchanged.
- An unallocated image or two false arguments leaves the pixels unchanged. Pending asynchronous loading is cancelled even for unchanged requests.
- Rebuilds the texture after a flip. See `Image` for when `update()` is required and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Image::mirrorH

- Equivalent to `mirror(true, false)`; dimensions are unchanged.
- Cancels pending asynchronous loading even if the image is unallocated or the result is unchanged. See `Image` for texture synchronization after rebuilding.

## Image::mirrorV

- Equivalent to `mirror(false, true)`; dimensions are unchanged.
- Cancels pending asynchronous loading even if the image is unallocated or the result is unchanged. See `Image` for texture synchronization after rebuilding.

## Image::resize

- `resize(newW, newH)` sets the target dimensions in pixels. Each axis uses BoxArea filtering when shrinking and Catmull-Rom bicubic filtering when enlarging, with a horizontal pass followed by a vertical pass.
- U8 RGB channels in three- or four-channel buffers use gamma 2.2 conversion to process in linear light. Alpha, one- and two-channel buffers and F32 values are processed directly.
- An unallocated image or nonpositive target dimension leaves pixels unchanged. The same dimensions also leave pixels unchanged, but still rebuild the texture. Pending asynchronous loading is cancelled for all requests, including invalid or unchanged ones.
- Preserves the channel count and pixel format. See `Image` for texture synchronization and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.
- This is CPU resampling. For resizing with the GPU sampler, draw the source into an `Fbo` at the target size, using mipmaps when needed.

## Image::save

- Saves the current CPU pixels without GPU readback or an `update()` requirement. Returns a `SaveResult` that is true on success; empty or F32 pixels return `WriteFailed`.
- Selects the encoder from the case-insensitive extension: `jpg` or `jpeg` uses JPEG quality 90, `bmp` uses BMP, and every other extension uses PNG. The supplied filename is retained.
- Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`, absolute paths are used as given, and missing parent directories are created. Paths inside the app bundle return `AccessDenied`.
- Encodes into memory, writes to `<file>.tmp`, checks writing and closing, then replaces the destination by rename. Failed writes preserve the previous file and remove the temporary file.
- Atomic replacement does not guarantee durability after a power loss.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!image.load("photo.png")) return;
    image.resize(320, 240);
    auto result = image.save("exports/photo.png");
    if (!result) logError("Image") << result.message;
}
```

## Image::setColor

- `setColor(x, y, color)` delegates to the internal `Pixels`. See `Pixels::getColor` for coordinates, bounds, channel handling and color ranges.
- Cancels pending asynchronous loading before attempting the edit and marks the image as dirty even if the coordinates are invalid or the color is unchanged.
- Does not upload pixels. See `Image` for synchronization, including the difference between Dynamic and Immutable textures.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.allocate(64, 64);
    image.setColor(10, 20, Color(1.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    image.update();
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Image::setDirty

- Sets the dirty flag without uploading pixels, changing texture usage or cancelling asynchronous loading.
- Call after direct CPU pixel edits, then call `update()` for a Dynamic texture. See `Image` for CPU and GPU synchronization.

## Image::update

- Attempts an upload only when the image is dirty and its texture is allocated. Use `setColor()`, or call `setDirty()` after direct pixel edits; see `Image` for CPU and GPU synchronization.
- Images created with `allocate()` use Dynamic textures. Loaded images use Immutable textures, whose uploads are ignored. A width, height or channel mismatch also prevents uploading.
- Clears the dirty flag after the upload attempt, even if the texture rejects it. With no allocated texture, it leaves the dirty flag unchanged.
- For ordinary Dynamic textures, a second upload to the same GPU image in the same device frame is skipped with a warning. `Image::update()` still clears the dirty flag, so a skipped change requires marking dirty again before a later frame.
- With Dynamic mipmaps, rebuilds the mip chain on the CPU and recreates the GPU image with all levels. This replaces the underlying GPU image rather than updating its existing levels.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and upload costs.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    image.allocate(64, 64);
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    image.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    image.update();
    image.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## ImageType

- The scoped enum provides `ImageType::Color` (RGBA, value `0`) and `ImageType::Grayscale` (grayscale, value `1`).
- `Image::allocate()` accepts an integer channel count, defaulting to `4`, rather than an `ImageType` value.

## Json

- v0.8: the bundled text parser rejects nesting beyond 64 levels, including direct `Json::parse` calls. Parsed values carry private provenance used by transactional settings reflection; see `JsonReadReflector`. Local documents have no byte-size cap.
- Defined as `using Json = nlohmann::json;` and used by `loadJson`, `saveJson`, `parseJson`, and `toJsonString`. Its full API is the nlohmann/json API.
- A default-constructed `Json()` holds JSON `null`, not an empty object or array; check it with `is_null()`.

## KeyEventArgs

- Used by `events().keyPressed`, `events().keyReleased`, and the `KeyEventArgs` versions of App and Node keyboard callbacks.
- `key` identifies the key, `isRepeat` identifies repeated presses, and `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, and `super` report the event's modifier state.
- See `Event<T>` for listener registration, lifetime, priority arguments, and delivery threads.
- See `EventPriority::BeforeApp` for listener priorities and `consumed`, and `App::mousePressed` for the shared order of listeners, App callbacks, and the node tree.

## KeyEventArgs::alt

- This boolean is `true` when the event's Alt modifier flag is set; it defaults to `false`.

## KeyEventArgs::consumed

- Defaults to `false`; a listener can mark the event as handled with `e.consumed = true`.
- See `EventPriority::BeforeApp` for how this stops remaining listeners, and `App::mousePressed` for its effect on App callbacks and the node tree.

## KeyEventArgs::ctrl

- This boolean is `true` when the event's Ctrl modifier flag is set; it defaults to `false`.

## KeyEventArgs::isRepeat

- Repeated key presses are delivered with `isRepeat == true`; the initial press and key release use `false`.
- Defaults to `false`; use `if (e.isRepeat) return;` to ignore repeated presses in a callback.

## KeyEventArgs::key

- Letter keys use uppercase codes, so compare with `e.key == 'A'` regardless of whether Shift is held.
- Compare special keys with constants such as `KEY_ENTER` and `KEY_LEFT`; `KEY_*` constants use the corresponding `SAPP_KEYCODE_*` values.
- This integer defaults to `0`; check `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, and `super` separately for modifier state.

## KeyEventArgs::shift

- This boolean is `true` when the event's Shift modifier flag is set; it defaults to `false`.

## KeyEventArgs::super

- This boolean is `true` when the event's Super modifier flag is set, including Command on macOS; it defaults to `false`.

## KinsokuLevel

- Set the level with `Font::setKinsoku()`; it applies to horizontal and vertical wrapping, and the default is `KinsokuLevel::Off`.
- `Off` disables the kinsoku character tables; separate Latin word-wrapping rules still apply.
- `PunctuationOnly` checks line starts for commas, periods, colons, semicolons, question marks, exclamation marks, and ellipses, including the supported Japanese and fullwidth forms; it adds no line-end restrictions.
- `Standard` also checks line starts for closing brackets, small kana, the long sound mark, and kana iteration marks, and checks line ends for opening brackets.

## LayoutDirection

- `LayoutDirection::Vertical` stacks active child `RectNode` objects from top to bottom; `Horizontal` stacks them from left to right.
- Pass it to the `LayoutMod` constructor or `setDirection()`; the default is `Vertical`.

## LayoutMod

- Add it with `container->addMod<LayoutMod>(direction, spacing)` to arrange a `RectNode` parent's active direct `RectNode` children in child-list order. Vertical layout proceeds downward; horizontal layout proceeds rightward. Other children are skipped.
- Defaults are `LayoutDirection::Vertical`, zero spacing and padding, and `AxisMode::None` for both axes. Spacing, padding, sizes, and positions use the parent's local coordinates.
- The main axis follows the layout direction; the cross axis is perpendicular. Cross-axis `Fill` sets each child's cross-axis size to the parent size minus padding. Cross-axis `Content` sizes the parent to the largest child plus padding.
- Main-axis `Content` sizes the parent to the sum of child sizes, gaps, and padding. Main-axis `Fill` currently leaves sizes unchanged, as `None` does.
- `setPadding(value)` sets all sides; `setPadding(vertical, horizontal)` sets opposite pairs; `setPadding(top, right, bottom, left)` sets each side separately.
- Placement starts at the left and top padding, aligns children to that cross-axis edge, and sets each arranged child's local Z position to zero.
- Layout runs on attachment, on layout setter calls, and on `updateLayout()`. Changes to children, active states, or sizes do not trigger automatic layout; call `updateLayout()` after those changes.
- Layout does nothing without a `RectNode` owner. Adding another `LayoutMod` to the same node replaces the previous instance of that type. See `Node` for scene graph threading and lifetime rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto container = make_shared<RectNode>();
    container->setSize(240, 120);
    container->addChild(make_shared<RectNode>());
    container->addMod<LayoutMod>(LayoutDirection::Vertical, 8.0f)
        ->setCrossAxis(AxisMode::Fill).setMainAxis(AxisMode::Content);
    addChild(container);
}
```

## LayoutMod::getCrossAxis

- Returns the stored `AxisMode`; the default is `AxisMode::None`.
- For the meaning of each mode and the axis direction, see `LayoutMod::setCrossAxis`.

## LayoutMod::getDirection

- Returns the stored `LayoutDirection`: `Vertical` arranges children from top to bottom, and `Horizontal` arranges them from left to right.
- The default is `LayoutDirection::Vertical`; the constructor can specify another direction.

## LayoutMod::getMainAxis

- Returns the stored `AxisMode`; the default is `AxisMode::None`.
- For the meaning of each mode and the axis direction, see `LayoutMod::setMainAxis`.

## LayoutMod::getPaddingBottom

- Returns the stored bottom padding as a `float`; the default is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::getPaddingLeft

- Returns the stored left padding as a `float`; the default is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::getPaddingRight

- Returns the stored right padding as a `float`; the default is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::getPaddingTop

- Returns the stored top padding as a `float`; the default is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::getSpacing

- Returns the stored spacing as a `float`; the default is `0.0f`, unless another value was supplied to the constructor.
- For coordinate units and which children participate, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setCrossAxis

- The cross axis is width for a vertical layout and height for a horizontal layout.
- `AxisMode::None` leaves sizes unchanged and is the default. `Fill` sets each participating child's cross-axis size to the owner's size minus padding; `Content` sets the owner's cross-axis size to the maximum of zero and the participating children's cross-axis sizes, plus the corresponding padding.
- Immediately calls `updateLayout()` and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. For shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setDirection

- Pass `LayoutDirection::Vertical` to arrange children from top to bottom, or `LayoutDirection::Horizontal` to arrange them from left to right. The default is `Vertical`.
- Immediately calls `updateLayout()` and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. For shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setMainAxis

- The main axis is height for a vertical layout and width for a horizontal layout.
- `AxisMode::Content` sets the owner's main-axis size to the sum of participating children's sizes, gaps, and padding. `None` is the default and leaves sizes unchanged; `Fill` currently also leaves main-axis sizes unchanged.
- Immediately calls `updateLayout()` and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. For shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setPadding

- `setPadding(padding)` sets all four sides; `setPadding(vertical, horizontal)` sets top and bottom from the first argument and left and right from the second.
- The four-argument order is `setPadding(top, right, bottom, left)`. All sides default to `0.0f`.
- Each overload immediately calls `updateLayout()` and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. For coordinate units and shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto container = make_shared<RectNode>();
    container->setSize(320, 240);
    addChild(container);
    container->addMod<LayoutMod>()->setPadding(12.0f, 20.0f);
}
```

## LayoutMod::setPaddingBottom

- Stores `v` as the bottom padding, immediately calls `updateLayout()`, and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. The default padding is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units and shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setPaddingLeft

- Stores `v` as the left padding, immediately calls `updateLayout()`, and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. The default padding is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units and shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setPaddingRight

- Stores `v` as the right padding, immediately calls `updateLayout()`, and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. The default padding is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units and shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setPaddingTop

- Stores `v` as the top padding, immediately calls `updateLayout()`, and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. The default padding is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units and shared layout rules, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::setSpacing

- Stores the `float` argument `spacing` as the gap between consecutive participating children, immediately calls `updateLayout()`, and returns `*this` as `LayoutMod&` for chaining. The default spacing is `0.0f`.
- For coordinate units and which children participate, see `LayoutMod::updateLayout`.

## LayoutMod::updateLayout

- Call this after adding, removing, resizing, or changing the active state of children, or after resizing the owner. Attachment and layout setters trigger layout, but `earlyUpdate()` does not automatically detect changes or repeat layout.
- Only active direct children that are `RectNode` instances or subclasses participate, in child-list order. Visibility is not checked, and descendants are not laid out recursively.
- Positions start at `(paddingLeft, paddingTop)` and advance along the layout direction by each child's size plus spacing. Each participating child's local position is replaced, including setting its Z coordinate to zero.
- Spacing, padding, and dimensions use the owner's local coordinate units. Calculations use stored widths and heights without accounting for child rotation or scale; negative values and negative space remaining after padding are used without clamping, except that the maximum child size used by cross-axis `Content` is floored at zero.
- Sizing follows `LayoutMod::setCrossAxis` and `LayoutMod::setMainAxis`. With no participating children, a dimension using `AxisMode::Content` becomes the sum of its two padding values.
- Returns no value and does nothing if there is no owner or the owner is not a `RectNode`.
- Changes take effect synchronously. Use the main thread; see `Node` for scene graph threading and ownership rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto container = make_shared<RectNode>();
    addChild(container);
    auto layout = container->addMod<LayoutMod>();
    container->addChild(make_shared<RectNode>());
    layout->updateLayout();
}
```

## Left

- This `inline constexpr Direction` equals `Direction::Left` and can be passed wherever a `Direction` value is accepted.

## Light

- Configure the light with `setDirectional()`, `setPoint()`, or `setSpot()`, then register it with `addLight(light)`; registration is per window, allows up to eight lights, and ignores duplicate registration.
- Positions use world coordinates; directions describe light travel and nonzero directions are normalized. Spot angles are half-angles in radians, defaulting to an inner angle of `0` and an outer angle of approximately `TAU / 8`.
- Defaults to an enabled directional light traveling along `(0, -1, 0)`, with position `(0, 0, 0)`, white diffuse and specular colors, ambient RGB `(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)`, intensity `1`, and attenuation coefficients `(1, 0, 0)`.
- For point and spot lights, CPU distance attenuation uses `1 / (constant + linear * distance + quadratic * distance * distance)` at nonzero distances and `1` at zero distance. GPU distance attenuation uses `1 / max(constant + linear * distance + quadratic * distance * distance, 1e-5)`. GPU PBR uses the diffuse color and intensity; ambient and specular colors are used by the CPU lighting calculation.
- `enable()` and `disable()` affect CPU lighting; GPU PBR currently uses registered lights without checking their enabled flag.
- Registration stores the object's address without taking ownership. Keep registered lights in stable storage; copying or moving to a new object does not transfer registration, and destruction unregisters the original object from every window.
- Projection textures and IES profiles are borrowed pointers; pass `nullptr` to detach them and keep attached objects alive at stable addresses. The GPU has one projector slot for the first registered spot light with a texture and one IES slot for the first registered light with a profile; additional lights do not receive these effects and produce a one-time warning.
- Shadows are initially disabled; directional and spot lights support shadow passes for up to four lights per frame. See `beginShadowPass` for the drawing sequence and `calculateLighting` for CPU lighting behavior.

## Light::calculate

- Pass the world-space surface position as `worldPos`, a normalized world-space normal as `worldNormal`, the surface `material`, and the world-space camera position as `viewPos`. The normal is not normalized internally.
- The material's base color supplies diffuse color and, multiplied by 0.2, ambient color. Specular color interpolates from 0.04 to the base color using metallic, and shininess is `(1 - roughness)² * 128`.
- Directional lights use the opposite of their travel direction without distance attenuation. Point and spot lights use `1 / (constant + linear * distance + quadratic * distance²)`; the denominator is not checked for zero. At zero distance, the surface-to-light direction is `(0, 1, 0)` and attenuation is 1.
- Intensity and attenuation multiply the diffuse and specular contributions, but not ambient. Spot cones, projection textures, IES profiles, shadows, material textures, and material emission are not evaluated.
- Returns an unclamped `Color` whose alpha is the material's base-color alpha. A disabled light returns `Color(0, 0, 0, 0)`.

## Light::computeProjectorViewProj

- Returns a `Mat4` equal to the projection matrix multiplied by the view matrix, looking from the stored position along the stored light direction.
- Uses the spot's outer half-angle as the vertical field-of-view half-angle and the stored projector aspect as width divided by height. Lens shifts offset the frustum by fractions of its half-width and half-height.
- `nearClip` and `farClip` are clipping distances in world units, defaulting to 0.1 and 10000. No validation of clipping distances or frustum dimensions is performed.
- Computes the matrix on the CPU without rendering or requiring a projection texture. It uses the stored parameters regardless of the light's type or enabled state.

## Light::computeShadowViewProj

- For spot lights, returns `computeProjectorViewProj()` with its default clipping distances, including the projector aspect and lens shift.
- For directional lights, returns an orthographic projection multiplied by a view matrix. The eye is one shadow-area radius behind the shadow-area center along the normalized light direction; horizontal and vertical bounds are `[-radius, radius]`, with near 0 and far `2 * radius`.
- Point lights return the same orthographic fallback. This does not provide point-light shadows: `beginShadowPass` warns and skips point lights.
- Computes only a CPU matrix and does not render or check whether shadows are enabled.

## Light::disable

- Sets `isEnabled()` to false, causing `calculate` to return transparent black and CPU lighting to skip this light.
- Does not unregister the light. See `Light::enable` for how the GPU PBR path handles this flag.

## Light::disableShadow

- Sets `isShadowEnabled()` to false without changing the requested resolution or releasing shadow resources.
- Shadow rendering does not check this flag. See `Light::enableShadow` for the required shadow-pass calls and current flag behavior.

## Light::enable

- Sets `isEnabled()` to true so that CPU lighting includes this light. Lights are enabled by default.
- Does not register the light; use `addLight` to register it in the current window.
- The GPU PBR path includes registered lights without checking this flag, even after `disable()`. Use `removeLight` to exclude a light from that window's registered lights.

## Light::enableShadow

- Sets `isShadowEnabled()` to true and stores `resolution` as the requested square map's width and height in pixels. The argument defaults to 1024 and is stored without validation; shadows are disabled by default.
- This call does not allocate a map or render shadows. Register the light with `addLight`, then render the casters with `shadowDraw` between `beginShadowPass(light)` and `endShadowPass()` before drawing the lit scene.
- Shadow rendering does not check `isShadowEnabled()`. Calling the shadow-pass functions still renders after `disableShadow()`, while calling `enableShadow()` alone does not render a shadow.
- Directional and spot lights support shadows; point-light passes warn and do nothing. At most four shadow passes are accepted per frame in each window, and further passes are skipped with a warning.
- Shadow passes share a map array that grows to the largest resolution requested by a pass so far and does not shrink for smaller requests. GPU allocation or reallocation occurs when a pass needs a larger map.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    // light is a Light member of tcApp.
    light.setDirectional(0, -1, 0);
    light.enableShadow(1024);
    addLight(light);
}
```

## Light::getAmbient

- Returns the stored color as `const Color&`; the default is `Color(0.2f, 0.2f, 0.2f, 1.0f)`. Color channels use the 0–1 convention, but stored values are not clamped.
- Used by CPU Phong lighting; the GPU PBR path does not read this color.

## Light::getConstantAttenuation

- Returns the stored `float` coefficient, which defaults to 1.
- For point and spot lights, the distance attenuation formula is `1 / (constant + linear * distance + quadratic * distance²)`, with distance measured in world units.
- GPU rendering clamps the denominator to at least `1e-5`. CPU `calculate()` does not clamp it, but uses attenuation 1 at zero distance regardless of the coefficients.

## Light::getDiffuse

- Returns the stored color as `const Color&`; the default is white, `Color(1, 1, 1, 1)`.
- Supplies the diffuse color for CPU Phong lighting and the light's main RGB color for GPU PBR rendering.

## Light::getDirection

- Returns the stored direction as `const Vec3&`; the default is `(0, -1, 0)`.
- `setDirectional` and `setSpot` normalize nonzero direction arguments. A zero direction argument leaves the previous direction unchanged.

## Light::getIesProfile

- Returns the stored `const IesProfile*`, or `nullptr` if no profile is attached; the default is `nullptr`.
- The light does not own the profile. Keep it alive while attached and in use.
- GPU PBR rendering uses the first registered light with an attached profile for its single IES slot; further attached profiles are ignored with a warning.

## Light::getIntensity

- Returns the stored `float` intensity multiplier, which defaults to 1. `setIntensity` stores the value without clamping.

## Light::getLensShiftX

- Returns the stored `float` shift as a fraction of the projection frustum's half-width; the default is 0. A value of 1 shifts the frustum by one half-width in the positive horizontal direction.
- Values are not clamped. See `Light::computeProjectorViewProj` for how lens shift affects the projection.

## Light::getLensShiftY

- Returns the stored `float` shift as a fraction of the projection frustum's half-height; the default is 0. A value of 1 shifts the frustum by one half-height in the positive vertical direction.
- Values are not clamped. See `Light::computeProjectorViewProj` for how lens shift affects the projection.

## Light::getLinearAttenuation

- Returns the stored `float` coefficient, which defaults to 0. See `Light::getConstantAttenuation` for the distance attenuation formula and units.

## Light::getPosition

- Returns the stored world-space position as `const Vec3&`; the default is `(0, 0, 0)`.
- Point and spot lighting use this position. Directional lighting uses the direction instead.

## Light::getProjectionTexture

- Returns the stored gobo texture as `const Texture*`, or `nullptr` if none is attached; the default is `nullptr`.
- The light does not own the texture. Keep it alive while attached and in use.
- GPU PBR rendering projects a texture only for the first registered spot light with an attached texture. Further textured spot lights render as ordinary spot lights with a warning.

## Light::getProjectorAspect

- Returns the stored width-to-height ratio as `float`; the default is `16.0f / 9.0f`.
- Attaching a projection texture does not update this value from its dimensions. Set the desired ratio explicitly with `setProjectorAspect`; values are stored without validation.

## Light::getQuadraticAttenuation

- Returns the stored `float` coefficient, which defaults to 0. See `Light::getConstantAttenuation` for the distance attenuation formula and units.

## Light::getShadowAreaCenter

- Returns the stored world-space center as `const Vec3&`; the default is `(0, 0, 0)`.
- See `Light::computeShadowViewProj` for the directional shadow volume. Spot shadows use the projector frustum instead.

## Light::getShadowAreaRadius

- Returns the stored radius as `float` in world units; the default is 500. It is the half-extent of the light-aligned box, not a spherical radius.
- See `Light::computeShadowViewProj` for the volume's placement and clipping distances. Spot shadows do not use this radius.

## Light::getShadowBias

- Returns the stored base depth bias as `float` in world units; the default is 1.
- During GPU shadow comparison, this value is multiplied by a slope factor based on the surface normal and light direction, then subtracted from receiver depth.

## Light::getShadowResolution

- Returns the stored `int` width and height in pixels for the square shadow map; the default is 1024, even when shadows are disabled.
- This is the requested resolution, not necessarily the shared map's actual size. See `Light::enableShadow` for allocation and resolution sharing.

## Light::getShadowSamples

- Returns the stored `int` PCF tap count used by PCSS soft shadows. The default is 16, and `setShadowSamples` clamps values to 1–36.
- Applies only when shadow softness is positive. More taps increase filtering work and reduce noise; the blocker search remains fixed at 16 samples, and hard shadows ignore this setting.

## Light::getShadowSoftness

- Returns the stored `float` value, which defaults to 0. Positive values enable PCSS soft shadows; zero or negative values use the fixed hard-shadow filter.
- For spot lights, the value represents effective emitter size in world units. Larger values widen the penumbra, which becomes sharper as the caster approaches the receiver.
- For directional lights, the value specifies penumbra growth in world units per 100 world units of separation between caster and receiver.

## Light::getSpecular

- Returns the stored color as `const Color&`; the default is white, `Color(1, 1, 1, 1)`.
- Used by CPU Phong lighting; the GPU PBR path does not read this color.

## Light::getSpotInnerCos

- Returns the stored cosine as `float`, not an angle. The default is 1, corresponding to an inner half-angle of 0.
- `setSpot` computes this value from its `innerHalfAngle` argument in radians. GPU lighting uses it as the inner boundary of the cone's smooth falloff only for spot lights that are not selected as the texture projector.

## Light::getSpotOuterCos

- Returns the stored `float` value, initially `0.707f`, regardless of the current light type.
- `Light::setSpot` stores the cosine of its `outerHalfAngle` argument, which is specified in radians.

## Light::getType

- Returns `LightType::Directional`, `LightType::Point`, or `LightType::Spot`; the initial type is `LightType::Directional`.
- The type is changed by `Light::setDirectional`, `Light::setPoint`, or `Light::setSpot`.

## Light::hasIesProfile

- Returns `true` when the stored profile pointer is not `nullptr`; the initial result is `false`.
- Does not check whether the profile is loaded or receives the GPU's IES slot. See `Light::setIesProfile` for attachment and lifetime rules.

## Light::hasProjectionTexture

- Returns `true` when the stored texture pointer is not `nullptr`; the initial result is `false`.
- Does not check the texture's GPU resources, light type, or projector slot allocation. See `Light::setProjectionTexture` for projection and lifetime rules.

## Light::isEnabled

- Returns the flag controlled by `Light::enable` and `Light::disable`; it is initially `true`.
- CPU lighting checks this flag, but GPU PBR rendering currently uses registered lights without checking it.
- The flag does not indicate whether the light is registered with `addLight`.

## Light::isShadowEnabled

- Returns the flag controlled by `Light::enableShadow` and `Light::disableShadow`; it is initially `false`.
- `beginShadowPass` currently does not check this flag. Shadow maps are rendered through explicit shadow passes; see `beginShadowPass` for supported light types and pass requirements.

## Light::setAmbient

- Accepts a `Color` or `r, g, b, a` components, with `a` defaulting to `1.0f`. The initial color is `Color(0.2f, 0.2f, 0.2f, 1.0f)`; component units follow `Light::setDiffuse`.
- CPU Phong lighting uses RGB for the ambient contribution, independently of intensity and distance attenuation; alpha is ignored.
- GPU PBR rendering does not use this color.

## Light::setAttenuation

- Sets `constant`, `linear`, and `quadratic` for Point and Spot lights using `1 / (constant + linear * d + quadratic * d * d)`, where `d` is the distance in world units. Directional lights ignore these coefficients.
- The initial coefficients are `(1, 0, 0)`, which give no distance falloff. The setter stores values without validation.
- GPU PBR clamps the denominator to at least `1e-5`. CPU lighting does not clamp it and uses attenuation `1` when the distance is zero.

## Light::setDiffuse

- Accepts a `Color` or floating-point `r, g, b, a` components on the 0–1 color scale, with `a` defaulting to `1.0f`. The initial color is white, `Color(1, 1, 1, 1)`.
- Stores the components without clamping or color-space conversion. The same component convention applies to `Light::setAmbient` and `Light::setSpecular`.
- GPU PBR uses RGB as the light color for both diffuse and specular reflection. CPU Phong lighting uses RGB for diffuse reflection only; both paths ignore the light color's alpha.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    Light light;
    void setup() override {
        light.setDirectional(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
        light.setDiffuse(1.0f, 0.8f, 0.6f);
        addLight(light);
    }
};
```

## Light::setDirectional

- Sets the type to `LightType::Directional` and accepts the direction the light travels as a `Vec3` or `dx, dy, dz` components.
- Normalizes nonzero directions. A zero vector leaves the previous direction unchanged while still changing the type; the initial direction is `(0, -1, 0)`.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    Light light;
    void setup() override {
        light.setDirectional(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
        addLight(light);
    }
};
```

## Light::setIesProfile

- GPU PBR uses the profile to modulate Point and Spot light intensity by the angle from the light's stored direction, independently of projection texture color. CPU lighting does not use the profile.
- Pass a pointer to a loaded `IesProfile`, or `nullptr` to detach it; initially no profile is attached. The setter does not check loading state.
- The pointer is non-owning: keep the profile alive while the light uses it, or detach it before destruction.
- The GPU has one IES slot, assigned to the first registered light with a profile. Further profiles are ignored with a one-time warning; a Directional light can occupy this slot even though its lighting is not modulated by IES.

## Light::setIntensity

- Stores the dimensionless multiplier `i` without clamping; its initial value is `1.0f`.
- Multiplies direct lighting in GPU PBR and the diffuse and specular contributions in CPU Phong lighting. The CPU ambient contribution is unaffected.

## Light::setLensShift

- Sets horizontal `sx` and vertical `sy` shifts as fractions of the projected frame's half-width and half-height. The intended range is `[-1, 1]`, but values are stored without clamping; both initially equal zero.
- Positive values move the projection frustum toward positive coordinates on the corresponding projector view axis.
- Affects texture projection and the Spot light's shadow frustum, but does not change an ordinary spot cone's angular falloff.

## Light::setPoint

- Sets the type to `LightType::Point` and stores a world-space position supplied as a `Vec3` or `x, y, z` components.
- Leaves other light settings unchanged, including the stored direction used by IES profiles; distance falloff is controlled by `Light::setAttenuation`.
- Point light shadows are unsupported; see `beginShadowPass`.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    Light light;
    void setup() override {
        light.setPoint(0.0f, 200.0f, 100.0f);
        addLight(light);
    }
};
```

## Light::setProjectionTexture

- GPU PBR projects the texture through a Spot light and multiplies its light color by the sampled RGB; texture alpha is ignored. Projection uses the rectangular frustum instead of ordinary spot cone falloff, and contributes no light outside that frustum.
- Pass a pointer to a usable `Texture`, or `nullptr` to detach it; initially no texture is attached. The pointer is non-owning, so keep the texture alive while the light uses it or detach it before destruction.
- The GPU has one projector slot, assigned to the first registered Spot light with a texture. Further textured Spot lights illuminate as ordinary spots and trigger a one-time warning.
- CPU lighting does not use this texture. Use `Light::setProjectorAspect` and `Light::setLensShift` to control the projection.

## Light::setProjectorAspect

- Stores the width-to-height ratio `a` without validation; the initial value is `16.0f / 9.0f`.
- Controls the horizontal extent of texture projection and Spot shadow frusta. Attaching a texture does not automatically update this ratio from its dimensions.

## Light::setShadowArea

- Sets a light-aligned orthographic box centered on the world-space `center`, with half-extent `radius` in world units on all three axes. The initial center is `(0, 0, 0)` and the initial radius is `500`.
- Enclose all shadow casters and receivers that need shadows; receivers outside the box render without this light's shadow.
- Spot lights use their perspective projector frustum instead, and Point lights do not support shadows.
- Stores the values without validating the radius and returns this `Light` by reference for chaining.

## Light::setShadowBias

- Stores `bias` in world units without clamping; the initial value is `1.0f`.
- The GPU subtracts a slope-scaled version of this bias from the receiver depth before shadow comparison. Increasing it reduces self-shadow artifacts but can separate shadows from their casters.

## Light::setShadowSamples

- Clamps `taps` to `[1, 36]` and returns this `Light` by reference for chaining; the initial count is `16`.
- Controls the PCF filter only when `Light::setShadowSoftness` is greater than zero. The hard-shadow path ignores this count.
- More samples reduce noise at approximately linear GPU sampling cost. The separate blocker search always uses 16 samples.

## Light::setShadowSoftness

- Positive `size` enables PCSS soft shadows: larger values widen the penumbra, with sharper contact shadows and increasing blur as the caster and receiver separate.
- For Spot lights, `size` is the effective emitter size in world units; the world-space filter radius is based on `size * (receiverDepth - blockerDepth) / blockerDepth`.
- For Directional lights, `size` specifies penumbra growth in world units per 100 world units of separation along the light direction; approximately `0.9f` represents sunlight.
- The initial value is `0`, and values are not clamped. Values at or below zero use the fixed 3×3 bilinear PCF hard-shadow path without the additional PCSS blocker search and variable filter.
- The soft-shadow filter radius is limited to 16 shadow-map texels. See `Light::setShadowSamples` for its sample count and cost; this setter returns this `Light` by reference for chaining.

## Light::setSpecular

- Accepts a `Color` or `r, g, b, a` components, with `a` defaulting to `1.0f`. The initial color is white, `Color(1, 1, 1, 1)`; component units follow `Light::setDiffuse`.
- CPU Phong lighting uses RGB for specular reflection and ignores alpha.
- GPU PBR does not use this separate color; its specular reflection uses the color from `Light::setDiffuse`.

## Light::setSpot

- Sets the type to `LightType::Spot`, stores the world-space position, and normalizes the direction the light travels. Accepts two `Vec3` values or `px, py, pz, dx, dy, dz` components; a zero direction preserves the previous direction.
- `innerHalfAngle` and `outerHalfAngle` are cone half-angles in radians, matching the glTF punctual-light convention. Their defaults are `0.0f` and `0.7854f` respectively, giving an approximately 90° full outer cone; the setter stores their cosines without validating or reordering the angles.
- GPU PBR fades the light between the inner and outer cones and applies distance attenuation. CPU Phong lighting treats Spot lights like Point lights without cone falloff; projector behavior is described in `Light::setProjectionTexture`.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    Light light;
    void setup() override {
        light.setSpot(Vec3(0, 200, 0), Vec3(0, -1, 0), TAU / 24, TAU / 8);
        addLight(light);
    }
};
```

## LightType

- `Directional` represents parallel light specified by direction, `Point` represents light at a position, and `Spot` adds a directional cone to a positional light.
- Select the type with `Light::setDirectional()`, `Light::setPoint()`, or `Light::setSpot()`; a new `Light` defaults to `Directional`.
- The inner and outer cone angles passed to `setSpot()` are half-angles in radians.

## Location

- `latitude` and `longitude` are geographic coordinates in degrees; `altitude` is in meters, and `accuracy` is horizontal accuracy in meters.
- A default value has zero latitude, longitude, and altitude, with `accuracy == -1` indicating that accuracy is unavailable.
- On macOS, the first `getLocation()` call starts GPS/WiFi location updates; on iOS, it requests authorization, and updates begin once permission is granted. Both return the latest received data, or default values until an update arrives.
- Android, Windows, Linux, and Web currently return a default `Location` without obtaining a location fix.

## Location::accuracy

- This `float` stores horizontal accuracy in meters; the default is `-1`, indicating that no location has been received yet.
- On macOS and iOS, location updates copy the platform's horizontal accuracy directly into this field.
- See `getLocation` for obtaining location data and platform availability.

## Location::altitude

- This `double` stores altitude in meters; the default is `0`.
- Zero alone does not indicate whether a location has been received. See `Location::accuracy` and `getLocation` for availability.

## Location::latitude

- This `double` stores latitude in degrees, not radians; the default is `0`.
- Zero alone does not indicate whether a location has been received. See `Location::accuracy` and `getLocation` for availability.

## Location::longitude

- This `double` stores longitude in degrees, not radians; the default is `0`.
- Zero alone does not indicate whether a location has been received. See `Location::accuracy` and `getLocation` for availability.

## LogEventArgs

- `Logger::onLog` passes this object to listeners; its constructor takes a `LogLevel` and message string and generates the timestamp.
- The object owns its strings, but a callback reference is valid only during that callback; copy the object or strings to retain them.
- See `Logger` for listener delivery and threading rules.

## LogEventArgs::level

- A `LogLevel` initialized from the level passed to the `LogEventArgs` constructor.
- See `Logger` for output filtering and `LogEventArgs` for argument lifetime.

## LogEventArgs::message
