- Use indices from `0` through `getNumSubpaths() - 1` with `Path::getSubpathRange` and `Path::isSubpathClosed`.

## Path::getPerimeter

- Returns a `float` sum of three-dimensional distances between consecutive vertices within each subpath, in the path's coordinate units. Separate subpaths are never connected.
- Includes each eligible closing edge as described in `Path::close`; subpaths with fewer than two vertices contribute zero.
- Measures the stored line segments, so curves use their sampled approximation; drawing transforms and stroke width do not affect the result.

## Path::getSubpathRange

- Returns a `pair<size_t, size_t>` containing `[begin, end)` indices into `Path::getVertices`; `end` is excluded.
- The zero-based index must satisfy `i < getNumSubpaths()`. Bounds are not checked; invalid indices cause undefined behavior. This requirement also applies to `Path::isSubpathClosed` and the indexed `Path::reverseWinding` overload.

## Path::getVertices

- Returns the path's `vector<Vec3>` by reference without copying; a const path returns a const reference. Vertices from all subpaths share this vector.
- Editing positions through the mutable reference changes the path directly. Structural vector edits do not update subpath boundaries, so use the path's vertex and subpath methods to change its structure.
- The vector belongs to the path and must not be used after the path is destroyed. Reallocation invalidates references, pointers, and iterators to its elements; clearing removes all elements. This also applies to vertex references from `Path::operator[]`.

## Path::isClosed

- Returns the current, last subpath's closed flag, rather than checking all subpaths. See `Path::close` for what this flag controls.

## Path::isSubpathClosed

- Returns the closed flag for subpath `i`; see `Path::close` for closing behavior and `Path::getSubpathRange` for index requirements.

## Path::lineTo

- An alias for `Path::addVertex`, accepting `(x, y, z = 0)`, `Vec2`, or `Vec3`. Connects the new point to the preceding vertex in the same subpath when drawn.
- With no preceding vertex, only establishes the first point. Does not start a new subpath or change its closed state.

## Path::moveTo

- Accepts `(x, y, z = 0)`, `Vec2`, or `Vec3` and appends the starting vertex. If the current subpath already contains vertices, starts a new open subpath without connecting it to the preceding one; otherwise reuses the existing empty subpath.
- Clears the accumulated `Path::curveTo` points so spline control points do not carry into the new contour.
- A single path can hold multiple separate contours, like repeated SVG `M` commands. `Font::getGlyphPath` uses these contours for outer rings and holes; see `Path::buildFillTriangles` for fill classification.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    Path path;
    path.moveTo(40, 40);
    path.lineTo(160, 40);
    path.moveTo(40, 100);
    path.lineTo(160, 100);
    path.drawStroke();
}
```

## Path::operator[]

- Accepts an `int` index into the combined vertex list and returns `Vec3&`, or `const Vec3&` for a const path. Editing a mutable reference directly changes that vertex.
- Requires `0 <= index && index < size()`; bounds are not checked, and invalid indices cause undefined behavior.
- See `Path::getVertices` for ownership and reference lifetime.

## Path::quadBezierTo

- Starts at the last stored vertex and takes one control point and an endpoint. If the path has no vertices, inserts `(0, 0, 0)` as the start.
- Accepts `Vec3` points, `Vec2` points, or `(cx, cy, x, y)`; two-dimensional control points and endpoints use `z = 0`.
- Uses `resolution = -1` by default. See `Path::bezierTo` for shared sampling rules, including explicit resolution, zero resolution, tolerance, and generation timing.

## Path::reverseWinding

- With no argument, reverses every subpath independently; with a `size_t` index, reverses only that subpath. Returns `Path&` referring to the same path for chaining, without changing subpath boundaries or closed flags.
- Reversing a simple inner contour changes whether its direction matches its outer contour, allowing it to become a hole. Reversing all contours preserves their relative directions and fill result, which is useful for imported outlines with the opposite winding convention; see `Path::buildFillTriangles` for the full winding rules.
- See `Path::getSubpathRange` for index requirements.

## Path::setClosed

- Sets the current, last subpath's flag to the supplied boolean without changing vertices or earlier subpaths. `true` closes it and `false` opens it; see `Path::close` for how drawing and length calculations use this flag.

## Path::size

- Returns the total vertex count across all subpaths as an `int`, including generated curve samples but excluding pending `Path::curveTo` points.

## Path::toFillMesh

- Returns a new `Mesh` in `PrimitiveMode::Triangles` using `Path::buildFillTriangles`; see that entry for concave contours, holes, winding, and self-intersection handling. If no triangles are produced, returns an empty mesh.
- Each triangle has three separate vertices at `z = 0`, normals `(0, 0, 1)`, UV coordinates `(0, 0)`, and triangle indices. Original Z coordinates are discarded, and no vertex colors are added.
- Triangulates on the CPU during conversion. Retain the returned mesh to avoid repeating `Path::drawFill` triangulation and to use `Mesh` drawing, including lighting; later path edits do not update the mesh.

## PixelFormat

- `PixelFormat::U8` stores each component as an unsigned 8-bit value and is the default for `Pixels::allocate()`; `PixelFormat::F32` stores each component as a float.
- Channel count is specified separately. Use `Pixels::getData()` for U8 data and `Pixels::getDataF32()` for F32 data; these accessors do not convert the buffer.
- See `TextureFormat` for GPU format definitions and `Pixels::getColor` for pixel access and color ranges.

## Pixels

- Owns its pixel buffer and releases it on destruction; a new instance is unallocated.
- Supports moving but prohibits copying; use `clone()` for an independent copy.
- See `Image` for the relationship between CPU pixels, GPU textures, and image updates, `Texture` for GPU resource rules, and `TextureFormat` for formats and channels.

## Pixels::allocate

- Call `allocate(width, height, channels, format)` with dimensions in pixels; `channels` must be 1–4 and defaults to 4, and `format` defaults to `PixelFormat::U8`. See `TextureFormat` for format and channel meanings.
- Releases the previous buffer first and initializes every new channel value to zero, including alpha.
- Negative dimensions, invalid channel counts, or byte counts that exceed `size_t` log an error and leave the buffer cleared; memory allocation exceptions are not caught.
- Zero dimensions are accepted and still set `isAllocated()` to `true`, although `getTotalBytes()` is zero.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(320, 240);
    pixels.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
}
```

## Pixels::clear

- Releases owned memory and resets width, height, and channel count to zero, the format to `PixelFormat::U8`, and `isAllocated()` to `false`.
- Previously obtained data pointers become invalid; calling this on an unallocated buffer is safe.

## Pixels::clone

- Allocates separate memory and copies all pixel data, preserving dimensions, channel count, and format.
- Returns an unallocated `Pixels` if the source is unallocated or has no data pointer; the source is unchanged.

## Pixels::copyTo

- Copies exactly `getTotalBytes()` bytes to `unsigned char* dst`; the destination must have enough space because its capacity is not checked.
- Copies F32 storage as raw bytes without converting it to U8; see `Pixels::getData` for layout.
- Does nothing if the source is unallocated, its data pointer is null, or `dst` is null; returns no value.

## Pixels::crop

- `crop(x, y, w, h)` replaces the buffer with a `w` × `h` region beginning at integer pixel coordinates `(x, y)`, preserving format and channel count.
- Samples outside the source repeat the nearest edge pixel, so the result retains the requested size.
- Does nothing if unallocated or if `w` or `h` is nonpositive; use a source with positive dimensions. Successful cropping replaces the storage and invalidates previous data pointers.

## Pixels::getChannels

- Returns the stored channel count, from 1 to 4, or zero for a new or cleared buffer; see `TextureFormat` for channel meanings.

## Pixels::getColor

- `getColor(x, y)` and `setColor(x, y, color)` use integer pixel coordinates with `(0, 0)` at the top left, x increasing rightward, and y increasing downward; valid coordinates satisfy `0 <= x < getWidth()` and `0 <= y < getHeight()`.
- Outside these bounds, or without allocated data, `getColor` returns `Color(0, 0, 0, 0)` and `setColor` does nothing.
- U8 reads divide channel values by 255 to return 0–1 floats. U8 writes multiply by 255 and convert to `unsigned char` without clamping; supply color components in the 0–1 range. F32 reads and writes preserve float values, including values outside that range, without gamma conversion.
- Three-channel pixels return alpha 1, and four-channel pixels read and write stored alpha. One- and two-channel pixels return the first channel as all three RGB components with alpha 1; writes store `0.299f * color.r + 0.587f * color.g + 0.114f * color.b` in the first channel and leave the second channel unchanged.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(1, 1);
    pixels.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f));
    Color color = pixels.getColor(0, 0);
}
```

## Pixels::getData

- Returns `unsigned char*`, or `const unsigned char*` for a const object, without copying or checking the format. F32 storage is exposed as bytes without conversion; use `getDataF32()` for float elements.
- Pixels are stored left to right in consecutive rows from row 0, with channels interleaved and no row padding. The channel-element offset is `(y * getWidth() + x) * getChannels() + channel`; row stride is `getWidth() * getChannels()` bytes for U8 and that amount times `sizeof(float)` for F32.
- The pointer is null for a new or cleared buffer and remains owned by `Pixels`; do not free it. Reallocation, storage replacement, clearing, or destruction invalidates it. Writes through the mutable pointer change CPU data directly; see `Image` for image update behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(2, 1, 1);
    unsigned char* data = pixels.getData();
    data[0] = 255;
    data[1] = 0;
}
```

## Pixels::getDataF32

- Returns `float*`, or `const float*` for a const object, by casting the stored pointer; it does not check the format or convert U8 values. Access elements through this pointer only when `isFloat()` is `true`.
- F32 rows contain `getWidth() * getChannels()` consecutive floats; see `Pixels::getData` for layout, pointer lifetime, and null behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(1, 1, 4, PixelFormat::F32);
    float* data = pixels.getDataF32();
    data[0] = 2.0f;
    data[3] = 1.0f;
}
```

## Pixels::getDataVoid

- Returns the stored pointer as `void*`, or `const void*` for a const object, without copying or converting either format.
- Use `getFormat()` or `isFloat()` to choose the element type; see `Pixels::getData` for layout, byte stride, pointer lifetime, and null behavior.

## Pixels::getFormat

- Returns the stored `PixelFormat::U8` or `PixelFormat::F32`; new and cleared buffers report U8 even though they are unallocated.
- See `TextureFormat` for CPU and GPU format distinctions.

## Pixels::getHeight

- Returns the stored height in pixels, or zero for a new or cleared buffer.

## Pixels::getTotalBytes

- Returns a `size_t` equal to width × height × channels for U8, or that product × `sizeof(float)` for F32; this excludes object and allocator overhead.
- Returns zero if any dimension or the channel count is zero, including new and cleared buffers.

## Pixels::getWidth

- Returns the stored width in pixels, or zero for a new or cleared buffer.

## Pixels::halve

- Replaces the buffer with dimensions `max(getWidth() / 2, 1)` × `max(getHeight() / 2, 1)`, using integer division and preserving format and channel count.
- Averages each 2 × 2 source block; an odd final row or column is omitted when its dimension exceeds one, and a dimension of one repeats the same sample.
- U8 RGB channels in three- or four-channel buffers are averaged in linear light using a gamma 2.2 conversion, then converted back and rounded. Alpha, one- and two-channel data, and F32 values are averaged directly.
- Does nothing if unallocated; use a source with positive dimensions. The operation allocates replacement storage and invalidates previous data pointers.

## Pixels::isAllocated

- Returns the allocation flag; it is `false` for new and cleared buffers.
- A successful zero-dimension allocation also returns `true`, so this does not guarantee positive dimensions or a nonzero byte count.

## Pixels::isFloat

- Returns whether `getFormat() == PixelFormat::F32`; it checks the format rather than allocation state.
- Returns `false` for new and cleared buffers.

## Pixels::load

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- Clears existing pixels, decodes with stb_image, and tries `loadPlatform()` if decoding fails; successful loading produces four-channel `PixelFormat::U8` data.
- Returns a `LoadResult` that evaluates to `true` on success; an unavailable file reports `LoadError::FileNotFound`, and failed decoding reports `LoadError::DecodeFailed`. The buffer remains cleared on failure.
- Performs no GPU work and can run on a worker thread; upload the result with `Texture::allocate(pixels)` on the main thread. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.
- See `Image::load` for supported file formats and path resolution, including relative paths through `getDataPath()` and unchanged absolute paths.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (!pixels.load("photo.png")) return;
    texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    if (texture.isAllocated()) texture.draw(0, 0);
}
```

## Pixels::loadFromMemory

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- `loadFromMemory(const unsigned char* buffer, int len)` reads encoded image bytes, with `len` in bytes, and produces four-channel `PixelFormat::U8` pixels; this is not an import of raw pixel values.
- Clears existing pixels before decoding and returns `LoadResult`; rejected data reports `LoadError::DecodeFailed`, size limits report `TooLarge`, and allocation failure reports `Unknown`. Failure leaves the buffer cleared. It does not try the platform decoder.
- Performs no GPU work and can run on a worker thread; see `Image::load` for stb_image formats and `Texture` for GPU upload rules.

## Pixels::loadHDR

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- Decodes Radiance HDR data into four-channel `PixelFormat::F32` pixels with linear RGB values and alpha set to 1; the float decoder also accepts supported non-HDR images and converts them to floats.
- Clears existing pixels first and returns `LoadResult`; unavailable files report `LoadError::FileNotFound`, and decoding failures report `LoadError::DecodeFailed`, leaving the buffer cleared. There is no platform decoder fallback.
- Performs no GPU work; see `Image::load` for path resolution, including relative paths through `getDataPath()` and unchanged absolute paths.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (!pixels.loadHDR("environment.hdr")) return;
    Color color = pixels.getColor(0, 0);
}
```

## Pixels::loadPlatform

- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding. Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- On macOS and iOS, uses ImageIO to decode the first image into four-channel U8 pixels and forces every alpha value to 255; see `Image::load` for supported formats and path resolution.
- Returns `true` after replacing the buffer on success; returns `false` without changing existing pixels on failure.
- On non-Apple platforms, checks file availability and always returns `false` without changing the buffer.

## Pixels::mirror

- `mirror(horizontal, vertical)` reverses left and right when `horizontal` is `true` and top and bottom when `vertical` is `true`; both `true` rotate the pixels by half a turn.
- Swaps stored pixels without replacing the buffer, preserving dimensions, format, channel count, and data pointers.
- Does nothing if unallocated or if both arguments are `false`.

## Pixels::mirrorH

- Calls `mirror(true, false)` to reverse left and right; see `Pixels::mirror` for buffer behavior.

## Pixels::mirrorV

- Calls `mirror(false, true)` to reverse top and bottom; see `Pixels::mirror` for buffer behavior.

## Pixels::resize

- `resize(newW, newH)` replaces the buffer at the requested pixel dimensions while preserving format and channel count; each axis independently uses area-weighted box averaging for reduction or Catmull-Rom bicubic interpolation for enlargement.
- U8 RGB channels in three- or four-channel buffers use gamma 2.2 conversion for filtering in linear light, followed by conversion back and rounding. Alpha, one- and two-channel data, and F32 values are filtered directly.
- Does nothing if unallocated, either target dimension is nonpositive, or both target dimensions already match; use a source with positive dimensions.
- Runs two CPU passes with intermediate and replacement buffers; successful resizing invalidates previous data pointers.

## Pixels::save

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Selects JPEG for `.jpg` or `.jpeg`, BMP for `.bmp`, and PNG for every other extension, ignoring extension case and preserving the requested filename. JPEG quality is 90.
- Returns `SaveResult`; unallocated data, a null data pointer, or F32 format returns `SaveError::WriteFailed`.
- Resolves relative paths through `getDataPath()`, leaves absolute paths unchanged, and creates missing parent directories. Paths inside the application bundle return `SaveError::AccessDenied`.
- Encodes in memory before writing to `<file>.tmp`, checks writing, flushing, and closing, and then attempts atomic replacement by renaming the temporary file. On failure, preserves the previous destination and attempts to remove a temporary file that was opened.
- Atomic replacement does not guarantee durability after power loss.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(1, 1);
    pixels.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
    auto result = pixels.save("red.png");
}
```

## Pixels::setColor

- `setColor(int x, int y, const Color& color)` changes one pixel in the existing CPU buffer and returns no value; it does not allocate storage.
- See `Pixels::getColor` for coordinates, bounds, 0–1 color values, format conversion, and channel behavior; see `Image` for image update behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(64, 64);
    pixels.setColor(32, 32, Color(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
}
```

## Pixels::setFromFloats

- `setFromFloats(const float* srcData, int width, int height, int channels)` always reallocates as `PixelFormat::F32` and copies width × height × channels floats without value conversion; dimensions are in pixels.
- The source must contain enough contiguous elements in the layout described by `Pixels::getData`, must remain valid during allocation and copying, and must not point into this buffer. Source capacity and null pointers are not checked.
- Allocation validation follows `Pixels::allocate`; rejected dimensions or channel counts leave the buffer cleared. This copies CPU data rather than uploading it; see `Image` for the CPU/GPU relationship.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    float rgba[] = {2.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f};
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.setFromFloats(rgba, 1, 1, 4);
}
```

## Pixels::setFromPixels

- `setFromPixels(const unsigned char* srcData, int width, int height, int channels)` always reallocates as `PixelFormat::U8` and copies width × height × channels bytes without conversion; dimensions are in pixels.
- The source must contain enough contiguous bytes in the layout described by `Pixels::getData`, must remain valid during allocation and copying, and must not point into this buffer. Source capacity and null pointers are not checked.
- Allocation validation follows `Pixels::allocate`; rejected dimensions or channel counts leave the buffer cleared. The buffer owns the copy, so the source may be released after the call.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    unsigned char rgba[] = {255, 128, 0, 255};
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.setFromPixels(rgba, 1, 1, 4);
}
```

## Font::PlacedGlyph

- `Font::forEachGlyph()` passes a `const Font::PlacedGlyph&` to the visitor for each placed glyph, allowing custom quad rendering, vector paths, or hit testing with the same layout.
- `codepoint` is the final character after any vertical-form substitution. `drawX` and `baselineY` locate the pen before glyph offsets; `scaleX` scales local horizontal offsets and widths, then `rotationCw` rotates the result around `pivotX` and `pivotY`.
- Positions and pivots use logical pixels in the layout's coordinate space, with positive Y downward; rotations use radians. Horizontal layout emits rotation 0 and scale 1; vertical layout may rotate by `TAU / 4` or compress combined runs.
- The callback reference is temporary; copy the value to retain it. It contains placement data only and does not own a glyph, font, or atlas.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::baselineY

- Glyph rendering adds the glyph's own Y offset to this position before rotation. Coordinate units and transformation order are described in `Font::PlacedGlyph`.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::codepoint

- Vertical layout substitutes a mapped vertical-form codepoint when the font supports it; otherwise this remains the original codepoint. See `Font::PlacedGlyph` for the shared layout contract.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::drawX

- Glyph rendering adds the glyph's own X offset multiplied by `scaleX` to this position before rotation. Coordinate units and transformation order are described in `Font::PlacedGlyph`.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::pivotX

- Used with `pivotY` only when `rotationCw` is nonzero. Coordinate units and transformation order are described in `Font::PlacedGlyph`.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::pivotY

- Used with `pivotX` only when `rotationCw` is nonzero. Coordinate units and transformation order are described in `Font::PlacedGlyph`.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::rotationCw

- Font layout emits 0 for upright glyphs or `TAU / 4` radians for glyphs rotated clockwise in vertical text. The rotation center and transformation order are described in `Font::PlacedGlyph`.

## Font::PlacedGlyph::scaleX

- Normally 1; `TcyMode::Combine` reduces it below 1 only when a run is wider than one font-size cell. It scales horizontal glyph offsets and widths without scaling height; see `Font::PlacedGlyph` for transformation order.

## Platform

- All methods are static `constexpr` functions based on target-platform macros and can be used in `if constexpr`.
- Individual checks are `isWeb()`, `isMacOS()`, `isIOS()`, `isWindows()`, `isAndroid()`, and `isLinux()`; the Linux check explicitly excludes Android and Web.
- `isApple()` combines macOS and iOS, `isMobile()` combines iOS and Android, and `isDesktop()` combines macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- `name()` returns `"web"`, `"macos"`, `"ios"`, `"windows"`, `"android"`, `"linux"`, or `"unknown"`.

## Platform::isAndroid

- Returns `true` when `__ANDROID__` is defined; otherwise, returns `false`.

## Platform::isApple

- Returns `Platform::isMacOS() || Platform::isIOS()`; returns `false` when neither condition holds.

## Platform::isDesktop

- Returns `Platform::isMacOS() || Platform::isWindows() || Platform::isLinux()`; returns `false` for iOS, Android, and Web builds.

## Platform::isIOS

- Returns `true` when `__APPLE__` is defined and `TARGET_OS_IOS` is true; otherwise, returns `false`.

## Platform::isLinux

- Returns `true` when `__linux__` is defined and neither `__ANDROID__` nor `__EMSCRIPTEN__` is defined; otherwise, returns `false`.

## Platform::isMacOS

- Returns `true` when `__APPLE__` is defined and `TARGET_OS_OSX || (TARGET_OS_MAC && !TARGET_OS_IPHONE)` is true; otherwise, returns `false`.

## Platform::isMobile

- Returns `Platform::isIOS() || Platform::isAndroid()`; returns `false` when neither condition holds, including Web builds running on mobile devices.

## Platform::isWeb

- Returns `true` when `__EMSCRIPTEN__` is defined; otherwise, returns `false`, regardless of the graphics backend.

## Platform::isWindows

- Returns `true` when `_WIN32` is defined; otherwise, returns `false`.

## Platform::name

- Returns a `const char*` pointing to `"web"`, `"macos"`, `"ios"`, `"windows"`, `"android"`, or `"linux"`, checking the platform predicates in that order; returns `"unknown"` if none matches.
- The result is a string literal and requires no deallocation. For compile-time platform detection, see `Platform`.

## PlayingSound

- `AudioEngine::play()` returns a `shared_ptr<PlayingSound>` on success; `buffer` holds the `SoundSource`, and `stream` holds per-instance streaming state or is null for an eagerly loaded source.
- `volume`, `pan`, `speed`, `loop`, `playing`, `paused`, and `mixMode` are atomic controls that can be set directly from the UI thread while the audio thread reads them.
- A newly started voice has volume `1`, centered pan `0`, normal speed `1`, looping disabled, `playing == true`, `paused == false`, and `MixMode::Auto`; pan uses `-1` for left and `1` for right, and `mixMode` stores the enum as an integer.
- `channelMap` and `channelGains` are atomically published shared snapshots read by the mixer; use `Sound::setChannelMap()` and `Sound::setChannelGains()` to replace routing settings.
- `positionF` is a non-atomic frame position: source frames for eager playback and engine-rate frames for streaming. Access while the device runs requires the engine lock; use the position APIs on `Sound` rather than directly accessing this field.
- `rateRatio` is set by the engine for sample-rate compensation; `level` is an atomic diagnostic peak of this voice's contribution over the latest audio callback, after volume, pan, and channel gains.

## PlayingSound::channelGains

- Each element multiplies the corresponding output channel after routing, independently of `channelMap` and `mixMode`; volume and pan also apply.
- A null pointer, an empty vector, or an output index beyond the vector uses a gain of `1.0`.
- For atomic replacement and thread handling, see `PlayingSound::channelMap`.

## PlayingSound::channelMap

- Each outer element corresponds to an output channel and lists the source-channel indices to sum into it without averaging. Empty inner lists and outputs beyond the outer vector are silent; invalid source indices contribute zero.
- A null pointer or empty outer vector uses `mixMode`; a nonempty map overrides it. Stream indices address the decoder's stereo output, with `0` for left and `1` for right.
- `channelMap` and `channelGains` hold shared pointers to const vectors. The UI thread publishes replacement vectors with `internal::sharedStore`, and the audio thread reads them with `internal::sharedLoad` once per voice per callback; storage uses C++20 atomic shared pointers when available and a spinlock fallback otherwise.

## PlayingSound::level

- Measures the peak absolute contribution to the mix during the most recent callback that mixed this voice, after volume, pan, and channel gains and before final output clipping. It is linear, with `1.0` representing full scale, and can exceed `1.0`.
- The audio thread writes this atomic float for metering; its initial value is `0.0`.
- Pausing or stalled callbacks do not themselves clear this field. Use `PlayingSoundInfo::level` for a snapshot that reports zero in those states.

## PlayingSound::loop

- Defaults to `false`; setting it to `true` repeats playback at the source boundary. For streams, the mixer also passes changes to the decoding worker.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::mixMode

- Stores a `MixMode` value as an atomic int and defaults to `(int)MixMode::Auto`. A nonempty `channelMap` overrides this setting.
- `Auto` sends mono buffers to every output and otherwise matches source and output indices, dropping extra source channels and leaving extra outputs silent. Streams use their decoded stereo channels. `DownmixMono` averages the available source channels and sends the result to every output.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::pan

- Uses `-1.0` for left, `0.0` for center, and `1.0` for right; the default is `0.0`. Positive values attenuate output channel `0`, negative values attenuate channel `1`, and channels `2` and above are unaffected.
- Direct writes are not clamped; `Sound::setPan()` clamps to `[-1.0, 1.0]`.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::paused

- Defaults to `false`. While `true`, the mixer skips this voice, so it produces no output and its playback cursor does not advance; `playing` remains `true` for a paused active voice.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::playing

- Defaults to `false`; `AudioEngine::play()` sets it to `true` for a new voice. The mixer skips voices whose value is `false` and can reuse their slots.
- Pausing leaves this value `true`; reaching the end without looping or calling `Sound::stop()` sets it to `false`.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::positionF

- Defaults to `0.0`. For a decoded `SoundBuffer`, it counts source frames and advances by `speed * rateRatio` per mixed output frame.
- For a stream, it counts frames at the engine rate used by that voice's decoder and advances by whole decoded frames consumed; underruns do not advance it. For known-length streams, rebuilding the decoder at another engine rate re-expresses the cursor at that rate; for unknown-length streams, it resets the cursor to zero.
- This double is not atomic. Use `Sound::getPosition()` and `Sound::setPosition()` for synchronized access in seconds; a stream seek updates this field when the mixer applies it, while `Sound::getPosition()` reports the pending target meanwhile.

## PlayingSound::rateRatio

- For a `SoundBuffer`, the engine sets this to the buffer's sample rate divided by the engine's sample rate when playback starts, or `1.0` if either rate is nonpositive. Multiplying `speed` by this factor preserves natural pitch at `speed = 1.0`.
- Defaults to `1.0`; streams keep `1.0` because their decoders already output at the engine rate. Active buffered voices have this factor recomputed when the engine rate changes.
- This is a non-atomic float managed by the engine.

## PlayingSound::speed

- Defaults to `1.0` for normal speed and natural pitch; `0.5` halves speed and pitch, and `2.0` doubles them. Zero holds the current sample without advancing, and negative values play buffered sources in reverse.
- The buffered mixer uses direct writes without clamping; the stream mixer clamps to `[0, 10]`. `Sound::setSpeed()` clamps buffered playback to `[-10, 10]` and streaming playback to `[0, 10]`.
- For atomic-field thread handling, see `PlayingSound::volume`.

## PlayingSound::volume

- Multiplies this voice's output after routing, channel gains, and pan. Defaults to `1.0`; `0.0` is silent and `1.0` preserves the level. Neither direct writes nor `Sound::setVolume()` clamp the value to `[0, 1]`.
- The `volume`, `pan`, `speed`, `loop`, `playing`, `paused`, and `mixMode` fields are atomic, allowing the UI thread to update them while the audio thread plays. Separate field updates are not one atomic operation.

## PlayingSoundInfo

- `AudioEngine::getPlayingSounds()` copies these values under the engine lock; subsequent playback changes are not reflected in the returned object.
- `slot` identifies the engine's reusable playback slot, `path` is the resolved source path and is empty for generated or memory buffers, and `streaming` distinguishes streaming from eager playback.
- `paused`, `loop`, `volume`, `pan`, and `speed` describe the sampled state; `position` and `duration` are in seconds.
- `level` is the voice's output peak from the latest audio callback on a linear scale where `1` is full scale; the snapshot reports `0` when paused or when the engine is stalled.

## PlayingSoundInfo::duration

- Copies the source's `getDuration()` value without adjusting for playback speed. Buffered duration is the frame count divided by the source sample rate; a stream with unknown length reports `0.0`.

## PlayingSoundInfo::level

- Copies `PlayingSound::level`, the peak absolute contribution during the last audio callback after volume, pan, and channel gains and before final clipping. The value is linear, with `1.0` representing full scale, and can exceed `1.0`.
- Reports `0.0` while paused, while the engine is not running, or when callbacks are detected as stalled.

## PlayingSoundInfo::loop

- Copies `PlayingSound::loop` when the snapshot is taken; `true` means looping is enabled.

## PlayingSoundInfo::pan

- Copies `PlayingSound::pan` when the snapshot is taken: `-1.0` is left, `0.0` is center, and `1.0` is right. For channel behavior, see `PlayingSound::pan`.

## PlayingSoundInfo::path

- An `fs::path` copied from `SoundBuffer::getPath()` or `SoundStream::getPath()`, matching the resolved source file used in logs.
- Empty for generated or memory-loaded buffers. `tc_get_audio_state` reports this path as UTF-8.

## PlayingSoundInfo::paused

- Copies `PlayingSound::paused` when the snapshot is taken; `Sound::pause()` sets that flag and `Sound::resume()` clears it. Paused active voices remain included in `AudioEngine::getPlayingSounds()`.

## PlayingSoundInfo::position

- Converts `PlayingSound::positionF` to seconds using the source sample rate for buffers or the voice's decoder-output rate for streams; reports `0.0` if that rate is nonpositive.
- During a pending stream seek, this reports the cursor already applied by the mixer, whereas `Sound::getPosition()` reports the requested target.

## PlayingSoundInfo::slot

- A zero-based engine slot index in `[0, maxPolyphony - 1]`. Slots can be reused after a voice stops, so this is not a permanent playback identifier.

## PlayingSoundInfo::speed

- Copies `PlayingSound::speed` when the snapshot is taken; `1.0` means normal speed and natural pitch. For zero, reverse playback, and stream limits, see `PlayingSound::speed`.

## PlayingSoundInfo::streaming

- `true` for a `SoundStream` source, as used by `Sound::loadStream()`, and `false` for a decoded `SoundBuffer` source.

## PlayingSoundInfo::volume

- Copies `PlayingSound::volume` when the snapshot is taken; `0.0` is silent and `1.0` preserves the level. The copied value is not clamped to `[0, 1]`.

## PointStyle

- Selects the shape for `PrimitiveMode::Points` meshes through `setPointStyle()`; all three styles use retained GPU point buffers.
- `Square`, the default, draws screen-facing squares and is the least costly splat style; `Round` draws screen-facing discs.
- `Square` and `Round` use `setPointSize()` in logical pixels; FBO rendering and pixel-perfect mode use target pixels.
- `Pixel` draws true one-device-pixel point primitives and ignores `setPointSize()`.
- `Round` smooths disc edges through alpha-to-coverage, which requires a multisampled render target for smooth edges.

## PrimitiveMode

- Set the mode with `Mesh::setMode()`; a new mesh defaults to `Triangles`, and indices determine vertex order when present.
- `Triangles` uses independent groups of three vertices, `TriangleStrip` shares vertices between successive triangles, and `TriangleFan` shares the first vertex among its triangles.
- `Lines` uses independent pairs, `LineStrip` connects consecutive vertices, `LineLoop` also connects the last vertex to the first, and `Points` draws individual points.
- Triangle fans are expanded into triangles, and line loops are closed explicitly when the drawing path lacks direct support.

## PrimitiveType

- The available values are `Points`, `Lines`, `LineStrip`, `Triangles`, `TriangleStrip`, and `Quads`; unlike `PrimitiveMode`, this enum has no triangle fan or line loop.
- The standard drawing writer supports all six values; `Quads` groups each four vertices into a quadrilateral.
- Custom shader drawing currently produces geometry only for `Triangles`, `TriangleStrip`, and `Quads`; strips become indexed triangles, and each complete quad becomes triangles `(0, 1, 2)` and `(0, 2, 3)`.
- In the custom shader path, `Lines` and `LineStrip` submissions are ignored, and `Points` produces no draw.

## QUARTER_TAU

- This `constexpr float` equals `TAU / 4.0f`, or π/2 radians, corresponding to 90 degrees.

## Quaternion

- Defaults to the identity rotation `(w, x, y, z) = (1, 0, 0, 0)`; the four-argument constructor also uses the order `(w, x, y, z)` and does not normalize its arguments.
- Use unit-length quaternions for rotations; `rotate(v)`, `toMatrix()`, and `toEuler()` do not normalize the quaternion automatically.
- `fromAxisAngle(axis, radians)` normalizes the supplied axis; use a nonzero axis. `fromEuler(pitch, yaw, roll)` takes radians about X, Y, and Z and composes `Mat4::rotateY(yaw) * Mat4::rotateX(pitch) * Mat4::rotateZ(roll)`; the `Vec3` overload uses the same component order.
- `a * b` composes rotations with `b` applied first; `conjugate()` negates `x`, `y`, and `z` and is the inverse for a unit quaternion.
- `normalized()` returns a normalized copy and returns the identity for a zero-length quaternion; `normalize()` modifies the quaternion but leaves a zero-length value unchanged.
- `slerp(a, b, t)` interpolates unit rotations along the shorter path, using normalized linear interpolation when their dot product exceeds `0.9995`; `t` is not clamped.
- `toEuler()` returns radians in `(pitch, yaw, roll)` order; when `abs(2 * (w * x - y * z)) >= 0.9999`, it sets pitch to signed `TAU / 4`, calculates yaw with `atan2(2 * (x * y - w * z), 1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z))`, and sets roll to zero.

## Quaternion::conjugate

- Returns `Quaternion(w, -x, -y, -z)` without changing the original.
- The conjugate is the inverse when the quaternion has unit length.

## Quaternion::fromAxisAngle

- Call `Quaternion::fromAxisAngle(axis, radians)` with a `Vec3` axis and an angle in radians; `TAU` represents one full turn.
- The axis is normalized internally, so its length does not affect the rotation when it is nonzero.
- Returns a new quaternion with `w = cos(radians / 2)` and vector components equal to the normalized axis multiplied by `sin(radians / 2)`.
- A zero axis produces zero vector components and `w = cos(radians / 2)`; the result is not necessarily a unit quaternion.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion q = Quaternion::fromAxisAngle(Vec3(0, 1, 0), TAU / 4);
}
```

## Quaternion::fromEuler

- Call `Quaternion::fromEuler(pitch, yaw, roll)` with angles in radians, or pass a `Vec3` whose `x`, `y`, and `z` contain pitch, yaw, and roll respectively.
- Pitch rotates around X, yaw around Y, and roll around Z; the composition is `Ry(yaw) * Rx(pitch) * Rz(roll)`, so a vector is rotated around Z first, then X, then Y.
- Returns a new unit quaternion. See `Quaternion::toEuler` for conversion back to Euler angles and its behavior near gimbal lock.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion q = Quaternion::fromEuler(TAU / 8, TAU / 4, 0.0f);
}
```

## Quaternion::identity

- Returns `Quaternion(1, 0, 0, 0)`, which represents no rotation and is also the default constructor value.

## Quaternion::length

- Returns `sqrt(w*w + x*x + y*y + z*z)` as a `float` without changing the quaternion.

## Quaternion::lengthSquared

- Returns `w*w + x*x + y*y + z*z` as a `float` without changing the quaternion or calculating a square root.

## Quaternion::normalize

- When the length is greater than zero, divides all four components by that length and returns `*this` as a `Quaternion&`, allowing chained calls.
- A zero-length quaternion is left unchanged; `Quaternion::normalized` instead returns the identity quaternion for zero length.
- Use unit quaternions with `Quaternion::rotate`, `Quaternion::toMatrix`, `Quaternion::toEuler`, and `Quaternion::slerp`; these functions do not normalize their input quaternions.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion q(2.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
    q.normalize();
}
```

## Quaternion::normalized

- Returns a new quaternion with all four components divided by the length when the length is greater than zero; the original is unchanged.
- Returns the identity quaternion `Quaternion(1, 0, 0, 0)` when the length is zero.

## Quaternion::operator!=

- Returns the negation of `Quaternion::operator==`; see that entry for the component comparison rules.

## Quaternion::operator*

- `a * b` returns the quaternion product without changing either operand.
- For unit quaternions, the result applies rotation `b` first and then rotation `a`, matching the matrix composition `a.toMatrix() * b.toMatrix()`.
- The product is not normalized automatically; see `Quaternion::normalize` for unit quaternion requirements.

## Quaternion::operator==

- Returns `true` only when all corresponding `w`, `x`, `y`, and `z` components compare equal using exact floating-point equality; no tolerance is applied.
- Compares component values rather than represented rotations, so a unit quaternion and its component-wise negation compare unequal even though they represent the same rotation.

## Quaternion::rotate

- `q.rotate(v)` returns the rotated `Vec3` without changing `q` or `v`.
- See `Quaternion::normalize` for unit quaternion requirements.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion q = Quaternion::fromAxisAngle(Vec3(0, 0, 1), TAU / 4);
    Vec3 direction = q.rotate(Vec3(1, 0, 0));
}
```

## Quaternion::slerp

- `Quaternion::slerp(a, b, t)` returns a new quaternion using spherical linear interpolation; `t = 0` selects the rotation of `a` and `t = 1` selects the rotation of `b`. The value of `t` is not clamped.
- When the component dot product is negative, all components of `b` are negated to take the shorter rotation path; the returned components can therefore differ in sign from `b` at `t = 1`.
- When the dot product after sign adjustment exceeds `0.9995`, uses normalized linear interpolation. Otherwise, uses spherical interpolation without normalizing the result.
- See `Quaternion::normalize` for unit quaternion requirements.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion a = Quaternion::identity();
    Quaternion b = Quaternion::fromAxisAngle(Vec3(0, 1, 0), TAU / 4);
    Quaternion halfway = Quaternion::slerp(a, b, 0.5f);
}
```

## Quaternion::toEuler

- Returns a `Vec3` containing pitch in `x`, yaw in `y`, and roll in `z`, all in radians, using the Y-X-Z convention of `Quaternion::fromEuler`; the original quaternion is unchanged.
- Normally, pitch is calculated with `asin` and yaw and roll with `atan2`, so the returned angles need not match the original input angles.
- When `abs(2 * (w*x - y*z)) >= 0.9999`, sets pitch to the signed value of `TAU / 4`, sets roll to zero, and calculates yaw as `atan2(2 * (x*y - w*z), 1 - 2 * (y*y + z*z))`.
- In that branch, `Quaternion::fromEuler(-TAU / 4, TAU / 8, 0).toEuler()` returns approximately `Vec3(-TAU / 4, -TAU / 8, 0)`.
- See `Quaternion::normalize` for unit quaternion requirements.

## Quaternion::toMatrix

- Returns a new 4×4 `Mat4` with the rotation in its upper-left 3×3 block, zero translation, and bottom row `(0, 0, 0, 1)`; the quaternion is unchanged.
- See `Quaternion::normalize` for unit quaternion requirements.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Quaternion q = Quaternion::fromAxisAngle(Vec3(0, 1, 0), TAU / 4);
    Mat4 rotation = q.toMatrix();
}
```

## Quaternion::w

- This public `float` member is initialized to `1.0f`. The four-component constructor takes arguments in the order `Quaternion(w, x, y, z)`.

## Quaternion::x

- This public `float` member is initialized to `0.0f` and represents the X component of the quaternion's vector part.

## Quaternion::y

- This public `float` member is initialized to `0.0f` and represents the Y component of the quaternion's vector part.

## Quaternion::z

- This public `float` member is initialized to `0.0f` and represents the Z component of the quaternion's vector part.

## Ray

- Stores public `origin` and `direction` vectors. The default ray starts at `(0, 0, 0)` and points along `(0, 0, -1)`; the two-vector constructor normalizes the supplied direction.
- Keep `direction` normalized when editing it directly. `at(t)` returns `origin + direction * t`, so `t` is a distance in the ray's coordinate system when the direction has unit length.
- `transformed(inverseMatrix)` transforms the origin as a point and the direction without translation, then normalizes the direction again. Scaling therefore changes the distance units used by the transformed ray.
- Plane, sphere, and axis-aligned box intersection methods return `Ray::Hit`; test its boolean value before using `t` or `point`.
- `fromScreenPoint2D(x, y, startZ)` creates a ray through `(x, y)` toward negative Z; `startZ` defaults to `1000`.

## Ray::Hit

- Returned by value by the intersection overloads without output arguments; `hit` indicates whether an intersection was found.
- The explicit bool conversion supports conditions such as `if (auto h = ray.intersectSphere(10.0f))`.
- When `hit` is true, `point` equals `origin + direction * t` in the ray's coordinate system; `t` is a distance in those coordinate units when `direction` has unit length.
- A default result has `hit == false`, `t == 0.0f`, and `point == Vec3(0, 0, 0)`; use `t` and `point` only when `hit` is true.

## Ray::Hit::hit

- This bool field defaults to false and is also returned by the explicit bool conversion of `Ray::Hit`.

## Ray::Hit::point

- This Vec3 field stores the intersection position; see `Ray::Hit` for its coordinate system and validity.

## Ray::Hit::t

- This float field gives the parameter used by `Ray::at`; see `Ray::Hit` for its distance units and validity.

## Ray::at

- Returns the Vec3 value `origin + direction * t` without restricting `t`; negative values extend behind the origin.
- See `Ray::Hit` for the relationship between `t` and distance.

## Ray::direction

- This public Vec3 field defaults to `(0, 0, -1)`.
- The constructor taking an origin and direction normalizes a nonzero direction; a zero vector remains zero.
- Direct assignment does not normalize the value; keep it at unit length when interpreting `t` as distance, as described in `Ray::Hit`.

## Ray::fromScreenPoint2D

- Returns a Ray with origin `(screenX, screenY, startZ)` and direction `(0, 0, -1)`; `startZ` defaults to `1000.0f`.
- Copies the supplied coordinates directly without camera projection or viewport conversion, for orthographic 2D use looking toward negative Z.

## Ray::intersectAABB

- `boxMin` and `boxMax` specify the minimum and maximum Vec3 coordinates of the box in the ray's coordinate system.
- Returns a `Ray::Hit` for the first overlap at `t >= 0`, or a default result on a miss; see `Ray::Hit` for result interpretation.
- Starting inside or on the box returns `t == 0` and `point == origin`; a single-point contact also counts as a hit.
- The deprecated overload `intersectAABB(boxMin, boxMax, outT)` returns bool and writes `outT` only on a hit; it is marked for removal in v1.0.0.

## Ray::intersectPlane

- `planeNormal` and `planeD` define the plane by `planeNormal.dot(p) + planeD == 0`; with normal `(0, 0, 1)`, a plane at `z = 5` uses `planeD = -5`.
- The normal is used without normalization; provide a unit normal when expressing `planeD` in distance units.
- Returns a default result when `abs(direction.dot(planeNormal)) < 1e-6f` or the computed `t` is negative; `t == 0` is accepted unless the parallel check rejects the ray.
- Otherwise returns the intersection as a `Ray::Hit`; see `Ray::Hit` for result interpretation.
- The deprecated overload `intersectPlane(planeNormal, planeD, outT, outPoint)` returns bool and writes both outputs only on a hit; it is marked for removal in v1.0.0.

## Ray::intersectSphere

- `radius` specifies the sphere's radius in the ray's coordinate units; its square is used, so negative values behave like their positive counterparts.
- Returns the nearest intersection with `t > 0` as a `Ray::Hit`, or a default result if none exists; see `Ray::Hit` for result interpretation.
- A ray starting inside the sphere returns the forward exit point; an intersection at `t == 0` is skipped, while a tangent at positive `t` counts.
- The deprecated overload `intersectSphere(radius, outT)` returns bool and writes `outT` only on a hit; it is marked for removal in v1.0.0.

## Ray::intersectZPlane

- Returns the intersection at `t = -origin.z / direction.z` as a `Ray::Hit`; see `Ray::Hit` for result interpretation.
- Returns a default result when `abs(direction.z) < 1e-6f` or `t < 0`; a ray starting on the plane is accepted at `t == 0` unless the parallel check rejects it.
- The deprecated overload `intersectZPlane(outT, outPoint)` returns bool and writes both outputs only on a hit; it is marked for removal in v1.0.0.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Ray ray = Ray::fromScreenPoint2D(100.0f, 80.0f);
    if (auto h = ray.intersectZPlane()) {
        Vec3 point = h.point;
    }
}
```

## Ray::origin

- This public Vec3 field defaults to `(0, 0, 0)` and is the position returned by `at(0)`.

## Ray::transformed

- Applies the supplied Mat4 and returns a new Ray without changing the original; pass an inverse transform to map a ray into local coordinates, since this function does not invert the matrix.
- Transforms the origin as a point with translation and homogeneous division; transforms the direction using only the upper-left 3×3 portion, then normalizes it.
- Because the direction is normalized again, scaling can change the meaning of `t`; intersection distances belong to the transformed coordinate system.

## Rect

- Stores public floating-point `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height` values, all initially zero. Constructors accept coordinates or a `Vec2`/`Vec3` position; any supplied Z coordinate is ignored.
- Right and bottom edges are `x + width` and `y + height`; center getters return the halfway point along each dimension.
- `contains(px, py)` includes the left and top edges and excludes the right and bottom edges. `intersects(other)` returns `false` when rectangles only touch at an edge.
- Negative dimensions are stored unchanged; containment and intersection calculations do not normalize them.

## Rect::contains

- Takes separate float coordinates `px` and `py` and returns whether `px >= x && px < x + width && py >= y && py < y + height`.
- Includes the left and top edges and excludes the right and bottom edges; zero or negative width or height cannot contain a point.

## Rect::getBottom

- Returns the float value `y + height` using the stored height without normalizing negative values.

## Rect::getCenter

- Returns `Vec2(x + width / 2, y + height / 2)` without changing the rectangle.

## Rect::getCenterX

- Returns the float value `x + width / 2`.

## Rect::getCenterY

- Returns the float value `y + height / 2`.

## Rect::getRight

- Returns the float value `x + width` using the stored width without normalizing negative values.

## Rect::height

- This public float field defaults to `0` and can be assigned directly.
- `getBottom()` uses `y + height`; negative values are stored without correction.

## Rect::intersects

- Takes `const Rect& other` and returns bool; for positive dimensions, both the horizontal and vertical intervals must overlap with positive length.
- Touching only at an edge or corner returns false.
- Uses stored bounds without normalizing negative dimensions or rejecting zero dimensions; a zero-size rectangle strictly inside another can return true.

## Rect::set

- Accepts either `set(float x, float y, float width, float height)` or `set(const Vec2& pos, float width, float height)`.
- Copies all four values directly without clamping or normalizing the size.
- Returns `Rect&` referring to this rectangle, allowing chained calls.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Rect bounds;
    bounds.set(Vec2(20.0f, 30.0f), 160.0f, 90.0f);
}
```

## Rect::width

- This public float field defaults to `0` and can be assigned directly.
- `getRight()` uses `x + width`; negative values are stored without correction.

## Rect::x

- This public float field defaults to `0` and can be assigned directly.
- It specifies the left edge when width is positive; changing it leaves width unchanged.

## Rect::y

- This public float field defaults to `0` and can be assigned directly.
- It specifies the top edge when height is positive; changing it leaves height unchanged.

## RectNode

- The rectangle occupies local `(0, 0)` to `(width, height)` on the `z = 0` plane and defaults to 100 × 100; position, rotation, and scale do not change the stored dimensions.
- Dimensions use local drawing units: ordinary window drawing uses logical pixels, while Fbo drawing and pixelPerfect mode use framebuffer pixels before Node transforms are applied.
- Hit testing includes the rectangle's edges and requires `enableEvents()`; events are disabled by default. See `Node::hitTest` and `Node::onMousePress` for the shared input rules.
- Clipping is disabled by default. When enabled, a GPU scissor restricts this node's drawing, its Mods, and its descendants on the current drawing target; nested clip regions are intersected and the previous scissor is restored afterward.
- The scissor uses the global positions of only `(0, 0, 0)` and `(width, height, 0)`, multiplied by the target's pixel scale; that scale is 1 for Fbo drawing and pixelPerfect mode, and the window DPI scale otherwise. It remains screen-aligned, does not follow rotated edges, and does not apply camera projection.
- Clipping also rejects the entire subtree during picking when the ray misses this rectangle, even if this node's own events are disabled; this check uses the local rectangle rather than the screen-aligned scissor.
- The default `draw()` draws nothing. See `Node` for creation and ownership, `Node::setup` for setup timing, and `Node::draw` for the drawing lifecycle.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto panel = make_shared<RectNode>();
    panel->setRect(20, 20, 240, 160);
    panel->enableEvents();
    panel->setClipping(true);
    addChild(panel);
}
```

## RectNode::getBottom

- Returns the stored height as a `float`; the node's position and transforms are not included.
- See `RectNode` for rectangle coordinates and units.

## RectNode::getHeight

- Returns the stored height as a `float`, initially `100.0f`, without applying Node transforms.
- See `RectNode` for size units.

## RectNode::getLeft

- Always returns `0.0f`, regardless of the node's position or transforms.
- See `RectNode` for rectangle coordinates and units.

## RectNode::getRight

- Returns the stored width as a `float`; the node's position and transforms are not included.
- See `RectNode` for rectangle coordinates and units.

## RectNode::getSize

- Returns a `Vec2` value with width in `x` and height in `y`, initially `(100, 100)`, without applying Node transforms.
- See `RectNode` for size units.

## RectNode::getTop

- Always returns `0.0f`, regardless of the node's position or transforms.
- See `RectNode` for rectangle coordinates and units.

## RectNode::getWidth

- Returns the stored width as a `float`, initially `100.0f`, without applying Node transforms.
- See `RectNode` for size units.

## RectNode::hitTest

- `hitTest(Vec2 local)` returns whether `0 <= local.x <= width` and `0 <= local.y <= height`; edges are included. Both overloads return `false` when events are disabled.
- `hitTest(const Ray& localRay, float& outDistance)` intersects the local `z = 0` plane and tests the intersection against the same bounds. It rejects rays with `abs(direction.z) < 1e-6f` or an intersection behind the origin.
- On a ray hit, returns `true` and writes the ray parameter `t` to `outDistance`; on failure, returns `false` and leaves `outDistance` unchanged.
- The tree's picking path calls the ray overload; overriding only the `Vec2` overload does not change that path. See `Node::hitTest` for the shared hit-testing rules and `RectNode` for clipping.

```cpp
class Panel : public RectNode {
public:
    bool hitTest(const Ray& localRay, float& outDistance) override {
        return RectNode::hitTest(localRay, outDistance);
    }
};
```

## RectNode::isClipping

- Returns the clipping flag as a `bool`; the default is `false`.
- See `RectNode` for the drawing and hit-testing effects of clipping.

## RectNode::mouseDragged

- This public `Event<MouseDragEventArgs>` is notified by the default `onMouseDrag` before the simple overload; an override must call the RectNode implementation to retain the notification.
- `pos` and `delta` are local to this node; `globalPos` and `globalDelta` remain in screen coordinates. A node that consumed the press receives drags even outside its rectangle.
- Register with `.listen(...)` and retain the returned `EventListener`. See `Node::onMousePress` for input delivery and `RectNode::onMousePress` for the limits of changing the listener's argument copy.

## RectNode::mousePressed

- This public `Event<MouseEventArgs>` is notified by the default `onMousePress` before the simple overload; `pos` is local to this node and `globalPos` remains in screen coordinates.
- Register with `.listen(...)` and retain the returned `EventListener`; destroying it disconnects the listener.
- See `Node::onMousePress` for input delivery and `RectNode::onMousePress` for default consumption and the limits of changing the listener's argument copy.

## RectNode::mouseReleased

- This public `Event<MouseEventArgs>` is notified by the default `onMouseRelease` before the simple overload; `pos` is local to this node and `globalPos` remains in screen coordinates.
- A node that consumed the matching press receives the release even outside its rectangle.
- Register with `.listen(...)` and retain the returned `EventListener`. See `Node::onMousePress` for input delivery and `RectNode::onMousePress` for the limits of changing the listener's argument copy.

## RectNode::mouseScrolled

- This public `Event<ScrollEventArgs>` is notified by the default `onMouseScroll` before the simple overload; `pos` is local to this node, `globalPos` remains in screen coordinates, and `scroll` contains horizontal and vertical scroll amounts.
- Register with `.listen(...)` and retain the returned `EventListener`. Setting the listener's `consumed` flag does not stop scrolling from reaching the parent; control that with the handler's return value.
- See `Node::onMousePress` for the shared input rules and `RectNode::onMouseScroll` for the default handler.

## RectNode::setClipping

- `setClipping(bool enabled)` stores the flag, which defaults to `false`; it does not immediately change the current scissor.
- See `RectNode` for what clipping restricts, coordinate units, nested clipping, picking, and transform limitations.
- Keep the flag unchanged between this node's `beginDraw()` and `endDraw()` so that scissor pushes and pops remain paired.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto panel = make_shared<RectNode>();
    panel->setRect(20, 20, 240, 160);
    panel->setClipping(true);
    addChild(panel);
}
```

## RectNode::setHeight

- `setHeight(float h)` stores the height without clamping and leaves the width unchanged.
- Calls `onSizeChanged()` immediately after storing a different height; an equal value does not trigger the callback.
- See `RectNode` for size units and bounds.

## RectNode::setRect

- `setRect(float x, float y, float w, float h)` calls `setPos(x, y)` first and `setSize(w, h)` second.
- The position is relative to the parent and its `z` component becomes `0`; the size remains local to the rectangle. See `Node::setPos` and `RectNode` for coordinates and units.
- The size call uses the virtual two-argument `setSize` overload, including any derived override.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto panel = make_shared<RectNode>();
    panel->setRect(20, 30, 240, 160);
    addChild(panel);
}
```

## RectNode::setSize

- Accepts `(float w, float h)`, a single `float` for both dimensions, or a `const Vec2&` with width in `x` and height in `y`; values are stored without clamping.
- The base two-argument implementation stores both dimensions before calling `onSizeChanged()` once if either differs; equal dimensions do not trigger the callback.
- The float overloads are virtual, and the single-float and Vec2 implementations forward to the two-argument overload. See `RectNode` for size units and bounds.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto panel = make_shared<RectNode>();
    panel->setSize(240, 160);
    addChild(panel);
}
```

## RectNode::setWidth

- `setWidth(float w)` stores the width without clamping and leaves the height unchanged.
- Calls `onSizeChanged()` immediately after storing a different width; an equal value does not trigger the callback.
- See `RectNode` for size units and bounds.

## RectNodeButton

- This `RectNode` subclass enables events on construction and draws a filled rectangle using `normalColor`, `hoverColor`, or `pressColor`; the pressed state takes precedence over hover.
- Set `label` to draw white bitmap text anchored at the rectangle's center. An empty label draws no text; bitmap text behavior follows `drawBitmapString`.
- Listen to the inherited `mousePressed` and `mouseReleased` events. `isPressed()` is set before the corresponding event is notified, and the button does not restrict presses to the left mouse button.
- See `RectNode` for dimensions and hit testing, `Node` for ownership and event handling, and `EventListener` for subscription lifetime.

## RectNodeButton::draw

- Fills the local rectangle from `(0, 0)` to `(getWidth(), getHeight())`, choosing `pressColor` while pressed, otherwise `hoverColor` when hovered, and otherwise `normalColor`.
- A nonempty `label` is drawn in opaque white with horizontal and vertical center alignment at `(getWidth() / 2, getHeight() / 2)`; an empty label is skipped. Text uses the default screen-fixed bitmap drawing, so glyphs do not rotate or scale with the button; see `drawBitmapString`.
- This public override leaves fill mode enabled and leaves the current color white when a label is drawn, or the selected background color otherwise. See `Node::draw` for shared drawing lifecycle and stack rules.

```cpp
class Ball : public RectNodeButton {
public:
    void draw() override {
        RectNodeButton::draw();
        setColor(1.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f);
        drawCircle(10, 10, 3);
    }
};
```

## RectNodeButton::hoverColor

- This public `Color` field defaults to `Color(0.4f, 0.4f, 0.5f)` with alpha 1. Color components use 0–1 floats.
- It is used when `isMouseOver()` is `true` and the button is not pressed; `pressColor` takes precedence. See `RectNodeButton::draw` for rendering behavior.

## RectNodeButton::isPressed

- Returns the stored `bool` state, initially `false`; it does not query the current physical mouse buttons.
- `RectNodeButton::onMousePress` sets it to `true` and `RectNodeButton::onMouseRelease` clears it, without filtering the button. Leaving the button does not clear it.

## RectNodeButton::label

- This public `string` field is empty by default; assigning text changes the label used on subsequent draws.
- Empty text is not drawn. See `RectNodeButton::draw` for the label's color, alignment, and transform behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto button = make_shared<RectNodeButton>();
    button->setRect(20, 20, 120, 40);
    button->label = "Start";
    addChild(button);
}
```

## RectNodeButton::normalColor

- This public `Color` field defaults to dark gray, `Color(0.3f, 0.3f, 0.3f)`, with alpha 1.
- It is used when the button is neither pressed nor hovered. See `RectNodeButton::hoverColor` for color units and `RectNodeButton::draw` for rendering behavior.

## RectNodeButton::pressColor

- This public `Color` field defaults to `Color(0.2f, 0.2f, 0.3f)` with alpha 1.
- It takes precedence over both other background colors whenever `isPressed()` returns `true`, including outside the button. See `RectNodeButton::hoverColor` for color units and `RectNodeButton::draw` for rendering behavior.

## ResizeEventArgs

- Passed to `events().windowResized` with integer `width` and `height`, both defaulting to `0`.
- Dimensions use logical pixels by default. The main window uses framebuffer pixels when `WindowSettings::pixelPerfect` is enabled; secondary-window resize events use logical pixels.
- For listener registration, lifetime, and delivery threads, see `Event<T>`.

## ResizeEventArgs::height

- An `int` defaulting to `0`; see `ResizeEventArgs` for logical-pixel and framebuffer-pixel units.

## ResizeEventArgs::width

- An `int` defaulting to `0`; see `ResizeEventArgs` for logical-pixel and framebuffer-pixel units.

## Right

- This `inline constexpr Direction` equals `Direction::Right` and can be passed wherever a `Direction` value is accepted.

## ScreenRecorder

- Captures automatically after each frame of the window that was current when recording began, using an underlying `VideoWriter`.
- The recording size is fixed in framebuffer pixels. Frames whose dimensions no longer match are skipped; a change in the source format, GPU device, or window owner stops the take with a failure.
- `VideoRecordSettings::fps` controls capture pacing and defaults to 60. Slower rendering produces fewer frames while preserving real-time playback; timestamps normally use a clock unaffected by `resetElapsedTimeCounter()`.
- A positive `duration` sets a cutoff in seconds, checked after each frame; its default of 0 records until stopped. Recording also stops on the owning window's exit, recorder destruction, or destruction of the recorded Fbo.
- With `audio = true`, the recorder taps the audio engine's master mix and uses the audio device clock for video timestamps. An uninitialized audio engine causes a Warning and video-only recording; missing sample rate and channel settings are filled from the engine.
- Capture runs in the owning window's frame callback; macOS window readback completes on a background thread. See `ScreenRecorder::stop` for completion waits and `VideoWriter` for submission failures.
- The recorder cannot be copied. Each take owns its recording state, and pending callbacks retain that state and its writer until completion.

## ScreenRecorder::getFrameCount

- Returns `int` from the underlying writer. Failed submissions and pending asynchronous captures are excluded; accepted frames do not guarantee successful finalization.
- The count remains available after stopping. A new take starts with a fresh writer and a count of 0.

## ScreenRecorder::getRejectedFrameCount

- Returns `uint64_t` counting capture/readback failures and mismatches in dimensions, pixel format, row layout, or byte capacity against the take or native buffer. Rejected frames are skipped whole; ordinary frame rejection does not fail the take.
- The writer resets this count in `open()`, and a new recording uses a fresh writer. Capture pacing and busy capture opportunities are not counted as rejected frames.
- See `ScreenRecorder` for source changes that stop the take with a failure.

## ScreenRecorder::getPath

- Returns the underlying writer's `fs::path` by value. Relative output paths are resolved through `getDataPath()` when the writer opens.
- The path is initially empty and remains available after stopping; the next recording replaces it.

## ScreenRecorder::isRecording

- Returns `true` when a capture source is selected and the underlying writer is open. This does not indicate that every submission or finalization will succeed.
- Becomes `false` as soon as stopping disconnects capture, even if pending work still keeps the writer open.

## ScreenRecorder::start

- `start(path)` records the window, and `start(fbo, path)` records the contents of an Fbo (without the on-screen UI). After that, a frame is captured automatically at the end of every frame until you call `stop()`. Keep the `ScreenRecorder` as a member of your tcApp. When you need only one recording at a time, `startRecording()` does the same with a shared recorder.
- A relative `path` is resolved with `getDataPath()`, and missing folders are created. Pass `VideoRecordSettings` to choose the codec, the frame rate or audio. To record for a fixed time, pass the length in seconds, as in `start("clip.mp4", 5.0f)`; the recording then stops and the file is finalized automatically.
- The video size is fixed at the actual pixel size of the source when recording starts. For the window this is the framebuffer size, which is twice the logical size on a Retina display. If the source changes size during recording, frames of the wrong size are skipped and counted by `getRejectedFrameCount()`, and recording continues once the original size returns.
- The returned `SaveResult` only tells you whether the file could be prepared and the encoder opened. Whether the file was written correctly is reported by the result of `stop()`.
- Calling `start()` while a recording is running first stops and finalizes the previous one. If frames of the previous recording are still being processed after that wait, `start()` returns that failure and does not begin a new recording.
- The recorder belongs to the window that is current when `start()` is called, and it stops automatically when that window closes. When you record an Fbo, keep the Fbo alive; if it is destroyed, the recording stops and the file is finalized.
- On macOS the window is read back in the background, one frame at a time. If the previous frame is still being processed, that frame is skipped, and the video keeps real-time timing.

```cpp
// tcApp.h (inside class tcApp : public App)
ScreenRecorder recorder;

// tcApp.cpp
void tcApp::keyPressed(int key) {
    if (key != 'R') return;   // letters arrive uppercase
    if (!recorder.isRecording()) {
        if (!recorder.start("capture.mp4")) logError() << "Could not start recording";
    } else if (auto result = recorder.stop(); !result) {
        logError() << "Recording failed: " << result.message;
    }
}
```

## ScreenRecorder::stop

- Disconnects capture and the audio listener, then returns a `SaveResult` for finalization or a retained failure. The destination is finalized directly without a temporary file or rename.
- Waits up to one second for audio callbacks; a callback still running at the limit produces a Warning. It then waits up to two seconds for pending captures and their diagnostic callbacks before finalizing; encoder finalization itself can take additional time.
- If work remains after the capture wait, logs one Error and returns `SaveError::WriteFailed` with the message `"recording still has frames in flight"`. Pending callbacks retain the recording state and writer; the last completion drains buffered audio and closes the file.
- Repeated calls retain the take's result, including a capture-wait timeout, without repeating its Error. Before any recording has begun, stopping returns success.
- Caller mistakes and transient readback failures do not fail the take. See `VideoWriter` for retained backend failures and `ScreenRecorder` for source-change failures.

## ScreenRecorder::writer

- Returns a mutable `VideoWriter&` for advanced inspection or control, without copying the writer.
- The reference belongs to the current take; do not retain it across a new recording or recorder destruction. Access does not acquire the recorder's writer lock, so avoid concurrent use with capture callbacks.

## ScrollBar

- This is a `RectNode` subclass. Construct with a `ScrollContainer*` and `ScrollBar::Vertical` or `ScrollBar::Horizontal`; vertical is the default. The pointer does not own the container, which must remain alive while the bar uses it.
- Call `updateFromContainer()` each frame or after scroll or size changes; synchronization is not automatic. Position is calculated in container-local coordinates, so adding the bar as a child of the container places it correctly.
- The thumb reflects the visible proportion of the content and has a minimum length of twice the bar width. It becomes inactive when there is no scroll range, no rectangular content, or no container.
- Defaults are width `5`, margin `2`, and white with alpha `0.5`. The vertical bar sits at the right edge, and the horizontal bar at the bottom edge.
- Left-button dragging changes the corresponding container scroll position. See `Node` for threading and ownership rules and `RectNode` for coordinate units.

## ScrollBar::getBarColor

- Returns a copy of the stored `Color`; the default is white with 50% opacity, `Color(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 0.5f)`.

## ScrollBar::getBarWidth

- Returns the stored thickness as a `float` in local coordinate units; the default is `5.0f`.
- For a horizontal bar, this is its height, rather than the length returned by `getWidth()`.

## ScrollBar::getMargin

- Returns the stored margin as a `float` in local coordinate units; the default is `2.0f`.
- This value sets both the inset from the right or bottom edge and the spacing at the ends of the bar's travel.

## ScrollBar::getOffset

- Returns `round(getBarWidth() / 2)` as a `float`; the default thickness of `5.0f` produces `3.0f`.
- The built-in drawing uses the unrounded half-thickness for its cap offset, rather than this return value.

## ScrollBar::setBarColor

- Copies `const Color& color` into the bar's drawing color, including alpha; color components use the 0–1 scale.
- The value is stored without clamping and is used the next time the bar is drawn.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    ScrollBar bar(nullptr);
    bar.setBarColor(Color(0.2f, 0.6f, 1.0f, 0.8f));
}
```

## ScrollBar::setBarWidth

- Stores `float width` in local coordinate units and immediately updates the node's width for a vertical bar or height for a horizontal bar.
- Recalculates the bar geometry and active state through `updateFromContainer()`; the minimum bar length is twice this thickness.
- The value is stored without validation or clamping.

## ScrollBar::setMargin

- Stores `float margin` in local coordinate units and immediately recalculates the bar geometry and active state through `updateFromContainer()`.
- The value is stored without validation or clamping; see `ScrollBar::getMargin` for where the margin is applied.

## ScrollBar::updateFromContainer

- Call this after the container's scroll position or dimensions change; synchronization is not automatic each frame. After changing the content size, call `ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds()` first because this method reads the existing scroll bounds.
- Uses the direction selected at construction to size and position the bar. Coordinates assume the bar is a direct child of the container; add it as an overlay child, rather than as scrollable content.
- Sets the bar inactive when the container pointer is null, the selected axis has no positive scroll range, or the content is not a `RectNode`; otherwise, it sets the bar active. Inactivity skips normal subtree updates, drawing, and hit testing, but this method can still be called directly to reactivate it.
- The constructor stores a non-owning `ScrollContainer*`; keep that container alive while using the bar. Only a null pointer is detected.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto scroll = make_shared<ScrollContainer>();
    scroll->setSize(240, 160);
    auto content = make_shared<RectNode>(); content->setSize(240, 480);
    scroll->setContent(content);
    auto bar = make_shared<ScrollBar>(scroll.get()); scroll->addChild(bar);
    bar->updateFromContainer(); addChild(scroll);
}
```

## ScrollContainer

- This `RectNode` subclass enables events and clipping on construction. `setContent()` retains one content node as the first child and removes the previous content; additional children remain fixed overlays, but are also clipped.
- Scroll bounds and movement require the content to be a `RectNode`. Other `Node` types can be attached, but produce zero scroll ranges and are not repositioned.
- Scroll positions are clamped from zero to the content size minus the container size, with a minimum range of zero. Applying scroll replaces the content position with `(-scrollX, -scrollY)`.
- Bounds are recalculated when content is assigned or the container size changes. Call `updateScrollBounds()` after changing the content size.
- Vertical wheel scrolling is enabled by default, horizontal wheel scrolling is disabled, and scroll speed defaults to `20`. Wheel deltas accumulate until `update()`, which subtracts each delta multiplied by the speed; explicit scroll setters work regardless of the wheel enable flags.
- A wheel event is consumed when an enabled axis has a positive scroll range, even at an endpoint; otherwise it can pass to the parent.
