- See `RectNode` for clipping behavior and coordinate units, and `Node` for ownership, threading, and update timing.

## ScrollContainer::getContent

- Returns a `Node::Ptr`, or an empty shared pointer when no content is set.
- See `ScrollContainer::setContent` for ownership and lifetime.

## ScrollContainer::getContentRect

- Returns a non-owning `RectNode*`, or `nullptr` when content is absent or is not a `RectNode` or its subclass.
- See `ScrollContainer::setContent` for ownership and lifetime.

## ScrollContainer::getMaxScrollX

- Returns the stored nonnegative horizontal limit as a `float`; the initial value is `0`.
- This getter does not recalculate the limit. See `ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds` for calculation and refresh timing, and `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units.

## ScrollContainer::getMaxScrollY

- Returns the stored nonnegative vertical limit as a `float`; the initial value is `0`.
- This getter does not recalculate the limit. See `ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds` for calculation and refresh timing, and `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units.

## ScrollContainer::getScroll

- Returns a `Vec2` containing the stored horizontal and vertical offsets; both initially equal `0`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units and content positioning.

## ScrollContainer::getScrollSpeed

- Returns the stored sensitivity as a `float`; the default is `20.0f`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScrollSpeed` for how this multiplier affects scrolling.

## ScrollContainer::getScrollX

- Returns the stored horizontal offset as a `float`; the initial value is `0`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units and content positioning.

## ScrollContainer::getScrollY

- Returns the stored vertical offset as a `float`; the initial value is `0`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units and content positioning.

## ScrollContainer::isHorizontalScrollEnabled

- Returns the horizontal input flag as a `bool`; the default is `false`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setHorizontalScrollEnabled` for which operations this flag affects.

## ScrollContainer::isVerticalScrollEnabled

- Returns the vertical input flag as a `bool`; the default is `true`.
- See `ScrollContainer::setVerticalScrollEnabled` for which operations this flag affects.

## ScrollContainer::setContent

- Accepts a `Node::Ptr`, removes the previous content from the container, and inserts the new content as the first child, removing it from any previous parent. Passing `nullptr` clears the content; other children remain in place and are not scrolled.
- Use a `RectNode` or its subclass for scrolling. Other node types are accepted, but their size is not used for scroll bounds and their position is not changed by scrolling.
- Recalculates the bounds immediately through `ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds`; replacing content does not unconditionally reset the scroll position to zero.
- The container retains shared ownership of the content, and `getContent()` returns an additional shared owner. The pointer from `getContentRect()` does not extend the content's lifetime; keep a shared pointer if it must remain valid after replacement or container destruction.
- These ScrollContainer methods are C++ only. Call `setContent` on the main thread after the container is owned by a shared pointer; see `Node` for shared ownership and child-creation rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto scroll = make_shared<ScrollContainer>();
    scroll->setSize(300, 200);
    auto content = make_shared<RectNode>();
    content->setSize(300, 800);
    scroll->setContent(content);
    addChild(scroll);
}
```

## ScrollContainer::setHorizontalScrollEnabled

- Sets whether horizontal wheel and trackpad deltas are accumulated and applied; horizontal scrolling is disabled by default.
- This only changes the input flag. It does not reset the current offset or recalculate bounds, and direct calls to `setScrollX` or `setScroll` still work when disabled.

## ScrollContainer::setScroll

- Accepts `setScroll(float x, float y)` or `setScroll(Vec2 pos)` and clamps each offset to the stored range from zero to its maximum.
- Offsets use the same local coordinate units as the container and content dimensions. Positive offsets reveal content farther right or down by moving the content left or up.
- Immediately sets RectNode content to `(-x, -y, 0)` using the clamped offsets, replacing its previous local position, including its Z coordinate. See `ScrollContainer::setContent` for supported content types.
- Horizontal and vertical input flags do not restrict this setter. It does not recalculate bounds; see `ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds` for when to refresh them.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto scroll = make_shared<ScrollContainer>();
    auto content = make_shared<RectNode>();
    content->setSize(400, 600);
    scroll->setContent(content);
    scroll->setScroll(Vec2(20, 100));
    addChild(scroll);
}
```

## ScrollContainer::setScrollSpeed

- Stores a `float` multiplier for wheel and trackpad deltas; the default is `20.0f`. Each input unit changes the corresponding offset by this many local coordinate units in the opposite direction.
- The value is stored without validation or clamping. Zero prevents input-driven movement, and a negative value reverses its direction.
- This does not move content immediately or affect direct scroll setters; the multiplier is used when `ScrollContainer::update` processes accumulated input.

## ScrollContainer::setScrollX

- Clamps `float x` between zero and the stored horizontal maximum, preserves the vertical offset, and immediately applies the current scroll position.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units, content positioning, and behavior when horizontal input is disabled.

## ScrollContainer::setScrollY

- Clamps `float y` between zero and the stored vertical maximum, preserves the horizontal offset, and immediately applies the current scroll position.
- See `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units, content positioning, and behavior when vertical input is disabled.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto scroll = make_shared<ScrollContainer>();
    auto content = make_shared<RectNode>();
    content->setSize(100, 600);
    scroll->setContent(content);
    scroll->setScrollY(scroll->getMaxScrollY());
    addChild(scroll);
}
```

## ScrollContainer::setVerticalScrollEnabled

- Sets whether vertical wheel and trackpad deltas are accumulated and applied; vertical scrolling is enabled by default.
- This only changes the input flag. It does not reset the current offset or recalculate bounds, and direct calls to `setScrollY` or `setScroll` still work when disabled.

## ScrollContainer::updateScrollBounds

- For RectNode content, sets each maximum to `max(0.0f, contentSize - containerSize)` using the corresponding width or height. It uses those dimensions directly, without accounting for transforms or descendant bounds.
- Clamps both current offsets to the new limits and immediately applies the resulting content position. Horizontal and vertical input flags do not affect this calculation; see `ScrollContainer::setScroll` for coordinate units and positioning.
- If content is absent or is not a RectNode, sets both maxima to zero and returns without changing the stored offsets or content position.
- Runs automatically when content is set or the container size changes. Content size changes alone, including changes made by layout, do not trigger it; call it after such changes. `ScrollContainer::update` does not recalculate bounds.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto scroll = make_shared<ScrollContainer>();
    auto content = make_shared<RectNode>();
    scroll->setContent(content);
    content->setSize(100, 600);
    scroll->updateScrollBounds();
    addChild(scroll);
}
```

## ScrollEventArgs

- Carries the cursor position, horizontal and vertical scroll amounts, modifier keys, and handled state for `mouseScrolled` events.
- See `MouseEventArgs::pos` for coordinates and units, and `ScrollEventArgs::scroll` for scroll units.
- See `App::mousePressed` for the order of listeners, App callbacks, and node callbacks.
- See `Event<T>` for listener registration, listener lifetime, priority arguments, delivery options, and threading.

## ScrollEventArgs::alt

- This bool field is `true` when the event reports Alt as held; it defaults to `false`.

## ScrollEventArgs::consumed

- Defaults to `false`; a listener can mark the event handled with `e.consumed = true`. See `EventPriority::BeforeApp` for how this stops later listeners.
- See `App::mousePressed` for how this flag affects App callbacks and delivery to the node tree.

## ScrollEventArgs::ctrl

- This bool field is `true` when the event reports Ctrl as held; it defaults to `false`.

## ScrollEventArgs::globalPos

- This `Vec2` position is preserved when the event is converted to a node's local coordinates; see `MouseEventArgs::pos` for the coordinate origin, units, and local versus screen coordinates.
- For main-window scroll events, the position comes from the stored mouse position rather than the scroll event's own cursor coordinates.

## ScrollEventArgs::pos

- This `Vec2` equals `globalPos` at App level and is converted to the receiving node's local coordinates in node callbacks; see `MouseEventArgs::pos` for the coordinate rules and units.
- For main-window scroll events, the position comes from the stored mouse position.

## ScrollEventArgs::scroll

- This `Vec2` contains horizontal scrolling in `scroll.x` and vertical scrolling in `scroll.y`; it defaults to (0, 0).
- Values use the platform backend's scroll units, which can include fractional amounts, rather than cursor-coordinate pixels. TrussC does not apply DPI scaling to them.
- Node coordinate conversion leaves `scroll` unchanged; a node's rotation or scale does not transform the scroll amounts.

## ScrollEventArgs::scrollX

- This float field mirrors `scroll.x` and defaults to 0. It is kept for compatibility and will be removed at v1.0; use `scroll.x` instead.
- It is copied from `scroll.x` by `syncLegacy()`, rather than being updated automatically when you assign to `scroll`.

## ScrollEventArgs::scrollY

- This float field mirrors `scroll.y` and defaults to 0. It is kept for compatibility and will be removed at v1.0; use `scroll.y` instead.
- It is copied from `scroll.y` by `syncLegacy()`, rather than being updated automatically when you assign to `scroll`.

## ScrollEventArgs::shift

- This bool field is `true` when the event reports Shift as held; it defaults to `false`.

## ScrollEventArgs::super

- This bool field is `true` when the event reports Super as held, corresponding to Command on macOS; it defaults to `false`.

## Serial

- Use `Serial::listDevices()` to enumerate devices, then `setup(devicePath, baudRate)` or `setup(deviceIndex, baudRate)` to connect. Both arguments are required; the rate is in baud. Desktop ports use 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit, and no hardware or software flow control.
- `available()` reports buffered bytes, and reads consume bytes already received without waiting for new input. Writes can return a partial count or an error and can wait on Windows and Android; see `Serial::readBytes` and `Serial::writeBytes` for return values and timeouts.
- Each open port has a receive worker and storage allocated on demand up to 64 MiB on desktop and Android. Overflow discards the oldest bytes; allocation failure discards unadmitted bytes. `getDroppedByteCount()` reports the exact discarded total. One Warning when buffering first exceeds 1 MiB and one on first loss are delivered automatically on the main thread by the frame or headless run loop, without another Serial call. Both OnceGates reset on a new connection and do not repeat per burst. Delivery runs from the main-thread queue, which the frame loop drains every frame (also EVENT_DRIVEN frames that skip update) and the headless loop drains between passes. A Warning captured before closing is still delivered, and receive workers never allocate or log for it.
- Desktop receive workers record device loss and driver warnings for delivery by the next `available()`, `readBytes()`, `readByte()`, or `writeBytes()` call. Windows uses overlapped reads and writes.
- `isConnected()` and `isInitialized()` report stored connection state without probing the device. On desktop, an I/O call that finds device loss closes the port and fires `onDisconnect` after releasing the lock. On Android, this happens when I/O observes loss recorded by the receive worker; a write error alone does not trigger immediate disconnection. By default, listeners run on the calling thread; retain the listener returned by `listen(callback, Deliver::Main)` when main-thread delivery is needed.
- I/O calls share a per-object lock, while setup, close, destruction, and moves require exclusive access and wait for active I/O. I/O calls can run concurrently, but new I/O waits once setup, close, destruction, or a move requests exclusive access. The application must coordinate which thread reads or writes which data. `isConnected()` and `getDevicePath()` do not wait for port I/O.
- The object owns its connection, cannot be copied, and can be moved. Destruction closes the port without firing `onDisconnect`; move assignment also closes the destination's previous port without that event. Event listeners stay with their original object.
- On Android, USB workers also emit logs. A logger listener running there must not perform serial I/O, setup, close, destruction, or moves; use `Deliver::Main` for such work. Setup and close are refused on USB worker threads, and device loss found by I/O there remains pending until another thread reports it. `isConnected()` and `getDevicePath()` are safe there.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    Serial serial;
    void setup() override {
        auto devices = Serial::listDevices();
        if (!devices.empty()) serial.setup(devices.front().devicePath, 115200);
    }
};
```

## Serial::available

- Returns the number of bytes currently held in the TrussC receive buffer without consuming them; returns 0 when disconnected.
- If this call detects device loss, it closes the connection, fires `onDisconnect`, and returns 0.
- See `Serial::setup` for threading rules and `Serial::getDroppedByteCount` for receive-buffer overflow.

## Serial::close

- Stops the receive worker, closes the port, and clears buffered input; on Android it also cancels a pending USB permission connection.
- Closing an open connection fires `onDisconnect` with `wasClean = true`; closing an already closed port does not fire it. See `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification details.
- Preserves the device path and dropped-byte count. Closing can wait for active I/O and the receive worker; see `Serial::setup` for threading rules and Android worker restrictions.

## Serial::drain

- On macOS and Linux, waits with `tcdrain`; on Windows, waits with `FlushFileBuffers`. This function sets no timeout and returns no success or error status.
- Does nothing when disconnected or on Android, where writes use synchronous USB transfers.
- A waiting `drain()` delays `setup()` or `close()` on another thread. See `Serial::setup` for shared threading rules.

## Serial::flush

- Clears the TrussC receive buffer and discards the operating system's pending input and output on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- On Android, clears only the TrussC receive buffer; output flushing does nothing. When disconnected, this function does nothing.
- Does not wait for transmission to finish or increase the dropped-byte count. Use `drain()` to wait for output; see `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::flushInput

- Clears the TrussC receive buffer and, on Windows, macOS, and Linux, the operating system's pending input.
- On Android, clears only the TrussC receive buffer. Does nothing when disconnected and does not increase the dropped-byte count.
- See `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::flushOutput

- Discards output queued in the operating system on Windows, macOS, and Linux; it does not wait for transmission to finish.
- Does nothing when disconnected or on Android, where writes use synchronous USB transfers.
- Use `drain()` to wait for output instead of discarding it. See `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::getDeviceList

- Returns the same device list as `Serial::listDevices()` and is retained for backward compatibility.
- Use `Serial::listDevices()` in new code; this alias is marked for removal in v1.0.0.

## Serial::getDroppedByteCount

- On desktop and Android, the receive buffer is limited to 64 MiB to bound memory use when input outpaces reading. Overflow discards the oldest bytes, and this `size_t` count includes those discards and unadmitted bytes on allocation failure; reading and intentional flushing do not increase it.
- Closing and flushing preserve the count, and moving a `Serial` transfers it. A successful desktop connection starts a new count; Android resets it when starting a new setup attempt, including one that fails, but preserves it when keeping the same USB permission request pending.
- Windows driver overrun and RX overflow flags are logged separately because they provide no exact lost-byte count; framing and parity errors are also log-only. See `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::getDevicePath

- Returns a string copy, so another thread changing the path cannot invalidate the returned value. The path is initially empty, remains after `close()` or a failed connection attempt, and also identifies an Android connection awaiting USB permission.
- Does not wait for `setup()`, `close()`, or I/O to finish; the path alone does not indicate a live connection. See `Serial::isConnected` for connection status and `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::isConnected

- Returns the recorded connection state without probing the device or waiting for `setup()`, `close()`, or I/O. Device loss is reported by `available()`, `readBytes()`, `readByte()`, or `writeBytes()`, which then closes the connection and fires `onDisconnect`; an idle device sending no data is not treated as lost. On desktop, device-loss cleanup logs one warning per ended connection; on Android, the USB worker logs the loss.
- On Android, this can become true after `setup()` returned false when USB permission is granted and opening succeeds. A worker-recorded loss leaves it true until a subsequent reporting call handles the loss; `close()` and `setup()` can also collect that Android state.
- To reconnect, retry `setup()` after this returns false; see `Serial::setup` for DTR behavior and shared threading rules, and `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification and reconnection details.

## Serial::isInitialized

- This older name is retained for existing code and directly returns `isConnected()`. See `Serial::isConnected` for device-loss detection and Android behavior.

## Serial::listDevices

- This static function returns a `vector<SerialDeviceInfo>` with consecutive zero-based `deviceId` values. Returns an empty vector when no matching devices are found or enumeration cannot proceed; use `printDevices()` to log the list.
- Windows tries to open COM1 through COM256 with exclusive read/write access and immediately closes each successful probe, so ports that cannot be opened, including busy ports, are omitted.
- macOS scans `/dev` for names beginning with `tty.usb`, `cu.usb`, `tty.serial`, `cu.serial`, `tty.SLAB`, `cu.SLAB`, `tty.wch`, or `cu.wch`; Linux scans for `ttyUSB`, `ttyACM`, or `ttyS`.
- Android enumerates USB Host devices exposing a CDC data interface, with paths such as `/dev/bus/usb/001/002`; its serial backend supports CDC-ACM devices.
- The list is rebuilt on each call. macOS, Linux, and Android results are not sorted here, and indices are not persistent device identifiers; `setup(index, baudRate)` enumerates again before selecting a path.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    for (const auto& device : Serial::listDevices()) {
        logNotice() << device.deviceId << ": " << device.devicePath;
    }
}
```

## Serial::onDisconnect

- This `Event<SerialDisconnectEventArgs>` fires once per open connection when device loss is reported or the app closes it. The arguments contain `portName`, `baudRate`, `reason`, and `wasClean`.
- Loss reported by `available()`, `readBytes()`, `readByte()`, or `writeBytes()` sets `wasClean = false`; `reason` describes the loss, such as `"read: Input/output error"` or `"hangup"`. Closing an open port with `close()`, including through `setup()`, sets `wasClean = true` and `reason = "closed by close()"`.
- Closing an already closed port, destroying a `Serial`, or moving another `Serial` over it does not fire this event. If `setup()` closes a replacement connection opened by a listener or another thread while the previous connection was being closed, it logs a warning without another event.
- Closing an unplugged device before an I/O call reports the loss still counts as an app close. On Android, if the USB worker already recorded the loss, `reason` adds `(the device had already been lost: <reason>)`, while `wasClean` remains true.
- Delivery is inline on the calling thread after the ended connection has been closed and the port lock released. Receive workers record loss for a subsequent reporting I/O call; Android also collects it through `close()` or `setup()`. Use `Deliver::Main` for a listener that must run on the main thread, and see `Serial::setup` for Android worker restrictions.
- A listener may reconnect with `setup(e.portName, e.baudRate)`; first check `!e.wasClean` so an intentional close does not reopen the port. The I/O call that reported the loss still returns its error value, or 0 for `available()`, and leaves a replacement connection alone.
- If other threads also open connections, check `isConnected()` and `getDevicePath()` in the listener before reconnecting, because another thread may already have opened a connection.
- Retain the returned `EventListener` for as long as the subscription is needed. Listeners remain attached to the original `Serial` object and are not transferred by a move.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    static Serial serial;
    static EventListener listener = serial.onDisconnect.listen([](SerialDisconnectEventArgs& e) {
        if (!e.wasClean) serial.setup(e.portName, e.baudRate);
    }, Deliver::Main);
    serial.setup(0, 115200);
}
```

## Serial::printDevices

- This static function calls `listDevices()` and logs `"Serial devices:"` followed by each device's index and path at Notice level.
- Does not return the list; use `Serial::listDevices()` to inspect it in code. The same enumeration behavior applies.

## Serial::readByte

- Consumes one byte from the receive buffer and returns its value from 0 to 255; returns -1 when no data is available, without waiting for new data.
- Returns -2 when disconnected or an error occurs. If it detects device loss, it closes the connection and fires `onDisconnect`.
- Uses `readBytes()` internally. See `Serial::setup` for threading rules and `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification behavior.

## Serial::readBytes

- `readBytes(void* buffer, int length)` consumes up to `length` bytes from the receive buffer and returns the actual count, including 0 when empty. It does not wait for new data; provide writable storage for at least `length` bytes when the length is positive.
- Returns -1 when disconnected or when device loss is detected. A detected loss closes the connection and fires `onDisconnect`; see `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification details.
- For the pointer overload, a connected port with `length <= 0` returns 0 after the loss check.
- `readBytes(string& buffer, int length)` first resizes the string to `length`, then reads into it and resizes it to the actual count on success. On a -1 result, the string remains resized to the requested length; a negative length reaches string resizing before the pointer overload checks it.
- See `Serial::setup` for threading rules and `Serial::getDroppedByteCount` for receive-buffer overflow.

```cpp
void tcApp::update() {
    static Serial serial;
    if (!serial.isConnected()) serial.setup(0, 115200);
    unsigned char buffer[64];
    int count = serial.readBytes(buffer, sizeof(buffer));
    if (count > 0) logNotice() << "Received " << count << " bytes";
}
```

## Serial::setup

- Call `setup(const string& portName, int baudRate)` with a device path, or `setup(int deviceIndex, int baudRate)` with a zero-based index from `listDevices()`. The baud rate is in bits per second, and neither argument has a default.
- Requests 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, and no flow control. Returns true when connected and false when opening or configuration fails, with an error log; Android USB permission waiting is a separate false-return case described below.
- The index overload enumerates devices again. An out-of-range index returns false without closing the existing connection; the path overload closes the previous connection first and fires `onDisconnect` with `wasClean = true` if it was open.
- Opening reasserts DTR, which resets auto-reset boards such as most Arduinos. Repeated successful setup calls therefore reopen the port rather than simply checking it.
- macOS and Linux accept positive driver-supported rates, including rates without a termios B-constant, such as 250000, 74880, or 921600 on macOS. Custom rates use `IOSSIOSPEED` on macOS and `termios2` on Linux; Windows passes the rate directly to the driver. A rejected desktop rate fails instead of silently selecting another speed.
- Linux reads back the applied rate when available, for standard and custom rates. A difference greater than 2% fails; a different rate within that tolerance succeeds with a warning naming the applied rate. If the driver retains its old rate even after an additional standard-rate probe, setup succeeds with a warning that baud rates have no effect, as with `/dev/ttyGS*`, `usb_serial_generic`, or xHCI DbC drivers.
- Android supports USB Host CDC-ACM devices. Without USB permission, setup requests permission, starts asynchronous connection work, and returns false; check `isConnected()` afterward. Repeating setup for the same pending device preserves the request and its original baud rate without restarting the dialog. An unanswered request times out after 60 seconds.
- On Android, rejection of the CDC line-coding request logs a warning but does not prevent connection; the backend also requests DTR and RTS.
- On desktop and Android, each open connection has a receive worker and storage allocated on demand up to 64 MiB. See `Serial::getDroppedByteCount` for overflow and counter resets, and `Serial::writeBytes` for platform-specific write waits.
- A `Serial` can be used from several threads. I/O calls and `getDroppedByteCount()` share its port lock, and receive-buffer access also uses a buffer mutex. `setup()`, `close()`, loss cleanup, destruction, and moves take exclusive access, wait for active I/O, and hold new I/O behind them; the app still controls which thread reads or writes which data and in what order.
- A long write or `drain()` delays opening and closing on another thread, while receive calls can proceed. Closing also stops and waits for the receive worker; macOS and Linux use a 50 ms receive poll timeout, Windows sleeps 5 ms when idle and waits up to 50 ms for a pending read, and Android bulk reads use a 250 ms timeout. Desktop moves transfer the worker with its connection, and Windows uses overlapped reads and writes.
- `isConnected()` and `getDevicePath()` do not wait for port operations. Ordinary Serial log callbacks run after its port lock is released, so an inline `Logger` listener may call the same `Serial`.
- Android USB workers also log permission timeouts, connections, losses, and open errors. An inline logger listener on such a worker must not perform Serial I/O, opening, closing, or destruction; use `Deliver::Main`. `isConnected()` and `getDevicePath()` are safe there.
- On any Serial USB worker thread, `setup()` and `close()` are refused before acquiring the port lock, do nothing, and log one refusal error per thread; setup returns false. An I/O call that finds loss there returns its error value without closing or firing `onDisconnect`, leaving `isConnected()` true until a call on another thread reports it.
- Android destruction and moves cannot refuse worker-thread calls. Destruction on the object's own worker leaves connection cleanup to that worker when it stops. Worker-thread destruction or movement is safe only while no other thread uses that `Serial`, because another thread can hold its port lock while waiting for the worker.
- On another Serial's USB worker, destruction waits for the destroyed object's worker, and move assignment waits for the destination's previous worker; move construction waits for no worker. A worker being waited for must not also wait for the calling thread, such as through simultaneous destruction or move assignment. I/O on a USB worker can deadlock for the same reason.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    static Serial serial;
    Serial::printDevices();
    if (!serial.setup(0, 115200)) {
        logWarning() << "Serial port is not connected yet";
    }
}
```

## Serial::writeByte

- Takes an `unsigned char` and returns true only when exactly one byte is written; returns false on an error or a write that transfers no byte.
- Calls `writeBytes()` internally, including its platform-specific waits, timeout behavior, and device-loss handling. See `Serial::setup` for threading rules.

## Serial::writeBytes

- `writeBytes(const void* buffer, int length)` writes up to `length` bytes and returns the actual count, or -1 on an error with no reported progress. `writeBytes(const string& buffer)` writes the string's bytes, including embedded null bytes, without adding a terminator.
- A disconnected port returns -1. After the loss and connection checks, a nonpositive length returns 0.
- On macOS and Linux, the port is nonblocking: a write can transfer fewer bytes than requested or return -1 while the output buffer is full, without closing the port.
- On Windows, waits for the driver to accept the data, with a timeout of `ceil(40000 / baudRate)` milliseconds per byte plus 5000 ms. This allows four times the 8N1 wire time, rounded up per byte: 9600 baud gives 5 ms per byte, about 5.5 minutes for 64 KiB; 40000 baud and above gives 1 ms per byte, about 70 seconds for 64 KiB. Native USB devices may ignore the baud rate.
- A Windows timeout returns the count written so far, possibly 0, logs one warning per connection, and leaves the port open without firing `onDisconnect`. Non-timeout write failures are treated as device loss.
- Android sends synchronous USB transfers of at most 16 KiB, applying the Windows timeout formula to each transfer: about 87 seconds at 9600 baud or 21 seconds at 115200 baud for 16 KiB. A timeout returns the count from completed transfers, possibly 0, logs one warning per connection, and leaves the port open. Bytes beyond that count may also have reached the device because Android does not report partial progress for the timed-out transfer.
- An Android transfer error logs an error and returns earlier progress, or -1 if none; that error alone does not close the connection. Once the receive worker records a loss, a subsequent reporting I/O call closes it and fires `onDisconnect`.
- A loss detected by this call closes the connection, fires `onDisconnect`, and returns -1; see `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification details. On Windows, receive status/read failures other than canceled reads also count as loss; framing and parity flags only produce warnings.
- Use a separate thread when a slow write must not stall the app; receive calls do not wait for the write itself. See `Serial::setup` for shared threading rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    static Serial serial;
    if (serial.setup(0, 115200)) {
        serial.writeBytes("hello\n");
    }
}
```

## SerialDeviceInfo

- `Serial::listDevices()` returns these records; `deviceId` is the device's index in that enumeration, `devicePath` identifies the port, and `deviceName` is its display name.
- Pass `devicePath` to `Serial::setup()` to open the port; examples include `COM3` on Windows, `/dev/ttyUSB0` on Linux, and a USB device path on Android.
- `getDeviceID()` returns the index; `getDevicePath()` and `getDeviceName()` return const references to the stored strings.

## SerialDeviceInfo::deviceId

- `Serial::listDevices()` assigns consecutive `int` indices starting at 0. This is a list position, not a persistent hardware identifier; enumeration can change between calls.
- The field has no member initializer; assign it before reading it in a manually default-initialized `SerialDeviceInfo`.

## SerialDeviceInfo::deviceName

- This `string` contains the COM port name on Windows, the device-node name without `/dev/` on macOS and Linux, and the USB product name on Android, falling back to the device path when the product name is empty.
- Use `devicePath` rather than this display name when opening a connection by path.

## SerialDeviceInfo::devicePath

- This `string` contains a path such as `COM3`, `/dev/tty.usbserial-A10172HG`, `/dev/ttyUSB0`, or Android's `/dev/bus/usb/001/002`.
- Pass this value to `Serial::setup(path, baudRate)` to open the listed device without selecting it by list index.

## SerialDeviceInfo::getDeviceID

- Returns `deviceId` as an `int` value without changing it. See `SerialDeviceInfo::deviceId` for index assignment and initialization.

## SerialDeviceInfo::getDeviceName

- Returns `deviceName` as a `const string&` without copying it. See `SerialDeviceInfo::deviceName` for platform-specific names.
- Both this getter and `getDevicePath()` return references to strings owned by the `SerialDeviceInfo`; keep that object alive and in place while using a reference, or copy the string for independent use.

## SerialDeviceInfo::getDevicePath

- Returns `devicePath` as a `const string&` without copying it. See `SerialDeviceInfo::devicePath` for path formats and use with `Serial::setup`.
- Reference lifetime follows the same rules as `SerialDeviceInfo::getDeviceName`.

## SerialDisconnectEventArgs

- `Serial::onDisconnect` supplies `portName`, the port passed to `setup()`, `baudRate`, the rate used by the connection, and `reason`, a human-readable explanation.
- `wasClean` is `true` when `close()` or a replacement `setup()` closes the connection, and `false` when an I/O call reports device loss or an error; it describes how the connection ended, so an unnoticed unplug can still be reported as a clean close.
- Notification occurs after the port is closed and its lock is released, inline on the calling thread by default; register with `Deliver::Main` when the listener must run on the main thread.
- See `Serial::onDisconnect` for notification conditions and reconnection behavior.

## SerialDisconnectEventArgs::baudRate

- This `int` contains the baud rate recorded for the connection, matching the rate in the connection log.
- Pass it with `portName` to `Serial::setup` to attempt reconnection: `serial.setup(e.portName, e.baudRate)`. Check `wasClean` first; see `Serial::onDisconnect` for reconnection precautions.
- The default value is `0`.

## SerialDisconnectEventArgs::portName

- This string contains the port name passed to `Serial::setup`. When connecting by device index, it contains the device path selected by that index.
- The default value is an empty string.

## SerialDisconnectEventArgs::reason

- Use this string for display or logging, and use `wasClean` to distinguish an application-requested close from a detected device loss. The default value is an empty string.
- For an application-requested close, the value is `"closed by close()"`. On Android, if the device loss was already recorded, `" (the device had already been lost: <reason>)"` is appended, while `wasClean` remains `true`.
- For a detected device loss, the value is the reason used in the loss warning, such as `"read: Input/output error"`.

## SerialDisconnectEventArgs::wasClean

- `true` means that `Serial::close` closed the connection, including when `Serial::setup` calls it to close the previous connection.
- `false` means that `available()`, `readBytes()`, `readByte()`, or `writeBytes()` detected a device loss or I/O error that ended the connection. The default value is `false`.
- If none of those I/O calls reports the loss before `close()` or `setup()`, the value is `true` even if the device has disappeared. On Android, `reason` may include an already recorded loss; see `SerialDisconnectEventArgs::reason`.

## Shader

- Holds vertex and fragment shader programs loaded through a sokol-shdc descriptor function; `load()` returns success or failure, and a new object starts unloaded.
- Use `begin()` and `end()`, or `pushShader()` and `popShader()`, around drawing calls; configure uniform blocks with `setUniform()` and texture bindings with `setTexture()`.
- The base vertex layout is position with three components, texture coordinates with two, and color with four. Direct submissions of `PrimitiveType::Lines` and `PrimitiveType::LineStrip` are discarded.
- The base pipeline uses alpha blending, always passes the depth test, disables depth writes, and disables face culling.
- Each window has its own shader stack, and each scope belongs to the render-target activation where it began. End scopes in reverse order on that same activation; keep each active shader loaded, alive, and at the same address until its scope ends.
- Ordinary shader draws record vertices, uniform bytes, and texture bindings for later replay. After ending its scope, the Shader object may be destroyed before replay; owned GPU resources are retained while recorded draws still reference them.
- Loading, drawing, clearing, and destruction must run on the main thread because they access GPU resources and shared drawing state. Copying is disabled; moving is supported when the object is not in an active shader scope.

## Shader::begin

- Pushes this shader onto the current window's shader stack so drawing functions that use the shader vertex writer submit through it; this does not immediately bind a GPU pipeline.
- Pair each successful `begin()` with `end()` in reverse nesting order, within the same window and render-target activation. Switching to another target temporarily suspends the scope until the original activation is restored.
- Calls the protected `onBegin()` hook after pushing the shader; an unloaded shader or a target whose recording has failed is ignored.
- Scope allocation failure or scope/layer count overflow logs an error and discards the target's recording.
- End the scope before clearing, moving, or destroying the shader, because the active stack stores its address. Resource lifetime after submission is described in `Shader::clear`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    shader.begin();
    drawTriangle(100, 100, 200, 100, 150, 200);
    shader.end();
}
```

## Shader::end

- Calls `onEnd()` before removing this shader from the current window's stack, restoring the previous shader; removing the last shader resets the sokol GPU state cache.
- Does nothing when unloaded or when the stack is empty. If another shader is on top, or the current target activation differs from the one recorded by `begin()`, logs a warning and leaves the scope open.
- Scope pairing and object lifetime rules are described in `Shader::begin`; this call does not flush deferred draws.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    shader.begin();
    drawTriangle(100, 100, 200, 100, 150, 200);
    shader.end();
}
```

## Shader::isLoaded

- Returns the stored `loaded` flag, which starts as `false`, becomes `true` after successful `load()`, and is reset by `clear()`.
- Does not validate GPU resources or guarantee that a compatible pipeline can be created for the current target.

## Shader::load

- Pass a non-null function with signature `const sg_shader_desc* (sg_backend)`; it is called with the current sokol backend to obtain the shader descriptor.
- Calls `clear()` first, then creates the GPU shader, captures the subclass's `createPipelineDesc()` result, and calls `createVertexBuffer()`.
- Returns `true` after the shader and required draw buffers are valid. A null descriptor or invalid shader or required buffer logs an error and returns `false`, leaving the shader unloaded.
- Target-compatible pipelines are created lazily when requested for drawing; target-specific pipeline failures are reported then rather than by `load()`. See `Shader::pipelineForCurrentTarget`.
- Reloading follows the scope and resource lifetime rules in `Shader::begin` and `Shader::clear`; stored uniforms and texture bindings are retained.

```cpp
#include "shaders/effect.glsl.h"
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!shader.load(rainbow_shader_desc)) {
        logError("Shader") << "Shader loading failed";
    }
}
```

## Shader::setTexture

- Accepts `(int slot, sg_view view, sg_sampler sampler)` or `(int slot, sg_image image, sg_sampler sampler)` and replaces the stored binding for that slot; binding to the GPU occurs when drawing.
- View slots are 0–31. Slots outside this range are ignored with a warning emitted only once.
- A sampler is bound at the same slot only for slots 0–11. For slots 12–31, a supplied nonzero sampler is ignored with a warning emitted only once; provide a sampler at binding 0–11 through another call or `setupBindings()`.
- The image overload creates and caches a texture view per slot, recreating it only when the image handle changes. Prefer the view overload when a view is already available.
- Supplied images, views, and samplers remain externally owned; only views created by the image overload are owned by the shader. Draw submissions copy handles rather than texture contents, so referenced resources must remain valid until execution; see `Shader::clear` for deferred resource retirement.

```cpp
void bindTexture(Shader& shader, const Texture& texture) {
    shader.setTexture(0, texture.getView(), texture.getSampler());
}
```

## Shader::setUniform

- `slot` is a uniform-block binding, not a variable name or byte offset. Each call copies data and replaces the entire stored block for that slot; GPU upload occurs when drawing.
- Accepts `float`, `Vec2`, `Vec3`, `Vec4`, `Color`, vectors of `float` or `Vec2`/`Vec3`/`Vec4`, and `(const void* data, size_t size)` for raw bytes.
- Single-value overloads store four floats, padding unused components with zero; `Color` stores RGBA. Vector overloads store arrays, with each `Vec3` padded to `Vec4` with `w = 0` for std140; the other vector overloads add no padding.
- Slots are 0–7; out-of-range slots are ignored with a warning emitted only once. The block size and layout must match the shader; the raw overload copies exactly `size` bytes.
- Values remain stored across draws, scope changes, and `clear()`. Submission snapshots are described in `Shader::submitVertices`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    // Slot 0 must declare a matching vec4 uniform block.
    shader.setUniform(0, Vec4(1.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    shader.begin();
    drawTriangle(100, 100, 200, 100, 150, 200);
    shader.end();
}
```

## Sound

- `load()` decodes a file into a `SoundBuffer`, while `loadStream()` uses a `SoundStream` on supported platforms. After loading succeeds, call `play()` to start playback.
- Copies share the source and any voice already started. When the last handle sharing a voice is destroyed or overwritten, that voice stops and its playback slot becomes reusable, whether playback is looping or one-shot. Keep playback handles alive, for example as members, to let sounds continue.
- `play()` stops this handle's previous voice before starting from the beginning; copies sharing that previous voice also observe it stopped. For overlapping one-shots, keep multiple `Sound` objects alive and play them separately.
- `stop()` releases the voice, including its streaming decoder and file; streaming cleanup can finish on the decoding worker if it is still using them.
- The default channel mixing mode is `MixMode::Auto`.
- Defaults are volume 1, centered pan 0, speed 1, and looping disabled. Serialize operations on each handle; audio-listener restrictions are described in `AudioEngine`.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
public:
    Sound sound;
    void setup() override {
        if (sound.load("sound.wav")) sound.play();
    }
};
```

## Sound::clearChannelGains

- Restores every output channel's gain multiplier to `1.0`, without changing volume, pan, or routing.
- Equivalent to `setChannelGains(vector<float>{})`; `getChannelGains()` subsequently returns a null shared pointer.

## Sound::clearChannelMap

- Removes the explicit channel map so that routing follows the current `MixMode` again.
- Equivalent to `setChannelMap(vector<vector<int>>{})`; `getChannelMap()` subsequently returns a null shared pointer.

## Sound::getChannelGains

- Returns `shared_ptr<const vector<float>>`, or a null shared pointer when no explicit gains are set; missing entries use `1.0`.
- Snapshot ownership and lifetime follow the same rules as `Sound::getChannelMap`.

## Sound::getChannelMap

- Returns `shared_ptr<const vector<vector<int>>>`, with one source-channel list per output channel; a null shared pointer means that `MixMode` rules apply.
- The returned pointer shares ownership of immutable settings rather than copying them. Retaining it keeps that snapshot alive even after the settings change or the `Sound` is destroyed.

## Sound::getDuration

- Returns the source duration in seconds, without adjusting for playback speed or looping.
- Returns `0` when no source is loaded or a stream's duration is unknown.

## Sound::getMixMode

- Returns the stored `MixMode`, initially `MixMode::Auto`; the other preset is `MixMode::DownmixMono`.
- A non-empty channel map overrides this mode during mixing without changing the returned value.

## Sound::getPan

- Returns the value stored for this `Sound`, from `-1.0` for left through `0.0` for center to `1.0` for right; the initial value is `0.0`.
- For the affected output channels, see `Sound::setPan`.

## Sound::getPosition

- Returns the playback position in seconds, rather than a normalized fraction; returns `0` when this `Sound` has no voice or no loaded source.
- While a stream seek is pending, returns the requested position before audio reaches it. For seek behavior and measured latency, see `Sound::setPosition`.
- This call takes an engine lock; for threading rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::getSpeed

- Returns the speed multiplier stored for this `Sound`; the initial value `1.0` means normal speed and natural pitch.
- For clamping, reverse playback, and zero-speed behavior, see `Sound::setSpeed`.

## Sound::getVolume

- Returns the volume multiplier stored for this `Sound`, initially `1.0`; this is a setting rather than a measurement of output loudness.
- The stored value is not clamped to `0.0`–`1.0`.

## Sound::isLoaded

- Returns `true` when this `Sound` holds a non-null source pointer, including a buffer supplied through `loadFromBuffer()`.
- Does not check for usable PCM samples or a running output device, and does not guarantee that `play()` will succeed.

## Sound::isLoop

- Returns whether looping is enabled for this `Sound`; the initial value is `false`.
- Reports the stored setting even when no audio is playing.

## Sound::isPaused

- Returns the retained voice's pause flag, or `false` when this `Sound` has no voice; this does not separately check whether the voice is still playing.
- `pause()` sets this flag, while `resume()` and `stop()` clear it.

## Sound::isPlaying

- Returns `true` only when this `Sound` has a voice marked as playing and not paused; paused, stopped, and ended voices return `false`.
- A stream halted by a decoder failure stops after its buffered audio drains, including looping streams. The error is logged once per halt, and TrussC does not retry automatically.
- For continuous music, check this state when playback is not intentionally paused or stopped. The application chooses when to retry with `loadStream()` and calls `play()` only after a successful load, checking its result as well.

## Sound::isStreaming

- Returns `true` when the current source is a stream, and `false` for an eagerly loaded buffer or no source.
- On Web, `loadStream()` falls back to `load()`, so this returns `false`; see `Sound::loadStream` for platform behavior.

## Sound::load

- Decodes the entire file into a `SoundBuffer` before returning; use this for short sounds or when full PCM data in memory is appropriate.
- Selects the decoder by extension: `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.ogg`, `.flac`, `.aac`, or `.m4a`. Extension matching ignores case without changing the file name; AAC/M4A decoding depends on the platform and is unsupported on Android.
- Resolves relative paths through `getDataPath()` and uses absolute paths as supplied.
- Returns a `LoadResult` that is true on success and contains an error and message on failure. Failure clears the assigned source, so `isLoaded()` becomes `false`.
- All `Sound` loading functions initialize the audio engine if needed and replace the source for future playback without stopping an existing voice or resetting playback settings. Loading success does not guarantee that an output device is running; check `play()` as well.
- For threading rules, see `Sound::play`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (sound.load("hit.wav")) {
        sound.play();
    }
}
```

## Sound::loadFromBuffer

- Accepts a `SoundBuffer`, such as one prepared by `ChipSound` or procedural waveform generation, without decoding a file.
- The `const SoundBuffer&` overload copies the buffer; the `shared_ptr<SoundBuffer>` overload shares ownership without copying PCM data.
- Returns no result and does not validate the buffer's samples. A null shared pointer clears the source; a non-null but empty buffer still makes `isLoaded()` return `true`.
- Shared loading behavior is described in `Sound::load`; threading rules are described in `Sound::play`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    buffer.generateSineWave(440.0f, 1.0f);
    sound.loadFromBuffer(buffer);
    sound.play();
}
```

## Sound::loadStream

- Supports WAV, MP3, and FLAC, selected by a case-insensitive extension. Decodes during playback on a worker thread into a small buffer instead of keeping the full PCM file in memory, making it suitable for long music files.
- `maxPolyphony` limits concurrent voices sharing this stream source, including copies of the `Sound`; it defaults to `1`, and smaller values become `1`. Repeated `play()` on one `Sound` restarts its voice rather than creating overlap.
- Resolves relative paths through `getDataPath()` and uses absolute paths as supplied. Loading probes the file, and each playback opens its own decoder; MP3 loading also prepares a shared seek table.
- Returns a `LoadResult` that is true on success; failure clears the assigned source. A successful load does not guarantee successful `play()`, because the file must be reopened and voice limits still apply.
- Streaming speed is limited to forward playback from `0` to `10`. Seeking requires decoding and buffer refilling; a stream with unknown duration reports `0` and cannot seek, and restarting the engine at another sample rate restarts that stream from the beginning.
- Shared loading behavior is described in `Sound::load`; threading and voice lifetime are described in `Sound::play`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (sound.loadStream("music.mp3")) {
        sound.setLoop(true);
        sound.play();
    }
}
```

## Sound::loadTestTone

- Generates a tone without a file for checking audio output; call `play()` separately to hear it.
- `frequency` is in hertz and defaults to `440.0`; `duration` is in seconds and defaults to `1.0`. The generated buffer is mono at `44100` Hz with amplitude `0.5`.
- Returns no result. Shared loading behavior is described in `Sound::load`; threading rules are described in `Sound::play`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    sound.loadTestTone(440.0f, 1.0f);
    sound.play();
}
```

## Sound::pause

- Sets the current voice's pause flag without releasing the voice or resetting its position; does nothing when this `Sound` has no voice.
- `isPlaying()` returns `false` while paused. Use `resume()` to clear the pause flag.
- For shared voice lifetime and threading rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::play

- Stops this `Sound`'s previous voice before starting a new voice at the beginning, using its stored volume, pan, speed, loop, mix mode, channel map, and channel gains. Use `resume()` to continue paused playback.
- Returns `true` when a voice is created, or `false` when no source is loaded or the engine rejects playback. Voice creation alone does not validate an externally supplied buffer's PCM data.
- The engine rejects playback when all slots are busy, copies sharing a stream reach its `maxPolyphony`, the stream file cannot be reopened, or no output device is running. Rejections are logged as warnings and counted in `AudioEngine::getStats()`.
- Copies share the current voice, so stopping or pausing through one copy affects the others, and restarting through one copy first stops that shared voice. Keep a `Sound` or a copy alive while it plays; destroying or overwriting its last handle stops the voice and frees its slot, including looping and one-shot playback.
- Serialize application access to each `Sound`; its stored settings are not synchronized between application threads. Settings can be changed while the audio thread mixes the voice, but loading, playback control, and position access belong outside audio callbacks because they can allocate, perform file I/O, or take engine locks.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (sound.load("hit.wav")) {
        if (!sound.play()) logWarning("Sound") << "Playback did not start";
    }
}
```

## Sound::resume

- Clears the current voice's pause flag so an active paused voice continues from its retained position.
- Does nothing when this `Sound` has no voice and does not restart an ended voice; use `play()` to start from the beginning.
- For shared voice lifetime and threading rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setChannelGains

- Copies the supplied `vector<float>` into immutable settings, with entry `c` multiplying output channel `c`; channels beyond the vector use `1.0`, and an empty vector clears the settings.
- Values are neither clamped nor normalized. Channel gains multiply the routed samples together with pan and the overall `setVolume()` gain.
- Updates this `Sound`'s stored settings and its current voice. For threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setChannelMap

- The `vector<int>` overload assigns one zero-based source-channel index to each output channel; `-1` or any negative entry makes that output silent.
- The `vector<vector<int>>` overload sums the listed source channels into each output without normalization. An empty inner list is silent, and out-of-range source indices contribute zero.
- Outputs beyond the map's size are silent. A non-empty map overrides `MixMode`; an empty map clears explicit routing and restores the current mode.
- For streamed audio, source indices refer to the decoder's stereo output, channels `0` and `1`, rather than the file's original channel layout.
- Stores immutable routing settings and updates the current voice. For threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setLoop

- Stores the loop flag for future playback and updates the current voice; the initial setting is `false`.
- Does not start playback or restart a voice that has already ended.
- For threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setMixMode

- `MixMode::Auto` is the default: mono sources are sent to every output channel, while multichannel sources use matching channel indices; extra outputs are silent and extra source channels are omitted.
- `MixMode::DownmixMono` averages all source channels and sends the same result to every output channel. Streams use the decoder's stereo output as their source channels.
- A non-empty channel map overrides the preset until cleared. Channel gains, pan, and overall volume still apply afterward.
- Updates this `Sound`'s stored mode and its current voice. For threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setPan

- Clamps the value to `-1.0` for left through `0.0` for center to `1.0` for right; the initial setting is `0.0`.
- Applies linear balance to output channels `0` and `1`: center leaves both unchanged, positive values attenuate channel `0`, and negative values attenuate channel `1`. Output channels `2` and above are unaffected.
- Updates this `Sound`'s stored value and its current voice. For threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

## Sound::setPosition

- `seconds` is an absolute time in seconds, rather than a normalized fraction. Requires a current voice and a loaded source; otherwise the call does nothing. Changing position does not start or resume playback.
- Negative times are clamped to the beginning. For an eager buffer, times at or beyond the end are clamped to its last frame, or zero for an empty buffer; known-length streams also clamp to their available frames.
- Eager playback changes position immediately. A stream changes audio position after the decoder seeks and the buffer refills; `getPosition()` reports the requested position immediately, the latest pending request wins, and a paused stream plays from that position when resumed.
- A stream with unknown length, reported by `getDuration()` as `0`, ignores the seek and logs a warning once per voice.
- Measurements from the seek request to the first output callback containing post-seek audio were about 1.5 callbacks on average and about 2 at p95 on WASAPI/CoreAudio, with means of 13–16 ms for 10 ms callbacks; the main-branch PulseAudio measurement averaged 25.4 ms. These are callback timings rather than speaker/DAC latency or silence duration, and slow storage or an MP3 several hours long can take longer; see issue #550 for the measurements.
- This call takes an engine lock; for threading and shared voice rules, see `Sound::play`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (sound.load("music.wav") && sound.play()) {
        sound.setPosition(10.0f);
    }
}
```

## Sound::setSpeed

- `speed` is a playback-rate multiplier: `1.0f` is normal speed and the default, and `2.0f` doubles the speed and raises the pitch. The setting updates the current voice and is retained for subsequent `play()` calls.
- Values are clamped to `[-10, 10]`. Negative values play fully decoded sounds backward from the current position; use `setPosition()` after `play()` to start near the end. If a streaming source is already loaded, negative input is clamped to `0`.
- A speed of `0` freezes the position while continuing to output the same interpolated sample; it does not pause or release the voice. Positive values have no minimum above zero.
- For non-looping reverse playback, call `setSpeed(0)`, `play()`, `setPosition(getDuration())`, then `setSpeed(-1)` on the sound; starting with negative speed can stop the voice before you seek, and seeking does not restart it.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!sound.load("music.ogg")) return;
    sound.setSpeed(0.5f);
    sound.play();
}
```

## Sound::setVolume

- `vol` is a linear amplitude multiplier: `0.0f` silences the sound, and `1.0f` preserves its amplitude and is the default.
- The value is not clamped to `[0, 1]`: values above `1` amplify the sound, and negative values invert its polarity. The final mixed output is clipped to `[-1, 1]`.
- The setting updates the current voice and is retained for subsequent `play()` calls. It can also be set before loading a sound; see `Sound` for shared-voice behavior.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Sound sound;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!sound.load("music.ogg")) return;
    sound.setVolume(0.5f);
    sound.play();
}
```

## Sound::stop

- Stops the current voice, clears its paused state, and frees its engine playback slot. Copies sharing the voice also observe it as stopped.
- The loaded source and playback settings are retained, and the next `play()` starts from the beginning. Calling `stop()` again has no effect; use `pause()` and `resume()` to retain the playback position.
- For a streaming voice, its decoder and file are also released. If the decoding worker is currently refilling that voice, they close when the worker releases its reference.

```cpp
// tcApp.h (inside class tcApp : public App)
Sound sound;
void keyPressed(int key) override;

// tcApp.cpp
void tcApp::keyPressed(int key) {
    if (key == KEY_SPACE) sound.stop();
}
```

## SoundBuffer

- File loading decodes the complete audio into interleaved float PCM in `samples`. `numSamples` counts frames, or samples per channel; the interleaved sample count is `numSamples * channels`.
- This `SoundSource` subclass inherits `channels`, `sampleRate`, and `kind()`; its kind is `SoundSource::Eager`, and `getDuration()` returns `numSamples / sampleRate` in seconds, or 0 when the sample rate is 0.
- It suits short sound effects and repeated or overlapping playback: after loading, playback and seeking read PCM from RAM without file decoding.
- Waveform generators, an ADSR envelope, and mixing helpers also allow procedural audio construction.
- Finish direct edits to a shared buffer before the mixer reads it; direct sample access and generation or mixing helpers do not lock the mixer. Audio-listener restrictions are described in `AudioEngine`.

## SoundBuffer::applyADSR

- `attack`, `decay`, and `release` are durations in seconds; `sustainLevel` is the sustain amplitude, normally 0–1, and is not clamped.
- The envelope rises linearly from 0 to 1, falls to `sustainLevel`, holds, then falls toward 0; sustain time is `max(0.0f, getDuration() - attack - decay - release)`, and the other stages are not shortened to fit.
- Only `samples[0]` through `samples[numSamples - 1]` are multiplied; for multichannel buffers, this does not process every channel of every frame.
- Cancels a pending `loadAsync` before checking for an empty buffer or a zero sample rate; either condition then leaves samples unchanged.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    buffer.generateSineWave(440.0f, 1.0f);
    buffer.applyADSR(0.01f, 0.1f, 0.6f, 0.2f);
}
```

## SoundBuffer::clip

- Replaces values above 1 with 1 and values below −1 with −1, across the entire `samples` vector.
- See `SoundBuffer::applyADSR` for cancellation of pending loads and `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    buffer.generateSineWave(440.0f, 1.0f, 1.5f);
    buffer.clip();
}
```

## SoundBuffer::createAdtsHeader

- This static helper writes seven bytes to `header`, which must point to writable storage of at least that size; it can wrap raw AAC frames extracted from a MOV container.
- `frameLength` is the payload size in bytes excluding the header, `sampleRate` is in Hz, and `channels` supplies the channel configuration; the encoded total length is `frameLength + 7`.
- `profile` defaults to 2 for AAC-LC; positive values are encoded as `profile - 1`, and nonpositive values also select AAC-LC.
- The header has no CRC; arguments are not validated, and unsupported sample rates use the fallback described in `SoundBuffer::getAdtsSampleRateIndex`.

## SoundBuffer::generateNoise

- Takes `duration`, `volume = 0.5f`, and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- Uses a fixed seed of 12345 on every call, so identical arguments produce the same sequence; noise values from −1 to 1 are multiplied by `volume`.

## SoundBuffer::generatePinkNoise

- Takes `duration`, `volume = 0.5f`, and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- Uses Paul Kellet's filtering method to approximate a 1/f spectrum, then multiplies the filtered output by `volume * 0.11f`.
- The random seed and filter state reset on every call, so identical arguments produce the same sequence.

## SoundBuffer::generateSawtoothWave

- Takes `frequency`, `duration`, `volume = 0.5f`, and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- Each positive-frequency cycle starts at `-volume` and rises linearly toward `volume` before resetting.

## SoundBuffer::generateSilence

- Takes `duration` and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- Uses `samples.resize(numSamples, 0.0f)`: only newly added elements become zero, while retained elements keep their previous values.
- A fresh buffer produces silence and can serve as the destination for `SoundBuffer::mixFrom`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    buffer.generateSilence(2.0f);
}
```

## SoundBuffer::generateSineWave

- `frequency` is in Hz, `duration` is in seconds, `volume` is an amplitude multiplier defaulting to 0.5, and `sr` is the sample rate in Hz defaulting to 44100.
- Writes `volume * sin(TAU * frequency * i / sampleRate)` for each sample, starting at phase zero.
- All waveform and noise generators, including `generateSilence`, set `channels = 1`, set `sampleRate = sr`, and resize storage to `numSamples = (size_t)(duration * sampleRate)`.
- Generation cancels a pending `loadAsync` and clears `getPath()`; arguments are not validated and amplitude is not clipped.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    buffer.generateSineWave(440.0f, 1.0f, 0.25f, 48000);
}
```

## SoundBuffer::generateSquareWave

- Takes `frequency`, `duration`, `volume = 0.5f`, and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- For positive frequencies, each cycle outputs `volume` for its first half and `-volume` for its second half.

## SoundBuffer::generateTriangleWave

- Takes `frequency`, `duration`, `volume = 0.5f`, and `sr = 44100`; see `SoundBuffer::generateSineWave` for units and shared generation behavior.
- For positive frequencies, each cycle starts at `-volume`, rises linearly to `volume` halfway through, then falls toward `-volume`.

## SoundBuffer::getAdtsSampleRateIndex

- This static AAC container helper accepts a sample rate in Hz and returns its index in `{96000, 88200, 64000, 48000, 44100, 32000, 24000, 22050, 16000, 12000, 11025, 8000, 7350}`, starting at 0.
- Rates outside this list return 4, the index for 44100 Hz.

## SoundBuffer::getDuration

- Returns `(float)numSamples / sampleRate`, or 0 when `sampleRate` is 0.
- Uses the stored metadata without inspecting `samples.size()`.

## SoundBuffer::getPath

- Returns an `fs::path` by value, including paths recorded by direct calls to `loadAac`.
- Returns an empty path after a failed load, a memory or PCM load, or waveform generation.

## SoundBuffer::load

- Selects the decoder by the case-insensitive extension `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.ogg`, `.flac`, `.aac`, or `.m4a`, and finishes decoding into interleaved float PCM before returning.
- File loaders resolve relative paths with `getDataPath()` and use absolute paths unchanged; successful loads record the resolved path in `getPath()`.
- Returns `LoadResult`, which converts to true on success; inspect `error` and `message` for failure details. Missing or unreadable files report `LoadError::FileNotFound`; an existing file with an unsupported extension reports `LoadError::UnsupportedFormat`.
- All synchronous file, encoded-memory, and PCM loaders cancel a pending `loadAsync` and clear `getPath()` before loading, including requests that fail.
- All encoded audio loaders preserve previous PCM and audio metadata on any failure and never publish a partial sound. Full loads have no length limit. Past 256 MiB decoded PCM, one process-lifetime Notice recommends `SoundStream::loadStream()` / `Sound::loadStream()` for long tracks. Encoded inputs above 64 MiB are not loaded fully; allocation failure is a clean Error.
- Serialize handle operations and direct sample access on the main thread. Synchronous loading, generation, and editing do not lock the audio mixer, so do not modify a buffer while any playing `Sound` reads it.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    auto result = buffer.load("sounds/chime.wav");
    if (!result) logError("SoundBuffer") << result.message;
}
```

## SoundBuffer::loadAac

- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::load` for path resolution, cancellation, and threading rules.
- On Web, waits for `OfflineAudioContext` decoding to finish even inside `setup()`, with a 30-second timeout, and stores PCM at 44100 Hz.
- On any failure, previous PCM and audio metadata are preserved; no partial sound is published. Full loads have no length limit. Past 256 MiB decoded PCM, one process-lifetime Notice recommends `SoundStream::loadStream()` / `Sound::loadStream()` for long tracks. Encoded inputs above 64 MiB are not loaded fully; allocation failure is a clean Error.

## SoundBuffer::loadAacFromMemory

- `data` points to encoded data and `dataSize` is its size in bytes; decoding completes before returning a `LoadResult`.
- See `SoundBuffer::loadWavFromMemory` for input lifetime and `SoundBuffer::load` for cancellation and threading rules.
- On any failure, previous PCM and audio metadata are preserved; no partial sound is published. Full loads have no length limit. Past 256 MiB decoded PCM, one process-lifetime Notice recommends `SoundStream::loadStream()` / `Sound::loadStream()` for long tracks. Encoded inputs above 64 MiB are not loaded fully; allocation failure is a clean Error.

## SoundBuffer::loadFlac

- Uses miniaudio to decode the complete file into interleaved float PCM, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::load` for path resolution, failure behavior, cancellation, and threading rules.

## SoundBuffer::loadFlacFromMemory

- Decodes `dataSize` bytes of encoded FLAC at `data` through miniaudio, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::loadWavFromMemory` for the shared memory-loading contract.

## SoundBuffer::loadMp3

- Uses miniaudio to decode the complete file into interleaved float PCM, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::load` for path resolution, failure behavior, cancellation, and threading rules.

## SoundBuffer::loadMp3FromMemory

- Decodes `dataSize` bytes of encoded MP3 at `data` through miniaudio, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::loadWavFromMemory` for the shared memory-loading contract.

## SoundBuffer::loadOgg

- Uses stb_vorbis to decode into interleaved float PCM, preserving the source channel count and sample rate; a stream with an unknown stated length can still load.
- Returns a failed `LoadResult` if no frames decode or sample storage cannot grow; see `SoundBuffer::load` for path resolution, failure behavior, cancellation, and threading rules.

## SoundBuffer::loadOggFromMemory

- Decodes `dataSize` bytes of encoded OGG Vorbis at `data` through stb_vorbis, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Null input or `dataSize == 0` returns `LoadError::DecodeFailed`; the decoder receives `dataSize` converted to `int`, without a range check.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::loadWavFromMemory` for the shared memory-loading contract.

## SoundBuffer::loadPcmFromMemory

- `dataSize` is in bytes, `numChannels` is the channel count, and `rate` is the sample rate in Hz; `bitsPerSample` defaults to 16 and `bigEndian` defaults to false.
- Supports signed 16-bit integers, converted by division by 32768, and 32-bit floats, copied without clipping; `bigEndian = true` reverses each sample's bytes.
- Requires whole frames of `(bitsPerSample / 8) * numChannels` bytes. Unsupported bit depths or fewer than one channel return `LoadError::UnsupportedFormat`; incomplete frames or excessive sample counts return `LoadError::DecodeFailed`.
- These validation failures preserve samples and audio metadata; `rate` and the input pointer are not validated.
- On success, copies the data, sets `channels`, `sampleRate`, and `numSamples`, and returns a successful `LoadResult`; the input need only remain valid during the call.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for cancellation, path clearing, and threading rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    float data[] = {0.0f, 0.25f, 0.0f, -0.25f};
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    auto result = buffer.loadPcmFromMemory(data, sizeof(data), 1, 44100, 32);
    if (!result) logError("SoundBuffer") << result.message;
}
```

## SoundBuffer::loadWav

- Uses miniaudio to decode the complete file into interleaved float PCM, preserving the source channel count and sample rate.
- Returns `LoadResult`; see `SoundBuffer::load` for path resolution, failure behavior, cancellation, and threading rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer;
    auto result = buffer.loadWav("sounds/chime.wav");
    if (!result) logError("SoundBuffer") << result.message;
}
```

## SoundBuffer::loadWavFromMemory

- `data` points to an encoded WAV file, including its header, and `dataSize` is its size in bytes; miniaudio produces interleaved float PCM with the source channel count and sample rate.
- Encoded-memory loaders finish decoding before returning and do not retain the input pointer; keep the input valid throughout the call.
- WAV, MP3, FLAC, and OGG memory loaders return a successful `LoadResult` on success or `LoadError::DecodeFailed` on failure, preserving existing samples and audio metadata on failure.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for cancellation, path clearing, and threading rules.

## SoundBuffer::mixFrom

- Adds `other` multiplied by `volume = 1.0f`, starting at `offsetSamples` frames; this is the same per-channel unit as `numSamples`, not an index into interleaved samples.
- Grows storage and `numSamples` when needed, filling newly added storage with zero before mixing; output is not clipped.
- Both buffers must have the same positive channel count. A mismatch, an excessive destination size, or a handled allocation failure logs an error and mixes nothing.
- Uses only complete source frames actually present, up to `other.numSamples`; an empty source does nothing. Sample rates are neither compared nor converted.
- See `SoundBuffer::applyADSR` for cancellation of pending loads and `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SoundBuffer buffer, other;
    buffer.generateSilence(2.0f);
    other.generateSineWave(440.0f, 0.5f);
    buffer.mixFrom(other, 44100, 0.5f);
}
```

## SoundBuffer::numSamples

- This public `size_t` member starts at 0 and counts samples per channel; interleaved storage normally contains `numSamples * channels` floats.
- Direct changes to `samples` do not update it automatically; keep it consistent with the audio data.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions.

## SoundBuffer::samples

- This public `vector<float>` stores channels consecutively within each frame; access channel `ch` of frame `i` with `samples[i * channels + ch]`.
- Direct edits neither cancel `loadAsync` nor update `numSamples`, `channels`, or `sampleRate`; keep the data and metadata consistent.
- See `SoundBuffer::load` for threading and editing restrictions; operations that reallocate the vector invalidate pointers and references to its elements.

## SoundSource

- The concrete source types used for playback are `SoundBuffer`, which holds fully decoded PCM in RAM, and `SoundStream`, which decodes file audio on demand.
- The shared interface provides `channels`, `sampleRate` in Hz, `kind()`, and `getDuration()` in seconds. `kind()` distinguishes `SoundSource::Eager` from `SoundSource::Stream`.
- Playback-handle ownership is described in `Sound`; source-specific storage and decoding behavior are described in `SoundBuffer` and `SoundStream`.

## SoundSource::Kind

- `SoundSource::Eager` identifies `SoundBuffer`, which holds the complete decoded PCM in RAM; `SoundSource::Stream` identifies `SoundStream`, which decodes audio on demand.
- The mixer uses this tag to select the playback path without a virtual call for each audio frame.

## SoundSource::channels

- This public `int` field is initially `0`; `1` means mono and `2` means stereo.
- For `SoundStream`, it describes the converted decoder output rather than the original file; see `SoundStream::loadStream`.

## SoundSource::getDuration

- This pure virtual function returns a `float` duration in seconds.
- `SoundBuffer` returns `numSamples / sampleRate`, or `0` when `sampleRate` is `0`; `SoundStream` returns the file duration recorded during loading, which can be `0` when unknown.

## SoundSource::kind

- Returns `SoundSource::Eager` for `SoundBuffer` and `SoundSource::Stream` for `SoundStream`.
- See `SoundSource::Kind` for the data storage and mixer behavior associated with each value.

## SoundSource::sampleRate

- This public `int` field stores the sample rate in Hz and is initially `0`.
- For `SoundStream`, it describes the converted decoder output rather than the original file; see `SoundStream::loadStream`.

## SoundStream

- This `SoundSource` subclass suits long music or spoken audio. Loading probes and closes the file; each playing voice opens its own file and decoder, and a worker decodes into a ring buffer.
- `loadStream(path, maxPolyphony)` supports WAV, MP3, and FLAC extensions without case sensitivity. The per-source voice limit defaults to 1 and values below 1 become 1; exceeding it rejects a new play.
- The source inherits `channels`, `sampleRate`, and `kind()` and reports `SoundSource::Stream`. Its `sampleRate` metadata retains the engine rate used when loading; each voice decodes stereo float audio at the current engine rate, including after reinitialization at a different rate. `getDuration()` returns seconds.
- Each opened voice uses a file handle, decoder, and a ring buffer of 16384 stereo float frames, or 128 KiB, instead of keeping the full decoded file in RAM.
- Playback speed supports 0 through 10; negative speeds are treated as 0, and 0 holds the current sample. Seeking requires decoder seeking and a ring-buffer refill; `Sound::getPosition()` reports the requested target while waiting. See `Sound::setPosition()` for seek behavior.
- A source with unknown duration reports 0 and cannot seek. Reinitializing the engine at a different sample rate restarts such a stream from the beginning.
- On Web, `Sound::loadStream()` logs a warning and falls back to full decoding into a `SoundBuffer`. Playback ownership and audio-listener restrictions are described in `Sound` and `AudioEngine`.

## SoundStream::getDuration

- Returns the duration recorded by a successful load as a `float` in seconds; the initial value is `0`.
- A file without a recorded length, such as a FLAC encoded to a pipe, also returns `0`. It can play to its end, but cannot seek; reinitializing the audio engine at a different sample rate restarts it from the beginning.

## SoundStream::getMaxPolyphony

- Returns the `maxPolyphony` value stored by the last successful `loadStream`; the initial value is `1`, and load arguments below `1` are raised to `1`.
