- This limits simultaneous voices sharing this source; decoders are opened when playback starts rather than reserved during loading.

## SoundStream::getPath

- Returns an `fs::path` by value; relative load paths are resolved through `getDataPath`, and absolute paths pass through unchanged.
- The path is empty initially and after a failed load.

## SoundStream::loadStream

- `loadStream(path, maxPolyphony = 1)` synchronously opens and probes WAV, MP3, or FLAC files, selecting the format from the extension without regard to case. OGG and AAC/M4A are unsupported by this entry point.
- Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath`; absolute paths pass through unchanged. Returns a `LoadResult` that converts to `true` on success and `false` on failure.
- On success, `channels` becomes `2`, `sampleRate` becomes the audio engine's current rate in Hz, and the duration is recorded in seconds. These fields describe the converted output at load time. This function does not initialize the audio engine.
- `maxPolyphony` limits simultaneous voices sharing this source, defaults to `1`, and is raised to `1` if smaller. Additional playback is rejected when the limit is reached; per-voice decoders and ring buffers are created when playback starts.
- Loading probes and closes the file; later playback reopens it and a worker decodes audio on demand. MP3 loading also scans frame headers to prepare a seek table shared by the voices.
- Failure includes unreadable files, unsupported formats, decoder or MP3 seek-table preparation errors, and files with no audio frames (`LoadError::DecodeFailed`). Failure clears the recorded path but preserves previously stored channels, sample rate, duration, and polyphony limit.
- Files with unknown length can still load successfully; see `SoundStream::getDuration` for their seek and engine reinitialization behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    AudioEngine::getInstance().init();
    static auto stream = make_shared<SoundStream>();
    if (stream->loadStream("music.flac", 2)) {
        AudioEngine::getInstance().play(stream);
    }
}
```

## StrokeCap

- `Butt` stops at the endpoint, `Round` adds a semicircle, and `Square` extends the endpoint by half the stroke width.
- Select the style with `setStrokeCap()`; the default is `StrokeCap::Butt`. Closed strokes do not have endpoint caps.

## StrokeJoin

- `Miter` makes pointed corners, `Round` makes rounded corners, and `Bevel` cuts corners flat.
- Select the style with `setStrokeJoin()`; the default is `StrokeJoin::Miter`.

## StrokeMesh

- Add points with `addVertex()` or `addVertexWithWidth()`, or copy a `Path` with `setShape()`. `setShape()` replaces the existing shape and clears per-vertex widths.
- Call `update()` after changes to rebuild the triangle mesh on the CPU, then call `draw()`. `draw()` does not call `update()`, and an unchanged `update()` does no work.
- Widths use the same coordinate units as the input points. Missing per-vertex widths use the default width, initially `2`; the initial color is opaque white.
- Supports butt, round, and square caps, plus miter, round, and bevel joins. Defaults are `CAP_BUTT`, `JOIN_MITER`, miter limit `10`, and an open stroke.
- Setting methods mark the geometry changed, but editing the vector returned by `getPolylines()` does not. Use `setShape()` to submit an edited path for rebuilding.
- `getMesh()` exposes the generated `Mesh`; see `Mesh` for drawing and GPU resource behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.addVertexWithWidth(50, 50, 2);
    stroke.addVertexWithWidth(150, 100, 12);
    stroke.setCapType(StrokeMesh::CAP_ROUND);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::CapType

- `StrokeMesh::CAP_BUTT` cuts the stroke flat at each endpoint, `StrokeMesh::CAP_ROUND` adds a semicircle, and `StrokeMesh::CAP_SQUARE` extends each end by half its width.
- The default is `StrokeMesh::CAP_BUTT`; closed paths do not receive caps.

## StrokeMesh::JoinType

- `StrokeMesh::JOIN_MITER` produces pointed joins, `StrokeMesh::JOIN_ROUND` rounds the corners, and `StrokeMesh::JOIN_BEVEL` cuts the corners flat.
- The default is `StrokeMesh::JOIN_MITER`; its extension is controlled by `StrokeMesh::setMiterLimit`.

## StrokeMesh::addVertex

- Accepts `Vec3`, `Vec2`, or `x, y, z`; `z` defaults to `0`, and `Vec2` also uses `z = 0`. The vertex is appended to the first source path.
- This function does not append a per-vertex width. Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.addVertex(20, 20).addVertex(120, 80);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::addVertexWithWidth

- Accepts `x, y, width` with `z = 0`, or `Vec3, width`. The vertex is appended to the first source path, and the full width is appended to the width list.
- Widths are assigned by list position. Mixing this function with `addVertex` does not insert missing widths for earlier vertices; use `setWidths` to supply an aligned list.
- Width units, rebuilding, and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.addVertexWithWidth(20, 40, 2);
    stroke.addVertexWithWidth(180, 40, 20);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::clear

- Removes all source paths, creates one empty open path, clears the width list, and immediately clears the generated mesh.
- Keeps the width, color, cap, join, miter limit, and stroke closure setting. A retained `true` closure setting closes newly added geometry at the next rebuild.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.addVertex(0, 0).addVertex(100, 0);
    stroke.clear();
    stroke.addVertex(20, 40).addVertex(160, 40);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::draw

- Draws the current internal `Mesh`; an empty mesh draws nothing. Geometry is not rebuilt automatically, so call `update()` after changing the stroke.
- Generated vertices contain the color set by `StrokeMesh::setColor` and have no normals. Drawing behavior is described in `Mesh`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.setWidth(8);
    stroke.addVertex(20, 40).addVertex(180, 40);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::getMesh

- Returns a mutable `Mesh&` without rebuilding it; call `update()` first to obtain geometry matching the current stroke settings.
- The mesh belongs to this `StrokeMesh`. Direct mesh edits do not change the source paths and are replaced by the next rebuild.

## StrokeMesh::getPolylines

- Returns a mutable `vector<Path>&` owned by this `StrokeMesh`, allowing access to multiple source paths.
- Direct edits through this reference do not request a rebuild. Call a setter such as `setWidth(2.0f)` with the desired default width to mark the stroke as changed, then call `update()`.
- Replacing or clearing paths can invalidate references to individual paths.

## StrokeMesh::setCapType

- Accepts `StrokeMesh::CAP_BUTT`, `StrokeMesh::CAP_ROUND`, or `StrokeMesh::CAP_SQUARE`; the default is `StrokeMesh::CAP_BUTT`. Shapes are described in `StrokeMesh::CapType`.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setClosed

- The default is `false`. With `true`, rebuilding closes each source path with at least two vertices, connecting its last vertex to its first.
- Setting `false` does not reopen paths that are already closed. To reopen them, set this option to `false`, call `setClosed(false)` on the affected paths through `getPolylines()`, and then call `update()`.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setColor

- Accepts a `Color` with floating-point RGBA components in the `0–1` range. The default is opaque white, and the color is written to every generated vertex during rebuilding.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.setColor(Color(1.0f, 0.3f, 0.1f, 1.0f));
    stroke.addVertex(20, 40).addVertex(180, 40);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## StrokeMesh::setJoinType

- Accepts `StrokeMesh::JOIN_MITER`, `StrokeMesh::JOIN_ROUND`, or `StrokeMesh::JOIN_BEVEL`; the default is `StrokeMesh::JOIN_MITER`. Shapes are described in `StrokeMesh::JoinType`.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setMiterLimit

- Sets the dimensionless ratio of miter length to half the local stroke width; the default is `10.0`. It affects only `StrokeMesh::JOIN_MITER`.
- When the computed ratio exceeds the limit, both sides use an offset of half the width along the averaged normal instead of the extended miter.
- The value is stored without clamping. Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setShape

- Copies the supplied `Path`, replaces all source paths with that copy, clears per-vertex widths, and copies its `isClosed()` value into the stroke closure setting. Other style settings are preserved.
- A Path containing multiple subpaths is processed as one continuous vertex list; subpath boundaries are not separated, and its last subpath supplies `isClosed()`.
- Rebuilding and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setWidth

- Sets the full width used where no per-vertex width is supplied; the default is `2.0`. Existing per-vertex widths are preserved.
- Width units, rebuilding, and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::setWidths

- Copies a `vector<float>` of full widths. For a single source path, values correspond to vertices in order; missing trailing widths use `setWidth()`, and extra values are unused.
- An empty list restores the default width for every vertex. Width units, rebuilding, and method chaining are described in `StrokeMesh::update`.

## StrokeMesh::update

- Call after editing and before `draw()`. When marked as changed, it replaces the generated mesh with CPU-generated triangles; otherwise it returns immediately.
- Stroke setters, vertex additions, and `clear()` return `StrokeMesh&` for chaining and mark the stroke as changed. Direct edits through `getPolylines()` or `getMesh()` do not mark it as changed.
- Widths are full widths in the same local coordinate units as vertices, are transformed with the geometry, and are not clamped. Stroke expansion changes X and Y while preserving each source vertex's Z; it is not a camera-facing 3D ribbon.
- Paths with fewer than two vertices produce no triangles. Within each path, a vertex is skipped if its squared distance from the last retained vertex is at most `0.0001`; fewer than two retained vertices also produce no triangles.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    StrokeMesh stroke;
    stroke.setWidth(12).setCapType(StrokeMesh::CAP_ROUND);
    stroke.addVertex(20, 40).addVertex(180, 40);
    stroke.update();
    stroke.draw();
}
```

## TcpClient

- Connect with a host name and port using `connect()` or `connectAsync()`. Threading is enabled by default on native platforms; `connect()` waits for TCP connection completion in that mode, while `connectAsync()` reports completion through `onConnect`.
- Received bytes arrive in the `data` member of the `onReceive` callback argument (`e.data` for `TcpReceiveEventArgs& e`); one event represents a read chunk, not an application message. Accumulate and separate messages in application code.
- `send()` waits for writing to finish or fail; use `sendAsync()` from frame callbacks to avoid waiting. Asynchronous sends own their payload and return a `SendResult`; completion is reported through `onSendComplete`.
- With threads enabled, connection, receive, and send events can run on their respective workers; immediate errors and explicit disconnection notifications can run on the caller. Use `listen(callback, Deliver::Main)` for listeners that access the Node tree, GPU resources, or unguarded application state; delivery from a worker copies the arguments for the next frame.
- `setUseThread(false)` makes network progress through an automatically registered update listener calling `processNetwork()`. Choose the mode before connecting; changing it while running is refused.
- TCP workers retain connection state until they finish. Inline listeners may disconnect, call `connectAsync()` from a receive callback, or destroy the client, including from a connect callback; teardown joins from another thread and requests shutdown without waiting for itself on a worker. Restarting uses fresh state; derived transports have their own teardown contracts.
- Simultaneous reentrant connection management is unsupported. In particular, do not launch `connectAsync()` from the local-disconnect notification produced inside another `connect()`; that outer call takes precedence over a connection opened by its disconnect listener.
- Explicit `disconnect()` reports `"Disconnected by client"` synchronously when connected; destruction disconnects without that notification. An automatic reconnect listener should distinguish this local request from a remote close or connection error.
- Copying is disabled. Only stopped state is moved; moving a running client first disconnects it and logs one Error, `"moved while running; stopped"`. Event listeners remain with the original handle.
- See `EventListener` for subscription lifetime; do not hold a listener's lock while joining its worker from another thread.

## TcpClient::connect

- `host` is an IPv4 address or hostname, and `port` is the server port number; hostname resolution is synchronous, and only the first resolved IPv4 address is tried.
- With threading enabled, waits for TCP connection success or failure; returns `false` on failure and reports the error through `onError`.
- With threading disabled, may return `true` while the TCP connection is still pending; use `isConnected()` or `onConnect` to check completion, which `processNetwork()` advances automatically through the update event.
- An existing connection is disconnected before the new attempt; see `onDisconnect` for the behavior of listeners that reconnect during this call.
- TCP deadlines are described in `TcpClient::setConnectTimeout`; with `TlsClient`, the TLS handshake continues separately, so wait for `onConnect` before sending.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    TcpClient client;
    client.setConnectTimeout(5);
    if (client.connect("127.0.0.1", 9000)) {
        client.send("hello\n");
    }
}
```

## TcpClient::connectAsync

- Starts connecting to `host` and `port` and reports the result through `onConnect`; the argument meanings are described in `TcpClient::connect`.
- While `isConnecting()` is true, repeating the identical host string and port does nothing and produces no warning; a different target replaces the pending attempt.
- With threading enabled, connection setup runs on a worker; without threads, DNS resolution and initial setup run on the caller, and pending connection and send work advances through `processNetwork()` on the update event.
- TCP sockets remain non-blocking, and connection waits use polling slices of at most 100 milliseconds; changing the target, calling `disconnect()`, or destroying the client cancels the old TCP wait before teardown waits for its workers.
- DNS resolution and user listeners can still delay teardown; the default TCP deadline is the operating system deadline, and `TcpClient::setConnectTimeout` can shorten it.
- Event delivery rules are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`, and worker lifetime rules are described in `TcpClient`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpClient client;
void tcApp::setup() {
    client.setConnectTimeout(5);
    client.connectAsync("127.0.0.1", 9000);
}
```

## TcpClient::disconnect

- Cancels a pending connection attempt, closes the socket, stops automatic update processing, and cancels unfinished sends.
- If the client was connected, reports `onDisconnect` with `reason == "Disconnected by client"` and `wasClean == true`; cancelling an attempt that has not connected does not produce this notification.
- Pending sends complete with `SendError::Disconnected` while the client remains alive; destruction instead suppresses new events.
- Worker lifetime and teardown rules are described in `TcpClient`; cancellation limits are described in `TcpClient::connectAsync`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpClient client;
void tcApp::exit() {
    client.disconnect();
}
```

## TcpClient::getRemoteHost

- Returns a copy of the host string recorded when socket connection setup begins, rather than a resolved peer address; an asynchronous worker may not have recorded its new target yet.
- Initially returns an empty string; the recorded value remains after connection failure or disconnection and does not indicate whether the client is connected.

## TcpClient::getRemotePort

- Returns the port recorded when socket connection setup begins; an asynchronous worker may not have recorded its new target yet.
- Initially returns `0`; the recorded value remains after connection failure or disconnection and does not indicate whether the client is connected.

## TcpClient::isConnected

- Returns the recorded connection flag without probing the peer; pending TCP connections return `false`, and `TlsClient` becomes connected only after its TLS handshake succeeds.
- A peer closure is reflected after network processing detects it.

## TcpClient::isUsingThread

- Returns the configured threading mode, even when no connection or worker is active; defaults and event delivery rules are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`.

## TcpClient::onConnect

- Receives `TcpConnectEventArgs`; `success` is `true` when the connection is ready, after the TLS handshake for `TlsClient`, and `message` describes the result.
- Failed asynchronous attempts, failed pending connections processed without threads, and failed TLS handshakes report `success == false`; a failed blocking TCP `connect()` returns `false` instead.
- An attempt replaced by a newer attempt does not report failure; if an `onError` listener starts a new connection, the old attempt stops reporting once that replacement is connected or connecting.
- The old `connect()` still returns `false` for its own failure even if `isConnected()` is already `true` for the replacement connection.
- Event delivery rules are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`, and listener teardown rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## TcpClient::onDisconnect

- Receives `TcpDisconnectEventArgs`; inspect `reason` and `wasClean` to distinguish the following cases.
- `"Connection closed by remote"` has `wasClean == true` and is reported by the receive worker when the peer closes the connection.
- `"Connection error"` has `wasClean == false` and is reported by the receive worker for a receive error; `TlsClient` uses `"TLS error: ..."` instead.
- `"Send failed"` has `wasClean == false` and is reported for a write failure or send timeout on the writer thread, or inline without threads; a replacement connection started by the preceding error listener can suppress this notification.
- `"Disconnected by client"` has `wasClean == true` and is reported synchronously on the calling thread by `disconnect()` or by `connect()` replacing an established connection.
- Without threads, receive notifications normally run from the update event on the main thread; destruction does not emit this event. For delivery options, see `TcpClient::setUseThread`.
- An automatic reconnect listener should ignore `e.reason == "Disconnected by client"` and schedule reconnection from the main thread.
- If `connect()` causes this event, a connection opened by the listener through `connect()` is closed without another disconnect notification, and the outer call proceeds to its requested target; without threads, a listener's `connectAsync()` is also overruled. Starting threaded `connectAsync()` from this particular listener is unsupported because connection management would overlap.
- Inline TCP listeners may reconnect, disconnect, or destroy the client; worker lifetime rules are described in `TcpClient`. Do not hold a lock needed by a listener while waiting for its worker, or manage connections from another thread before the listener's connection operation returns; derived transports have their own teardown rules.

## TcpClient::onError

- Receives `TcpErrorEventArgs` with a descriptive `message` and `errorCode`; errors without an explicit code use `0`.
- Connection setup errors, rejected sends, write failures, and send timeouts can produce this event; plain TCP receive errors are reported through `onDisconnect` instead.
- Immediate send rejection runs the error listener on the calling thread, so retrying a rejected send directly from that listener can recurse.
- General event delivery rules are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`, and listener teardown rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## TcpClient::onReceive

- Receives `TcpReceiveEventArgs`; `data` contains the bytes from one successful read, with no added null terminator.
- TCP does not preserve individual send boundaries, so accumulate or split the received bytes according to the application's message format.
- `TcpClient::setReceiveBufferSize` limits each read; copy `data` if it must remain available after the listener returns.
- Event delivery rules are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`, and listener teardown rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## TcpClient::send

- Accepts a pointer and byte count, a `vector<char>`, or a `string`; sends the exact byte count without adding a terminator or newline.
- Uses the same FIFO queue as `sendAsync()` and borrows the caller's bytes until this call returns; keep them valid and unchanged during the call.
- Returns `true` when the entire payload has been written to the transport, without confirming receipt by the remote application; returns `false` if disconnected, cancelled, or a write fails.
- Waits for queue space when the configured high-water mark is reached; send timeout behavior is described in `TcpClient::setSendTimeout`, and a write failure or timeout closes the connection and reports `onError`.
- With `TlsClient`, uses the same queue and timeout through TLS writes.
- Use `sendAsync()` from frame callbacks and main-thread listeners to avoid waiting; `send()` returns `false` when called inline on its own writer thread or while a non-threaded send queue is already being drained.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    TcpClient client;
    if (client.connect("127.0.0.1", 9000)) {
        client.send("hello\n");
    }
}
```

## TcpClient::setBlocking

- `false` applies non-blocking mode to an existing socket; if no socket exists, the call does nothing and does not save a setting.
- `true` is ignored with a warning when a socket exists, because owned sockets remain non-blocking so connection, receive, and send work can be cancelled.
- This setting does not make `connect()` or `send()` return immediately; those functions can wait around non-blocking socket operations.

## TcpClient::setReceiveBufferSize

- `size` is the receive buffer size in bytes, initially `65536`; each read receives at most this many bytes, and remaining stream data is read later.
- Stores the value unchanged and resizes the client-side buffer on a subsequent receive pass; it does not configure the operating system socket buffer.
- Limits each receive allocation rather than the total stream size; without threads, each network-processing call delivers at most one successful receive chunk.

## TcpClient::setUseThread

- Configure the mode before connecting; a change while the client is running is ignored with a warning.
- Defaults to `true` on native platforms and `false` on Emscripten; requesting `true` on Emscripten is rejected with a warning.
- With threads enabled, network events can run on connection, receive, or writer workers; synchronous calls and immediate errors can also notify on their calling thread. Plain `listen(...)` runs inline on whichever thread emits the event.
- With threads disabled, automatic network processing runs through the update event, normally on the main thread; manual processing and synchronous operations notify on their calling thread.
- For listeners that access the Node tree, GPU resources, or app state owned by the main thread, use `listen(callback, Deliver::Main)` and retain the returned `EventListener`; delivery from a worker copies the event arguments and queues the callback for the main thread, while delivery already on the main thread runs immediately.
- Worker lifetime, listener-triggered teardown, and restart rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## TcpClientConnectEventArgs

- `TcpServer::onClientConnect` supplies the server-assigned `clientId`, the client's IP address in `host`, and its source port in `port`.
- TCP server listeners run on the thread that fires the event: acceptance uses the accept thread, received data uses the client's receive thread, and queued send failures use its writer thread. Errors from public calls can run on the calling thread.
- Use `listen(fn, Deliver::Main)` before accessing the Node tree, GPU resources, or app state shared with the main thread. Delivery from a worker copies the arguments and queues the listener for the main thread; retain the returned `EventListener` to keep it registered.
- Event argument references are valid during the callback. Copy any fields that must remain available afterward.

## TcpClientConnectEventArgs::clientId

- This server-assigned `int` identifies the connection in calls such as `TcpServer::send()` and `TcpServer::disconnectClient()`.

## TcpClientConnectEventArgs::host

- Contains the peer's numeric IPv4 address as a `string`, rather than a hostname.

## TcpClientConnectEventArgs::port

- Contains the peer's source port as an `int` in host byte order; this is distinct from the server's listening port.

## TcpClientDisconnectEventArgs

- `TcpServer::onClientDisconnect` supplies `clientId`, a diagnostic `reason`, and `wasClean`, which distinguishes a normal peer closure from an error.
- A peer closure reports `"Connection closed by client"` with `wasClean = true`; receive errors report `"Connection error"` with `wasClean = false`. Failure to start a receive thread also reports `wasClean = false`.
- Explicit `disconnectClient()`, `disconnectAllClients()`, and `stop()` do not themselves emit this event. See `TcpClientConnectEventArgs` for threading and argument lifetime.

## TcpClientDisconnectEventArgs::clientId

- Contains the same server-assigned `int` ID that identified this connection in `TcpClientConnectEventArgs::clientId`.

## TcpClientDisconnectEventArgs::reason

- Contains `"Connection closed by client"` for a peer close, `"Connection error"` for a receive or readiness error, or `"Could not start a receive thread"` when starting the receive thread fails.
- `TcpServer::disconnectClient()` and `TcpServer::disconnectAllClients()` do not emit this event themselves.

## TcpClientDisconnectEventArgs::wasClean

- Is `true` when receiving detects that the peer closed the connection, and `false` for a connection error or failure to start the receive thread.

## TcpConnectEventArgs

- `TcpClient::onConnect` supplies `success` and a diagnostic `message`. Successful TCP connections report `true` and `"Connected"`; reported failures use `false` and `"Connection failed"`.
- A failed blocking TCP `connect()` returns `false` without emitting `onConnect(false)`. Asynchronous or pending attempts can emit a failure event; cancelled or replaced attempts can finish without one.
- Plain listeners run on the notifying thread: blocking connection results use the caller; `connectAsync()` attempts use the connect thread when threading is enabled and the caller otherwise. Pending connection completion is reported during receive processing, which runs on the receive thread with threading enabled or through the update event without it.
- Use `listen(fn, Deliver::Main)` before accessing the Node tree, GPU resources, or app state shared with the main thread. Delivery from a worker copies the arguments and queues the listener for the main thread; retain the returned `EventListener` to keep it registered.
- Event argument references are valid during the callback. Copy any fields that must remain available afterward.

## TcpConnectEventArgs::message

- `TcpClient` sets this to `"Connected"` on success or `"Connection failed"` when it emits a failed connection result.
- Defaults to an empty `string`.

## TcpConnectEventArgs::success

- Is `true` for a successful connection notification and `false` for a failed connection notification; the default is `false`.
- See `TcpClient::onConnect` for when failed attempts emit this event.

## TcpDisconnectEventArgs

- `TcpClient::onDisconnect` supplies `reason` and `wasClean`. A remote closure reports `"Connection closed by remote"` with `true`; a receive error reports `"Connection error"` with `false`; a failed or timed-out send reports `"Send failed"` with `false`.
- An explicit local disconnection reports `"Disconnected by client"` with `wasClean = true` synchronously on the calling thread. Connecting again while connected also closes the old connection this way; destruction does not emit this event.
- Automatic reconnection code should distinguish a remote closure from `"Disconnected by client"`. See `TcpConnectEventArgs` for threading and argument lifetime.

## TcpDisconnectEventArgs::reason

- `TcpClient` reports `"Connection closed by remote"` when the peer closes the connection, `"Connection error"` for a receive error, and `"Send failed"` for a send failure or timeout.
- An explicit `disconnect()`, or `connect()` replacing an existing connection, reports `"Disconnected by client"`; destruction does not emit this event.
- Defaults to an empty `string`; see `TcpClient::onDisconnect` for listener threading and reconnection rules.

## TcpDisconnectEventArgs::wasClean

- `TcpClient` sets this to `true` for a peer close or an explicit local disconnection, and `false` for a receive error, send failure, or send timeout.
- Defaults to `true`; see `TcpDisconnectEventArgs::reason` for the corresponding messages.

## TcpErrorEventArgs

- `TcpClient::onError` supplies a diagnostic `message` and an integer `errorCode`. The code is `0` when no specific code is supplied.
- Errors are notified on the thread where they occur, including the caller of a rejected send or a connection attempt and the writer thread for queued send failures. See `TcpConnectEventArgs` for main-thread delivery and argument lifetime.

## TcpErrorEventArgs::errorCode

- Contains the `int` code supplied by the failed operation, such as a socket operation or hostname lookup; codes are not converted to a common TrussC error enumeration.
- Is `0` when no code is supplied, including errors such as `"Not connected"` or `"Send queue full"`; the default is also `0`.

## TcpErrorEventArgs::message

- Contains a `string` describing the failed operation, such as `"Not connected"`, `"Send queue full"`, or `"Send timed out; client disconnected"`.
- Defaults to an empty `string`; a message can be present even when `errorCode` is `0`.

## TcpReceiveEventArgs

- `TcpClient::onReceive` supplies the received bytes in `vector<char> data`; use `data.size()` for the byte count. A terminating null character is not added.
- Each event contains one receive chunk, which can split a sent message or combine several messages. Accumulate and separate messages according to your protocol.
- See `TcpConnectEventArgs` for threading and argument lifetime.

## TcpReceiveEventArgs::data

- Contains a `vector<char>` with exactly the bytes returned by one receive operation; no null terminator is appended and no message framing is performed.
- Copy the vector if its contents are needed after the listener returns.
- See `TcpClient` for listener threading rules.

## SendError

- `None` means that a `SendResult` accepted the payload into the queue, or that a completion handed the entire payload to the kernel; it does not confirm receipt by the remote application.
- `ClientNotFound` means that the server has no client registered under the requested ID; `NotRunning` means that the server is stopped or the client is not connected.
- `QueueFull` means that pending bytes have already reached the configured queue high-water mark; this is not a per-message size limit.
- `Disconnected` reports a cancelled or failed write, including queued sends cancelled by disconnection.
- `Timeout` is reported by `TcpServer` when the send timeout expires without writing any payload bytes, leaving the connection open; a server timeout after a partial write drops the client and reports `Disconnected`, and `TcpClient` send timeouts close the connection and report `Disconnected`.

## SendResult

- `sendAsync()` returns `error == SendError::None` and a nonzero `id` when it queues the payload; a rejected request returns the reason in `error` and an `id` of `0`.
- As with `LoadResult`, an explicit Boolean conversion supports `if (result)` and returns the same value as `result.ok()`; it tests `error`, not `id`.
- Acceptance into the queue does not mean that transmission has completed; match `id` with `TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::sendId` to identify the completion.
- A default-constructed result has `error == SendError::None` and `id == 0`, so it evaluates to `true` without representing a queued send.

## SendResult::error

- Is `SendError::None` when `sendAsync()` accepts the payload, or the reason the request was rejected; the default is `SendError::None`.
- Describes queue acceptance rather than the final transmission outcome; see `SendResult`.

## SendResult::id

- `sendAsync()` returns a nonzero `uint64_t` ID when it queues the payload and `0` when it rejects the request; the default is `0`.
- The completion reports the same value in `TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::sendId`.

## SendResult::ok

- Returns `error == SendError::None`, the same test used by the explicit Boolean conversion.
- Does not inspect `id`, so a default-constructed `SendResult` returns `true`; see `SendResult` for queue acceptance semantics.

## sendErrorName

- Returns a string literal as `const char*`: `"None"`, `"ClientNotFound"`, `"Disconnected"`, `"Timeout"`, `"QueueFull"`, or `"NotRunning"`, matching the `SendError` enumerator.
- Returns `"Unknown"` for an unrecognized value. The labels are suitable for log messages.

## TcpSendCompleteEventArgs

- Match `sendId` with the `SendResult::id` returned when the payload was queued; `error` and `bytesSent` describe its final outcome.
- While the sender exists, each accepted send completes exactly once, including queued sends cancelled by disconnection or server shutdown; cancelled sends that never started report `SendError::Disconnected` and zero bytes.
- Blocking `send()` calls also produce completion events because they use the same queue.
- Success means that the entire payload reached the kernel; it does not confirm receipt by the remote application.
- Server listeners run on that client's writer thread, and threaded client listeners run on the client's writer thread; without client threads, they run on the thread processing the send queue, including during update processing, blocking sends, or disconnection.
- Default listeners run inline; use `listen(callback, Deliver::Main)` for main-thread delivery, which copies the arguments and runs at the start of the next frame when called from a worker, or immediately when already on the main thread.
- Keep the returned `EventListener` alive to receive callbacks; copy any arguments needed after a callback returns, and note that destroying the sender or listener can prevent subsequent callbacks.

## TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::clientId

- Contains the server-assigned client ID for `TcpServer` completions, or `-1` for `TcpClient` completions; the default is `-1`.

## TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::sendId

- Contains the `uint64_t` ID assigned when this payload was queued, matching `SendResult::id` for an asynchronous request; the default is `0`.
- See `TcpSendCompleteEventArgs` for completion delivery rules.

## TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::error

- Is `SendError::None` when the whole payload reached the kernel, or a failure value otherwise; the default is `SendError::None`.
- See `SendError` for the distinction between `Timeout` and `Disconnected`, including differences between server and client sends.

## TcpSendCompleteEventArgs::bytesSent

- Contains a `size_t` count of payload bytes accepted by the send operations, rather than bytes confirmed received by the remote application.
- Equals the payload size on success and can be partial or zero on failure; sends cancelled before writing report `0`, which is also the default.

## TcpServer

- `start(port, maxClients)` listens on all IPv4 interfaces and returns whether startup succeeded. Port `0` lets the OS choose a port, available through `getPort()`; the default client limit is 64; explicit nonpositive limits are configuration errors.
- A connection accepted while the client limit is reached is closed immediately. Connected clients have IDs for `send()`, `sendAsync()`, and disconnection; `broadcast()` and `broadcastAsync()` target the connected clients.
- `send()` and `broadcast()` wait for writes; use their asynchronous counterparts from frame callbacks. Queued sends report completion through `onSendComplete`. The TCP byte-stream and `Deliver::Main` rules are explained under `TcpClient`. Inside a callback running on a server send thread (for example `onSendComplete` or `onError`), a synchronous send or broadcast does not wait for the server-wide send buffer (`setTotalSendBufferSize`) and fails at once when it is full; it still waits for room in the destination client's own queue.
- The server always uses workers: `onClientConnect` normally runs on the accept thread, `onReceive` on a client's receive thread, and `onSendComplete` on its writer thread. Error and disconnect callbacks can also run on the thread performing the operation.
- `stop()` clears the running state, disconnects clients, and joins workers when called from another thread. Destruction also stops the server; workers retain their state until they return.
- Inline worker listeners may call `stop()`, `disconnectClient()`, or `disconnectAllClients()` without waiting for server threads. On the accept thread, `stop()` closes the listening socket immediately and disconnects clients after the listener returns; other worker calls disconnect the relevant clients before returning.
- Workers left running by such callbacks are joined later, including by `stop()`, `start()`, or destruction on another thread. `start()` from a server worker logs an error and returns `false`; elsewhere it stops the old session and waits for teardown before restarting.
- Keep event subscriptions alive as described under `EventListener`, and use main-thread delivery for listeners that touch the scene or GPU.

## TcpServer::broadcast

- Accepts a pointer and byte count, `vector<char>`, or `string`. The payload is borrowed until this call returns; see `TcpServer::send` for the byte format.
- Takes a snapshot of the clients, queues the payload for each client, and then waits for all accepted sends to finish or fail. A full client queue can block the queuing pass before later clients are reached. Inside a callback running on a server send thread (for example `onSendComplete` or `onError`), a synchronous send or broadcast does not wait for the server-wide send buffer (`setTotalSendBufferSize`) and fails at once when it is full; it still waits for room in the destination client's own queue.
- Returns no result. Calling it from a client's own writer thread silently skips that client.
- See `TcpServer::setSendTimeout` for timeout behavior. Use `TcpServer::broadcastAsync` in frame callbacks to avoid waiting for network writes.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpServer server;
void tcApp::update() {
    server.broadcast("hello\n");
}
```

## TcpServer::broadcastAsync

- Accepts a pointer and byte count, `vector<char>`, or `string`, and returns without waiting for network writes. The payload is copied once and shared by all client queues.
- Returns the number of clients that accepted the payload, or 0 if the server is not running. Clients whose queues are full or closed are skipped without an `onError` notification, so the count can be smaller than `getClientCount()`.
- Each accepted send produces an `onSendComplete` event. See `TcpServer::sendAsync` for send ordering and `TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize` for queue limits.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpServer server;
void tcApp::update() {
    server.broadcastAsync("hello\n");
}
```

## TcpServer::disconnectAllClients

- Disconnects the clients in the current snapshot while leaving the server listening. A client that connects during this call can remain connected.
- Waiting for client threads and completing pending sends follow the rules in `TcpServer::disconnectClient`. On a thread outside the server, this also joins remaining threads of clients already removed from the registry.

## TcpServer::disconnectClient

- Removes `clientId` from the connected clients and shuts down its connection. An unknown ID does not create an error notification.
- Pending sends still complete: queued payloads that have not started report `SendError::Disconnected`, and an interrupted write can report a partial `bytesSent`. This call does not itself emit `onClientDisconnect`.
- On a thread outside the server, waits for that client's receive and writer threads that it takes ownership of. The writer finishes completion notifications for pending sends before exiting.
- An inline listener on any of this server's accept, receive, or writer threads can disconnect its own client or another client without waiting for any server thread. Finished threads are joined later while the server runs, or by `stop()`, `start()`, or destruction on another thread.

## TcpServer::getClient

- Returns a `const TcpServerClient*` for `clientId`, or `nullptr` if the client is not registered.
- The server owns the object; removing the client or destroying the server invalidates the pointer and references obtained from it. The lookup lock is released before return, so dereferencing the pointer requires ensuring that no other thread removes the client. Connection events provide copied host and port values when those are sufficient.

## TcpServer::getClientCount

- Returns the current number of registered clients as an `int`, or 0 when none are registered.
- The count is read under a lock, but connections and disconnections can change it immediately after return.

## TcpServer::getClientIds

- Returns a copied `vector<int>` containing the currently registered client IDs, or an empty vector if none are registered. The order is unspecified.
- Clients can disconnect after the snapshot is taken, so a later lookup or send using an ID can fail.

## TcpServer::getPort

- After a successful `start(port)`, returns the bound port as an `int`. After `start(0)`, returns the port selected by the operating system.
- The initial value is 0. `stop()` does not reset it, so use `isRunning()` to check whether the server is listening.

## TcpServer::getSendAsyncBufferSize

- Returns the current per-client threshold in bytes as a `size_t`.
- The default is `16 * 1024 * 1024` bytes. See `TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize` for admission rules and overshoot behavior.

## TcpServer::getSendAsyncPendingBytes

- Returns the total payload bytes accepted but not yet completed for `clientId`, including the payload currently being written. Returns 0 for an unknown client.
- The count decreases by the whole payload size when that send completes, rather than after each partial write. Compare it with `getSendAsyncBufferSize()` to monitor queue pressure; see `TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize` for the threshold rules.
- To estimate pending bytes across all clients, iterate `server.getClientIds()` and sum `server.getSendAsyncPendingBytes(id)`; the counts can change between calls.

## TcpServer::isRunning

- Returns the server's atomic running flag. `stop()` clears it before waiting for shutdown, so `false` does not mean that all worker threads have already ended.

## TcpServer::onClientConnect

- Delivers `TcpClientConnectEventArgs` containing `clientId`, the client's IP address in `host`, and its source `port`.
- Fires on the accept thread after the client and its writer are registered, before its receive thread starts. An inline listener can send a greeting here; a later failure to start receiving can still disconnect the client.
- See `TcpServer::onReceive` for shared event delivery and listener lifetime rules, and `TcpServer::start` and `TcpServer::stop` for lifecycle calls from listeners.

## TcpServer::onClientDisconnect

- Delivers `TcpClientDisconnectEventArgs` with `clientId`, `reason`, and `wasClean`. A receive result of 0 sets `wasClean` to `true`; receive errors or failure to start the receive thread set it to `false`.
- Receive-side notifications fire on the client's receive thread before it removes the client. If the receive thread cannot start, the accept thread removes the client first and then emits the event.
- `disconnectClient()`, `disconnectAllClients()`, and `stop()` do not themselves emit this event, so it is not a notification for every removal.
- See `TcpServer::onReceive` for shared event delivery and listener lifetime rules.

## TcpServer::onError

- Delivers `TcpServerErrorEventArgs` containing `message`, `errorCode`, and `clientId`. A `clientId` of -1 identifies a server-level error; `errorCode` can be 0 when no operating-system error code is supplied.
- Startup failures and rejected `send()` or `sendAsync()` calls notify on the calling thread. Queued write failures notify on that client's writer thread. `sendAsync()` returning `NotRunning` and clients skipped by `broadcastAsync()` do not notify this event.
- Connection-wait, accept, and new-client thread-start failures notify on the accept thread, at most once every 5 seconds for each failure kind while it persists. Logs count suppressed occurrences, and retries use a short back-off.
- An inline accept-thread listener may call `stop()` but cannot call `start()`. See those entries for shutdown timing, and `TcpServer::onReceive` for shared delivery and listener lifetime rules.

## TcpServer::onReceive

- Delivers `TcpServerReceiveEventArgs` with `clientId` and a `vector<char>` named `data`, containing the bytes from one successful read. TCP does not preserve send boundaries; assemble messages across events or split combined messages as needed.
- Fires on that client's receive thread. Across server events, plain `listen(fn)` runs inline on the firing thread, and callbacks for different clients can run concurrently.
- For Node, GPU, or unguarded application state, use `listen(fn, Deliver::Main)`. Worker-thread events copy their arguments for delivery at the start of a subsequent frame; events already fired on the main thread run immediately.
- Keep the returned `EventListener` alive, usually as a member. Removing the listener or destroying the server cancels pending main-thread callbacks; it does not wait for a callback already executing, so synchronize destruction of state used by that callback.
- Event argument references are valid only during the callback. Copy data that must outlive it. See `TcpServer::start`, `TcpServer::stop`, and `TcpServer::disconnectClient` for lifecycle calls from inline listeners.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    TcpServer server;
    EventListener receiveListener;
    void setup() override {
        receiveListener = server.onReceive.listen([](TcpServerReceiveEventArgs& e) { logNotice() << e.data.size(); }, Deliver::Main);
        server.start(9001);
    }
};
```

## TcpServer::onSendComplete

- Delivers `TcpSendCompleteEventArgs` containing `clientId`, `sendId`, `error`, and `bytesSent`. `SendError::None` means the entire payload reached the kernel; failures can report a partial byte count.
- Each accepted send completes once, including sends pending during disconnection or `stop()`. This also covers accepted `send()`, `broadcast()`, and `broadcastAsync()` payloads; rejected queue submissions have no completion.
- Fires on the client's writer thread. A synchronous sender is released before listeners run, so `send()` can return before its completion listener finishes.
- See `TcpServer::onReceive` for shared delivery and listener lifetime rules, including cancellation during server destruction.

## TcpServer::send

- Accepts `clientId` followed by a pointer and byte count, `vector<char>`, or `string`. Sends the supplied bytes without adding a terminator or message framing; a string sends `message.size()` bytes.
- Borrows the payload without copying it and waits until the write completes or fails. Keep the data unchanged until return. Returns `true` when the whole payload reaches the kernel, or `false` on failure; success does not confirm processing by the peer application. Inside a callback running on a server send thread (for example `onSendComplete` or `onError`), a synchronous send or broadcast does not wait for the server-wide send buffer (`setTotalSendBufferSize`) and fails at once when it is full; it still waits for room in the destination client's own queue.
- Shares the client's queue and send ordering with `sendAsync()`. A slow peer blocks this call without blocking other clients' writers or the accept loop; use `sendAsync()` in frame callbacks.
- An unknown client, a closed connection, or a call from that client's own writer-thread listener returns `false` and reports `onError`. Use `sendAsync()` from that writer thread.
- See `TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize` for waiting on a full queue and `TcpServer::setSendTimeout` for write timeouts.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpServer server;
void tcApp::update() {
    for (int id : server.getClientIds()) {
        server.send(id, "hello\n");
    }
}
```

## TcpServer::sendAsync

- Returns without waiting for network writes. The pointer-and-byte-count and `string` overloads copy the payload; the `vector<char>&&` overload takes ownership by moving it. Byte format follows `TcpServer::send`.
- A successful `SendResult` has a nonzero `id` matched by `onSendComplete`. A false result means nothing was queued, with `error` set to `NotRunning`, `ClientNotFound`, `Disconnected`, or `QueueFull`.
- On a running server, an unknown `clientId` returns `SendResult{SendError::ClientNotFound, 0}`, which evaluates to false, and emits `onError` with the message `"Client not found"`.
- A full queue returns `QueueFull` without disconnecting the client. See `TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize` for the threshold rules and `TcpServer::onError` for error notifications.
- Each client has a writer thread that processes accepted sends in queue order, including synchronous sends. Calls from different threads are ordered when they enter the queue.
- Use this from frame callbacks when a slow peer must not make the frame wait. See `TcpServer::onSendComplete` for completion and `TcpServer::setSendTimeout` for write timeouts.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpServer server;
void tcApp::update() {
    for (int id : server.getClientIds()) {
        auto result = server.sendAsync(id, "hello\n");
        if (!result) logWarning() << sendErrorName(result.error);
    }
}
```

## TcpServer::setSendTimeout

- Sets the allowed time without write progress in seconds for all clients. The default is 60 seconds; 0 disables the timeout, and negative values are stored as 0.
- The writer reads the setting when it starts each payload. The inactivity timer restarts whenever bytes are accepted, so a continuously progressing send can take longer than the timeout.
- Time spent waiting in the queue or waiting for queue space is not included. This is not a limit on the total duration of `send()` or `broadcast()`.
- A timeout before any bytes are written reports `SendError::Timeout` and keeps the connection open. A timeout after a partial write shuts down the connection and reports `SendError::Disconnected`, preventing a later payload from continuing a truncated stream.

## TcpServer::setSendAsyncBufferSize

- Default: 16 MiB. Zero logs a configuration Error and leaves the setting unchanged (v0.8 change).
- Bound (security): slow peers retain sends; a finite item bounds one-item overshoot. Overflow rejects whole async sends (sync sends wait) and is counted. Inside a callback running on a server send thread (for example `onSendComplete` or `onError`), a synchronous send or broadcast does not wait for the server-wide send buffer (`setTotalSendBufferSize`) and fails at once when it is full; it still waits for room in the destination client's own queue.
- Pending bytes include queued and executing sync/async sends. An item may cross the mark; later async sends return `QueueFull` and broadcast skips that client. Owned items also obey `setSendItemLimit()` and `setTotalSendBufferSize()`.
- Each channel admits at most 4096 pending entries, including empty sends. Each bound warns once and counts rejections for the server object's lifetime. A rejection does not disconnect the client.
- Changes preserve existing sends and wake waiting sync senders. Borrowed sync sends do not copy payloads; large transfers use finite write windows. See `setSendTimeout()` for idle timeouts.

## TcpServer::setSendItemLimit

- Default: 16 MiB. Zero logs a configuration Error and keeps the previous value. Changes apply to subsequent admissions without discarding pending sends.
- Bound (security): bulk owned sends need a finite pre-copy budget. Overflow rejects the whole send with `QueueFull` and is counted.
- Checked before copying or moving data, including a moved vector's capacity. Broadcast checks each recipient before fanout and copies its payload only after the first admission. The high-water mark and aggregate credits also apply.
- One Warning per bound and cumulative internal rejection totals last for the server object's lifetime, across stop/start. No public statistics API is added. Borrowed synchronous sends use finite credit windows instead of owning the whole payload.

## TcpServer::setTotalSendBufferSize

- Default: 64 MiB. Zero logs a configuration Error and preserves the setting. Lowering the limit preserves existing sends; admissions wait or fail until credits fit again.
- Bound (security): slow peers must not multiply retained sends across clients. Overflow rejects whole async sends (sync sends wait except in send-thread callbacks) and is counted. Inside a callback running on a server send thread (for example `onSendComplete` or `onError`), a synchronous send or broadcast does not wait for the server-wide send buffer (`setTotalSendBufferSize`) and fails at once when it is full; it still waits for room in the destination client's own queue.
- Reserve before copying/moving data or broadcast fanout. Every recipient consumes credits, even when sharing one payload. Shared storage retains its original credit until its last reference is released. Borrowed sync sends charge a finite window bounded by the item and aggregate limits.
- Completion, failure, cancellation and disconnect release credits. Each bound warns once with cumulative internal rejection totals for the server object's lifetime. Changes wake waiting synchronous senders.

## TcpServer::setReceiveBufferSize

- Sets the maximum bytes requested in one read, with a default of 65536 bytes. Additional data remains for subsequent reads; this does not define message boundaries.
- Each client's receive thread allocates its buffer once at startup, so changing this setting does not resize existing buffers. Configure it before `start()` to avoid concurrent access to the setting.
- Stores the supplied size without validation or clamping, including 0.

## TcpServer::start

- `start(port, maxClients = 64)` listens on all local IPv4 interfaces. Pass 0 for `port` to let the operating system select one, then read it with `getPort()`.
- Returns `true` when listening and the accept thread have started. Socket, bind, listen, bound-port lookup, or accept-thread startup failures return `false` and notify `onError`.
- Bound (security): finite connection slots bound per-client channels and workers, including closed workers still in callbacks. Overflow closes new sockets before channel/thread creation and is counted. One Warning and cumulative internal totals last for the server object's lifetime. The default is 64; nonpositive values log an Error, notify `onError`, and return `false` without stopping a running server (v0.8 change). Slots free when workers return.
- The listen backlog is 128, subject to operating-system limits, and is independent of `maxClients`. Finished client threads are joined while running, and persistent accept failures use short delays before retrying.
- Calls `stop()` first and waits for any concurrent stop teardown to finish before starting a new session. See `TcpServer::stop` for shutdown and lifetime rules.
- Cannot restart from an inline listener on this server's accept, receive, or writer thread: logs an error and returns `false` without stopping the server. Use main-thread delivery when restarting from a listener.
- Uses `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX systems and `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` on Windows when configuring the listening socket.

```cpp
class tcApp : public App {
    TcpServer server;
    void setup() override {
        if (!server.start(9001, 8)) {
            logError() << "Could not start TCP server";
        }
    }
};
```

## TcpServer::stop

- Clears `isRunning()` immediately and requests shutdown of listening and client connections. Calling it again is allowed.
- On a thread outside the server, normally returns after the accept and client threads have ended. With concurrent calls, only one caller takes and waits for the accept thread; another call does not wait for that caller's remaining teardown. `start()` waits for all such teardown to finish.
- From an inline listener on this server's accept, receive, or writer thread, waits for no server thread. On a receive or writer thread it disconnects all clients before returning; on the accept thread it closes the listening socket and leaves client disconnection until the listener returns.
- Threads left by a listener's stop are joined by a later `stop()` or `start()` on another thread, or during destruction. See `TcpServer::disconnectClient` for pending-send completion behavior.
- Destruction closes event delivery and uses the same shutdown rules. If destruction occurs on a server thread, the shared server state remains alive until its workers return. See `TcpServer::onReceive` for listener and callback lifetime rules.

```cpp
// tcApp member: TcpServer server;
void tcApp::cleanup() {
    server.stop();
}
```

## TcpServerClient

- `getId()` returns the server-assigned client ID, `getHost()` returns its IP address, and `getPort()` returns its source port. Send data through `TcpServer` using the client ID.
- `TcpServer::getClient(clientId)` returns a borrowed pointer, or `nullptr` if the client is absent. Disconnection, server shutdown, or destruction invalidates the pointer.
- Clients can be removed on background threads. For stored peer information, retain the ID and copies of the connection event fields instead of retaining this pointer.

## TcpServerClient::getHost

- Returns the remote IPv4 address recorded when the connection was accepted, as a `const string&`.
- The reference shares the client object's lifetime. See `TcpServer::getClient` for ownership and concurrent-removal rules.

## TcpServerClient::getId

- Returns the assigned `int` ID. A server's IDs start at 1 and continue increasing across `stop()` and `start()` calls.
- See `TcpServer::getClient` for client object lifetime and concurrent-removal rules.

## TcpServerClient::getPort

- Returns the remote source port recorded when the connection was accepted, as an `int`. Use `TcpServer::getPort` for the server's listening port.
- See `TcpServer::getClient` for client object lifetime and concurrent-removal rules.

## TcpServerErrorEventArgs

- `TcpServer::onError` supplies a diagnostic `message`, an integer `errorCode`, and `clientId`. A `clientId` of `-1` identifies a server-level error; other values identify the affected client.
- `errorCode` is `0` when no specific code is supplied. See `TcpClientConnectEventArgs` for threading and argument lifetime.

## TcpServerErrorEventArgs::clientId

- This `int` contains the server-assigned client ID when the error concerns a specific client.
- The default value is `-1`, which indicates a server-level error without a specific client.

## TcpServerErrorEventArgs::errorCode

- For socket failures, this `int` contains a Winsock error code on Windows or an `errno` value on other platforms; thread creation failures use the exception's `code().value()`.
- The default value is `0`, which is also used for errors without a numeric code, such as an unknown client ID or a full send queue; it does not indicate success in this event.

## TcpServerErrorEventArgs::message

- This `string` contains a message supplied by TrussC describing the failed operation, such as `"Client not found"`; inspect it together with `errorCode` and `clientId`.

## TcpServerReceiveEventArgs

- `TcpServer::onReceive` supplies the sender's `clientId` and the received bytes in `vector<char> data`. Use `data.size()` for the byte count; a terminating null character is not added.
- Each event contains one receive chunk, which can split or combine application messages. Keep a separate receive buffer for each client when assembling messages.
- See `TcpClientConnectEventArgs` for threading and argument lifetime.

## TcpServerReceiveEventArgs::clientId

- This `int` contains the server-assigned ID of the sending client, matching its `TcpClientConnectEventArgs::clientId` and `TcpServerClient::getId()` value.
- Use it as the client ID argument to `TcpServer::send` or `TcpServer::sendAsync` to reply to that client.

## TcpServerReceiveEventArgs::data

- This `vector<char>` contains the bytes returned by one receive operation; `data.size()` is the byte count, and no null terminator is added.
- TCP message boundaries are not preserved: one send may span multiple events, and one event may contain bytes from multiple sends.
- Each receive uses a buffer whose default capacity is 65,536 bytes; `TcpServer::setReceiveBufferSize` sets the capacity used when a client's receive thread starts.

## TcyMode

- `Rotate` rotates a run clockwise by `QUARTER_TAU`, `Upright` places each glyph upright in its own cell, and `Combine` places the run horizontally in one cell, compressing its width only when necessary.
- Configure ASCII digit runs (`0`–`9`) with `Font::setTcyDigits(maxDigits, inMode, overflowMode)` and ASCII letter runs (`A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`) with `Font::setTcyLatin(mode)`. ASCII digit runs longer than `maxDigits` use `overflowMode`.
- The default digit limit is `0`, so all ASCII digit runs use the default overflow mode `Rotate`; the mode within the limit is `Combine`. ASCII letter runs also default to `Rotate`. These settings apply to `WritingMode::VerticalRL`.

## Texture

- Allocate a texture before drawing it or uploading data; see `Image` for the relationship between CPU pixels, textures, and images.
- Allocate, upload, draw, bind, change sampling settings, and release GPU resources on the main thread, including destruction of an allocated texture; use `runOnMainThread` when starting from a worker thread.
- GPU allocation requires initialized graphics; before graphics initialization and in headless applications, allocation leaves the texture unallocated and uploads and drawing do nothing.
- All windows share the GPU device, so the same texture can be used in multiple windows.
- Allocation creates GPU resources, and uploading transfers CPU data to the GPU; reusing an allocated texture avoids repeated allocation, and drawing does not read its pixels back to the CPU.
- Textures cannot be copied but can be moved; destruction calls `clear`, and released GPU resources remain alive while recorded drawing commands still reference them.

## Texture::allocate

- Replaces the previous allocation with storage sized in pixels, using dimensions or a `Pixels` buffer; the channel-count overload defaults to four channels.
- The `TextureFormat` overload selects the GPU format explicitly; the channel-count overload selects RGBA8 only for four channels and R8 for every other channel count, without converting the supplied data.
- Usage defaults to `TextureUsage::Immutable`; `allocate(pixels)` uploads its initial data, and later `loadData` calls cannot update it. The dimension-based overloads provide no initial data, so their default Immutable usage fails sokol validation.
- Choose `TextureUsage::Dynamic` for periodic uploads or `TextureUsage::Stream` for uploads every frame; both initially allocate empty storage, including when passed `Pixels`, so call `loadData` afterward. `TextureUsage::RenderTarget` creates attachment storage for off-screen rendering; see `Fbo::begin`.
- Floating-point `Pixels` select RGBA32F; other `Pixels` use the channel-count format selection. See `TextureFormat` for format and channel definitions.
- For `Pixels`, `mipmaps` defaults to `false`; Immutable generates the mip chain during allocation only for four-channel pixels, Dynamic regenerates it through `loadData(pixels)`, and Stream and RenderTarget ignore this option. Generated mip counts are limited to the GPU descriptor capacity.
- Dimension-based overloads default `sampleCount` to 1; for RenderTarget usage, values above 1 currently fail validation. Use `Fbo::allocate` for multisampling. The format overload also accepts `mipLevels`, defaults it to 1, clamps values below 1 to 1, and allocates the requested chain for RenderTarget usage; it does not generate mip contents.
- Returns no value; check `isAllocated` for success. Missing graphics initialization leaves it false; exceeding the device size limit or a recoverable GPU image creation failure logs an error and leaves it false. Validation errors terminate the process by default in validation-enabled builds. Requested dimensions and channel count remain stored.
- Filter, wrap, and premultiplied-alpha settings survive reallocation; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(1, 1);
    pixels.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
    texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() { texture.draw(20, 20, 256, 256); }
```

## Texture::allocateCubemap

- `allocateCubemap(sideSize, format, usage, mipLevels)` allocates six square faces without initial data; `sideSize` is the width and height of each face in pixels.
- `usage` defaults to `TextureUsage::RenderTarget`; render into individual faces with `getCubemapFaceAttachmentView()`, or select `Dynamic` or `Stream` and upload all six faces with `loadCubemapData()`.
- `mipLevels` includes the base level and defaults to `1`; values below `1` become `1`. RenderTarget supports multiple levels, but this call does not generate their contents.
- The existing texture is cleared first. `Immutable`, or `Dynamic` / `Stream` with more than one mip level, logs an error and leaves the texture unallocated.
- The sample count is set to `1`, and both U and V wrap modes are set to `ClampToEdge`.
- Without an initialized graphics device, the texture remains unallocated. Otherwise, this method marks it allocated after resource creation without checking whether sokol accepted the resources.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture cubemap;
void tcApp::setup() {
    cubemap.allocateCubemap(256, TextureFormat::RGBA16F,
                           TextureUsage::RenderTarget, 9);
}
```

## Texture::bind

- Enables texturing in the current sokol_gl drawing context and selects this texture and its sampler; an unallocated texture leaves the current state unchanged.
- Does not assign a custom shader texture slot; use `Shader::setTexture` for that purpose.
- Call `unbind` to disable texturing afterward; it does not restore the previous texture. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Texture::clear

- Releases the allocation and resets width, height, and channel count to 0; `isAllocated` becomes false, and the mip count returns to 1.
- Preserves filter, wrap, premultiplied-alpha, usage, and sample-count settings; this releases storage rather than filling it with a color.
- May be called repeatedly; GPU destruction is deferred while recorded draws still reference the resources. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (pixels.load("image.png")) texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::exit() {
    texture.clear();
}
```

## Texture::draw

- `draw(x, y)` draws the whole texture at its pixel width and height; `draw(x, y, w, h)` stretches it to the requested size without preserving its aspect ratio.
- `(x, y)` is the rectangle origin in the current drawing coordinates, and `w` and `h` use the same units; the current drawing transform applies.
- Multiplies the texture by the current drawing color; use `setColor(1.0f)` for an untinted draw. Under `BlendMode::Alpha`, the premultiplied-alpha flag selects the blending behavior on both windows and Fbos; other blend modes take priority.
- Does nothing when unallocated, requires no explicit `bind`, and disables texturing afterward rather than restoring a previous binding. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (pixels.load("image.png")) texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    setColor(1.0f);
    texture.draw(20, 20, 256, 256);
}
```

## Texture::drawFlippedY

- `drawFlippedY(x, y, w, h)` draws the entire texture with its vertical texture coordinates reversed; it does not modify the stored pixels.
- Position and size use the current drawing coordinates, and color, transform, blending, and binding behavior follow `Texture::draw`; an unallocated texture draws nothing.
- `Fbo::draw` already applies this reversal when required by an OpenGL backend. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (pixels.load("image.png")) texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    setColor(1.0f);
    texture.drawFlippedY(20, 20, 256, 256);
}
```

## Texture::drawSubsection

- `drawSubsection(x, y, w, h, sx, sy, sw, sh)` draws the source rectangle `(sx, sy, sw, sh)` into the destination rectangle `(x, y, w, h)`.
- Source coordinates and sizes are texture pixels, with `(0, 0)` mapping to texture coordinates `(0, 0)`; destination coordinates and sizes use the current drawing coordinates.
- Source coordinates are not clipped to the texture bounds; sampling outside the texture follows its wrap modes.
- Does nothing when unallocated or when texture width or height is nonpositive. Color, transform, blending, and binding behavior follow `Texture::draw`; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    if (pixels.load("sprites.png")) texture.allocate(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() {
    setColor(1.0f);
    texture.drawSubsection(20, 20, 128, 128, 32, 0, 32, 32);
}
```

## Texture::getChannels

- Returns the channel count recorded during allocation; it is 0 for a newly constructed or cleared texture.
- The channel-count allocation overload preserves the requested count even when its selected GPU format differs; failed allocation can also retain the count. See `Texture::allocate` and `TextureFormat`.

## Texture::getHeight

- Returns the texture height in pixels; it is 0 for a newly constructed or cleared texture.
- Failed allocation can retain the requested height, so use `isAllocated` to check allocation success.

## Texture::getMagFilter

- Returns the stored `TextureFilter` value; the initial value is `TextureFilter::Linear`, and `clear` preserves it.

## Texture::getMinFilter

- Returns the stored `TextureFilter` value; the initial value is `TextureFilter::Linear`, and `clear` preserves it.

## Texture::getNumMipLevels

- Returns an `int` including the base level, whose index is `0`.
- The initial value is `1`, and `clear()` resets it to `1`.
- This reads stored metadata rather than querying the GPU, so it does not confirm how many levels currently exist on the GPU.

## Texture::getSampleCount

- Returns an `int`; `1` means no multisampling. The initial value is `1`, and `allocateCubemap()` sets it to `1`.
- The dimension-based `allocate()` overloads store the requested sample count, but apply it to the GPU image only for `RenderTarget` usage.
- This does not query GPU allocation success, and `clear()` does not reset the stored sample count.

## Texture::getUsage

- Returns a `TextureUsage` value: `Immutable`, `Dynamic`, `Stream`, or `RenderTarget`.
- The initial value is `Immutable`; allocation methods record their selected usage, and `allocateCompressed()` selects `Immutable`.
- This does not query the GPU or confirm allocation success. `clear()` does not reset the stored usage.

## Texture::getWidth

- Returns the texture width in pixels; it is 0 for a newly constructed or cleared texture.
- Failed allocation can retain the requested width, so use `isAllocated` to check allocation success.

## Texture::getWrapU

- Returns the stored horizontal `TextureWrap` value; the initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`, and `clear` preserves it.

## Texture::getWrapV

- Returns the stored vertical `TextureWrap` value; the initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`, and `clear` preserves it.

## Texture::isAllocated

- Returns the stored allocation flag; it is false for a newly constructed or cleared texture. Ordinary `allocate(...)` calls leave it false on recoverable GPU image creation failure.
- Compressed allocation does not check GPU image creation success before setting the flag to true.
- Does not separately validate the texture views or sampler.

## Texture::isCompressed

- Returns the result of `getPixelFormat() >= SG_PIXELFORMAT_BC1_RGBA`; valid formats in this range include BC, ETC/EAC, and ASTC formats.
- This does not check GPU allocation or device support. A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `false`.

## Texture::isCubemap

- `allocateCubemap()` sets the flag to `true` after its usage checks; this does not confirm GPU allocation success.
- The initial value is `false`, and `clear()` resets it to `false`.
- Moving a Texture currently neither transfers this flag to the destination nor resets it on the source.

## Texture::isPremultipliedAlpha

- Returns the stored flag without inspecting the pixels; the initial value is false, and `clear` preserves it.
- See `Texture::setPremultipliedAlpha` for how the flag affects drawing.

## Texture::loadData

- Use after allocating a Dynamic or Stream texture and whenever its CPU data changes; accepts `Pixels` or a data pointer with width, height, and channel count, and replaces the whole texture rather than a subsection.
- Width, height, and channel count must match the allocation exactly; mismatches, an unallocated texture, Immutable usage, or missing graphics initialization return without uploading. The function returns no value and does not resize or convert the input.
- Pointer data must be tightly packed in the allocated GPU format and remain valid during the call; the byte count is computed from the explicit format, or from the stored channel count for channel-count allocations, and the pointer overload does not receive a buffer length. `Pixels` uploads do not validate that the component type matches the texture.
- With channel-count allocations of two or three channels, the GPU format is R8 but uploads supply two or three bytes per pixel and fail size validation. Use explicit `TextureFormat::R8` for single-channel data or `TextureFormat::RG8` for two-channel data.
- Ordinary updates allow one upload to the same GPU image per device frame across all windows; another call in that frame logs a warning and is skipped.
- For a mipmapped non-Immutable texture, `loadData(pixels)` generates lower mip levels on the CPU and replaces the GPU image and view. Each replacement changes the image handle, so another call in the same device frame can rebuild it again; the pointer overload does not regenerate mipmaps.
- For RGBA16, the current upload byte count is four bytes per pixel rather than eight, so sokol validation rejects the incomplete data when enabled.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and upload costs.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    Pixels pixels;
    pixels.allocate(1, 1);
    pixels.setColor(0, 0, Color(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
    texture.allocate(pixels, TextureUsage::Dynamic);
    texture.loadData(pixels);
}
void tcApp::draw() { texture.draw(20, 20, 256, 256); }
```

## Texture::setFilter

- Sets both filters to `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear`; both initially use Linear. Nearest selects a single texel, while Linear interpolates neighboring texels.
- A changed setting recreates the sampler of an allocated texture without uploading pixels; unchanged settings do nothing. Mipmapped textures retain linear interpolation between mip levels.
- Can be set before allocation and survives `clear`; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Texture::setMagFilter

- Sets the filter used when enlarging the texture to `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear`; the initial value is Linear, and the minification filter is unchanged.
- A changed value recreates the sampler of an allocated texture without uploading pixels; the same value does nothing.
- Can be set before allocation and survives `clear`; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Texture::setMinFilter

- Sets the filter used when reducing the texture to `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear`; the initial value is Linear, and the magnification filter is unchanged.
- A changed value recreates the sampler of an allocated texture without uploading pixels; the same value does nothing. Mipmapped textures retain linear interpolation between mip levels.
- Can be set before allocation and survives `clear`; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Texture::setPremultipliedAlpha

- Pass true when the stored RGB values have already been multiplied by alpha; this changes only a flag and does not modify or upload pixel data.
- Under `BlendMode::Alpha`, texture drawing uses this flag on both windows and Fbos; explicitly selected non-Alpha blend modes take priority.
- The initial value is false, Fbo color textures are marked true automatically, and `clear` and reallocation preserve the flag.

## Texture::setWrap

- Sets both axes to `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`, `TextureWrap::Repeat`, or `TextureWrap::MirroredRepeat`; both initially use ClampToEdge. These modes extend edge texels, repeat the texture, or repeat it with alternating reflections outside texture coordinates 0–1.
- A changed setting recreates the sampler of an allocated texture without uploading pixels; unchanged settings do nothing.
- Can be set before allocation and survives `clear`; see `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## Texture::setWrapU

- Sets the horizontal axis to a `TextureWrap` mode; the initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`, and the vertical setting is unchanged. See `Texture::setWrap` for mode behavior.
- A changed value recreates the sampler of an allocated texture without uploading pixels; the same value does nothing.
