- Names are converted through `pathToUtf8()`; see `pathToUtf8` for encoding rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    for (const auto& name : listDirectory("images")) {
        logNotice() << name;
    }
}
```

## listNetworkInterfaces

- Returns a `vector<NetworkInterface>` with one entry per IPv4 or IPv6 address, including loopback and down interfaces; one interface can therefore appear several times.
- Entries contain the interface name, address, MAC address when available, and IPv4, loopback, and up flags; IPv4 netmasks are populated when available, while IPv6 netmasks remain empty.
- Returns an empty vector and logs a warning if operating-system enumeration fails.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    for (const auto& ni : listNetworkInterfaces()) {
        logNotice("Network") << ni.name << ": " << ni.address;
    }
}
```

## listSystemFonts

- Returns a sorted `vector<string>` of UTF-8 family names, not a list of every font file or face. Name availability depends on the operating system and installed fonts.
- Linux includes available localized family names and removes duplicates. Windows selects the English US family name when available, otherwise the first localized name, and removes duplicates.
- An unavailable backend or failed enumeration can return an empty vector.

## loadDialog

- Arguments are `title`, `message`, `defaultPath` for the initial directory, and `folderSelection`. Text and path arguments default to empty values, and `folderSelection` defaults to `false`.
- Selects one file, or one folder when `folderSelection` is `true`; this function does not read the selected file.
- Returns `FileDialogResult` with `success = true`, the full `filePath`, and the final path component in `fileName` after selection. Cancellation or failure returns `success = false` with empty paths.
- Threading and blocking behavior follow `alertDialog`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto result = loadDialog("Open a text file");
    if (result.success) {
        logNotice() << loadTextFile(result.filePath);
    }
}
```

## loadDialogAsync

- Takes `title`, `message`, `defaultPath`, `folderSelection`, and `callback`, with no default arguments; `defaultPath` is the initial directory, and `folderSelection` selects folders when `true` or files when `false`.
- Pass `{}` for no initial directory; paths are passed to the platform picker without resolution through `getDataPath()`.
- The `void(const FileDialogResult&)` callback receives `success = true`, the selected full `filePath`, and its `fileName` on selection; cancellation or failure gives `success = false` and empty paths. The picker does not read the selected file.
- The result reference is valid only during the callback; copy the result or its paths if you need to keep them. This also applies to `saveDialogAsync`.
- On iOS, a missing root view controller logs an error and supplies an empty result; load and save pickers share one retained delegate, so finish one picker before opening another.
- See `alertDialogAsync` for shared threading, callback timing, and app run lifetime rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    loadDialogAsync("Open XML", "", getDataPath(""), false, [](const FileDialogResult& result) {
        if (!result.success) return;
        Xml xml;
        if (xml.load(result.filePath)) logNotice() << xml.root().name();
    });
}
```

## loadJson

- Local files have no byte-size cap. Nesting is limited to 64 levels; deeper input is rejected as a whole. Files above 16 MiB produce a Notice. Caught allocation exceptions log an Error and return `Json()`; recovery during JSON DOM cleanup is not guaranteed.
- Accepts a file path and returns the parsed `Json` value. Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`; absolute paths are used directly.
- A missing, unreadable, or non-regular file, or a JSON parse error, logs an Error and returns `Json()`, which holds JSON `null`.
- A valid file containing `null` returns the same value as these failures. Caught parsing and allocation exceptions are reported as failures.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json settings = loadJson("settings.json");
    if (!settings.is_null()) {
        logNotice() << toJsonString(settings);
    }
}
```

## loadMatrix

Kept as a backward-compatible alias for `setMatrix()` (identical behavior — it replaces the current matrix). New code should call `setMatrix()`; this name is scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## loadTextFile

- `loadTextFile(path)` returns the file's bytes as a string. Binary mode preserves line endings, including Windows `"\r\n"`, and embedded null bytes without decoding the text.
- Relative paths are resolved through `getDataPath()`; absolute paths are used unchanged. The target must be an openable regular file.
- A missing, non-regular, or unopenable file logs an Error with a file-not-found message and returns an empty string. An empty file also returns an empty string. Detected I/O or allocation failure logs an Error and returns an empty string. libc++ and MSVC filebuf can report read errors as EOF; a partial result is possible there.
- The whole file is read synchronously, appending only bytes actually read in chunks, without a local size cap. Reads of at least 256 MiB emit a Notice. Use `FileReader` to retain only part of the file.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    string text = loadTextFile("notes.txt");
    logNotice() << text;
}
```

## loadXml

- Accepts a file path and returns an `Xml` object; relative paths are resolved through `getDataPath()`, and absolute paths are used directly.
- Returns the object even if loading fails, without returning a success flag; use `Xml::load` when you need to check success, and refer to it for failure behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto xml = loadXml("settings.xml");
    if (auto root = xml.root()) logNotice() << root.name();
}
```

## log

- `log(x)` computes the logarithm to base `e`; use a positive `x` for a finite real result.
- This is the standard `<cmath>` function included by TrussC; `exp` performs the inverse calculation.

## logAt

- Takes a `LogLevel`, defaulting to `LogLevel::Notice`, and returns a `LogStream` that accepts values through `<<`; this function has no module-name argument.
- The stream sends its message to the global logger when destroyed, normally at the end of the statement; see `LogStream` for stream lifetime and `Logger` for output filtering and threading.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    logAt(LogLevel::Warning) << "Using default settings";
}
```

## logError

- Append values with `<<`; the returned `LogStream` emits one Error message when destroyed, normally at the end of the statement. The optional module string defaults to empty; a nonempty module adds a `[module] ` prefix.
- Console, file, and system outputs apply their own level thresholds, while `getLogger().onLog` listeners receive every message. Logging an Error does not terminate the application.
- Separate log streams can be used from any thread. Console and file writes are synchronized, and listeners run outside that output lock on the calling thread by default. Listeners registered with `Deliver::Main` run on the main thread and are queued when logging from a worker; the same rules apply to `logWarning`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    logError("App") << "Could not load the requested resource";
}
```

## logFatal

- Returns a `LogStream` with `LogLevel::Fatal`; the optional module string defaults to empty and adds `[module] ` before the message when nonempty.
- This function only logs; it does not abort the process or request application exit.
- See `LogStream` for message construction and emission timing, and `Logger` for output filtering and threading.

## logLevelToString

- Returns a `const char*` to a string literal: `VERBOSE`, `NOTICE`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `FATAL` or `SILENT`.
- Returns `UNKNOWN` for a value outside the declared `LogLevel` enumerators; the returned text does not require freeing.

## logNotice

- Returns a `LogStream` at `LogLevel::Notice`; append values with `<<`. The message is sent to the global logger when the stream is destroyed, normally at the end of the statement.
- The optional `module` argument defaults to an empty string. A nonempty module prefixes the message with `[module] `.
- Notice messages pass the default output thresholds. Console, file, and system output each apply their own threshold, while `onLog` listeners receive the message regardless of those thresholds. See `Logger` for output destinations and thread rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    logNotice() << "Application ready";
    logNotice("App") << "Setup complete";
}
```

## OnceGate

- A default-constructed gate returns `true` from `isFirstTime()` only on its first call. Passing a positive interval in seconds, such as `OnceGate{5.0}`, allows another `true` once that interval has passed since the previous `true`, using a steady clock.
- The gate object holds the state: use a local `static` for one gate per call site, or a member for one gate per object. Use it in place of a shared `static bool` flag.
- Put the action inside the condition; any log level or other action can be guarded, and message construction inside the condition is skipped while the gate is closed.
```cpp
static OnceGate warned;
if (warned.isFirstTime()) logWarning() << "Reported once";
```
- `reset()` restores the initial state for both gate modes, allowing the next `isFirstTime()` call to return `true` immediately.
- Calls are thread-safe and use atomic operations without a mutex; competing calls allow one caller through each opening. `reset()` is also safe from any thread.
- Intervals are truncated to whole nanoseconds; zero, negative values, NaN, and positive values below one nanosecond select once-only behavior. Values at least 9.2 billion seconds are clamped to the maximum `int64_t` nanosecond interval.
- The type is constexpr-constructible and trivially destructible, so a static gate remains usable during static destruction. It cannot be copied or moved.

## OnceGate::isFirstTime

- Returns `true` on the first call and `false` on subsequent calls for a once-only gate.
- For an interval gate, returns `true` again when the configured interval in seconds has elapsed since the last `true`, measured with a steady clock.
- `reset()` allows the next call immediately; see `OnceGate` for thread safety.

## OnceGate::reset

- Restores the never-fired state for both once-only and interval gates, so the next `isFirstTime()` can return `true` immediately.
- Uses an atomic store without a lock and is safe to call from any thread; see `OnceGate` for the shared threading contract.

## logVerbose

- Returns a `LogStream` that accepts values with `<<`; the optional `module` string defaults to empty and, when nonempty, prefixes the message with `[module] `.
- The message is submitted when the stream is destroyed, normally at the end of the statement; `endl` inserts a newline but does not submit the message early.
- All output thresholds default to `LogLevel::Notice`, so verbose messages are hidden by default; use `setConsoleLogLevel(LogLevel::Verbose)` to enable them in the console.
- Message construction still occurs when output thresholds hide the message, and `getLogger().onLog` still receives it.
- See `Logger` for threading rules, output destinations, and independent output thresholds.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setConsoleLogLevel(LogLevel::Verbose);
    logVerbose("setup") << "Window size: " << getWidth() << " x " << getHeight();
}
```

## logWarning

- Append values with `<<`; the returned `LogStream` emits one Warning message when destroyed. The optional module string defaults to empty.
- See `logError` for module prefixes, output filtering, message lifetime, and thread rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    logWarning("App") << "Using default settings";
}
```

## max

- The standard-library function `max(a, b)` compares values with `<`; use arguments of the same type, such as `max(0.0f, value)` for a `float` value.
- The two-argument overload returns a const reference to the selected argument and selects `a` when the values compare equal. Copy the result if an argument is temporary.

## min

- The standard-library function `min(a, b)` compares values with `<`; use arguments of the same type, such as `min(1.0f, value)` for a `float` value.
- The two-argument overload returns a const reference to the selected argument and selects `a` when the values compare equal. Copy the result if an argument is temporary.

## multMatrix

- Multiplies the current matrix by `mat` and keeps the result as the new current matrix: a relative transform, the same way `translate()` / `rotate()` / `scale()` are each really a multiply by a small matrix.
- Useful for applying a precomputed or combined `Mat4` (for example a node's local transform) in one call instead of separate `translate()` / `rotate()` / `scale()` calls.
- Unlike `setMatrix()`, this builds on top of whatever transform is already active rather than replacing it.

## nextPowerOfTwo

- `nextPowerOfTwo(int n)` returns an `int`; for example, `nextPowerOfTwo(1000)` returns `1024`, and an existing power of two is unchanged.
- All values `n <= 1`, including zero and negative values, return `1`.
- The required power of two must fit in `int`. Overflow from repeated doubling is not checked.

## noFill

- With stroke enabled, shapes are drawn as outlines only, using the current color and `setStrokeWeight()`; `fill()` switches back to solid shapes. Fill and stroke are mutually exclusive: turning one on turns the other off.
- Default is fill enabled, so `noFill()` is needed to see outlines.
- `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` save and restore this along with the rest of the drawing style; `resetStyle()` restores fill enabled (stroke disabled).
- Check the current state with `isStrokeEnabled()`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    noFill();
    setStrokeWeight(3.0f);
    drawRect(20, 20, 100, 60);  // outline only, 3px thick
}
```

## nodeToJson

- Returns a JSON object containing `type`, `id`, reflected `members`, and `name` when the node has a name. Attached mods appear in `mods` with their type and reflected data.
- `maxDepth` defaults to `-1`; any negative value includes all descendants. `0` includes only this node, and positive values limit the number of child levels.
- Included children appear in `children` in the order returned by `Node::getChildren()`. At the depth limit, a node with children reports their number in `childCount` instead.
- `includeDerived` defaults to `false`. When `true`, derived values such as `globalPos` are included in `members`, and their member paths are listed in `derived` for each node or mod that has them.
- Member encoding follows `reflectToJson`. This function does not reconstruct nodes; use `reflectFromJson` to apply member values to existing objects.
- For scene access and thread rules, see `Node`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json j = nodeToJson(*this, 0);
    logNotice() << toJsonString(j);
}
```

## noise

- Accepts one to four `float` coordinates, a `Vec2`, or a `Vec3`. Vector overloads use the vector components as coordinates.
- Coordinates have no fixed units. Nearby coordinates produce smoothly changing values; multiplying coordinates by a larger scale produces faster variation over the same input distance.
- Returns a `float` calculated as `signedNoise(...) * 0.5f + 0.5f`, with a nominal range of 0–1. The result is not clamped.
- The seeded 3D overload is `noise(float x, float y, float z, int seed)`. An `int` fourth argument selects this overload; a `float` fourth argument selects the four-coordinate overload. Only the lowest eight bits of `seed` are used, so seeds differing by 256 produce the same pattern.
- The four-coordinate overload averages signed 3D samples at `(x, y, z)` and `(x + w, y + w, z + w)` before remapping the result. It approximates 4D noise rather than evaluating a four-dimensional gradient field.
- The same coordinates and seed produce the same value; overloads without a seed use seed `0`. The underlying 3D pattern repeats every 256 coordinate units along each axis.
- `noise`, `signedNoise`, and `fbm` calculate values on the CPU without changing shared state or requiring graphics initialization, and can be called from any thread.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    float value = noise(getElapsedTimef() * 0.2f);
    drawCircle(100.0f + value * 300.0f, 200.0f, 20.0f);
}
```

## operator*

- Multiplying two `Vec2`, `Vec3`, or `Vec4` values multiplies corresponding components; it returns a new vector rather than a dot product. Scalar multiplication scales every component and supports either operand order, including integer scalars with `IVec2` and `IVec3`.
- `Color * scalar` and `ColorLinear * scalar` scale all four channels, including alpha; `ColorLinear * ColorLinear` multiplies corresponding channels. These operations do not clamp the result.
- Matrix multiplication composes transformations or transforms a vector; see `Mat3` and `Mat4` for application order and homogeneous-coordinate division.
- Quaternion multiplication composes rotations; see `Quaternion` for order and normalization requirements.

## parseJson

- Input has no byte-size cap; documents above 16 MiB produce a Notice. Nesting deeper than 64 levels rejects the whole input. Parsed values retain their external-input provenance for transactional settings reflection.
- Accepts a `const string&` and returns its parsed JSON value without accessing a file.
- Syntax and nesting failures, raw NUL bytes, and caught allocation exceptions log an Error and return `Json()`, which holds JSON `null`. Recovery during JSON DOM cleanup is not guaranteed.
- Valid input `"null"` returns the same value as a parse failure, so `is_null()` alone cannot distinguish them.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json settings = parseJson(R"({"enabled":true,"count":3})");
    if (!settings.is_null()) {
        logNotice() << toJsonString(settings);
    }
}
```

## parseXml

- Accepts a UTF-8 XML string and returns an `Xml` object.
- Returns an empty object if parsing fails; use `Xml::parse` when you need to check success, and refer to it for parsing behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto xml = parseXml("<settings><title>Demo</title></settings>");
    logNotice() << xml.root().child("title").text().as_string();
}
```

## pathToUtf8

- Accepts an `fs::path` and returns a `string`. Windows converts the native UTF-16 path to UTF-8; other platforms return the native bytes unchanged without validating their encoding.
- Use this function for UTF-8 text instead of `path.string()`, which uses the process code page on Windows and can throw for characters that code page cannot represent.
- On Windows, a path containing invalid UTF-16, such as an unpaired surrogate, can still throw. For logging, use `logNotice() << path`; path logging replaces invalid UTF-16 with replacement characters rather than throwing for the name.

## popMatrix

- Pops the top entry off the matrix stack and makes it the current matrix again, undoing any `translate()` / `rotate()` / `scale()` done since the matching `pushMatrix()`.
- Calling `popMatrix()` with nothing pushed (an unmatched call) is refused: TrussC prints a warning and leaves the matrix stack untouched, instead of popping into a parent's or a sibling node's transform.
- Inside a Node's `draw()`, the floor is that node's own stack depth, so an unmatched `popMatrix()` there is refused the same way rather than reaching into the parent's transform.

## popScissor

- If no clipping was active at the matching `pushScissor()`, clipping is turned off again.
- When the stack is empty, it does the same as `resetScissor()`, without a warning.
- Coordinates and nesting are explained in `pushScissor`.
- Known issue: [#914](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/914) (popping an empty stack silently resets the scissor without a warning).

## popShader

- Calls `end()` on the current shader, removing it from the stack and restoring the previous shader; when the stack becomes empty, ordinary drawing resumes.
- Does nothing if there is no current shader for the active render-target activation.
- Scope, threading, and object-lifetime rules are described under `Shader`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Shader shader;
void tcApp::draw() {
    if (!shader.isLoaded()) return;
    pushShader(shader);
    drawRect(20, 20, 120, 80);
    popShader();
}
```

## popStyle

- `popStyle()` takes the style saved by the matching `pushStyle()` off the stack and makes it current again. The color, fill and stroke, point and curve settings, text alignment, and blend mode all return at once. See `pushStyle` for the full list of saved items and for how TrussC resets the style before each Node's `draw()`.
- If nothing is left on the stack (more pops than pushes), a rate-limited warning is logged and nothing happens. The stack and the current style stay as they are. Inside a Node's `draw()`, a pop that would remove a style pushed outside that node is refused in the same way.
- The depth test setting is not saved by `pushStyle()` and is not restored by `popStyle()`. `popStyle()` restores the blend mode with the current depth test setting, so call `disableDepthTest()` yourself when you want the depth test off.
- Known issue: [#915](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/915) (inside a camera scope this turns the depth test off unless enableDepthTest() is on).

## pow

- `pow(x, y)` computes `x^y`, with `x` as the base and `y` as the exponent.
- This is the standard `<cmath>` function included by TrussC; `sq(x)` is also available for squaring.

## printNetworkInterfaces

- Calls `listNetworkInterfaces()` and uses `logNotice("Network")` to print a count header followed by one line per address entry.
- Each entry shows its name, address, IPv4 or IPv6 label, loopback status, and up or down status, plus the netmask and MAC address when present.
- Returns no value and still prints the count header when the list is empty; see `listNetworkInterfaces` for platform availability and failure behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    printNetworkInterfaces();
}
```

## pushMatrix

- Copies the current matrix onto an internal stack; `popMatrix()` restores it later. Always pair one `pushMatrix()` with one `popMatrix()`.
- A typical pattern is `pushMatrix()` → `translate(...)` → `rotate(...)` → draw → `popMatrix()`, so the translate/rotate only affects what is drawn in between.
- The order of operations matters: translating first and then rotating rotates around the translated point; rotating first and then translating moves along the rotated axes. Apply `translate()` before `rotate()` to rotate a shape around its own position.
- Each Node already wraps its own `draw()` in a `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()` pair and applies the node's own transform in between, so an app rarely needs nested calls when drawing through nodes; it is mainly useful inside `draw()` itself or in `App::draw()` for manual 2D/3D drawing.
- Inside a Node's `draw()`, a missing `popMatrix()` is detected and popped right after that node's `draw()` returns. Inside `App::draw()`, it is caught at the end of the frame (`present()`). Either way TrussC prints a warning instead of leaving the matrix stack growing or corrupting later drawing.
- Prefer `scopedMatrix()` when a function has several early returns or can throw; it pushes now and pops automatically at the end of the scope.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    pushMatrix();
    translate(100, 100);   // move origin first
    rotate(TAU / 8);       // then rotate around that point
    drawRect(0, 0, 50, 50);
    popMatrix();
}
```

## pushScissor

- After this call, only the pixels inside the rectangle are drawn; everything outside is left unchanged. Always pair it with `popScissor()` in the same `draw()`.
- `x`, `y` are the top-left corner and `w`, `h` the size. **The values are pixels of the render target, not logical coordinates.** On the window they are framebuffer pixels, so multiply logical values by `getDpiScale()` (2 on Retina screens). In pixelPerfect mode and inside an `Fbo`, use the values as they are (inside an `Fbo` they are pixels of the `Fbo`).
- The rectangle is not affected by `translate()`, `rotate()`, `scale()` or a camera. It is always measured from the top-left corner of the window or `Fbo`. To clip an area that moves with a node, use `RectNode::setClipping(true)`, which converts the position and the DPI scale for you.
- Nested calls are intersected with the current rectangle, so an inner rectangle never extends beyond the outer one. When they do not overlap, nothing is drawn until the matching `popScissor()`.
- Values are cut down to whole pixels.
- The clipping state is not reset at the start of each frame or before each Node's `draw()`. A push without a pop stays active in later frames.
- `fbo.begin()` starts with no clipping and an empty stack, and the window's clipping returns after `fbo.end()`. Pushes left unpopped inside an `Fbo` are discarded at `end()` with a warning.
- A `RectNode` with clipping enabled uses this same stack, so a `pushScissor()` inside such a node is intersected with the node's area.
- Known issue: [#914](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/914) (the rectangle is given in render-target pixels, unlike other drawing functions).

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    float s = getDpiScale();                   // logical -> window pixels (use 1 inside an Fbo)
    pushScissor(50 * s, 50 * s, 200 * s, 100 * s);
    setColor(0.2f, 0.6f, 1.0f);
    drawCircle(150, 100, 120);                // only the part inside the rectangle appears
    popScissor();
}
```

## pushShader

- Takes `Shader&` and calls its `begin()`; drawing routed through TrussC's vertex writer uses this shader until the matching `popShader()`.
- An unloaded shader does not push a scope, so a later `popShader()` can end an already active outer shader; check `isLoaded()` before entering a conditional scope.
- Scope nesting, render-target restrictions, threading, and object lifetime are described under `Shader`.

```cpp
// tcApp member: Shader shader;
void tcApp::draw() {
    if (!shader.isLoaded()) return;
    pushShader(shader);
    drawRect(20, 20, 120, 80);
    popShader();
}
```

## pushStyle

- `pushStyle()` saves the whole current style on a stack. This includes the draw color, whether fill and stroke are on, the stroke weight, cap and join, the point size and shape, the curve quality settings, the text alignment, the bitmap text line height, and the blend mode. `popStyle()` restores all of it to the state at the time of the push.
- Call `popStyle()` once for every `pushStyle()`. For code with several exits or long blocks, `scopedStyle()` is convenient because it pops automatically when the scope ends.
- `resetStyle()` returns the style to its defaults: white color, fill on, stroke off, stroke weight 1 with the `Butt` cap and `Miter` join, point size 1 with the `Square` point style, curves in tolerance mode at 0.1 pixels, text aligned to the top-left, and blend mode `Alpha`.
- TrussC calls `resetStyle()` automatically right before each Node's `draw()`. For this reason, a node does not inherit the style that its parent or an earlier sibling left behind, and it always starts drawing from the defaults. `resetStyle()` runs again after the node and its children have finished drawing, so the node's changes do not carry over to what is drawn next.
- If you call `popStyle()` more times than `pushStyle()`, a warning is logged (rate-limited) and the extra call is ignored. A `pushStyle()` left without a matching pop is removed with a warning at the end of that Node's `draw()`, or at the end of the frame or callback, so it does not pile up. It is still a bug that you should fix.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    pushStyle();
    setColor(1, 0, 0);
    noFill();  // outline only
    drawRect(10, 10, 100, 100);
    popStyle();  // color and fill/stroke back to what they were before
}
```

## rad2deg

- Takes a `float` angle in radians and returns `rad * 360.0f / TAU` as a `float`.
- Does not wrap or clamp the angle; negative angles and multiple turns are preserved.

## random

- `random()` returns a `float` in `[0, 1)`; with increasing bounds, `random(max)` uses `[0, max)` and `random(min, max)` uses `[min, max)`.
- Bounds are passed directly to the distribution without validation or reordering.
- Each thread has its own Mersenne Twister engine, initially seeded from `random_device`; `random` and `randomInt` share that engine within the thread, and `randomSeed` reseeds only the calling thread's engine.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    float chance = random(1.0f);
    Vec2 position(random(640.0f), random(480.0f));
    float angle = random(0.0f, TAU);
}
```

## randomInt

- `randomInt(max)` returns an `int` from 0 through `max - 1`, excluding `max`; `randomInt(min, max)` includes both `min` and `max`.
- Supply `max > 0` for the one-argument form and `min <= max` for the two-argument form; bounds are not validated or reordered.
- See `random` for the shared engine and thread-local seeding behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    int index = randomInt(10);
    int die = randomInt(1, 6);
}
```

## randomSeed

- `randomSeed(seed)` takes an `unsigned int`, resets the engine used by subsequent `random` and `randomInt` calls, and returns no value.
- Repeating the same seed and the same sequence of calls reproduces the sequence with the same distribution implementation.
- See `random` for the shared engine and thread-local seeding behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    randomSeed(42);
    float first = random(1.0f);
    randomSeed(42);
    float repeated = random(1.0f);
}
```

## recordingFrameCount

- Returns `int` from the global recorder's `ScreenRecorder::getFrameCount()`; see that entry for counting and finalization behavior.
- See `isRecording` for the global recorder's scope.

## recordingPath

- Returns an `fs::path` by value from the global recorder's `ScreenRecorder::getPath()`; see that entry for path resolution and retention.
- See `isRecording` for the global recorder's scope.

## redraw

- With `setFps(EVENT_DRIVEN)`, requests `count` draws, defaulting to `1`; the usual synchronized update also runs for each drawn frame.
- Sets the remaining draw count to the larger of its current value and `count`, rather than adding counts. Zero or negative values do not cancel pending draws, and continuous rendering modes keep their normal pacing.
- Controls only the main window; calls from a secondary-window context warn once and do nothing.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setFps(EVENT_DRIVEN);
    redraw(2);
}
```

## reflectFromJson

- v0.8: JSON parsed from files or strings (including MCP input) is validated as a whole before application. All present fields, nested groups, unknown keys, numeric ranges, enum labels, and writable access are validated before any assignment or setter. Invalid input applies nothing and logs an Error naming the field; `applied` stays empty. Parsed provenance survives copies, moves, and child extraction. JSON constructed directly by app code keeps the permissive behavior described below. Setter exceptions during commit and JSON DOM cleanup are outside the recovery guarantee. Allocation recovery requires standard-library configurations without iterator debugging; MSVC Debug with `_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL != 0` can allocate iterator proxies in noexcept container construction/moves and is outside this guarantee.
- Calls `obj.reflectMembers()` with a JSON reader, updating only members whose keys are present in `j`. It updates an existing object and does not create nodes or mods.
- Returns a `JsonReadReflector` containing `applied`, `skipped`, `readOnly`, and `unknownKeys()` results.
- See `JsonReadReflector` for accepted JSON forms, setter behavior, processing order, and result naming.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto r = reflectFromJson(*this, Json{{"visible", false}});
    logNotice() << r.applied.size();
}
```

## reflectToJson

- Calls `obj.reflectMembers()` and returns a JSON object of its members, including read-only members. It works with reflected types such as `Node` and `Mod`.
- `includeDerived` defaults to `false`, excluding `TC_DERIVED` values such as `Node`'s `globalPos`; pass `true` to include them. The returned object does not contain a separate `derived` list.
- Numbers, booleans, and strings become JSON scalars; `Vec2`, `Vec3`, and `Color` become `[x, y]`, `[x, y, z]`, and `[r, g, b, a]`. Color components conventionally use a 0–1 scale, but are serialized unchanged, including values outside that range.
- Enum values with a matching label become label strings; other enum values become integers. Composite members become nested JSON objects.
- For scene access and thread rules when reading nodes, see `Node`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json j = reflectToJson(*this);
    logNotice() << toJsonString(j);
}
```

## releaseSglBuffers

- Releases the current window's swapchain sokol_gl CPU vertex, uniform, and command buffers and its GPU vertex buffer; later drawing recreates them automatically.
- Call between frames when no target owns unfinished work. If a nested target, active or started pass, open shader scope, deferred draw, or pending sokol_gl draw remains, logs a Warning and returns without releasing anything.
- A rejected call is not scheduled for retry; call again after the work has finished.

## remap

- `remap(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)` takes and returns `float` values, using `outMin + (outMax - outMin) * ((value - inMin) / (inMax - inMin))`; either range may be reversed.
- Does not clamp the input or output, so values outside the input range are extrapolated.
- `inMin` and `inMax` must differ; equal input bounds cause division by zero without a fallback.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    float level = remap(75.0f, 0.0f, 100.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
    float reversed = remap(level, 0.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
}
```

## removeFile

- Resolves `path` through `getDataPath()` and removes that single filesystem entry. It can remove an empty directory, but does not recursively remove directory contents; a symbolic link is removed without removing its target.
- Returns `true` if an entry was removed and `false` if no entry existed. Filesystem exceptions during removal are logged as Error and return `false`.

## removeLight

- Accepts the same `Light&` object passed to `addLight` and removes its address from the current window's list. An unregistered object has no effect.
- The Light object is not destroyed or changed. Registration and lifetime rules are described in `addLight`.

## requestExitApp

- Requests exit through the event loop; it does not terminate the application immediately.
- Before exiting, `events().exitRequested` notifies listeners with `ExitRequestEventArgs`. A listener can set `e.cancel = true` to keep the application running; retain the returned `EventListener` to keep that listener registered.
- Use `exitApp()` for an exit that bypasses this cancellation event. The request also works in `runHeadlessApp`.
- On iOS and Android, this request does not drive shutdown or deliver the cancellation event because the operating system owns the application lifecycle.

```cpp
void tcApp::update() {
    if (isKeyPressed(KEY_ESCAPE)) requestExitApp();
}
```

## resetBlendMode

- This is the same as `setBlendMode(BlendMode::Alpha)`. Call it after a temporary `Add`, `Multiply`, `Screen` or `Subtract` so that later drawing is not affected. See `setBlendMode` for how long a mode stays in effect.

## resetElapsedTimeCounter

- Makes `getElapsedTime()`, `getElapsedTimef()`, `getElapsedTimeMillis()`, `getElapsedTimeMicros()`, and `getFrameElapsedTime()` report time relative to this reset.
- These functions share a `steady_clock` origin established during program initialization; system clock adjustments do not affect it. Resetting changes only a shared display offset, including across hot-reload host and guest code.
- `resetElapsedTimeCounter()`, `getElapsedTime()`, `getElapsedTimef()`, `getElapsedTimeMillis()`, and `getElapsedTimeMicros()` can be called from worker threads. The offset is atomic, and readings are clamped to zero if a concurrent reset would otherwise make them negative. `getFrameElapsedTime()` requires the application thread.
- Node timers, the application loop, recording, and the uptime reported by `tc_get_health` continue using their underlying timing and are unaffected.
- Differences between readings taken across a reset do not measure the elapsed duration: floating-point differences can become negative, and unsigned millisecond or microsecond differences can wrap. To measure across resets, use signed differences of `getSystemTimeMicros()` readings and account for its system clock adjustments.

## resetMatrix

- Discards every `translate()` / `rotate()` / `scale()` / `multMatrix()` applied so far and sets the current matrix back to identity (no offset, no rotation, no scaling).
- Only affects the current matrix, not the matrix stack: anything already saved by `pushMatrix()` is unaffected and will still be restored by a later `popMatrix()`.
- Used far less often than `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()`; prefer those for the common case of temporarily changing the transform and then undoing exactly that change.

## resetScissor

- It does not empty the `pushScissor()` stack. A later `popScissor()` still restores the saved rectangle.
- It is useful at the start of `draw()` to recover when a `pushScissor()` was left without its `popScissor()`, because clipping is not reset between frames.

## resetStyle

- `resetStyle()` sets the current style back to its defaults: white color (1, 1, 1, 1), fill on, stroke off, stroke weight 1 logical pixel with the `Butt` cap and `Miter` join, point size 1 with the `Square` point style, curves in tolerance mode at 0.1 pixels, text aligned to the top-left, and blend mode `Alpha`.
- It changes only the current style and does not touch the `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` stack. A later `popStyle()` therefore restores what was pushed before `resetStyle()` was called, not these defaults.
- TrussC also calls `resetStyle()` automatically right before and right after each Node's `draw()`. See `pushStyle` for what this means for your own `draw()` code.
- Known issue: [#915](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/915) (inside a camera scope this turns the depth test off unless enableDepthTest() is on).

## rotate

- All TrussC angles are radians; use `TAU` (`= 2 * PI`, a full turn) instead of degrees or `PI`. A quarter turn is `TAU / 4`.
- The single-float overload rotates around the Z axis, which is the one used for ordinary 2D drawing.
- Overloads: three floats or a `Vec3` rotate around X, Y, then Z in that order (Euler angles); a `Quaternion` rotates directly without going through Euler angles, avoiding gimbal-lock issues for compound 3D rotations.
- Every function with a *Deg suffix (`rotateDeg`, `rotateXDeg`, ...) takes the same angle in degrees instead; see `rotateDeg`.
- Rotation always happens around the current origin, which is `(0, 0, 0)` unless moved first with `translate()`. Call `translate()` before `rotate()` to rotate a shape around its own center or position.
- Like `translate()` and `scale()`, this changes the current matrix until it is restored by `popMatrix()`, `resetMatrix()`, or another call that replaces it.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    pushMatrix();
    translate(150, 150);   // move origin to the rotation center
    rotate(TAU * 0.125f);  // rotate 45 degrees
    drawRect(-25, -25, 50, 50);
    popMatrix();
}
```

## rotateDeg

- Same as `rotate()` (Z-axis rotation; three floats or `Vec3` rotate X, Y, then Z), except the angle is given in degrees instead of radians.
- Prefer `rotate()` with `TAU`-based radians for new code; `rotateDeg()` exists mainly for porting code or math that is naturally expressed in degrees.

## rotateX

Rotates the current matrix around the X axis only (pitch). Angle is in radians; use `rotate(x, y, z)` for a combined Euler rotation, or `rotateXDeg()` for the same rotation in degrees.

## rotateXDeg

Same as `rotateX()`, with the angle given in degrees instead of radians.

## rotateY

Rotates the current matrix around the Y axis only (yaw). Angle is in radians; use `rotate(x, y, z)` for a combined Euler rotation, or `rotateYDeg()` for the same rotation in degrees.

## rotateYDeg

Same as `rotateY()`, with the angle given in degrees instead of radians.

## rotateZ

Rotates the current matrix around the Z axis (roll) — the same axis `rotate()` uses for ordinary 2D drawing. Angle is in radians; use `rotateZDeg()` for the same rotation in degrees.

## rotateZDeg

Same as `rotateZ()`, with the angle given in degrees instead of radians.

## round

- The standard-library function `round(x)` rounds halfway cases away from zero; `round(2.5f)` returns `3.0f`, and `round(-2.5f)` returns `-3.0f`.
- A `float` argument produces a `float` result, not an integer type.

## runApp

- Call `runApp<tcApp>(settings)` from `main()`, or return `TC_RUN_APP(tcApp, settings)` to support hot reload builds. `runApp` accepts an optional `WindowSettings` argument with default settings.
- The framework creates and owns the App after graphics initialization. See `App` for setup, update, draw, shutdown, and callback thread rules.
- On desktop, returns `1` if startup ends before App creation is reached; otherwise returns the application exit code, normally `0` or the value passed to `exitApp(code)`. Returning `TC_RUN_APP(...)` from `main()` passes this status to the process.
- On Linux, failure to open an X display aborts the process instead of returning a status.
- Android stores the application descriptor and returns `0`; Web starts the browser-owned asynchronous loop and returns `0`. These return values do not report eventual shutdown.

```cpp
int main() {
    WindowSettings settings;
    settings.setSize(960, 600);
    return TC_RUN_APP(tcApp, settings);
}
```

## runHeadlessApp

- Pass the app class as the template argument, as in `runHeadlessApp<tcApp>()`. Optional `HeadlessSettings` sets the target update rate, which defaults to 60 updates per second; the function returns the process exit code.
- Constructs the app as the scene root, registers its `update()` and `exit()` at `EventPriority::App` (100), then calls `setup()` once. Each fixed step notifies `events().update`: BeforeApp → App::update() → AfterApp. Equal priorities use registration order; explicit 100 listeners registered before the runner precede the App, and those registered in setup follow it. The App registration survives `clear()`. There is no draw or traversal of child nodes, mods, or node timers.
- Updates use a fixed step, so `getDeltaTime()` is `1 / settings.targetFps`. Each loop pass runs at most `setMaxUpdateSteps()` steps, with a default limit of 10; a nonpositive limit removes the cap.
- Excess whole steps after a stall or slow update are discarded with a one-time warning. Between passes, the loop sleeps until the next step is due, requesting at most 1 ms of sleep.
- The runner's thread is used as the main thread, and queued `runOnMainThread` callbacks are processed between update passes.
- On exit, notifies `events().exit` once: BeforeApp → App::exit() → AfterApp shutdown hooks. Mandatory framework teardown survives `events().exit.clear()` in App::exit(). Then it detaches the app's audio callbacks, waits for running callbacks, and calls `cleanup()`. The audio device remains running.
- Update-event services now work headless: Tween, update-mode TcpClient/UdpSocket receive, tcxBox2d auto stepping, and WebSocket timeouts.
- Known issue: [#906](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/906) (headless updates call only the app's `update()`, leaving child, mod, and timer updates unprocessed).

```cpp
int main() {
    return runHeadlessApp<tcApp>();
}
```

## runOnMainThread

- `runOnMainThread(fn)` runs immediately when called on the main thread; otherwise, it queues the callback and returns without waiting. Empty callbacks are ignored.
- The windowed loop processes queued work before update and draw; the headless loop processes it between update passes. Each pass takes the queued work as one batch and executes it in order.
- Worker submissions during batch execution wait for the next pass. A callback that calls `runOnMainThread` from the main thread executes the new callback immediately.
- `runOnMainThread(fn, weakToken)` accepts a `weak_ptr<atomic<bool>>` liveness token, as used by `Deliver::Main`. At execution time, an expired token or a value of `false` causes the callback to be discarded.
- The token does not wait for a callback already running. Serialize destruction of the target with callback delivery, normally on the main thread; without a token, the caller must keep captured objects alive until execution.
- The queue has no size limit, and the single-argument form does not discard callbacks. Producers that can discard values should use their own bounded buffer or retain only the latest value.
- On Web, both forms execute immediately; the two-argument form still checks its token. `tc_get_health` reports the latest batch's starting count as `mainQueuePending`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    runOnMainThread([this] { setVisible(true); });
}
```

## sameSubnet

- Takes IPv4 strings `a`, `b`, and `netmask`, such as `"192.168.1.10"`, `"192.168.1.20"`, and `"255.255.255.0"`. Returns whether their parsed values satisfy `(a & netmask) == (b & netmask)`.
- Uses the IPv4 text format described in `isPrivate`. Returns `false` if any argument cannot be parsed, including IPv6 addresses, hostnames, and CIDR notation such as `"/24"`.
- Does not require the mask to have contiguous set bits. A mask of `"0.0.0.0"` returns `true` for any two valid IPv4 addresses.

## saveDialog

- Arguments are `title`, `message`, `defaultPath` for the initial directory, and `defaultName` for the initial filename; all default to empty values.
- Returns `FileDialogResult` with `success = true`, the full `filePath`, and `fileName` after selection. Cancellation or failure returns `success = false` with empty paths.
- Selects a destination without writing the file. Check `success`, then save data to `filePath` with a file-writing API.
- Threading and blocking behavior follow `alertDialog`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto result = saveDialog("Save text", "", {}, "notes.txt");
    if (result.success) {
        saveTextFile(result.filePath, "Hello, TrussC!\n");
    }
}
```

## saveDialogAsync

- Takes `title`, `message`, `defaultPath`, `defaultName`, and `callback`, with no default arguments; `defaultPath` is the initial directory and `defaultName` is the initial filename.
- Pass `{}` for an unspecified directory or filename; paths are passed to the platform picker without resolution through `getDataPath()`.
- On desktop platforms, selects a destination without writing your data; after a successful result, write the data to `result.filePath`.
- On iOS, exports an empty temporary file named `defaultName`, or `"untitled"` when empty, and reports the export destination; it removes the temporary file after the callback.
- The `void(const FileDialogResult&)` callback receives `success = true`, the destination `filePath`, and its `fileName` on selection, or an empty unsuccessful result on cancellation or failure; a missing iOS root view controller logs an error and supplies an empty result.
- See `loadDialogAsync` for result reference lifetime and the shared iOS picker restriction, and `alertDialogAsync` for threading, callback timing, and app run lifetime rules.

## saveJson

- Call `saveJson(j, path, indent = 2)` with the JSON value first. Nonnegative `indent` sets the number of spaces per indentation level; any negative value produces compact output.
- Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`, absolute paths are used directly, and missing parent folders are created. Paths inside the app bundle on macOS and iOS return `SaveError::AccessDenied`; use `getUserDataPath()` for writable application data.
- Returns `SaveResult`, which can be checked with `if (result)` or `result.ok()`. Serialization exceptions derived from `exception` are logged as Errors and returned as `SaveError::WriteFailed`.
- Writes to `<file>.tmp`, checks the write, flush, and close, then renames the temporary file to replace the destination. Failures preserve the previous destination and attempt to remove a temporary file that was opened; failures are logged as Errors.
- The temporary filename is fixed, so simultaneous saves to the same destination share it. Atomic replacement does not guarantee durability after power loss.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json settings = {{"enabled", true}, {"count", 3}};
    auto result = saveJson(settings, getUserDataPath("settings.json"));
    if (!result) logError() << result.message;
}
```

## saveScreenshot

- Call from main-thread setup, update, draw, or event callbacks. Captures the current window's completed frame after `present()`, even when called while drawing into an Fbo.
- Returns `true` when the destination is prepared and capture is queued, not when the file is written. Native platforms check the path and create missing parent folders before returning; an empty path or preparation failure returns `false`.
- Native relative paths resolve against the data folder. Paths inside an application bundle on macOS/iOS are refused with an Error directing you to `getUserDataPath()`.
- Native capture and encoding run later during frame processing; the checked write uses a temporary file and replacement, and a write failure logs one Error.
- A request ensures a frame in the main window even when event-driven rendering is idle. Secondary-window requests wait for that window's next rendered frame.

```cpp
void tcApp::keyPressed(int key) {
    if (key == 'S') saveScreenshot("screenshot.png");
}
```

## saveTextFile

- `saveTextFile(path, content)` saves all bytes of `content` in binary mode without changing line endings or embedded null bytes. Returns `SaveResult`; use `if (result)` to test success or `result.ok()` when a `bool` value is required.
- `saveTextFile`, `appendToFile`, and `FileWriter::open` resolve relative paths through `getDataPath()`, keep absolute paths unchanged, and create missing parent directories. Empty paths, paths without a filename, and directory destinations return a failed `SaveResult`.
- These writers refuse paths inside an app bundle on macOS and iOS with `SaveError::AccessDenied` and an Error naming `getUserDataPath()`. Use `getUserDataPath("name.txt")` for files the app writes and keeps.
- Writes to `<file>.tmp`, checks the write, flush, and close, then renames the temporary file to replace the destination. An existing destination must be a regular file; the previous file is preserved if writing, closing, or replacement fails.
- Reported failures log an Error and return a failed `SaveResult`. If the temporary file was opened, failure cleanup attempts to remove it. The fixed temporary name is shared by saves to the same path.
- Atomic replacement does not guarantee durability after power loss. For appending directly to an existing file, use `appendToFile()`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto result = saveTextFile(getUserDataPath("notes.txt"), "Hello\n");
    if (!result) logError() << result.message;
}
```

## scale

- `scale(s)` scales X and Y uniformly (Z stays 1); `scale(sx, sy)` scales X and Y independently (Z stays 1); `scale(sx, sy, sz)` scales all three axes independently.
- Scaling happens around the current origin, so it also scales any later `translate()` offsets; call `translate()` first to pick the point that stays fixed, or scale first if you want the origin itself to move by the scaled amount.
- `getScale()` reads back the effective uniform scale of the current matrix (the larger of the X/Y basis lengths), which is what curve tessellation (see `drawCurve`) uses to keep circles smooth at any zoom level.
- Negative scale values flip the drawing along that axis (a cheap way to mirror a shape).

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    pushMatrix();
    translate(200, 200);  // fixed point stays put
    scale(2.0f);          // drawing after this is doubled in size
    drawRect(0, 0, 50, 50);
    popMatrix();
}
```

## scopedMatrix

- `auto m = scopedMatrix();` immediately calls `pushMatrix()` and returns a `MatrixScope` guard; when that guard goes out of scope — including an early `return` or a thrown exception — it calls `popMatrix()` automatically.
- Useful in functions with several exit points or long blocks, where a plain `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()` pair is easy to mismatch; `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()` remain the main, more common form.
- Marked `[[nodiscard]]`: writing `scopedMatrix();` alone, without storing the guard in a variable, pops immediately (the temporary is destroyed at the end of the statement) and is a compiler warning, since it does nothing useful.
- The guard cannot be copied or moved, so it cannot be returned or stored outside the scope it was created in.
- C++ only: Lua has no scope-bound guard, so in Lua use `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    auto m = scopedMatrix();   // pushMatrix() now
    translate(100, 100);
    if (!visible) return;     // popMatrix() still runs
    drawRect(0, 0, 50, 50);
}   // popMatrix() runs here too
```

## scopedStyle

- `auto s = scopedStyle();` calls `pushStyle()` immediately and returns a `StyleScope` guard. The guard calls `popStyle()` when it goes out of scope, whether the block ends normally, returns early, or throws an exception.
- It is meant for code with several exits or long blocks, where a plain `popStyle()` is easy to forget. For everyday code, `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` remain the usual form.
- Always assign the result to a named variable. The guard is marked `[[nodiscard]]`, so writing `scopedStyle();` alone causes a compiler warning, and the style is popped again right away.
- This is C++ only. Lua has no scope guard, so Lua code uses `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` directly.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    auto s = scopedStyle();
    setColor(0, 1, 0);
    if (!shouldDraw) return;  // style still pops here automatically
    drawCircle(50, 50, 20);
}
```

## screenToWorld

- `screenToWorld(screenPos, worldZ = 0.0f)` returns a `Vec3` where the screen ray intersects the plane `z = worldZ`; `worldZ` is a world coordinate, not normalized depth.
- Screen coordinates start at the top-left, with Y increasing downward. See `worldToScreen` for camera selection, coordinate units, and model-transform handling.
- Unprojects points at the near plane and an intermediate depth using the active backend's depth convention, then intersects their line with the plane. Intersections behind the near point are not rejected.
- If either unprojected homogeneous coordinate has `abs(w) < 1e-7f`, returns `(screenPos.x, screenPos.y, worldZ)`. If `abs(rayDir.z) < 0.0001f`, returns the near point's X and Y with Z replaced by `worldZ`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    Vec3 point = screenToWorld(getMousePos());
    drawCircle(point.x, point.y, 5.0f);
}
```

## setBeepVolume

- Set the volume used to generate beep sounds, clamping values below `0.0f` to `0.0f` and values above `1.0f` to `1.0f`.
- Every call clears the sound cache and stops its playing sounds, even if the volume is unchanged. Later calls to `beep` generate sounds at the new volume.
- See `beep` for shared state and threading rules.

## setBitmapLineHeight

- Changes the pixel distance between lines for every `\n` in `drawBitmapString` from then on, and for the height returned by `getBitmapStringHeight()`. It does not affect `getBitmapStringBounds()`, which always measures multi-line height using the font's fixed default height regardless of this setting.
- Takes effect immediately and stays in effect until changed again or restored by `popStyle()` (it is saved and restored together with color and other style state by `pushStyle()`/`popStyle()`).

## setBlendMode

- `setBlendMode()` chooses how new drawing is combined with what is already on the target. The modes are `BlendMode::Alpha` (the default, normal alpha blending), `Add` (additive), `Multiply`, `Screen`, `Subtract`, and `Disabled` (no blending; the new color simply overwrites the old one).
- The mode stays in effect until you change it. It works the same way on the main window and inside an `Fbo`, it carries over to later frames, and it is passed on to a later `Fbo::begin()`. A forgotten `Add` or `Multiply` can therefore affect drawing you did not intend. When you are done with a temporary mode, call `resetBlendMode()` or wrap the change in `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()`.
- With `Add`, the resulting RGB is `sourceRGB * sourceAlpha + destinationRGB` (RGB factors `SRC_ALPHA` and `ONE`). With `Screen`, the source RGB is multiplied by its alpha first, and the RGB factors are `ONE` and `ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR`.
- For the output alpha, `Alpha`, `Multiply` and `Screen` use `sourceAlpha + destinationAlpha * (1 - sourceAlpha)` (alpha factors `ONE` and `ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`). For example, drawing twice with alpha `0.5` on a transparent target gives `0.75`. `Add` and `Subtract` add the two alpha values (alpha factors `ONE` and `ONE`). `Disabled` overwrites without blending.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setBlendMode(BlendMode::Add);
    drawCircle(100, 100, 50);
    resetBlendMode();  // back to Alpha before drawing anything else
}
```

## setCameraPosition

- Accepts a `Vec3` or `x, y, z` in world coordinates and stores it in the current render target's camera state for specular and PBR view-vector calculations.
- This function does not change the view or projection matrix. A newly initialized camera state uses `(0, 0, 0)`.
- The value follows render-target and camera scopes rather than a single global setting; `getCameraPosition()` reads the current value.

## setCircleResolution

- This is an old name kept so that existing code still builds. Using it shows a deprecation warning at compile time, and it is scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.
- It does the same as `setCurveResolution(res)`: circles, arcs and other curves are drawn with a fixed number of segments. In new code, call `setCurveResolution()`, or `setCurveTolerance()` if you want the quality to adapt to the size and scale of each shape.
- The value set here is returned by `getCurveResolution()`, and also by the deprecated `getCircleResolution()`.

## setClipboardString

- Pass a UTF-8 string; the function returns `void` and provides no success status.
- The clipboard buffer defaults to 65,536 bytes and is configured with `WindowSettings::setClipboardSize`. Text at least that many bytes logs a truncation warning, but actual behavior varies: Linux with desktop GL rejects oversized text, while Linux with GLES logs an additional Error, still attempts to take clipboard ownership, and truncates text to the buffer capacity minus one byte; macOS limits its local buffer, and Windows can reject text that does not fit its conversion buffer.
- On Web, call from a user input event handler to request a browser copy. On iOS and Android, only the internal clipboard buffer is updated; the system clipboard is not written.

```cpp
void tcApp::keyPressed(int key) {
    if (key == 'C') setClipboardString("Hello from TrussC");
}
```

## setColor

- TrussC colors use float channels in the 0-1 range instead of 0-255; `setColor(1, 0, 0)` is pure red. There are three overloads: `setColor(r, g, b, a = 1)`, grayscale `setColor(gray, a = 1)`, and `setColor(const Color&)`, which also accepts the named colors in the `colors` namespace (`colors::white`, `colors::crimson`, ...).
- This color applies to both fill and stroke: whichever of `fill()` / `noFill()` is active decides which one is actually drawn, but both use the same current color until you call `setColor` again.
- `setColorHSB`, `setColorOKLCH`, and `setColorOKLab` set the same underlying color from a different color space; after any of them, `getColor()` returns the equivalent sRGB value, not the original HSB/OKLCH/OKLab numbers.
- The color you set stays in effect until the next `setColor*` call. `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` save and restore it along with the rest of the drawing style.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setColor(1.0f, 0.3f, 0.3f);      // red-ish, 0-1 floats
    drawRect(20, 20, 100, 60);
    setColor(colors::skyBlue);       // named color
    drawCircle(200, 60, 30);
}
```

## setColorHSB

- All three channels are 0-1: hue is one full turn (0 = 0°, 1 = 360°, wrapping back to red), saturation 0 is gray and 1 is fully saturated, and brightness 0 is black and 1 is the brightest version of that hue. Alpha defaults to 1.
- This sets the same underlying drawing color as `setColor`; see `setColor` for how it applies to fill/stroke and the style stack. After calling this, `getColor()` returns the converted sRGB value, not the original H/S/B numbers.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    float hue = fmodf(getElapsedTime() * 0.1f, 1.0f); // cycles through hues
    setColorHSB(hue, 0.8f, 1.0f);
    drawCircle(getWidth() / 2, getHeight() / 2, 50);
}
```

## setColorOKLCH

- OKLCH is a perceptually uniform color space, useful when you want equal numeric steps to look like equal visual steps (for gradients, palettes, or animating lightness without the color looking like it changes hue). `L` (lightness) is 0-1, `C` (chroma, how saturated) is roughly 0-0.4 depending on hue and lightness, and `H` (hue) is one full turn, 0-1 (0 = 0°, 1 = 360°) and wraps around outside that range. Alpha defaults to 1.
- Not every L/C/H combination maps to a displayable color; out-of-range results are not clamped here, so very high chroma can produce colors outside 0-1 sRGB.
- This sets the same underlying drawing color as `setColor`; see `setColor` for how it applies to fill/stroke and the style stack.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    // same lightness and chroma, different hue
    setColorOKLCH(0.7f, 0.15f, 0.3f);
    drawRect(0, 0, 100, 100);
}
```

## setColorOKLab

- OKLab is the Cartesian form of the same perceptually uniform space as OKLCH: instead of chroma and hue, it uses two axes, `a` (green-red) and `b` (blue-yellow). `L` (lightness) is 0-1, and `a`/`b` are each roughly in the -0.4 to 0.4 range; (0, 0) is gray at that lightness. Alpha defaults to 1. `setColorOKLCH(L, C, H)` sets the same color as `setColorOKLab(L, C * cos(H * TAU), C * sin(H * TAU))`.
- Not every L/a/b combination maps to a displayable color; out-of-range results are not clamped here.
- This sets the same underlying drawing color as `setColor`; see `setColor` for how it applies to fill/stroke and the style stack.

## setConsoleLogLevel

- Sets the global logger's console threshold; messages below it are omitted. The initial value is `LogLevel::Notice`, and `LogLevel::Silent` disables console output.
- Changes only the console threshold, including `os_log` on iOS and logcat on Android; a later `setLogLevel()` overwrites it.
- See `Logger` for all output destinations, listener delivery and threading rules.

## setCursor

- Pass a `Cursor` value such as `Cursor::Hand`; custom slots require an image bound with `bindCursorImage` first. Changing the shape preserves cursor visibility.
- Cursor shape and visibility controls target the main window through sokol. Call them from main-thread callbacks; from a secondary-window context, `setCursor`, `showCursor`, and `hideCursor` each warn once and do nothing.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setCursor(Cursor::Crosshair);
}
```

## setCurveResolution

- Switches curve quality to resolution mode and sets the number of segments for a full circle. The stored value is 60 by default, but the default mode is tolerance mode (see `setCurveTolerance`). Calling `setCurveTolerance()` switches back to it.
- Every curved shape shares this setting: circles, ellipses, arcs, Bezier curves, `drawCurve()` curves and rounded rectangles. An arc uses a share of the count in proportion to its angle, and each Bezier or `drawCurve()` piece is split into this many segments (at least 2).
- It is useful for a deliberately low-poly look, or to put a hard limit on the vertex count when you draw many small shapes, whatever their radius.
- In resolution mode, `drawCircle()` uses at least 3 segments, so `setCurveResolution(1)` draws a triangle.
- `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` save and restore it.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setCurveResolution(8);  // chunky, low-poly circles
    drawCircle(100, 100, 50);
}
```

## setCurveTolerance

- Switches curve quality to tolerance mode (the default) and sets how far, in on-screen pixels, the drawn polygon may stray from the true curve. The default is 0.1 pixels. Calling `setCurveResolution()` switches to a fixed segment count instead.
- A smaller value gives smoother curves with more segments. The segment count follows the shape's radius and the current scale, so a large or zoomed-in circle automatically gets more segments, and a small one gets fewer.
- In this mode a full circle uses between 6 and 1024 segments.
- The scale comes from the current transform, such as `scale()`. Camera perspective is not taken into account.
- `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` save and restore it.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setCurveTolerance(1.0f);  // looser (fewer segments) than the 0.1px default
    drawCircle(100, 100, 50);
}
```

## setDataPathRoot

- Store `path` as the root used by `getDataPath`. Relative roots are resolved against the executable directory; absolute roots, including Windows paths such as `C:/assets`, are used directly.
- An explicit root overrides automatic Apple folder selection. This call does not create the directory.
- See `getDataPathRoot` for threading rules; set the root before starting threads that load files.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setDataPathRoot("assets");
    auto path = getDataPath("settings.json");
}
```

## setDataPathToResources

- On macOS and iOS, calls `setDataPathRoot("../Resources/data/")`; on other platforms it does nothing. It takes no arguments and returns no value.
- The root is relative to the executable directory, pointing to `Contents/Resources/data` in a macOS app bundle. This explicit setting overrides automatic data-folder selection.
- On iOS, this path points outside the flat app bundle and overrides automatic selection of the bundled `data` folder beside the executable.
- Call it before starting threads that load files, for example in `setup()`; see `setDataPathRoot` for the shared path-root rules.

## setUserDataPathRoot

- Set the root returned by `getUserDataPath`, for example to separate installations, app instances, or tests. Relative roots are resolved against the executable directory, as with `setDataPathRoot`; absolute roots are used directly.
- The setter does not create the directory; creation occurs when `getUserDataPath` next resolves a relative or empty path. See `getUserDataPath` for shared initialization and threading rules.
- On macOS and iOS, a root inside the app bundle is not created and `saveJson` and `FileWriter` still refuse writes there.

## setDefaultScreenFov

- Accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovRadians < TAU/2` for perspective projection in radians. The initial default is `TAU/8`, or 45 degrees.
- Stores the default applied at frame start; it does not change the current projection immediately. Use `setupScreenFov` for the current projection, or `setupScreenOrtho()` and `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for explicit orthographic setup and defaults.
- Invalid values warn once and are ignored, preserving both the stored default and the current projection.

## setDefaultScreenFovDeg

- Accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovDeg < 180` for perspective projection; invalid values produce a one-time warning and leave the default unchanged.
- This is the degree version of `setDefaultScreenFov`; see that entry for when the default is applied.
- Use `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for an orthographic default or `setupScreenOrtho()` to change the current projection.

## setDefaultScreenOrtho

- Equivalent to `setDefaultScreenFov(0)`; subsequent screen frames start with orthographic projection, and `getDefaultScreenFov()` returns `0`.
- The current projection is unchanged; use `setupScreenOrtho()` to change it immediately.
- `Fbo::begin()` uses its own 45° projection regardless of this setting; call `setupScreenOrtho()` after beginning the FBO when needed.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setDefaultScreenOrtho();
}
```

## setEnvironment

- Takes `Environment&` and stores its address for subsequent PBR mesh draws in the current window; other windows retain their own selections.
- Does not load the environment or check `isLoaded()` when selecting it; PBR uses IBL only when the selected environment reports loaded.
- Ownership, lifetime, and threading rules are described under `Environment`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    static Environment environment;
    if (environment.loadProcedural()) {
        setEnvironment(environment);
    }
}
```

## setFarClip

- Stores a far clipping distance in drawing coordinate units; a positive value is used when a screen projection helper receives `farDist = 0`.
- The initial value is `0`; a nonpositive stored value selects automatic calculation as ten times the camera distance, and orthographic projection uses the range `-farDist` to `farDist`.
- This does not change the current projection. See `setNearClip` for the shared override behavior.

## setFileLogLevel

- Sets the global logger's file threshold; ordinary messages below it are omitted. The initial value is `LogLevel::Notice`, and `LogLevel::Silent` disables ordinary file output.
- Does not open or close a file; use `setLogFile()` to open one. A later `setLogLevel()` overwrites this threshold.
- See `Logger` for the runtime exit record exception, other outputs and threading rules.

## setFps

- Takes a target rate in fps. In the main window, `VSYNC` (-1) follows the refresh rate of the display containing the window and `EVENT_DRIVEN` (0) waits for a frame request such as `redraw()`. In a secondary window's callbacks, it sets that window's throttle; values at or below zero, including `EVENT_DRIVEN`, run at the display refresh rate without additional throttling. A fixed fps at or just above the display's refresh rate draws every display frame; a lower target reduces the update and draw rate. Under VSYNC the rate follows the display, so move things with `getDeltaTime()` rather than a fixed step per frame.
- Under `setFps`, `update()` and `draw()` are called together at the same rate; to run them at independent rates (for example a fast simulation with a slower draw, or the reverse), use `setIndependentFps()` instead.
- Switching the rate at runtime takes effect immediately from the moment of the call, with no catch-up: on a fixed fps the next frame is drawn right away, and the first `update()` after the switch has a `getDeltaTime()` that excludes time spent in the previous mode. Called between updates, the new timer starts from the call; called from inside an `update()`, it starts from that update's beginning. The time this drops is under one frame in the usual modes, and only grows larger after an idle period such as `EVENT_DRIVEN` waiting for a redraw.
- Calling `setFps` again with the rate it is already at does nothing, so it is safe to call every frame (for example from a GUI slider). On the one frame where the value actually changes, that update's `getDeltaTime()` is shorter than a normal frame, since it is measured only from the moment of the call.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setFps(60);        // fixed 60 fps
    // setFps(VSYNC);        // sync to the display's refresh rate
    // setFps(EVENT_DRIVEN); // redraw only on request
}
```

## setFullscreen

- Pass `true` to enter fullscreen or `false` to leave it; requesting the current state does nothing.
- Targets the main window in its context and the corresponding secondary window inside that window's callbacks.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setFullscreen(true);
}
```

## setImmersiveMode

- Pass true to hide system bars or false to restore them. The stored setting is initially false and is returned by `getImmersiveMode`.
- Android controls the status bar and, when the API 30 or later window-insets methods are available, the navigation bar. Hidden bars can appear temporarily after an edge swipe; enabling also allows drawing under the bars. Earlier devices retain status-bar-only behavior.
- iOS requests hiding the status bar and automatic hiding of the home indicator by updating the root view controller.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setImmersiveMode(true);
}
```

## setIndependentFps

- `updateFps` and `drawFps` independently accept a positive rate in frames per second or `VSYNC`; `VSYNC` updates or draws once per display tick.
- `EVENT_DRIVEN` disables independent updates when used for `updateFps`; for `drawFps`, it draws when `redraw()` is requested or a pending screenshot or deferred capture request forces a draw.
- A positive update rate runs fixed steps with `getDeltaTime() = 1 / updateFps`; drawing skips display ticks as needed and runs at most once per tick.
- Fixed updates are limited by `setMaxUpdateSteps()` to 10 steps per frame by default; excess time after a stall, slow updates, or an update rate above that multiple of the display rate is discarded with a one-time warning.
- Changing the update mode starts its timing again without catching up the previous mode. A fixed rate runs one step on the next frame; its duration can exceed or fall short of the actual time since the last update, such as about 9.7 ms extra when switching from 144 Hz updates to fixed 60 Hz updates.
- Entering `VSYNC` discards the time since the previous update, usually less than a frame but potentially longer after `EVENT_DRIVEN` idle. Its next measured delta starts at the call, or at the current update's start if called inside an update; changing the update mode inside a fixed step also cancels the remaining old steps in that frame.
- Reapplying the same independent rates does nothing. Changing only `drawFps` preserves update timing; a changed positive draw rate draws on the next frame.
- Switching from synchronized `setFps()` to independent updates counts as an update-mode change even at the same rate; `setFps(VSYNC)` followed by `setIndependentFps(VSYNC, 30)` can discard up to a frame.
- This function controls only the main window; calls from a secondary window's context warn once and are ignored. Use `setFps()` or `Window::setFps()` for a secondary window.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setIndependentFps(120, 60);
}
```

## setKeepScreenOn

- Pass true to request that the screen stay on, or false to release the request. The initial setting is false; `getKeepScreenOn` returns the stored state.
- Android sets the activity's keep-screen-on flag, iOS changes the idle-timer setting, and macOS creates or releases a display-sleep assertion. Windows requests both display and system wakefulness.
- iOS applies the change asynchronously on the main queue, so the getter can reflect the request before the OS setting changes.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setKeepScreenOn(true);
}
```

## setLogFile

- Takes an `fs::path` and opens it in append mode, preserving existing contents. Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`, absolute paths are used directly, and missing parent folders are created.
- Returns a `SaveResult` for path preparation and opening; use `if (setLogFile(path))` or `.ok()` to check it. See `SaveResult` for conversion to bool.
- On success, replaces the previous log file and makes `getLogger().getLogFilePath()` return the resolved path. On failure, preserves the current file and logs an Error; that error also reaches the current file if its threshold permits.
- Paths inside an app bundle on macOS and iOS are rejected with a failed result and an error suggesting `getUserDataPath()`.
- Subsequent log lines are appended directly, and each write and flush is checked. The first failure closes the file, clears its path and reports an Error through the logger; the successful open result does not guarantee later writes.
- Like Logger, `FileWriter` stops writing and reports an Error on its first write or flush failure; its `write()` returns `FileWriter&`, while `flush()` and `close()` return no value.
- See `Logger` for file filtering, environment configuration and threading rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (setLogFile(getUserDataPath("logs/app.log"))) {
        logNotice() << "Log file opened";
    }
}
```

## setLogLevel

- Sets the global logger's console, file and system thresholds to the supplied `LogLevel`, replacing their previous settings.
- A later `setConsoleLogLevel()`, `setFileLogLevel()` or `setSystemLogLevel()` changes only its own output. There is no `getLogLevel()` because the three thresholds can differ.
- See `Logger` for filtering, defaults, platform differences and threading rules.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setLogLevel(LogLevel::Warning);
    setFileLogLevel(LogLevel::Verbose);
    setSystemLogLevel(LogLevel::Silent);
}
```

## setMaxUpdateSteps

- Sets the fixed-update limit per frame for `setIndependentFps()` and per loop pass for `runHeadlessApp()`; the default is `10`.
- Time beyond the limit is discarded with a one-time warning when steps accumulate after a stall, when updates are too slow, or when the update rate exceeds this multiple of the display rate.
- A value of `0` or less removes the limit and runs every pending step, which can support deterministic simulations but can freeze processing while a long stall is replayed or make passes grow while updates remain too slow.
- The setting is stored atomically and is shared by the hot-reload host and guest.

## setMaterial

- Accepts a `Material&` and selects it in the current window. Ordinary `Mesh::draw()` uses GPU PBR when the mesh has a normal for every vertex; point meshes use their separate drawing path.
- Selection stores the object's address without copying or owning it. Keep it at a stable address while selected; subsequent draws read its current values. Destroying it clears matching selections in all window contexts.
- The selection persists until another material is selected or `clearMaterial()` is called; clearing does not restore an earlier selection.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    Material material = Material::gold();
    Mesh mesh = createBox(100);
    setMaterial(material);
    mesh.draw();
    clearMaterial();
}
```

## setMatrix

- Sets the current matrix to `mat` directly, discarding whatever `translate()` / `rotate()` / `scale()` / `multMatrix()` had built up — an absolute replacement, unlike `multMatrix()` which builds on top of the existing matrix.
- The active camera's view/projection is kept as-is; only the model matrix is replaced, so drawing still goes through the current camera correctly.
- Anything already saved on the matrix stack by `pushMatrix()` is unaffected and still restored normally by a later `popMatrix()`.
- `loadMatrix()` is a deprecated alias for the same function.

## setNearClip

- Stores a near clipping distance in drawing coordinate units; the initial value is `0`. Screen projection helpers use a positive stored override when their corresponding distance argument is `0`; an explicit nonzero argument takes precedence.
- A nonpositive stored value selects automatic calculation: near distance is one tenth of the camera distance, and far distance is ten times that distance. Orthographic projection does not use the near distance.
- Near and far overrides are shared across screen and FBO projection setup. Setters store values without validation and do not change the current projection; the next projection setup uses them.

## setOrientation
