- Pass an `Orientation` mask such as `Portrait`, `Landscape`, or `All`. Individual flags include `PortraitUpsideDown`, `LandscapeLeft`, and `LandscapeRight`; combine flags with `|`.
- iOS uses the mask as its supported orientations. Android maps it to an activity orientation request and does nothing if no native activity is available.
- Android checks combinations in this order: all four directions, portrait plus both landscape directions, both portrait directions, both landscape directions, then individual directions. Mixed masks use the first matching case.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setOrientation(Orientation::Landscape);
}
```

## setSystemLogLevel

- Sets the global logger's system threshold; messages below it are omitted. The initial value is `LogLevel::Notice`, and `LogLevel::Silent` disables this output.
- Applies to `os_log` on macOS and `OutputDebugStringW` on Windows; it has no output effect on iOS, Android, Linux or web. Use `setConsoleLogLevel()` for the OS log on iOS and Android.
- A later `setLogLevel()` overwrites this threshold; see `Logger` for viewers, Xcode suppression, encoding limitations, output cost and threading rules.

## setScissor

- Only the pixels inside the rectangle are drawn. It uses the same pixel coordinates as `pushScissor`; see `pushScissor` for units and DPI.
- Unlike `pushScissor()`, it saves nothing and is not intersected with the current rectangle. A later `popScissor()` replaces it with the saved rectangle.
- There are `int` and `float` versions. Pass all four values as the same type.
- For nested areas, or inside nodes, use `pushScissor()` / `popScissor()`. For a node's own area, `RectNode::setClipping(true)` is simpler.
- Known issue: [#914](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/914) (the rectangle is given in render-target pixels, unlike other drawing functions).

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    float s = getDpiScale();
    setScissor(0.0f, 0.0f, getWidth() / 2 * s, getHeight() * s);   // left half only
    drawCircle(getWidth() / 2, getHeight() / 2, 200);
    resetScissor();
}
```

## setSelectedNode

- Pass a `Node*` to select it in the current window, or `nullptr` to clear selection; a node not owned by a `shared_ptr` also clears selection.
- It stores `weak_from_this()` without taking ownership and returns no value. Selection lookup and pointer lifetime follow `getSelectedNode`.

## setStrokeCap

- Controls how the open ends of a stroked line or path are drawn, as one of the `StrokeCap` enum values:
- `StrokeCap::Butt` — cut flat at the endpoint (default).
- `StrokeCap::Round` — a semicircle extending past the endpoint.
- `StrokeCap::Square` — extended by half the stroke width past the endpoint.
- `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` save and restore this along with the rest of the drawing style.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    noFill();
    setStrokeWeight(8.0f);
    setStrokeCap(StrokeCap::Round);
    drawLine(20, 20, 150, 20);
}
```

## setStrokeJoin

- Controls how corners between segments of a stroked path are drawn, as one of the `StrokeJoin` enum values:
- `StrokeJoin::Miter` — pointed, sharp corners (default). Very sharp angles can extend far past the corner; `StrokeMesh::setMiterLimit` bounds that.
- `StrokeJoin::Round` — rounded corners.
- `StrokeJoin::Bevel` — flat, cut-off corners.
- `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` save and restore this along with the rest of the drawing style.

## setPointSize

- Sets the size of each point when a mesh is drawn with `PrimitiveMode::Points`. It is the point-cloud counterpart of `setStrokeWeight()`. The default is 1.
- The unit is **logical pixels**, the same as the stroke weight, so points look the same size on any display density.
- It applies to the `Square` and `Round` point styles (see `PointStyle`). `Pixel` always draws true 1-pixel points and ignores this size.
- `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` save and restore it.
- The projection, view and model matrices of the current target move the point centers, but scaling with the model matrix does not make the points larger.
- Inside an Fbo, the size is measured in the Fbo's own pixels, regardless of the window's display density or pixelPerfect.

## getPointSize

- Returns the value last set with `setPointSize()`. The default is 1, in logical pixels like `setStrokeWeight()`.
- The value is saved and restored by `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()`, and `resetStyle()` sets it back to 1.

## setPointStyle

- Chooses how a mesh drawn with `PrimitiveMode::Points` looks. The shapes are listed in `PointStyle`, and all of them are drawn on the GPU.
- `Square` is the default and the lightest to draw. `Square` and `Round` draw a small square or disc that faces the camera, and `setPointSize()` sets its size.
- `Pixel` draws true 1-pixel points and ignores the point size entirely.
- `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` save and restore it.

## getPointStyle

- Returns the shape last set with `setPointStyle()`. The default is `PointStyle::Square`.
- The value is saved and restored by `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()`, and `resetStyle()` sets it back to `PointStyle::Square`.

## setStrokeWeight

- Sets the width, in logical pixels, used when drawing shape outlines (`noFill()` mode) via `StrokeMesh`. Default is 1.0.
- `drawLine()` is not affected by this setting: it always draws a fixed 1px line regardless of `setStrokeWeight()`.
- `pushStyle()` / `popStyle()` save and restore this along with the rest of the drawing style.
- Known issue: [#915](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/915) (drawLine() ignores it).

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    noFill();
    setStrokeWeight(5.0f);
    drawCircle(100, 100, 40);
}
```

## setSystemBrightness

- macOS and iOS clamp `brightness` to 0.0–1.0 before applying it to the main display or screen. For the meaning of brightness values, see `getSystemBrightness`.
- macOS uses a private CoreDisplay API; iOS sets the main screen brightness directly.

## setSystemVolume

- Accepts `volume` from 0.0 to 1.0. macOS clamps it to this range and sets the default output device's volume.
- Android multiplies the value by the maximum music-stream volume, truncates it to an integer, clamps it to the supported steps and applies it without showing the system volume UI.
- Does nothing if the required output device or Android audio service is unavailable; no success result is returned.

## setTextAlign

- Sets the horizontal anchor `h` (`Left`, `Center`, or `Right`) and vertical anchor `v` (`Top`, `Center`, `Bottom`, or `Baseline`) used by every `drawBitmapString` overload and by `drawBitmapStringHighlight` for the (x, y) position passed to them. The default is `(Left, Top)`.
- The horizontal anchor is measured against each string's own width at draw time, so it follows the text as its content changes between calls; for multi-line text it aligns the whole block to its widest line (see `drawBitmapString`).
- The vertical anchor of `drawBitmapString` does not grow with the number of lines: `Center` and `Bottom` always use a single line's height (16px), not the full height of a multi-line string. For example, with `Bottom` only the first line ends at y, and the remaining lines extend below it.
- `Baseline` positions (x, y) at the character baseline (a fixed offset above the glyph's bottom, not affected by `setBitmapLineHeight()`), matching how most text editors and other font APIs place a baseline.
- This value is part of the saved drawing style, so it is captured and restored by `pushStyle()`/`popStyle()`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setTextAlign(Center, Center);
    drawBitmapString("CENTERED", getWidth() / 2, getHeight() / 2);
}
```

## setTouchAsMouse

- Enabled by default on all platforms; pass `false` to disable mouse events generated from touch input, including on Android and iOS.
- Only the first finger drives the left mouse button: touch begin generates a press, movement generates a drag, and ending or cancelling that touch generates a release.
- The finger used for mouse input is identified by its ID, so changing the order of `touches` does not switch it to `touches[0]`.
- Touch events are delivered before the corresponding mouse events and remain enabled when this setting is `false`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setTouchAsMouse(false);
}
```

## setWindowDecorated

- Pass `false` to hide the title bar, borders, and window buttons, or `true` to restore standard decorations; keyboard focus and programmatic closing remain available.
- Always targets the main window, including calls from a secondary window's callbacks; it can be changed at runtime.

## setWindowPosition

- Sets the outer window frame's top-left position to `(x, y)`. For coordinate units and the macOS screen conversion, see `getWindowPosition`.
- Does nothing when no native window is available. On Windows, moving the window does not resize it, activate it or change its stacking order.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setWindowPosition(100, 100);
}
```

## setWindowSize

- `width` and `height` specify the content size in logical pixels, or framebuffer pixels when `pixelPerfect` is enabled.
- In pixel-perfect mode, dimensions are divided by the target window's DPI scale and truncated to integers before resizing.
- Targets the main window in its context and the corresponding secondary window inside that window's callbacks; `setWindowSizeLogical()` always targets the main window.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setWindowSize(1280, 720);
}
```

## setWindowSizeLogical

- `width` and `height` specify the content size in logical pixels without the `pixelPerfect` conversion performed by `setWindowSize()`.
- Always targets the main window, including calls from a secondary window's callbacks.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setWindowSizeLogical(1280, 720);
}
```

## setWindowTitle

- Pass the title as a string; calls inside a secondary window's callbacks change that window's title, while the main context changes the main window's title.
- In development builds, the main window title receives an ` [MCP]` suffix unless it already contains `[MCP]`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    setWindowTitle("TrussC Sketch");
}
```

## setup

- Initializes `sokol_gfx` and `sokol_gl`, prepares the main drawing target, and creates the initial drawing pipelines and bitmap-font sampler.
- `runApp()` calls this free function automatically on the main thread before user setup; override the callback described in `App` to initialize your application.
- For a manually managed graphics lifecycle, call it with a valid graphics environment and pair it with `cleanup()`; `runHeadlessApp()` does not initialize this graphics backend.

## setupScreenFov

- Pass `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovRadians < TAU / 2` for perspective projection; invalid values produce a warning once across the FOV helpers and leave the projection and default unchanged.
- Uses the active drawing target's size: FBO attachment pixels, or window logical pixels unless `pixelPerfect` is enabled. At `z = 0`, the origin is the upper-left corner, X increases rightward, and Y increases downward.
- Replaces the current projection and camera view while preserving the current model transform. The camera is centered above the drawing area and looks at `z = 0`; its distance is `viewH / (2 * tan(fovRadians / 2))`, using `TAU / 36` for that calculation in orthographic mode.
- `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0` and use drawing coordinate units; see `setNearClip` for overrides and automatic calculation. Orthographic projection uses the range `-farDist` to `farDist` and ignores `nearDist`.
- Updates the matrices used for coordinate conversion and picking. This changes the current target only; use `setDefaultScreenFov()` or `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for the screen default, and `setupScreenOrtho()` for an explicit orthographic call.
- Projection setup does nothing in headless mode.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setupScreenFov(TAU / 8);
    drawCircle(getWidth() * 0.5f, getHeight() * 0.5f, 40);
}
```

## setupScreenFovDeg

- Converts `fovDeg` to radians and calls `setupScreenFov`; accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovDeg < 180` for perspective projection.
- Invalid values warn once and are ignored; `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0`. See `setupScreenFov` for coordinates, clipping, and target behavior.
- Use `setupScreenOrtho()` for an explicit orthographic call or `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for an orthographic default.

## setupScreenFovWithSize

- `viewW` and `viewH` specify the drawing area's width and height in drawing coordinate units; they determine the projection and camera distance without resizing the target or changing its viewport.
- Accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovRadians < TAU / 2` for perspective projection. Invalid values warn once and leave the current projection and default unchanged.
- `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0`; see `setupScreenFov` for shared coordinates, clipping, transforms, and headless behavior.
- Use `setupScreenOrtho()` for orthographic projection with the active target's size, or `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for an orthographic screen default.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setupScreenFovWithSize(TAU / 8, 800, 600);
    drawCircle(400, 300, 40);
}
```

## setupScreenFovWithSizeDeg

- Converts `fovDeg` to radians and calls `setupScreenFovWithSize`; accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovDeg < 180` for perspective projection.
- Invalid values warn once and are ignored; `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0`. See `setupScreenFovWithSize` for dimensions and shared projection behavior.
- Use `setupScreenOrtho()` for orthographic projection with the active target's size, or `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` for an orthographic screen default.

## setupScreenOrtho

- Equivalent to `setupScreenFov(0)`; sets a projection with the origin at the upper-left corner and Y increasing downward.
- See `setupScreenFov` for target dimensions, clipping, and transform behavior; use `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` to make orthographic projection the screen default.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setupScreenOrtho();
    drawCircle(100, 100, 40);
}
```

## setupScreenPerspective

- Calls `setupScreenFov` with a default field of view of `TAU / 8` radians, or 45°; `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0`.
- Also accepts `0` for orthographic projection; otherwise the valid range is `0 < fovRadians < TAU / 2`. Invalid values warn once and leave the projection and default unchanged.
- See `setupScreenFov` for camera placement, units, clipping, and target behavior; `setupScreenOrtho()` and `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` explicitly select orthographic setup and defaults.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    setupScreenPerspective();
    drawCircle(getWidth() * 0.5f, getHeight() * 0.5f, 40);
}
```

## setupScreenPerspectiveDeg

- Converts `fovDeg` to radians and calls `setupScreenPerspective`; the default is `45` degrees, and `nearDist` and `farDist` default to `0`.
- Accepts `0` for orthographic projection or `0 < fovDeg < 180` for perspective projection; invalid values warn once and are ignored.
- See `setupScreenPerspective` for shared behavior; `setupScreenOrtho()` and `setDefaultScreenOrtho()` explicitly select orthographic setup and defaults.

## shadowDraw

- Accepts `const Mesh&` and draws shadow depth using the current model transform, without evaluating materials. Mesh buffers are uploaded to the GPU as needed.
- Does nothing without an active shadow pass, for line meshes, or when no GPU vertex buffer is available. Calling while a child render target is active is rejected with a warning.
- Pass order, supported lights, and limits are described in `beginShadowPass`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    static Light light;
    light.enableShadow();
    addLight(light);
    Mesh mesh = createBox(100);
    beginShadowPass(light);
    shadowDraw(mesh); endShadowPass();
}
```

## shortTypeName

- Accepts a `type_info`, for example `shortTypeName(typeid(Node))`, and shortens the readable name obtained from `typeName`.
- Removes qualification before the outer type while preserving template arguments; `ns::Outer<a::B>` becomes `Outer<a::B>`.
- Returns a `const string&` cached per type in a mutex-protected cache that is never cleared. See `typeName` for readable-name conversion and RTTI behavior.

## showCursor

- Makes the cursor visible; it is visible by default.
- Only accepts calls from the main window's context; calls from a secondary window's context warn once and do nothing because cursor visibility is application-wide on macOS and the cursor API targets the main window.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    showCursor();
}
```

## shutdownAudio

- Closes the audio device, releases its device context, clears the audio meters, and marks the global `AudioEngine` as uninitialized.
- The windowed app loop calls it automatically during shutdown after application cleanup, so an explicit call is usually unnecessary; repeated calls are safe when the device is already closed.
- `runHeadlessApp()` leaves the audio device running when it returns; call this function explicitly when audio is no longer needed. See `AudioEngine` for threading rules.

## sign

- Takes a `float` and returns `-1.0f` for a negative value, `0.0f` for zero, or `1.0f` for a positive value.

## signedNoise

- Accepts one to four `float` coordinates, a `Vec2`, a `Vec3`, or three `float` coordinates followed by an `int` seed. Returns a `float` centered on zero, with a nominal range of -1–1; the result is not clamped.
- The one- and two-coordinate overloads sample 3D noise with omitted coordinates set to zero. One- through three-coordinate forms, including the seeded form, return zero when all supplied coordinates are integers.
- Coordinate units, seed selection, the four-coordinate approximation, determinism, and threading rules are described in `noise`.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    float offset = signedNoise(getElapsedTimef() * 0.2f) * 100.0f;
    drawCircle(200.0f + offset, 200.0f, 20.0f);
}
```

## sin

- `sin(angle)` takes an angle in radians, with `TAU` representing one full turn, and returns a value from `-1` to `1` for finite angles.
- This is the standard `<cmath>` function included by TrussC.

## sleepMicros

- Accepts the duration as an `int` number of microseconds.
- For blocking behavior and scheduling precision, see `sleepMillis`.

## sleepMillis

- Accepts the duration as an `int` number of milliseconds and suspends the calling thread using `this_thread::sleep_for`; the actual wait can be longer because of thread scheduling.
- On the application thread, sleeping also delays event handling and subsequent update and draw calls until the function returns. `sleepMicros()` has the same behavior with microsecond units.

## splitString

- `splitString(source, delimiter, ignoreEmpty, trim)` returns a `vector<string>` split at exact, case-sensitive matches of the entire delimiter; the input is unchanged.
- Both options default to `false`. With `trim = true`, remove spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and line feeds from both ends of each element before applying `ignoreEmpty`.
- By default, retain empty elements, including those caused by leading, trailing, or adjacent delimiters. An empty source produces one empty element unless `ignoreEmpty` is `true`.
- An empty delimiter always returns one element containing the unchanged source, bypassing both `trim` and `ignoreEmpty`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto names = splitString("red, green,, blue", ",", true, true);
    auto label = joinString(names, " / ");
}
```

## sq

- Takes a `float` and returns `value * value` as a `float`.

## sqrt

- `sqrt(x)` returns the nonnegative square root for a nonnegative `x`.
- This is the standard `<cmath>` function included by TrussC.

## srgbToLinear

- Takes and returns a single float channel (not a whole color): the inverse gamma step used when going from `Color` (sRGB) to `ColorLinear`, needed before physically-based math such as lighting, blending, or HDR work.
- Below 0.04045 it is a straight scale by 1/12.92; above that it is a power curve, matching the standard sRGB transfer function.
- Most apps never call this directly; `Color::toLinear()` applies it per channel for you.

## startRecording

- Use `startRecording(path, settings)` for the current window or `startRecording(fbo, path, settings)` for an Fbo. Capture runs automatically after frames, and the initial source dimensions determine the recording size. An Fbo records its own contents without window UI.
- Relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`, and missing parent directories are created. Recording uses native encoders without ffmpeg; defaults are H.264, 60 fps and no audio. See `VideoRecordSettings` for options.
- Instead of settings, pass a duration in seconds, such as `startRecording(path, 5.0f)`, or set `settings.duration`. Positive durations automatically stop and finalize when frame processing observes that elapsed wall time has reached the requested duration. Zero or negative durations record until stopped.
- Returns a `SaveResult` for path preparation and encoder opening. The file is written directly at its destination; successful opening does not guarantee successful finalization. Check the result of `stopRecording()` for completion.
- Calling again first stops the previous recording, then opens a new one; reusing its path overwrites the previous file. If GPU frames remain pending after the stop wait times out, it returns the failure without starting a new recording, and the old recording finalizes after its pending frames complete.
- The global recorder is shared across the process and binds to the window whose callbacks are active when recording starts. It automatically stops on that window's exit. Keep a recorded Fbo alive; destroying it causes recording to stop and finalize on the next frame.
- For shared capture behavior and costs, see `ScreenRecorder`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto result = startRecording("capture.mp4", 5.0f);
    if (!result) logError("Recording") << result.message;
}
```

## stopRecording

- Returns the `SaveResult` from the global recorder's `ScreenRecorder::stop()`. See that entry for completion waits, retained failures, repeated calls, and direct file finalization.
- See `isRecording` for the global recorder's scope.

```cpp
void tcApp::exit() {
    auto result = stopRecording();
    if (!result) logError() << result.message;
}
```

## stringReplace

- `stringReplace(input, searchStr, replaceStr)` modifies `input` directly and returns no value. Matches are case-sensitive and replaced from left to right without overlapping.
- Only the original input is searched; replacement text is not searched again. An empty replacement removes matches, and an empty search string leaves the input unchanged.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    string label = "red-green-red";
    stringReplace(label, "red", "blue");
}
```

## stringTimesInString

- `stringTimesInString(haystack, needle)` returns a `size_t` count of case-sensitive, nonoverlapping matches from left to right; `stringTimesInString("aaaa", "aa")` returns `2`.
- An empty `needle` returns `0`.

## systemFontPath

- Accepts a UTF-8 PostScript name or family name and returns its file path as `fs::path`. An empty name or failed lookup returns an empty path; accepted names depend on the platform.
- The result contains only the path, not the face index within a font collection. Pass the name directly to `Font::load` to preserve the face selected by the operating system.
- `Font::load` already performs this lookup when its input does not identify a usable file, so direct calls are mainly useful for font selection and inspection.

## tan

- `tan(angle)` is the standard C++ function `std::tan`, available without qualification when using `using namespace std;`. The angle is in radians; one full turn is `TAU`.
- Floating-point arguments return the corresponding floating-point type; integer arguments return `double`.

## tcCloseLogFile

- Calls `closeLogFile()` with identical behavior; use `closeLogFile()` in new code and see its entry for the contract.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcGetLogger

- Returns the same global `Logger&` as `getLogger()`; use `getLogger()` in new code and see `Logger` for its behavior.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcLog

- Forwards the `LogLevel` to `logAt()` and returns its `LogStream`; the default level is `LogLevel::Notice`. Use `logAt()` in new code and see its entry for the contract.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcLogError

- Forwards the optional module string, empty by default, to `logError()` and returns its `LogStream` with identical behavior; use `logError()` in new code.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; see `LogStream` and `Logger` for shared logging rules.

## tcLogFatal

- Forwards the optional module string, empty by default, to `logFatal()` and returns its `LogStream` with identical behavior; use `logFatal()` in new code and see its entry for the contract.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcLogNotice

- Forwards the optional module string, empty by default, to `logNotice()` and returns its `LogStream` with identical behavior; use `logNotice()` in new code.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; see `LogStream` and `Logger` for shared logging rules.

## tcLogVerbose

- Forwards the optional module string, empty by default, to `logVerbose()` and returns its `LogStream` with identical behavior; use `logVerbose()` in new code.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; see `LogStream` and `Logger` for shared logging rules.

## tcLogWarning

- Forwards the optional module string, empty by default, to `logWarning()` and returns its `LogStream` with identical behavior; use `logWarning()` in new code.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; see `LogStream` and `Logger` for shared logging rules.

## tcSetConsoleLogLevel

- Forwards the supplied `LogLevel` to `setConsoleLogLevel()` with identical behavior; use `setConsoleLogLevel()` in new code and see its entry for the contract.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcSetFileLogLevel

- Forwards the supplied `LogLevel` to `setFileLogLevel()` with identical behavior; use `setFileLogLevel()` in new code and see its entry for the contract.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## tcSetLogFile

- Forwards the `fs::path` to `setLogFile()` and returns its `SaveResult` with identical behavior; use `setLogFile()` in new code and see its entry for path and failure rules.
- Marked deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0.

## toBase64

- Accept an `unsigned char` pointer with a byte count, a `vector<unsigned char>`, or a `string`. String input includes embedded zero bytes; pointer input must provide at least the requested number of readable bytes.
- Return standard Base64 using `+` and `/`, with `=` padding and no line breaks. Empty input returns an empty string.
- Decode the result with `fromBase64`; encoding does not compress the input.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    string encoded = toBase64(string("hello"));
    auto bytes = fromBase64(encoded);
}
```

## fromBase64

- Return decoded bytes as `vector<unsigned char>`; this is the counterpart of `toBase64`.
- Recognize `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `+`, and `/`. Skip `=` padding, whitespace, and every other character, allowing line-wrapped input but providing no validity check or error result.
- Return every complete decoded byte and discard remaining incomplete bits. Empty input or input without alphabet characters returns an empty vector.
- Pass decoded image bytes to `Image::loadFromMemory` to load an image.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    auto bytes = fromBase64("aGVsbG8=");
    string text(bytes.begin(), bytes.end());
}
```

## toBinary

- The `int` and `unsigned int` overloads return exactly 32 binary digits, including leading zeros; `char` and `unsigned char` overloads return exactly 8 digits.
- The string overload returns one 8-digit group per byte, separated by a single space. Empty string input returns an empty string.
- There is no `0b` prefix or minus sign; negative integers are represented by their low 32 bits.

## toBool

- Return `true` for `"true"`, `"yes"`, or `"1"`, ignoring letter case.
- Return `false` for every other string, including empty strings. Whitespace is not trimmed, so `" true "` returns `false`.

## toComplex

- `toComplex(real)` takes a `vector<float>` and returns a new `vector<complex<float>>` of the same length, with each input value as the real part and `0.0f` as the imaginary part.
- The input is unchanged. No FFT, windowing, padding, or power-of-two validation is performed; empty input returns an empty vector.

## toDouble

- Parse the leading floating-point number as `double`, accepting leading whitespace, a sign, and exponent notation. Trailing text is ignored, so `toDouble("1.5seconds")` returns `1.5`.
- Return `0.0` if no number can be parsed or conversion reports an out-of-range value, including underflow. Conversion exceptions do not escape.

## toFloat

- Parse the leading floating-point number as `float`, accepting leading whitespace, a sign, and exponent notation. Trailing text is ignored, so `toFloat("1.5seconds")` returns `1.5f`.
- Return `0.0f` if no number can be parsed or conversion reports an out-of-range value, including underflow. Conversion exceptions do not escape.

## toHex

- The `int` overload returns uppercase hexadecimal without a `0x` prefix. Its optional `width` defaults to `0`; positive widths specify a minimum length padded with leading zeros, without truncation.
- The `string` overload returns two uppercase hexadecimal digits per byte, with no separators. Use `toHex(string("AB"))` to get `"4142"`; empty string input returns an empty string.
- The generic overload inserts the value into an output stream with hexadecimal and uppercase formatting. A string literal uses this generic overload and is output as text rather than encoded as bytes.

## toInt

- Parse the leading base-10 integer as `int`, accepting leading whitespace and a sign. Trailing text is ignored, so `toInt("42px")` returns `42` and `toInt("3.5")` returns `3`.
- Return `0` if no integer can be parsed or the value is outside the `int` range. Conversion exceptions do not escape, so failure cannot be distinguished from a parsed zero.
- Hexadecimal prefixes are not recognized as base selectors; use `hexToInt` for hexadecimal input.

## toInt64

- Parses a signed decimal integer, accepting leading whitespace and an optional sign. Parsing stops at the first character that is not part of the number, so `toInt64("42px")` returns `42`.
- Returns `0` if no integer can be parsed or the value is out of range; conversion exceptions are caught. A failed conversion is therefore indistinguishable from a valid zero.

## toJsonString

- `toJsonString(j, indent = 2)` returns a `string` without writing a file.
- Nonnegative `indent` sets the number of spaces per indentation level; any negative value produces compact output.
- Serialization exceptions, including errors for invalid UTF-8 in strings, propagate to the caller.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    Json settings = {{"enabled", true}, {"count", 3}};
    string text = toJsonString(settings, -1);
    logNotice() << text;
}
```

## toLower

- Convert each byte using the current C locale's lowercase conversion, leaving the input string unchanged.
- This is byte-based conversion and does not perform Unicode case conversion on UTF-8 text.

## toString

- `toString(value)` formats a value through its output-stream insertion operator; supported types must provide `operator<<`.
- `toString(value, precision)` uses fixed-point formatting with the specified number of digits after the decimal point for floating-point values.
- `toString(value, width, fill)` pads to a minimum width with the chosen character; `toString(value, precision, width, fill)` combines both options. Width never truncates longer output.
- The vector overload returns elements enclosed in braces and separated by `", "`, such as `"{1, 2, 3}"`; an empty vector returns `"{}"`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    string number = toString(42, 5, '0');
    string decimal = toString(6.28318, 2);
}
```

## toUpper

- Convert each byte using the current C locale's uppercase conversion, leaving the input string unchanged.
- See `toLower` for the shared limits of byte-based case conversion.

## toggleFullscreen

- Enters fullscreen when windowed and leaves fullscreen when already fullscreen.
- Follows the current window's context; see `setFullscreen` for main and secondary window targeting.

## translate

- `translate()` composes an additional translation with the current matrix; it does not restore it. The two-argument form adds zero Z translation, so from identity, `translate(0, 0, 7); translate(10, 20);` produces `(10, 20, 7)`. Use `popMatrix()` to restore a saved matrix or `resetMatrix()` to return to identity.
- Units are the same logical pixels (or world units in 3D) as `drawRect` and the other drawing functions; see `drawRect` for the coordinate basics.
- Order matters when combined with `rotate()` / `scale()`: `translate()` then `rotate()` rotates around the translated point; doing it the other way around rotates around the original origin and then moves along the rotated axes.
- Usually wrapped in a `pushMatrix()` / `popMatrix()` pair so the offset does not leak into drawing that follows.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    pushMatrix();
    translate(200, 150);     // move origin to (200, 150)
    drawCircle(0, 0, 30);    // drawn centered at the new origin
    popMatrix();
}
```

## trim

- Return a new string with spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and line feeds removed from both ends. The input and whitespace between other characters are unchanged.
- Empty input or input containing only these characters returns an empty string. Other whitespace characters are not removed.

## trimBack

- Return a new string with spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and line feeds removed from the end only. The input is unchanged.
- Empty input or input containing only these characters returns an empty string. See `trim` for the shared whitespace rules.

## trimFront

- Removes leading spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and newlines; other whitespace characters and trailing whitespace are preserved.
- Returns a new string without modifying `src`; an empty string or a string containing only these whitespace characters produces an empty string.

## typeName

- Use `typeName<T>()` for a static type or `typeName(typeid(object))` for a `type_info` value. RTTI is required; `typeid(*ptr)` reports the dynamic type when the pointed-to type is polymorphic.
- Returns a `const string&` into a mutex-protected cache that is never cleared. Each type is demangled once per cache; Windows hot-reload modules can have separate caches.
- GCC and Clang use demangling and fall back to the original name on failure. The other implementation removes a leading `class `, `struct `, or `enum ` from the compiler-provided name.

## unbindCursorImage

- Removes the image bound to the specified `Cursor` slot and releases its native cursor resources; a slot without a bound image is unchanged.
- If that slot is currently selected, the displayed cursor immediately returns to its system fallback; the selected `Cursor` value itself does not change.

## utf8ToPath

- Accepts a `string_view` and returns an `fs::path`. Windows decodes the bytes as UTF-8 independently of the process code page; other platforms copy the bytes without validating their encoding.
- On Windows, `fs::path(string)` instead uses the process code page. TrussC's Windows manifest selects UTF-8 for that code page on Windows 10 version 1903 and later; this function does not depend on that manifest.

## vertex

- Adds one point to the buffer that is open: `beginShape`, `beginLines` or `beginStroke`. If none of them is open, `vertex()` does nothing.
- You can pass 2D points (`vertex(x, y)`, `vertex(Vec2)`) or 3D points (`vertex(x, y, z)`, `vertex(Vec3)`). For a 2D point, z is 0.
- Inside `beginShape()`, only the position is stored. `endShape()` uses the color that is set when it is called.
- Inside `beginLines()`, each point also stores the **current color**. Changing the color between points gives each segment its own colors.
- Inside `beginStroke()`, each point also stores the **current stroke weight**, so you can change the width along one line. The whole stroke uses the color of its first point.

## videoCodecName

- Takes a `VideoCodec` and returns a `const char*`: `"H.264"`, `"HEVC"`, `"ProRes 422"`, or `"ProRes 4444"` for the corresponding enum value.
- Returns `"?"` for any other value. The returned string literal does not require deallocation.

## windowFunction

- `windowFunction(type, i, n)` returns a `float` coefficient for zero-based sample index `i` among `n` samples. For nonrectangular windows, use `n >= 2` and `0 <= i < n`; indices and lengths are not validated.
- With `t = (float)i / (n - 1)`, `Hanning` uses `0.5f * (1 - cos(TAU * t))`, `Hamming` uses `0.54f - 0.46f * cos(TAU * t)`, and `Blackman` uses `0.42f - 0.5f * cos(TAU * t) + 0.08f * cos(2 * TAU * t)`.
- `WindowType::Rect` and unrecognized enum values return `1.0f`. For a nonrectangular window with `n == 1` and `i == 0`, the calculation divides zero by zero and does not provide a valid coefficient.

## worldToScreen

- `worldToScreen(worldPos)` returns a `Vec3`: X and Y are screen coordinates from the top-left, with Y increasing downward; Z is normalized depth, with 0 at the near plane and 1 at the far plane across graphics backends.
- Both coordinate-conversion functions use the active window and render target's stored view, projection, and viewport size. Window coordinates use logical pixels unless pixel-perfect mode is enabled; Fbo coordinates use target pixels. A zero viewport dimension falls back to the corresponding target size.
- Both functions use world coordinates without applying the current model transform. Call them while the intended camera scope is active, such as between `EasyCam::begin` and `EasyCam::end`.
- Returns `(0, 0, 0)` when `abs(clip.w) < 0.0001f`. Otherwise, coordinates and depth are not clamped, and points behind the camera are not rejected.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: EasyCam camera;
void tcApp::draw() {
    camera.begin();
    Vec3 screen = worldToScreen(Vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f));
    camera.end();
    drawCircle(screen.x, screen.y, 5.0f);
}
```

## wrap

- `wrap(value, min, max)` takes and returns `float` values; for `max > min`, it wraps cyclically and maps `max` to `min`, but rounding can return `max`. For finite angles strictly in `[0, TAU)`, use `float a = wrap(angle, 0.0f, TAU); if (a >= TAU) a = 0.0f;`.
- Negative offsets wrap from the upper end; `wrap(-30, 0, 360)` returns 330, and `wrap(370, 0, 360)` returns 10.
- Returns `min` when `max <= min`, without reordering the bounds.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    float angle = wrap(-TAU / 4.0f, 0.0f, TAU);
}
```

## atanh

- `atanh(x)` computes the inverse of `tanh`; a finite real result requires `-1 < x && x < 1`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC; overloads and handling of out-of-domain inputs follow the standard library.

## tanh

- `tanh(x)` computes the hyperbolic tangent of `x`; it is not the circular tangent of an angle.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC and uses the standard library overloads.

## exp2

- `exp2(x)` computes `2` raised to `x`; for example, `exp2(3.0f)` returns `8.0f`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC; overloads and overflow or underflow handling follow the standard library.

## log2

- `log2(x)` computes the base-two logarithm; a finite real result requires `x > 0`. For example, `log2(8.0f)` returns `3.0f`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC; overloads and handling of zero or negative inputs follow the standard library.

## log10

- `log10(x)` computes the base-ten logarithm; a finite real result requires `x > 0`. For example, `log10(100.0f)` returns `2.0f`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC; overloads and handling of zero or negative inputs follow the standard library.

## trunc

- `trunc(x)` returns the integral part as a floating-point value; `trunc(2.8f)` is `2.0f`, and `trunc(-2.8f)` is `-2.0f`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC and uses the standard library overloads.

## remainder

- `remainder(x, y)` computes `x - n * y`, where `n` is the nearest integer to `x / y`; an exact tie selects the even integer.
- The result can have the opposite sign to `x`; for example, `remainder(7.0f, 4.0f)` returns `-1.0f`.
- This is the standard C++ `<cmath>` function exposed by TrussC; overloads and handling of invalid inputs such as a zero divisor follow the standard library.

## TAU

- `TAU` is a `constexpr float` defined as `6.28318530717958647693f`, approximately `6.28318`, and equals twice pi.
- It is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its radius; the circumference is `TAU * radius`.
- Use `HALF_TAU` for half a turn and `QUARTER_TAU` or `TAU / 4` for a quarter turn, as in `rotate(QUARTER_TAU)`.
- Mathematically, `e^(iτ) = 1` describes a full turn returning to its start, while `e^(iπ) = -1` describes a half turn.

## PI

- `PI` is a `constexpr float` equal to `HALF_TAU`, approximately `3.14159`.
- It is marked deprecated; use `HALF_TAU` for half a turn and see `TAU` for the angle constants and their mathematical identities.

## CameraContext

- Stores `view`, `projection`, viewport dimensions `viewW` and `viewH`, and the `pickable` flag. Defaults are identity matrices, zero dimensions, and `pickable = true`.
- Screen setup, `EasyCam::begin()`, and `Fbo::begin()` register camera contexts; nodes retain the current context during drawing so picking uses the camera that rendered them.
- Registered contexts are shared as const snapshots, and a new registration creates a new snapshot rather than changing one retained by a node.
- `screenPointToRay(x, y)` converts a viewport point with a top-left origin into a world-space ray. Nonpositive viewport dimensions or a near-zero homogeneous divisor produce a vertical 2D screen ray instead.
- `worldToScreen(pos)` returns viewport coordinates and depth, with depth mapped from 0 to 1 between the clipping planes; if the projected homogeneous `w` is below `1e-4f`, it returns `(0, 0, -1)`.
- Projection matrices use the graphics backend's clip-space convention. `Fbo::begin()` initially registers a context with `pickable = false`, so screen picking skips geometry drawn under that context. Another camera setup can replace it; `EasyCam::begin()` inside an FBO registers a context with `pickable = true`.

## ShaderVertex

- Contains nine `float` fields in this order: position `x, y, z`, texture coordinates `u, v`, and color `r, g, b, a`; there is no normal field.
- Initialize all fields before use; the structure provides no default member values. Color components use the 0–1 convention.
- `Shader::submitVertices()` accepts an array of these vertices and copies it when recording a draw.

## HasTexture

- Base class for types such as `Image`, `Fbo`, and `VideoPlayer`; subclasses implement mutable and const `getTexture()` methods returning references.
- The default `hasTexture()` checks whether the texture is allocated; the default `draw(x, y)` and `draw(x, y, w, h)` draw only when it is allocated.
- Filter and wrap setters and getters delegate to the returned texture. See `Texture` for texture settings and GPU usage rules.
- The default `save(path)` returns a failed `SaveResult` with `SaveError::WriteFailed`; subclasses must override it to support saving.

## VideoPlayerBase

- Use `VideoPlayer` for the concrete standard player. This base class cannot be instantiated and cannot be copied.
- Inherits `HasTexture` and provides shared playback controls, state queries, and an owned texture. Derived classes implement loading, closing, updating, seeking, and backend playback operations.
- Playback times are in seconds, positions are normalized from 0 to 1, and dimensions are in pixels. Initial settings are volume 1, speed 1, pan 0, looping disabled, and a resynchronization threshold of 0.5 seconds.
- Call the concrete player's `update()` on the main thread to update frames and deliver runtime errors. See `VideoPlayerBase::onError` for error delivery and `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## LogStream

- Returned by `logAt()`, `logVerbose()`, `logNotice()`, `logWarning()`, `logError()` and `logFatal()`; append values with `<<`.
- Sends the accumulated message once to the global logger when destroyed. A temporary normally logs at the end of the statement; a named local logs when its lifetime ends, even if no text was inserted.
- The constructor takes a `LogLevel` and an optional module string, empty by default; a nonempty module adds `[module] ` before the accumulated text.
- Supports stream manipulators such as `endl`, but they affect the buffered text and do not send the log early. Output filtering occurs after message construction; see `Logger` for filtering and threading.
- An inserted `fs::path` is written without added quotes, using UTF-8 on Windows and native bytes on POSIX. Invalid UTF-16 units in Windows paths become U+FFFD instead of causing a path-conversion exception.
- Supports move construction only; copying and both forms of assignment are disabled, and the moved-from object does not send a message.

## VideoPlayerBase::load

- This is a pure virtual interface implemented by concrete players such as `VideoPlayer`; it returns `LoadResult`, which succeeds in `if (video.load("movie.mp4"))` and provides `error` and `message` on failure.
- `VideoPlayer` resolves relative file paths through `getDataPath()` and leaves absolute paths and HTTP(S) URLs unchanged; URL decoding support depends on the backend.
- `VideoPlayer` closes an existing loaded video before attempting the replacement, so a failed replacement does not preserve the previous video.
- A successful load initializes the player and creates its textures; picture readiness is described in `VideoPlayerBase::isReady`.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::update` for thread and update requirements.

```cpp
VideoPlayer video;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (video.load("movie.mp4")) video.play();
}
```

## VideoPlayerBase::close

- This is a pure virtual interface; `VideoPlayer` releases the backend, textures, and pixel buffers, then resets dimensions and playback, readiness, and completion flags.
- `VideoPlayer` clears recorded playback errors even when already unloaded; volume, pan, speed, loop, and resynchronization settings remain stored.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::update` for thread requirements.

## VideoPlayerBase::update

- This is a pure virtual interface; call the concrete player once per application frame, typically from `tcApp::update()`, before drawing. Unloaded players do nothing.
- `VideoPlayer` clears its new-frame flag, processes available backend frames, uploads them to GPU textures, checks completion, and handles deferred poster uploads; each call does not necessarily produce a new frame.
- Runtime playback errors are delivered through `onError` during this call; playback stops without rewinding, the last picture remains, and the playback, pause, new-frame, and completion flags are cleared.
- Keep loading, playback control, updating, drawing, and closing on the main thread; these operations share player state and can create, update, or release GPU resources.
- HapPlayer clears its new-frame flag only while actively playing, preserving frames produced by explicit frame seeking while stopped or paused.

```cpp
VideoPlayer video;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (video.load("movie.mp4")) video.play();
}
void tcApp::update() { video.update(); }
void tcApp::draw() { video.draw(0, 0); }
```

## VideoPlayerBase::isFrameNew

- Returns `true` only when both the new-frame flag and the first-picture flag are set; reading the value does not clear either flag.
- `VideoPlayer` clears the new-frame flag at each loaded `update()` and sets it when a backend frame is uploaded. On Web, copying an available video image counts as a new frame even if the image has not changed.
- HapPlayer also sets it after explicit frame seeking and preserves it across stopped or paused updates; use `VideoPlayerBase::isReady` to decide whether a picture is ready for drawing.

## VideoPlayerBase::getDuration

- Return the total playback duration as a `float` in seconds.
- This is a pure virtual function implemented by each player; `VideoPlayer` returns `0` when unloaded.

## VideoPlayerBase::getPosition

- Express the playback position as a fraction of the duration, where `0` is the beginning and `1` is the end; `getCurrentTime()` converts this value to seconds.
- This is a pure virtual function; `VideoPlayer` returns `0` when unloaded or the duration is unavailable, and a seek may not be reflected immediately.
- On Web, `VideoPlayer` reports the fraction in increments of `0.001`.

## VideoPlayerBase::setPosition

- Specify `pct` as a fraction of the duration: `0` is the beginning and `1` is the end; finite values outside this range are clamped.
- Do nothing when unloaded; otherwise, pass the position to the backend without changing the base class playback flags.
- Seeking can be asynchronous, so the reported position and displayed frame may update later; use `setCurrentTime()` to specify seconds.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: VideoPlayer video_;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (video_.load("movie.mp4")) video_.setPosition(0.5f);
}
```

## VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate

- Return frames per second through a pure virtual function; `VideoPlayer` returns `0` when unloaded or the rate is unknown, without logging a warning.
- Public frame APIs require a loaded player and a positive, finite rate; otherwise, queries return `0` and operations do nothing, with one shared warning per instance for an unknown rate while loaded, even across reloads.
- Web always reports `0`; `HapPlayer` divides the video sample count by the duration to obtain an average rate. Use `getPosition()`, `setPosition()`, and `getDuration()` for portable time-based control.

## VideoPlayerBase::canUseFrameApis

- This protected helper returns `true` only when the player is loaded and `getFrameRate()` is positive and finite.
- Unloaded players return `false` silently; unknown rates while loaded use the shared warning rules described in `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate`.

## VideoPlayerBase::getCurrentFrame

- Return the backend frame index; native `VideoPlayer` backends estimate it by multiplying playback time by the frame rate and truncating to an integer.
- Return `0` when frame APIs are unavailable; see `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate` for the shared availability and warning rules.

## VideoPlayerBase::getTotalFrames

- Native `VideoPlayer` backends estimate the count as duration multiplied by frame rate, truncated to an integer; `HapPlayer` returns the video sample count.
- Return `0` when frame APIs are unavailable; see `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate` for the shared availability and warning rules.

## VideoPlayerBase::setFrame

- Pass a zero-based integer index to the backend; the base class does not clamp it, and native `VideoPlayer` seeking derives the target time from the frame rate.
- `HapPlayer` clamps the index to the available frames and decodes and uploads the frame synchronously.
- Do nothing when frame APIs are unavailable; see `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate` for the shared availability and warning rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: VideoPlayer video_;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (video_.load("movie.mp4")) video_.setFrame(30);
}
```

## VideoPlayerBase::nextFrame

- Request one forward step from the backend; macOS and iOS use native frame stepping, Windows uses `FrameStep`, and Linux seeks forward by one frame interval.
- This function does not pause playback in the base class; pause first for controlled stepping.
- Do nothing when frame APIs are unavailable; see `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate` for the shared availability and warning rules.

## VideoPlayerBase::previousFrame

- Request one backward step from the backend; macOS and iOS use native frame stepping, while Windows and Linux seek backward without going before the beginning.
- This function does not pause playback in the base class; pause first for controlled stepping.
- Do nothing when frame APIs are unavailable; see `VideoPlayerBase::getFrameRate` for the shared availability and warning rules.

## VideoPlayerBase::getPixels

- Provide mutable and const pointer overloads for 8-bit RGBA data; `nullptr` means no RGBA buffer is available. `VideoPlayer` can allocate a zero-filled buffer before decoding, so a non-null pointer does not prove that a frame is ready.
- The player owns the memory: do not free it, copy data needed beyond later updates, and do not retain the pointer across close, reload, or destruction. `VideoPlayer` returns its CPU buffer without copying or locking; this is not GPU texture readback.
- Linux `VideoPlayer` returns `nullptr` on its NV12 path even during playback; `HapPlayer` instead decodes its compressed frame to RGBA on the CPU when the cached pixels are invalid, including through the const overload.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: VideoPlayer video_;
void tcApp::update() {
    video_.update();
    Pixels pixels;
    if (const auto* data = video_.getPixels()) {
        pixels.setFromPixels(data, (int)video_.getWidth(), (int)video_.getHeight(), 4);
    }
}
```

## VideoPlayerBase::hasAudio

- The base implementation returns `false`; native `VideoPlayer` backends and `HapPlayer` inspect the loaded audio track.
- Audio access is optional: the base codec, sample-rate, and channel getters return `0`, and the base data getter returns an empty vector.
- Web `VideoPlayer` always returns `false` here; its other four audio accessors log unsupported-operation warnings and return their empty or zero values.

## VideoPlayerBase::getAudioCodec

- Return a `uint32_t` codec identifier, commonly a FourCC such as `'aac '` or `'mp3 '`; return `0` in the base implementation or when no audio information is available.
- Windows `VideoPlayer` returns the audio subtype GUID's `Data1` value, which is not necessarily a FourCC.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::hasAudio` for shared audio support and Web behavior.

## VideoPlayerBase::getAudioData

- Return an owned `vector<uint8_t>` containing audio data without decoding it; supported extraction paths add ADTS headers to AAC packets.
- Native `VideoPlayer` extraction reads the audio track synchronously on each call and can allocate memory for the entire track.
- The base implementation returns an empty vector; extraction also returns empty when no audio is available or reading cannot start, while a later read failure can leave already collected bytes in the result.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::hasAudio` for shared audio support and Web behavior.

## VideoPlayerBase::getAudioSampleRate

- Return the audio track sample rate in Hz, or `0` in the base implementation or when unavailable.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::hasAudio` for shared audio support and Web behavior.

## VideoPlayerBase::getAudioChannels

- Return the audio track channel count, or `0` in the base implementation or when unavailable.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::hasAudio` for shared audio support and Web behavior.

## VideoPlayerBase::isUsingHwAccel

- The base implementation returns `false`; Linux `VideoPlayer` checks whether a hardware decoder device is selected.
- On macOS, iOS, Windows, and Web, `VideoPlayer` returns `true` whenever its backend handle exists; this does not verify whether the current codec is actually decoded on the GPU.
- This is a status query, not a preference setting; use `VideoPlayer::setUseHwAccel` before loading to control the Linux preference.

## VideoPlayerBase::getHwAccelName

- The base implementation and an unloaded `VideoPlayer` return `"none"`.
- Loaded `VideoPlayer` backends report `"videotoolbox"` on macOS and iOS, `"mediafoundation"` on Windows, and `"browser"` on Web; Linux returns the selected FFmpeg hardware device name, such as `"vaapi"`, `"v4l2m2m"`, `"drm"`, or `"cuda"`, or `"software"` without a hardware device.
- See `VideoPlayerBase::isUsingHwAccel` for the limits of hardware reporting.

## VideoPlayerBase::getTexture

- Return the player's stored `Texture` by mutable or const reference without copying or uploading; a reference is returned even when the texture is unallocated.
- The player owns the texture and can clear or replace its contents during playback, close, or reload; the reference must not outlive the player.
- Use the player's `draw()` for its intended output: Linux NV12 playback uses separate textures, and Hap Q drawing applies a YCoCg conversion shader that this getter does not apply.

## HasTexture::hasTexture

- The default virtual implementation returns `getTexture().isAllocated()`.
- Tests GPU texture allocation rather than CPU pixel availability; an `Image` can have CPU pixels without a texture. Use `Image::isAllocated` to test its CPU image allocation.

## HasTexture::draw

- The default virtual implementation calls `getTexture().draw(...)` only when `hasTexture()` is true; otherwise, it does nothing.
- `draw(x, y)` uses the texture's pixel width and height. `draw(x, y, w, h)` stretches the whole texture to the requested rectangle without preserving its aspect ratio.
- Position and size use the current drawing coordinates and transform. The current drawing color multiplies the texture; use `setColor(1.0f)` for an untinted draw.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and `Texture::draw` for drawing-state behavior. Subclasses can override drawing; see `Fbo::draw` for framebuffer orientation handling.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() { image.load("photo.png"); }
void tcApp::draw() {
    setColor(1.0f);
    image.draw(20.0f, 20.0f, 200.0f, 150.0f);
}
```

## HasTexture::setMinFilter

- Forwards to `getTexture().setMinFilter(filter)`, selecting `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear` for minification without changing magnification. The initial value is Linear.
- See `HasTexture::setFilter` for sampler updates, setting persistence, and GPU resource rules.

## HasTexture::setMagFilter

- Forwards to `getTexture().setMagFilter(filter)`, selecting `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear` for magnification without changing minification. The initial value is Linear.
- See `HasTexture::setFilter` for sampler updates, setting persistence, and GPU resource rules.

## HasTexture::setFilter

- Forwards to `getTexture().setFilter(filter)`, setting both filters to `TextureFilter::Nearest` or `TextureFilter::Linear`; both initially use Linear. Nearest selects a single texel, while Linear interpolates neighboring texels.
- A changed setting recreates the sampler when graphics are initialized and the texture is allocated, without uploading pixels; unchanged settings do nothing. Mipmapped textures retain linear interpolation between mip levels.
- Settings can be changed before allocation and survive texture `clear()`. See `Texture` for main-thread and GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!image.load("sprite.png")) return;
    image.setFilter(TextureFilter::Nearest);
}
```

## HasTexture::getMinFilter

- Returns `getTexture().getMinFilter()` as a `TextureFilter`, including before allocation; the initial value is `TextureFilter::Linear`.

## HasTexture::getMagFilter

- Returns `getTexture().getMagFilter()` as a `TextureFilter`, including before allocation; the initial value is `TextureFilter::Linear`.

## HasTexture::setWrapU

- Forwards to `getTexture().setWrapU(wrap)`, changing the horizontal wrap mode without changing V. The initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`.
- See `HasTexture::setWrap` for available modes and sampler behavior.

## HasTexture::setWrapV

- Forwards to `getTexture().setWrapV(wrap)`, changing the vertical wrap mode without changing U. The initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`.
- See `HasTexture::setWrap` for available modes and sampler behavior.

## HasTexture::setWrap

- Forwards to `getTexture().setWrap(wrap)`, setting both axes to `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`, `TextureWrap::Repeat`, or `TextureWrap::MirroredRepeat`; both initially use ClampToEdge.
- Outside texture coordinates 0–1, ClampToEdge extends edge texels, Repeat repeats the texture, and MirroredRepeat repeats it with alternating reflections.
- Changes recreate the sampler under the same conditions as `HasTexture::setFilter`, without uploading pixels; unchanged settings do nothing. Settings can be changed before allocation and survive texture `clear()`. See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

## HasTexture::getWrapU

- Returns `getTexture().getWrapU()` as a `TextureWrap`, including before allocation; the initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`.

## HasTexture::getWrapV

- Returns `getTexture().getWrapV()` as a `TextureWrap`, including before allocation; the initial value is `TextureWrap::ClampToEdge`.

## HasTexture::save

- `save(path)` returns a `SaveResult`. The base implementation ignores the path and returns `SaveError::WriteFailed` with the message `Texture saving is not implemented`, without writing a file.
- Subclasses implement saving: `Image::save` saves CPU pixels without GPU readback, while `Fbo::save` first reads back framebuffer contents. See those entries for formats, timing, and platform restrictions.
- For the Image and Fbo implementations, relative paths resolve through `getDataPath()`, missing parent directories are created, and paths inside the app bundle return `SaveError::AccessDenied`.
- Those implementations write to `<file>.tmp`, check writing and closing, then replace the destination by rename. Failed writes preserve the previous file and remove the temporary file.
- Atomic replacement does not guarantee durability after power loss.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!image.load("photo.png")) return;
    HasTexture& source = image;
    auto result = source.save("exports/photo.png");
    if (!result) logError("Save") << result.message;
}
```

## Texture::allocateCompressed

- `allocateCompressed(width, height, format, data, dataSize)` takes pixel dimensions, a sokol `sg_pixel_format` such as `SG_PIXELFORMAT_BC1_RGBA`, and already compressed data whose size is specified in bytes.
- Clears the existing texture, records `Immutable` usage and four channels, and supplies data for the base mip level only. This method does not compress ordinary pixel data or generate mipmaps.
- The device must support the supplied format; `sg_query_pixelformat(format).sample` reports sampling support. There is no decompression fallback.
- Without initialized graphics, the texture remains unallocated. Otherwise, this method marks it allocated after resource creation without checking whether sokol accepted the resources or data.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Texture texture;
void tcApp::setup() {
    if (!sg_query_pixelformat(SG_PIXELFORMAT_BC1_RGBA).sample) return;
    uint8_t block[8] = {};
    texture.allocateCompressed(4, 4, SG_PIXELFORMAT_BC1_RGBA, block, sizeof(block));
}
```

## Texture::getPixelFormat

- Returns an `sg_pixel_format`, rather than a `TextureFormat`.
- A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `SG_PIXELFORMAT_NONE`. The channel-based `allocate()` overload also stores `NONE`, even though it chooses a GPU format from the channel count.
- This does not query the GPU or confirm allocation success; see `TextureFormat` for format definitions.

## Texture::getImage

- Returns the stored `sg_image` for advanced sokol interoperability without copying image data or transferring ownership.
- A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `sg_image{}`; this getter does not check the resource state.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getView

- Returns the stored `sg_view` for custom shader bindings such as `sg_bindings.views`; it covers the whole mip chain and, for cubemaps, all six faces.
- A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `sg_view{}`; this getter does not create a view or check its resource state.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getSampler

- Returns the stored `sg_sampler` for custom shader bindings such as `sg_bindings.samplers`; it reflects the texture's filter and wrap settings.
- A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `sg_sampler{}`. Changing filter or wrap settings on an allocated texture recreates the sampler, so retrieve the handle again afterward.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getAttachmentView

- Returns the stored `sg_view` for mip level `0` of a 2D `RenderTarget`, suitable for a sokol color attachment.
- No such view is created for other usage modes or cubemaps; use `getCubemapFaceAttachmentView()` for a cubemap face. A default-constructed or cleared texture returns `sg_view{}`.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getAttachmentViewForMip

- For a 2D `RenderTarget` allocated with multiple mip levels, returns the pre-created `sg_view` for `level`, where `0` is the base level.
- If no per-level view exists, including negative or out-of-range indices, returns `getAttachmentView()` instead. With one mip level, every index therefore returns the base attachment view.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getViewForMip

- For a 2D `RenderTarget` allocated with multiple mip levels, returns a pre-created `sg_view` restricted to `level`, where `0` is the base level; this allows sampling one mip while rendering into another without overlapping the view ranges.
- If no per-level view exists, including negative or out-of-range indices, returns `getView()` instead. Textures with other usage modes and cubemaps therefore return the full sampling view.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Texture::getCubemapFaceAttachmentView

- `getCubemapFaceAttachmentView(face, mipLevel)` targets face indices `0` through `5` in the order `+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z`; mip level `0` is the base level.
- Creates the `sg_view` on first access for each face and mip pair, then returns the cached handle on later calls.
- Returns `sg_view{}` if graphics is unavailable, the texture is unallocated or is not marked as a cubemap, `face` is outside `0` through `5`, or `mipLevel` is outside `0` through `getNumMipLevels() - 1`.
- Use a `RenderTarget` cubemap. This method does not check the usage mode before asking sokol to create the color attachment view, and it does not check creation success.
- See `Texture` for GPU resource rules and handle lifetime.

## Fbo::getColorImage

- Returns the current color texture's `sg_image` handle for advanced interoperation, including the resolved single-sample image when MSAA is enabled.
- Does not transfer ownership. The handle can change as texture versions change; see `Fbo::getTexture` for texture access and `Texture` for GPU resource lifetime rules.

## Fbo::getTextureView

- Returns the current color texture's sampling `sg_view` handle for advanced interoperation, including the resolved texture when MSAA is enabled.
- Does not transfer ownership. The handle can change as texture versions change; see `Fbo::getTexture` for texture access and `Texture` for GPU resource lifetime rules.

## Fbo::getSampler

- Returns the current color texture's `sg_sampler` handle for advanced interoperation.
- Does not transfer ownership. Texture version changes or filter/wrap changes can replace the sampler; obtain the handle again when needed. See `Texture` for GPU resource lifetime rules.

## Mesh::getGpuVertexBuffer

- Returns the stored `sg_buffer` for custom sokol pipelines. Call `uploadToGpu()` first, or use `drawGpuPbr()`; an ordinary `draw()` only prepares this buffer when it selects the PBR path.
- The buffer contains interleaved position, normal, UV, and tangent data. Use `getGpuVertexCount()` for its vertex count and `getGpuIndexCount()` for an indexed draw.
- The handle has `id == 0` before creation or after release. For the layout, upload behavior, and handle ownership and lifetime, see `Mesh::uploadToGpu`.

## Mesh::getGpuIndexBuffer

- Returns the stored `sg_buffer` of unsigned integer indices created by `uploadToGpu()`. Use `getGpuIndexCount()` for the uploaded count; for upload behavior and handle ownership and lifetime, see `Mesh::uploadToGpu`.
- `TriangleStrip` and `TriangleFan` expand into triangle lists, and `LineStrip` and `LineLoop` expand into line lists. Custom pipelines must draw triangle modes as triangle lists and line modes as line lists.
- If the mesh has no source indices, the source sequence is `0` through `N - 1`, where `N` is the vertex count, including for `Points`. The handle has `id == 0` before creation or after release.

## Mesh::getGpuPointBuffer

- Returns the stored `sg_buffer` prepared by `uploadPointsToGpu()` or `drawGpuPoints()`, for use in a custom rendering pipeline such as a particle rendering shader.
- Each point contains seven tightly packed floats, `{ pos.xyz, color.rgba }`. Use `getGpuPointCount()` for the uploaded point count.
- The handle has `id == 0` before creation or after release. For upload behavior, see `Mesh::uploadPointsToGpu`; for handle ownership and lifetime, see `Mesh::uploadToGpu`.

## Font::getAtlas

- Returns a borrowed `const internal::AtlasState*`, or `nullptr` if no font is loaded. A loaded font does not check the index; require `index < getAtlasCount()` before calling.
- Pages store glyph coverage in the R channel of an R8 texture. Drawing a page view with the normal texture pipeline displays it in red; font drawing uses a coverage pipeline instead.
- This accessor does not upload textures. Adding glyphs may invalidate page pointers, and atlas updates may replace GPU images and views; reacquire them after changes. Clearing or releasing the owning atlas also invalidates them.

## Font::getSampler

- Returns the shared `sg_sampler` with linear filtering, edge clamping, and LOD limited to approximately mip level 0. Normal font rendering may choose a different sampler for minified text.
- Creates shared samplers lazily when sokol-gfx is initialized; before initialization, the returned handle can be zero. The sampler is shared framework state and must not be destroyed by the caller.

## IesProfile::getView

- Returns an `sg_view` by value for advanced pipeline binding; returns a zero handle before loading or after resources are released or moved away.
- Ownership and handle lifetime follow `IesProfile`.

## IesProfile::getSampler

- Returns an `sg_sampler` by value for advanced pipeline binding, with linear minification and magnification filtering and clamp-to-edge wrapping on U and V.
- Returns a zero handle before loading or after resources are released or moved away; ownership and handle lifetime follow `IesProfile`.

## Node::getCameraContext

- Returns a `shared_ptr<const CameraContext>`; it is initially `nullptr` until a context is recorded during drawing or assigned with `setCameraContext()`.
- For an active node, drawing records the current camera context before `beginDraw()`, even when the node is invisible. If no current context exists, the stored context is retained.
- Returns only this node's stored context, without searching its parents; inherited context selection for picking is handled by `Node::resolvePickRay`.

## Node::setCameraContext

- Accepts a `shared_ptr<const CameraContext>` for a manually managed node; pass `nullptr` to clear the stored context.
- Changes only this node's stored context for picking; it does not change the active rendering camera or assign contexts to children.
- Normal tree drawing records the current camera context automatically and replaces this value when a current context exists; see `Node::getCameraContext`.

## CameraContext::screenPointToRay

- Takes `screenX` and `screenY` in viewport-relative screen pixels, with the origin at the top left and Y increasing downward.
- Inverts `projection * view` and unprojects near-plane and middle-depth points; returns a `Ray` starting at the near-plane point with a normalized direction toward the middle-depth point.
- If either viewport dimension is nonpositive, or either unprojected homogeneous W has an absolute value below `1e-7f`, returns a ray from `(screenX, screenY, 1000)` in direction `(0, 0, -1)`.
- Matrix inversion uses `Mat4::inverted()`, which substitutes the identity matrix when the determinant has an absolute value below `1e-10f`; this condition does not itself trigger the screen-ray fallback.

## RectNode::draw

- The default implementation draws nothing; override `void draw()` in a RectNode subclass and use local coordinates or the protected rectangle drawing helpers.
- See `Node::draw` for the drawing lifecycle and style handling, and `RectNode` for size and clipping.

```cpp
class Panel : public RectNode {
public:
    void draw() override {
        setColor(0.2f, 0.4f, 0.8f);
        drawRectFill();
    }
};
```

## Shader::clear

- Releases the loaded shader's vertex/index buffers and cached pipelines, releases internally created texture views, resets resource handles and stream accounting, and sets `loaded` to `false`; the destructor also calls this function.
- Actual GPU destruction is deferred until after a commit and until no unconsumed recorded draws reference the resources. A shader may therefore be destroyed after its scope ends even when its submitted draws have not executed.
- Does not erase `pendingUniforms` or `pendingViews`. Retained bindings can reference views retired by this call, so rebind affected textures after reloading.
- Does not remove an active shader scope; follow the scope lifetime rules in `Shader::begin`.

## Shader::submitVertices

- Accepts `(const ShaderVertex* data, int count, PrimitiveType type)`. Deferred replay draws `Triangles`, `TriangleStrip`, and `Quads` using generated triangle indices; `Lines` and `LineStrip` are ignored, and `Points` produces no draw.
- Copies vertices, stored uniform bytes, and binding handles at submission time, and selects a pipeline for the current target. Later setter calls do not alter that submission; no vertex transformation is applied by this function.
- Calls `setupBindings()` while capturing bindings. The captured draw can execute without accessing the Shader object; resource lifetime is described in `Shader::clear`, and texture ownership in `Shader::setTexture`.
- Records into the current target for execution during its drawing flush, including FBO flushes and window presentation. Stream capacity behavior is described in `Shader::createVertexBuffer`.
- Does nothing for zero vertices, an unloaded shader, or a target whose recording has failed. A negative count, null data with a positive count, unrepresentable size, or recording allocation failure logs an error and discards the target's recording.
- If no compatible pipeline is available, skips the submission.

## Reflector::visit

- Backends implement overloads taking a member name and a mutable reference to `float`, `int`, `bool`, `string`, `Vec2`, `Vec3`, or `Color`; these overloads are pure virtual.
- Return `true` when the value should be treated as edited. Getter/setter reflection uses this result to decide whether to call the setter.
- The enum overload also receives an `EnumLabelSpan`; its default implementation ignores the labels and calls the plain integer overload.
- Backends that refuse read-only edits must check `isReadOnly()`; see `Reflector::isReadOnly` for the scope contract.

## Reflector::isReadOnly

- Returns `true` while at least one `pushReadOnly()` remains unmatched by `popReadOnly()`; nested scopes remain read-only until all are closed.
- The scope marks intent and does not itself block assignments. Backends check this flag to disable editing or refuse writes.
- Getter-only `TC_VALUE(name, getter)` visits a temporary inside this scope and discards edits because it has no setter.

## Reflector::pushReadOnly

- Increments the read-only nesting depth; pair each call with `popReadOnly()` after visiting the relevant members.
- For how backends enforce this flag, see `Reflector::isReadOnly`.

## Reflector::popReadOnly

- Decrements the read-only nesting depth if it is positive; calling it at depth zero has no effect.
- For nested-scope behavior, see `Reflector::isReadOnly`.

## Reflector::isDerived

- Returns `true` while at least one `pushDerived()` remains unmatched by `popDerived()`.
- `TC_DERIVED` uses this scope for values computed from other members and supports writing through its setter; derived does not mean read-only.
- `JsonWriteReflector` omits derived values by default and includes them when `includeDerived` is `true`. The scope flag itself does not prevent reading or writing.

## Reflector::pushDerived

- Increments the derived-value nesting depth; pair each call with `popDerived()` after visiting the relevant members.
- For the meaning of derived values, see `Reflector::isDerived`.

## Reflector::popDerived

- Decrements the derived-value nesting depth if it is positive; calling it at depth zero has no effect.
- The derived flag remains set while an outer derived scope is open; see `Reflector::isDerived`.

## Reflector::beginGroup

- Composite reflection brackets nested members with `beginGroup(name)` and `endGroup()`, using the composite member's name.
- The base implementation does nothing, so backends that do not override it receive nested members as a flat sequence.
- Override both group functions when a backend needs nested objects or grouped presentation.

## Reflector::endGroup

- Completes the matching `beginGroup(name)` call after its nested members have been visited.
- The base implementation does nothing; see `Reflector::beginGroup` for the grouping contract.

## JsonReadReflector::unknownKeys

- For parsed external JSON, group names are recognized and invalid group shapes or unknown nested keys reject the whole transaction. The permissive group behavior below applies to app-constructed JSON.
- Call after `reflectMembers()` to obtain a `vector<string>` of top-level source keys not encountered by a top-level `visit()`. A non-object source returns an empty vector.
- Recognized top-level keys are excluded even when skipped or read-only; unknown keys inside nested groups are not reported.
- `beginGroup()` does not mark its group name as recognized, so a composite member's top-level key can appear here even when its nested values were applied.

## JsonReadReflector::visit

- Looks up `name` in the current source object and writes an accepted value into the supplied reference. The reflection caller invokes a property setter when applicable; `visit()` itself does not call it.
- Returns `true` and records the name in `applied` for accepted values, even if the value is unchanged. Returns `false` for absent, mismatched, or read-only values.
- See `JsonReadReflector` for accepted types and result-list rules.

## JsonReadReflector::beginGroup

- For parsed external JSON, group names are recognized and invalid group shapes or unknown nested keys reject the whole transaction. The permissive group behavior below applies to app-constructed JSON.
- Selects the object under `name` in the current source; subsequent visits read that object until the matching `endGroup()`.
- If the key is absent or its value is not an object, visits inside the group find no values and add nothing to the result lists.
