```cpp
        ScrollContainer::update();
    }
};
```

## ScrollContainer::onMouseScroll

- This protected callback accepts `const ScrollEventArgs& e` and adds `e.scroll.x` and `e.scroll.y` to the corresponding accumulators only for enabled axes with positive maximum scroll values. Movement is deferred to `ScrollContainer::update`.
- Returns `true` if either axis is enabled and has a positive maximum, even at an end of its range, with zero input on that axis, or with zero scroll speed. Otherwise it returns `false`, allowing the event to continue to a parent; see `Node::onMouseScroll` for input delivery.
- This override does not call the RectNode implementation, so it does not notify the inherited `mouseScrolled` event or invoke the `onMouseScroll(Vec2, Vec2)` overload.
- When overriding it in a ScrollContainer subclass, call the base implementation and preserve its return value to retain the default accumulation and event handling.

```cpp
class ScrollView : public ScrollContainer {
protected:
    bool onMouseScroll(const ScrollEventArgs& e) override {
        return ScrollContainer::onMouseScroll(e);
    }
};
```

## ScrollBar::updateVertical

- This protected method places the bar at the container's right edge with the configured margin and sets its thickness to `getBarWidth()`.
- The height is `max(2 * thickness, (containerHeight - 2 * margin) * containerHeight / contentHeight)`; its vertical position follows `getScrollY() / getMaxScrollY()` along the remaining travel. The minimum height is not capped to the available space.
- Sets the bar inactive if the vertical scroll range is not positive or the content is not a `RectNode`; otherwise, it sets the bar active.
- Requires a valid container pointer. See `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer` for synchronization, coordinate assumptions, and container lifetime.

## ScrollBar::updateHorizontal

- This protected method places the bar at the container's bottom edge with the configured margin and sets its thickness to `getBarWidth()`.
- The length is `max(2 * thickness, (containerWidth - 2 * margin) * containerWidth / contentWidth)`; its horizontal position follows `getScrollX() / getMaxScrollX()` along the remaining travel. The minimum length is not capped to the available space.
- Sets the bar inactive if the horizontal scroll range is not positive or the content is not a `RectNode`; otherwise, it sets the bar active.
- Requires a valid container pointer. See `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer` for synchronization, coordinate assumptions, and container lifetime.

## ScrollBar::draw

- This protected override draws one vertical or horizontal stroke in local coordinates, using the stored bar color and thickness; it draws no track.
- The stroke's endpoints are inset by half the thickness so the round caps reach the ends of the node's rectangle. It saves and restores the drawing style with `pushStyle()` and `popStyle()`.
- Drawing does not synchronize the bar with the container; see `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer`. See `Node::draw` for callback timing and coordinates.
- Known issue: [#915](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/915) (the internal popStyle() turns depth testing off inside a camera scope unless enableDepthTest() is enabled).

```cpp
class CustomScrollBar : public ScrollBar {
public:
    using ScrollBar::ScrollBar;
protected:
    void draw() override {
        ScrollBar::draw();
    }
};
```

## ScrollBar::onMousePress

- This protected override accepts `const MouseEventArgs& e`. A left-button press with a non-null container starts dragging, records the bar-local `e.pos.y` or `e.pos.x` for the selected direction, and returns `true`.
- Other buttons or a null container return `false` without changing the drag state. See `Node::onMousePress` for coordinates, propagation, and how returning `true` establishes the pointer grab.
- ScrollBar's press, release, and drag overrides do not call the RectNode implementations, so they do not notify the inherited `mousePressed`, `mouseReleased`, or `mouseDragged` events or forward to the simpler `Vec2` overloads.

```cpp
class CustomScrollBar : public ScrollBar {
public:
    using ScrollBar::ScrollBar;
protected:
    bool onMousePress(const MouseEventArgs& e) override {
        return ScrollBar::onMousePress(e);
    }
};
```

## ScrollBar::onMouseRelease

- This protected override accepts `const MouseEventArgs& e` and clears the drag state only when `e.button == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT`.
- Always returns `true`, including for other buttons, when not dragging, or with a null container.
- See `Node::onMouseRelease` for release delivery and `ScrollBar::onMousePress` for inherited event behavior.

```cpp
class CustomScrollBar : public ScrollBar {
public:
    using ScrollBar::ScrollBar;
protected:
    bool onMouseRelease(const MouseEventArgs& e) override {
        return ScrollBar::onMouseRelease(e);
    }
};
```

## ScrollBar::onMouseDrag

- This protected override accepts `const MouseDragEventArgs& e` and uses bar-local `e.pos.y` for a vertical bar or `e.pos.x` for a horizontal bar to update the container's scroll position.
- Returns `false` if dragging has not started or the container is null; otherwise, it returns `true`, even when no scrolling occurs. It does not check `e.button`.
- It does not update the bar's own position; call `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer` to synchronize the display. See `Node::onMouseDrag` for delivery and `ScrollBar::onMousePress` for inherited event behavior.

```cpp
class CustomScrollBar : public ScrollBar {
public:
    using ScrollBar::ScrollBar;
protected:
    bool onMouseDrag(const MouseDragEventArgs& e) override {
        return ScrollBar::onMouseDrag(e);
    }
};
```

## ScrollBar::handleVerticalDrag

- This protected method accepts `float localY` in the bar's local coordinates and computes a proposed top position by adding the difference from the recorded grab offset to `getY()`.
- Clamps that position between the margin and `containerHeight - margin - barHeight`, then maps it proportionally to `0` through `getMaxScrollY()` using `setScrollY()`. This does not depend on whether wheel scrolling is enabled for the axis.
- Does nothing if the maximum vertical scroll or the bar's available travel is not positive. It requires a valid container pointer and does not check the drag state or move the bar itself; see `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer` for synchronization and lifetime.

## ScrollBar::handleHorizontalDrag

- This protected method accepts `float localX` in the bar's local coordinates and computes a proposed left position by adding the difference from the recorded grab offset to `getX()`.
- Clamps that position between the margin and `containerWidth - margin - barWidth`, then maps it proportionally to `0` through `getMaxScrollX()` using `setScrollX()`. This does not depend on whether wheel scrolling is enabled for the axis.
- Does nothing if the maximum horizontal scroll or the bar's available travel is not positive. It requires a valid container pointer and does not check the drag state or move the bar itself; see `ScrollBar::updateFromContainer` for synchronization and lifetime.

## TweenMod::earlyUpdate

- This protected callback runs during node tree updates, before the owner's timers and `update()`. An inactive node or an inactive ancestor prevents these updates.
- While playing and not completed, it adds `getDeltaTime()` to elapsed time; without an owner it does nothing, and while elapsed time is negative it waits without changing properties.
- It applies easing to normalized progress and updates enabled properties. Position and scale use linear interpolation, rotation uses angle interpolation, and quaternion rotation uses spherical interpolation.
- Once normalized progress reaches `1.0f`, it stops playback, marks completion, and notifies `complete` after applying the property values.
- Known issue: [#906](https://github.com/TrussC-org/TrussC/issues/906) (`runHeadlessApp` calls only `App::update()`, so this callback is not run automatically).

## ChipSoundBundle::Entry

- Contains a `ChipSoundNote` value in `note` and a start time in `time`; see `ChipSoundBundle::add` for timing conventions.
- `ChipSoundBundle::entries` stores these values in a public vector, so notes can be inspected or edited directly as well as appended with `add()`.
- Edits affect subsequent duration calculations and builds, but do not change previously built sounds.

## ChipSoundNote::Wave

- Use values such as `ChipSoundNote::Wave::Square` or the type alias `Wave::Square`.
- `Noise` and `PinkNoise` ignore `hz`. Each generation starts from the same noise seed, so identical settings produce the same samples.
- `Silent` represents a rest with the specified duration. See `ChipSoundNote::generateBuffer` for its behavior when reusing a buffer.

## Font::setOversampling

- Clamps `n` to an integer from 1 to 4 and returns this `Font` by reference. A value of 1 disables oversampling; the initial factor comes from the default in effect when the `Font` is constructed.
- Glyphs are rasterized at `n` times the resolution on each axis and box-filtered, retaining a denser atlas for drawing under scaling and rotation. Atlas memory grows roughly with `n * n`; oversized glyphs may use a lower raster resolution to fit an atlas page.
- This setter and `Font::setMipmaps` can be called before or after loading. A changed option selects or creates the corresponding shared atlas for a loaded file; an unloaded font records it for the next load. For URL-loaded fonts, the change takes effect on the next load and produces a warning.
- Both setters cancel a pending asynchronous load before checking whether the value changed. Threading and cancellation rules are described in `Font::loadAsync`.

## Font::getOversampling

- Returns the configured integer from 1 to 4, where 1 disables oversampling. Atlas replacement, reduced resolution for oversized glyphs, and deferred changes for URL fonts are described in `Font::setOversampling`.

## Font::setDefaultOversampling

- This static setter clamps `n` to an integer from 1 to 4. The initial default is 1.
- The value is copied when a `Font` is constructed. Existing objects are unaffected, including objects that have not loaded a font yet; use `Font::setOversampling` to change them.

## Font::getDefaultOversampling

- Returns the current static default from 1 to 4, initially 1. The value is adopted at construction as described in `Font::setDefaultOversampling`.

## Font::setMipmaps

- Enables or disables mipmap generation and returns this `Font` by reference. The default is `true`; mipmaps reduce flicker when text is drawn small.
- Generation is requested lazily when drawing exceeds two atlas texels per target pixel, accounting for oversampling, load-time DPI, the drawing transform, and target pixel scale. The chain is generated during a subsequent dirty-atlas texture update.
- A full chain adds approximately one third to the base atlas texture memory and adds CPU filtering work when dirty atlas textures are rebuilt. Disabling it avoids that chain and its rebuild cost.
- Atlas replacement, deferred changes for URL fonts, and cancellation of pending loads follow `Font::setOversampling`.

## Font::getMipmaps

- Returns the configured permission, initially `true`, rather than whether a mip chain has already been built. Generation timing and deferred URL-font changes are described in `Font::setMipmaps`.

## Font::setGridFit

- Sets the placement option and returns this `Font` by reference. It is enabled by default and does not reload the font, rebuild the atlas, or add atlas memory.
- When `Font::gridFitLands` permits fitting, accumulated baseline offsets are rounded once, shifting a baseline by at most half a logical pixel. Horizontal layout rounds once per line; reported metrics and glyph advances remain unchanged.
- The anchor itself is not rounded, allowing smooth fractional movement. Fitting automatically stands down when the scale test fails; see `Font::gridFitLands` and `Font::fitY`.

## Font::getGridFit

- Returns the configured flag, initially `true`. This does not test whether the current transform permits fitting; that test is described in `Font::gridFitLands`.

## Font::gridFitLands

- This protected helper returns `true` only when grid fitting is enabled and the effective scale differs from 1 by less than `0.01`.
- Effective scale is the larger X/Y basis length of the model-view matrix, replaced with 1 if nonpositive, then multiplied by the target pixel scale. The test does not account for anchor translation or camera projection, so `true` does not guarantee that the final baseline lies on an absolute device-pixel boundary.

## Font::fitY

- This protected helper returns `round(offsetFromAnchor)` when `Font::gridFitLands` is `true`; otherwise, it returns the input unchanged. The offset is measured in logical pixels.
- Pass the offset accumulated from the anchor, such as `getAscent() + lineIdx * getLineHeight()`, then round once. Rounding the line height before repeated addition causes layout error to accumulate across lines.
- Add the returned offset to the unchanged anchor. This preserves fractional anchor movement while limiting each fitted baseline offset to half a unit of rounding error.

## TcpClient::isConnecting

- Returns `true` during asynchronous connection setup or a pending TCP connect; for `TlsClient`, also includes the TLS handshake.
- During a successful asynchronous `onConnect` listener, it can remain `true` until the connection worker finishes its setup call, even though `isConnected()` is already `true`.

## TcpClient::setConnectTimeout

- `seconds` sets the TCP connection deadline in seconds; the default `0` uses the operating system deadline, and non-positive values are stored as `0`.
- Measures from socket connection setup after DNS resolution, so it does not limit DNS resolution or the TLS handshake; using an IP address avoids hostname resolution.
- Applies to an already pending TCP connection as well as later attempts; a positive value such as `setConnectTimeout(5)` allows a failed attempt to end sooner than the operating system deadline.
- Cancellation remains available when the value is `0`; failure notification behavior is described in `TcpClient::onConnect`.

## TcpClient::setSendTimeout

- `seconds` is the maximum time without write progress, in seconds; defaults to `60`, and non-positive values are stored as `0`, which disables the deadline.
- Each payload captures the timeout when it becomes the active send, and successful writes restart its idle timer; waiting in the queue is not included, and changing the setting does not alter an already active payload's timeout.
- Applies to both `send()` and `sendAsync()`, including TLS writes; expiry closes the connection, reports the timeout through `onError`, and completes the send with `SendError::Disconnected`.

## TcpClient::sendAsync

- Pointer-and-size and `string` overloads copy the bytes, while `vector<char>&&` transfers ownership; shares FIFO order and idle timeout behavior with `send()`.
- Returns a `SendResult`; success means the data was queued and supplies a non-zero `id`, which is later reported as `onSendComplete`'s `sendId`.
- Immediate rejection returns `NotRunning`, `QueueFull`, or `Disconnected` with id `0` and emits `onError` on the calling thread; it does not produce a send completion. Retrying directly from that error listener can recurse.
- Queue admission rules are described in `TcpClient::setSendAsyncBufferSize`; `QueueFull` does not disconnect the client.
- With threads, the writer advances the queue; without threads, `processNetwork()` advances it without waiting for socket readiness and reports completions inline. Completion delivery is described in `TcpClient::onSendComplete`.
- Timeout behavior, including completion as `SendError::Disconnected` after the connection closes, is described in `TcpClient::setSendTimeout`; use this API instead of `send()` from inline send completion or send-error listeners.

```cpp
// tcApp members: TcpClient client; EventListener connectListener;
void tcApp::setup() {
    connectListener = client.onConnect.listen([this](TcpConnectEventArgs& e) {
        if (e.success) client.sendAsync("hello\n");
    }, Deliver::Main);
    client.connectAsync("127.0.0.1", 9000);
}
```

## TcpClient::onSendComplete

- Receives `TcpSendCompleteEventArgs`; `clientId` is `-1`, `sendId` identifies the queued payload, `error` gives its result, and `bytesSent` records how many bytes were written.
- `SendError::None` means the entire payload was written, without confirming receipt by the remote application; a failed send can report a partial byte count.
- Every accepted send, including `send()` and pending sends cancelled by `disconnect()`, reports completion once while the client remains alive; destruction stops workers and wakes waiting senders without emitting new events.
- With threads enabled, notifications run on the writer; without threads, they run from `processNetwork()`, `send()`, or `disconnect()`. Main-thread delivery options are described in `TcpClient::setUseThread`.

## TcpClient::setSendAsyncBufferSize

- `bytes` sets the threshold in bytes for the shared `send()` and `sendAsync()` queue; defaults to `16 * 1024 * 1024`, and `0` removes the limit.
- Admission checks the current unfinished byte count before adding the next payload, rather than the resulting total; an empty queue accepts any payload size, and a single accepted payload can carry the queue above the mark.
- When the unfinished byte count is at or above the mark, `sendAsync()` returns `QueueFull` without disconnecting, while `send()` waits for room; this limits further queue growth when a peer stops reading.
- Changing the mark does not discard accepted data and wakes senders waiting for room.

## TcpClient::getSendAsyncBufferSize

- Returns the configured threshold in bytes, initially `16 * 1024 * 1024`; `0` means unlimited.
- Queue admission and oversized-payload behavior are described in `TcpClient::setSendAsyncBufferSize`.

## TcpClient::getSendAsyncPendingBytes

- Counts both `send()` and `sendAsync()` payloads, including the full original size of the active payload until it completes; partial writes do not reduce this count.
- Returns `0` when there is no send channel; this is a queue accounting value rather than the operating system's remaining socket-buffer byte count.

## TcpClient::state

- This protected hook returns a `shared_ptr<State>` for the current run; load it once at function entry and use the same pointer throughout that operation.
- A restart can replace the client's current state, while a retained pointer keeps the previous run's state alive.
- Retaining state does not keep the public client object alive; listener-triggered teardown rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## TcpClient::setTransport

- This protected hook stores the supplied `shared_ptr<Transport>` in the current connection state; call it before connecting.
- The transport supplies connection setup, writes, connection-progress checks, and network processing; the default is plain TCP, and `TlsClient` installs its TLS transport here.
- Later connections retain the configured transport, and workers retain transport ownership for their run; worker lifetime rules are described in `TcpClient`.

## Fbo::setDebugName

- `setDebugName(name)` assigns the name used by MCP inspection. `tc_list_fbos` lists live objects with their index, name, width, height, and format; unnamed objects remain selectable by index.
- `tc_analyze_image` accepts `source = {fbo: name or index}` and reads the final Fbo contents after the frame. Duplicate names require selecting an index.
- Moves transfer the name and index to the destination and remove the moved-from registry entry; destruction removes the entry. Naming a moved-from object registers it again.
- MCP analysis rejects Fbo readback on Web and float Fbo readback on iOS. These are inspection-tool restrictions; direct API readback is described in `Fbo::readPixels` and `Fbo::readPixelsFloat`.
- MCP analysis converts non-float Fbo formats to RGBA8 for byte readback. A Texture cannot be selected directly as an analysis source; draw it into a named Fbo first.

## Fbo::getDebugName

- Returns the name set by `setDebugName()` as `const string&`; unnamed and moved-from objects return an empty string.

## Image::setDebugName

- `setDebugName(name)` names this image for `tc_list_images` and `tc_analyze_image`. The list includes live images with `index`, `name`, `width`, `height` and `format`; unnamed images remain selectable by index.
- Moves transfer the name and index and remove the moved-from registry entry; destruction removes the entry. Duplicate names are ambiguous for analysis, so select by index.
- `tc_analyze_image` reads CPU pixels with `source = {"image": nameOrIndex}`. Other selectors are `window`, `fbo` and `path`; Texture, VideoPlayer and VideoGrabber objects are not sources.
- Analysis returns `width`, `height`, `format` (`RGBA8` or `float`), `colorSpace` (`sRGB` or `linear`) and `results` in `ops` order. Byte colors become normalized RGBA; float values, including values above 1, are preserved.
- Supported operations are `pixel(x,y)` returning `color`, `histogram(bins)` returning `histogram[channel][bin]`, `count(color,tolerance)` or `count(min,max)` returning `count`, `bbox` and `centroid`, `stats()` returning `mean`, `min` and `max`, `grid(cols,rows)` returning mean `colors[row][col]`, `diff(path,threshold)` returning `count`, `bbox` and `maxDifference`, and `line(x0,y0,x1,y1)` returning `colors`.
- Each operation accepts an optional `rect = [x,y,w,h]`, defaulting to the whole image. Coordinates start at the top left; `bbox` is `[x,y,w,h]` and `centroid` is `[x,y]`. Empty matches return null bounding boxes and centroids. Rectangles must be nonempty and inside the image, and grid cells must be nonempty.
- Histograms divide 0–1 into equal bins and put outliers in the end bins. Count accepts RGB or RGBA bounds, or a color with a nonnegative scalar tolerance. Lines use inclusive Bresenham samples, require endpoints inside the image and retain only samples inside the rectangle.
- Diff requires equal image dimensions, compares raw RGBA values and counts pixels whose maximum absolute channel difference is strictly above the nonnegative threshold. It also accepts an optional `save`.
- Optional top-level `save` and `diff.save` follow `tc_save_screenshot` path rules: UTF-8 paths, data-directory-relative resolution, parent creation and `.png` appended to unsupported extensions. Omitted or null paths write nothing. Float file output is clamped to 0–1 without changing analysis values.
- Default analysis limits are 4096 histogram bins, 65536 grid cells and 256 operations; excessive parameters are rejected before their scratch allocation. Replies default to 64 MiB and aggregate MCP working memory to 256 MiB. Configure limits with `mcp::setAdmissionLimits()` while the HTTP server is stopped and no work is outstanding.
- File sources and diff references use a bounded encoded snapshot, inspect stb or platform metadata, and reserve decoded storage and estimated codec workspace before decoding. macOS and iOS retain ImageIO formats, including HEIC, TIFF and JPEG 2000 where supported.

## Image::getDebugName

- Returns the stored name as `const string&`; unnamed and moved-from images return an empty string.
- See `Image::setDebugName` for inspection and registry behavior.

## VideoErrorEventArgs

- The player's `onError` event supplies `message`, a readable error description, and `errorCode`, a backend-specific integer that defaults to zero when unavailable.
- Call the player's `update()` on the main thread to receive queued runtime errors; decoder callbacks do not invoke listeners directly.
- Playback is stopped before notification without rewinding or replacing the last frame. Only the first pending error is retained, and further notifications are suppressed until playback is restarted or the error state is reset.

## VideoErrorEventArgs::message

- A `string` containing the error text supplied by the backend or player. See `VideoPlayerBase::onError` for event delivery.

## VideoErrorEventArgs::errorCode

- An `int64_t` initialized to zero; zero is also used when no code is available.
- Codes are backend-specific and are not portable between backends. See `VideoPlayerBase::onError` for event delivery.

## VideoPlayerBase::onError

- Keep calling `update()` on the main thread to receive this event once per error stop; `VideoErrorEventArgs` contains a message and a backend-specific error code, or zero when unavailable.
- Error handling stops playback without unloading, rewinding, or replacing the last frame; `isPlaying()`, `isPaused()`, `isFrameNew()`, and `isDone()` become false.
- There is no automatic retry. The application may seek, call `play()` to retry playback, or reload; seeking and `play()` retain the delivered error message, while successful loading and `close()` clear it.
- Query `hasError()` and `getErrorMessage()` on the main thread after `update()`; backend threads only queue reports and do not notify listeners directly.
- Normal end of file and stalls alone are not errors. The Linux decoder warns about and skips individual invalid packets or frames.
- Listeners may close or reload the player during notification. Moving a player does not move its `onError` listeners; they stay with their original object.

## VideoPlayerBase::hasError

- Returns true when the stored error message is nonempty; a queued report alone does not make it true.
- Successful loading and `close()` clear the error; seeking and `play()` retain it.
- For main-thread query and delivery rules, see `VideoPlayerBase::onError`.

## VideoPlayerBase::getErrorMessage

- Returns a `const string&` to the stored message, or an empty string when no error is stored.
- For error retention and main-thread query rules, see `VideoPlayerBase::onError`.

## VideoPlayerBase::reportPlaybackError

- Subclasses may call this protected helper from any thread with a message and an optional backend-specific `int64_t` code, which defaults to zero.
- The queue retains the first nonempty pending message and its code until consumed; further reports do not replace it.
- This function does not change playback state or notify listeners; delivery rules are described in `VideoPlayerBase::onError`.

## VideoPlayerBase::dispatchPlaybackError

- Subclasses call this protected helper from `update()` on the main thread, outside backend locks; playback and listener rules are described in `VideoPlayerBase::onError`.
- It consumes the pending report and returns false without notification if its message is empty or the player is already stopped by an error.
- Otherwise, it stores the message, pauses the backend, updates the error-stop state, logs the message and code using `logModule` (default `"VideoPlayer"`), notifies `onError`, and returns true.
- Return immediately from the caller when this function returns true, because a listener may have closed or reloaded the player.

## VideoPlayerBase::clearPlaybackError

- Subclasses call this protected helper on successful loading and closing to discard the pending report, clear the stored message, and reset the error-stop flag.
- It does not resume playback or notify listeners; the shared error contract is described in `VideoPlayerBase::onError`.

## VideoPlayerBase::movePlaybackErrorFrom

- Subclasses use this protected helper when moving a player to transfer its delivered message, error-stop flag, and pending report, then clear the source error state.
- The destination message and error-stop flag are replaced; if the destination already has a nonempty pending report, that report takes precedence over the source pending report.
- Event listeners stay with their original object; see `VideoPlayerBase::onError` for the shared error contract.

## AudioBackend

- `Default` tries miniaudio's backend order for the platform; `Null` explicitly runs the mixer and audio callbacks silently without a physical output device.
- With `Default`, failure to create any real backend context can fall back to Null and log a Warning. If a real backend context opens but its device cannot open or start, initialization fails without switching to Null.
- Set the choice through `AudioSettings::backend`.

## AudioSettings::backend

- The default is `AudioBackend::Default`. For silent headless operation, set `AudioBackend::Null` and successfully call `AudioEngine::getInstance().init(settings)` before loading sounds.
- Playback device enumeration uses the engine's existing backend context; before a context exists, it probes the default backend order. Native `MicInput` follows a real engine backend or an explicitly requested Null backend; an automatic playback fallback to Null does not enable synthetic microphone capture.
- Zero-argument `AudioEngine::init()` uses `AudioBackend::Default` rather than retaining this choice. See `AudioBackend` for fallback behavior.

## AudioInitFailure

- `None` indicates no recorded initialization failure, `NoBackend` indicates context creation failure, `DeviceOpen` indicates device initialization failure, and `DeviceStart` indicates device start failure.
- Read the value through `AudioEngine::getInstance().getStats().initFailure`. A failure remains recorded until initialization succeeds.

## AudioStats::initFailure

- `AudioInitFailure::NoBackend`, `AudioInitFailure::DeviceOpen`, and `AudioInitFailure::DeviceStart` indicate failure to create a backend context, open the output device, or start it, respectively; `AudioInitFailure::None` means no failure is recorded.
- The failure record survives `shutdown()` and is cleared only by successful initialization. Its result code and backend are available in `initFailureResult` and `initFailureBackend`.
- `tc_get_audio_state` includes an `initFailure` object with the reason, result code, backend, and requested device name only while a failure is recorded.

## AudioStats::initFailureResult

- Contains the miniaudio result code, such as `-401` for failure to open a backend device; it is `0` when no failure is recorded.
- For failure meanings and record lifetime, see `AudioStats::initFailure`.

## AudioStats::initFailureBackend

- Points to a static backend-name string resolved from the same atomic failure snapshot as `initFailure` and `initFailureResult`; no backend context or no recorded failure produces an empty string.
- For failure record lifetime, see `AudioStats::initFailure`.

## console::start

- Call `console::start()` explicitly in `setup()` for either a windowed or headless app. Neither runner starts input automatically; this is a breaking change in v0.8.0.
- Commands are delivered through `events().console` on the main thread before updates. Input is split on whitespace, text from `#` onward is ignored, and lines with no arguments are discarded.
- Discards queued commands before enabling delivery. Calling it while delivery is already enabled does nothing.
- The first call creates the process's only detached reader, which consumes standard input until EOF or process exit. Later calls reuse it; a reader that has reached EOF is not restarted.
- `console::stop()` disables delivery while the reader continues consuming input and discards lines read while stopped. Both runners stop delivery before the app's `exit()` and `cleanup()`.
- Supports LF and CRLF line endings, including a final line without a newline at EOF.
- External control text is bounded to 1 MiB per line (excluding LF, including CR), 1024 pending commands and 16 MiB of pending raw text. An oversized line is drained and rejected whole; a full queue drops the new whole command. Reading continues without waiting for app delivery. Each store emits one Warning on its first rejection and retains cumulative internal loss counts for the process lifetime; stopping/restarting delivery does not reset them.
- On Web, logs a notice and leaves delivery disabled.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    console::start();
}
```

## console::stop

- Disables delivery and discards queued commands. On Web, does nothing.
- The reader continues consuming input; its lifetime and resuming delivery with `console::start()` are described in `console::start`.

## console::isEnabled

- Returns `false` initially and after `console::stop()`, and `true` after `console::start()` enables delivery. Always returns `false` on Web.
- Reports the delivery flag, not whether the reader is still running; EOF does not clear this flag. Reader lifetime is described in `console::start`.

## mcp::ToolLevel

- The levels are ordered `Public < ReadOnly < Control`; a grant includes tools at lower levels.
- Custom tools default to `Public`; the only Public built-in tool is the health query. The host grant initially defaults to Public, or Control in native development builds.
- ReadOnly includes inspection, screenshots, status, and alerts; capture tools may write files. Control also includes input, scene changes, recording, and quitting.
- Built-in key input accepts the 120 defined nonzero sokol key codes, so synthetic input can hold at most 120 distinct keys. Mouse buttons are 0–2; mouse movement also accepts -1.
- Built-in input requires finite coordinates and scroll deltas that fit in a float, and boolean modifier flags. Invalid input returns JSON-RPC error -32602 before callbacks or state changes.
- An environment-started Public endpoint exposes only health information. Explicitly calling `mcp::startHttpServer` also permits Public custom tools.

## mcp::setToolLevel

- Pass a `mcp::ToolLevel`. ReadOnly or Control opens an HTTP listener on loopback if no listener is running; `TRUSSC_MCP_PORT` selects the port when set.
- Tool registration may occur before or after this call. The grant belongs to the host and survives hot reload.
- Native development builds retain Control regardless of the requested level; their automatic listener configuration also accepts `TRUSSC_MCP_HOST` and `TRUSSC_MCP_TOKEN`.
- `TRUSSC_MCP=0` prevents HTTP startup and closes an existing listener without changing the stored grant.
- Downgrading to Public preserves an explicitly opened listener. Otherwise, an environment request keeps the listener in health-only mode; without that request, the listener stops.
- Call `mcp::startHttpServer` first when choosing the listener address or token explicitly.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly);
}
```

## mcp::getToolLevel

- Returns the stored `mcp::ToolLevel`; the server checks this grant for every `tools/list` and `tools/call` request.
- The value is shared across hot reloads and does not indicate whether HTTP is running.

## mcp::isDebuggerEnabled

- This compatibility query returns `mcp::getToolLevel() >= mcp::ToolLevel::Control`.
- It checks the grant rather than whether an HTTP listener is running.

## mcp::tool

- Pass the tool name and description, then finish the returned `mcp::ToolBuilder` with `bind()`.
- Names starting with `tc_` are reserved: the builder logs an Error and does not register them. The `tcx_` prefix is available.
- Creating or binding a tool does not start HTTP. Access follows the current host grant.
- See `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly);
    mcp::tool("app_fps", "Return the frame rate")
        .level(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly)
        .bind(function<json()>([] { return json{{"fps", getFrameRate()}}; }));
}
```

## mcp::ToolBuilder

- Create one with `mcp::tool(name, description)`, optionally call `level()` and `arg<T>()`, then call `bind()` to register the handler.
- The required level defaults to `mcp::ToolLevel::Public`; destroying an unbound builder does not register a tool.
- See `mcp::tool` for name restrictions and `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime.

## mcp::ToolBuilder::level

- Stores the supplied `mcp::ToolLevel` and returns the builder by reference for chaining; it does not change the host grant.
- The default is Public. Core and official addon tools explicitly specify their required levels.

## mcp::ToolBuilder::arg

- Call `arg<T>(name, description, required)`; `required` defaults to true. Returns the builder by reference for chaining.
- `int` maps to `integer`, float and double to `number`, bool to `boolean`, and json to `object`; other types use `string`.
- Arguments retain declaration order for typed binding. Setting `required` to false changes the schema but does not supply a default value; see `mcp::ToolBuilder::bind`.

## mcp::ToolBuilder::bind

- Accepts `function<json(const json&)>` for direct argument access, or a typed `function` returning json with zero to three arguments. Returns void.
- For typed handlers, declare at least as many schema arguments as handler parameters before binding; names are selected in declaration order and values are read with `args.at(name).get<T>()`.
- Typed handlers still require arguments marked optional in the schema. Use the JSON handler overload to provide defaults for omitted arguments.
- Returned JSON is serialized as text content unless it is a nonempty array whose first element contains `type`, in which case it is used as MCP content. Handler exceptions become tool errors.
- See `mcp::Tool` for main-thread execution, replacement behavior, and callback lifetime; access follows the current host grant.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::tool("echo_value", "Return the supplied value")
        .arg<int>("value", "Value to return")
        .bind<int>([](int value) { return json{{"value", value}}; });
}
```

## mcp::resource

- Pass the resource URI and display name, optionally chain `desc()` and `mime()`, then call `bind()` with a function returning text.
- Returns `mcp::ResourceBuilder`; creating or binding a resource does not open HTTP.
- See `mcp::Resource` for exposure and `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::resource("app://info", "Application info")
        .desc("Application information")
        .mime("text/plain")
        .bind([] { return string("Ready"); });
}
```

## mcp::ResourceBuilder

- Create one with `mcp::resource(uri, name)`, set optional description and MIME type with `desc()` and `mime()`, then finish with `bind()`.
- Description and MIME type initially contain empty strings; destroying an unbound builder does not register a resource.
- See `mcp::Resource` for resource behavior and `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime.

## mcp::ResourceBuilder::desc

- Copies the supplied string into the resource description and returns the builder by reference for chaining.

## mcp::ResourceBuilder::mime

- Copies the supplied MIME type string and returns the builder by reference for chaining; the string is not validated.
- The default is an empty string, represented as null in resource listings and as an empty string in resource reads.

## mcp::ResourceBuilder::bind

- Accepts `function<string()>` and returns void. Registering the same URI replaces the previous resource.
- The producer runs on the main thread when the resource is read; its returned string is placed in the response's `text` field, and standard exceptions become resource-read errors.
- See `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime.

## mcp::hasTool

- Returns true if the exact name exists in the registry, regardless of the host grant, health-only mode, or HTTP listener state.
- See `mcp::Tool` for registry threading.

## mcp::Tool

- Stores `name`, `description`, `level`, `args`, `handler`, and the registration `owner`; level defaults to Public and owner to null.
- `getSchema()` returns an object input schema built from the arguments. Registering an existing tool name replaces its metadata and handler and logs a Warning.
- Perform tool, resource, and status registration, and registry queries such as `mcp::hasTool`, on the main thread; HTTP request processing accesses these registries there without registry locks.
- Tool handlers and resource producers run on the main thread. Registrations retain copies of callbacks; objects referenced by captures must remain alive while the callbacks can run.
- Hot reload removes registrations belonging to the outgoing app before deleting it. Registrations without an owner remain registered.

## mcp::ToolArg

- Stores the argument's `name`, schema `type`, `description`, and `required` flag; required defaults to true.
- The type string is copied into the schema unchanged, except `string|null`, which becomes the type array `["string", "null"]`.
- This metadata declares the input schema; it does not itself validate handler arguments or provide defaults.

## mcp::Resource

- Stores `uri`, `name`, `mimeType`, `description`, a `function<string()>` handler, and the registration `owner`; owner defaults to null.
- Resource reads return the handler's string in the `text` field, even if the string contains base64 data.
- Resources have no ToolLevel field. Health-only mode hides them and rejects reads; otherwise, resource access is not filtered by the tool grant.
- See `mcp::Tool` for registration threading, callback lifetime, and hot-reload cleanup.

## mcp::startHttpServer

- Call `startHttpServer(port, host, token)`; defaults are 0, `"127.0.0.1"`, and `""`. A nonpositive port lets the OS choose; retrieve the bound port with `mcp::getHttpPort`.
- JSON-RPC requests use `POST /mcp`. A configured token requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; hosts other than `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1` require a nonempty token.
- Returns void; refusal or bind failure logs an Error. `TRUSSC_MCP=0` prevents startup and closes an existing listener.
- The first successful opener chooses the address and token. Call this before `mcp::setToolLevel` to choose them explicitly; later mismatched parameters log an Error and change nothing.
- Matching parameters reuse the listener; the original requested port or the actual bound port is accepted. A matching explicit call also permits Public custom tools on a health-only listener.
- Default admission limits are 1 MiB each for wire and decoded bodies, 8 KiB per request/header/trailer line, 64 KiB total HTTP metadata, 128 header/trailer fields, 32 outstanding connections, and 4 workers.
- Oversized bodies return 413, excessive metadata returns 431, and excess connections close. Rejections log one Warning per admission store and increment counters that persist across HTTP restarts.
- Request JSON nesting defaults to 64 levels. Parse admission failures return HTTP 503 with a reason; configure limits with `mcp::setAdmissionLimits` while the server is stopped.
- The HTTP APIs `startHttpServer`, `stopHttpServer`, `processHttpQueue`, and `getHttpPort` are available on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android; they are not declared for Web.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::startHttpServer(0, "127.0.0.1");
    mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly);
}
```

## mcp::stopHttpServer

- Answers queued, deferred, and other active requests with shutdown errors to release waiting workers, then stops the listener. Results arriving after a shutdown reply are discarded.
- Normally waits for the listener thread to finish; when called from HTTP handling or the listener thread, it detaches instead of joining itself.
- Resets the HTTP port to 0 and clears explicit-open and health-only state. If an error reply cannot fit the limits, the response is HTTP 503 with `X-MCP-Reason`.
- For platform availability, see `mcp::startHttpServer`.

## mcp::processHttpQueue

- Drains queued requests on the calling thread. Call it only on the main thread so tool handlers and resource producers run there.
- The normal frame loop calls it before update and draw; the headless loop also calls it automatically. Deferred results remain pending until their after-frame processing.
- For platform availability, see `mcp::startHttpServer`.

## mcp::getHttpPort

- Returns the actual bound port as an int, or 0 when the listener is not running.
- For platform availability, see `mcp::startHttpServer`.

## mcp::deferToolResultUntilAfterFrame

- Call inside a tool handler with `function<json()>`; the handler's immediate return value is ignored and the producer's JSON becomes the result.
- The producer runs on the main thread just after the target window's next present, with that window's context current. This permits GPU readback after drawing has completed.
- `targetWindow` defaults to null for the main window; a non-null value must identify the target's `WindowContext`, such as `&window.context()`.
- For non-null targets, the main window's after-frame processing rejects overdue requests after five seconds if the target has not rendered. Without presented frames, such as in a headless loop, producers do not run.
- The HTTP worker waits for the result. Shutdown or removal of the registering app during hot reload answers pending requests with an error instead of running their producers.
- Keep captured objects alive until completion; producer exceptions become tool errors. See `mcp::deferToolResultTwoStage` to move expensive CPU work to the HTTP worker.

## mcp::deferToolResultTwoStage

- Inside a tool handler, pass `function<function<json()>()>`: the main stage returns the worker stage that produces the result JSON.
- The main stage runs after the target window presents; perform GPU readback there. The returned stage and result serialization run on the waiting HTTP worker, allowing expensive resizing or encoding without doing that work in the frame loop.
- The worker stage must use data that remains valid and is safe to access from a worker thread.
- Target selection, ignored immediate return values, frame requirements, timeouts, and pending-request cleanup follow `mcp::deferToolResultUntilAfterFrame`. Main-stage exceptions become tool errors; in the worker stage, only exceptions derived from `std::exception` are converted to tool errors.

## mcp::status

- Pass a name and either `function<double()>` or `function<string()>`. The ReadOnly tool `tc_get_status` evaluates the getter on demand on the main thread and returns its value with mode `"status"`.
- Registering the same name again replaces the previous `status` or `statusGraph` entry.
- A throwing getter is omitted from that response without removing its registration or failing the other getters.
- Registration does not start HTTP. See `mcp::Tool` for registration threading, callback lifetime, and hot-reload cleanup.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly);
    mcp::status("version", [] { return string(getVersion()); });
}
```

## mcp::statusGraph

- Pass a name and `function<double()>`. The ReadOnly tool `tc_get_status` returns the current value with mode `"graph"`; this function does not store sample history.
- Evaluation, replacement by name, exception handling, registration threading, and callback lifetime follow `mcp::status`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly);
    mcp::statusGraph("fps", [] { return double(getFrameRate()); });
}
```

## mcp::statusImage

- Pass a name and `function<Pixels()>`. `tc_get_status` lists the name, and the ReadOnly tool `tc_get_status_image` fetches the image on demand.
- The getter runs on the main thread after the main window presents and returns Pixels by value; resizing and JPEG encoding run on the HTTP worker.
- Fetch width defaults to 512 pixels and is clamped to 16–4096; aspect ratio is preserved and images are never enlarged. JPEG quality defaults to 75 and is clamped to 1–100.
- An unknown name, a throwing getter, missing pixel data, or nonpositive dimensions produces an error result.
- Registering the same image name replaces its getter; image names are separate from numeric and string status names.
- Registration does not start HTTP. See `mcp::Tool` for registration threading and callback lifetime, and `mcp::deferToolResultUntilAfterFrame` for frame requirements and pending-request cleanup.

## mcp::alert

- Pass a message string; it is logged at Warning level under `"alert"` and queued with `at` and `text` fields. The timestamp uses the format `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S`.
- The ReadOnly tool `tc_get_alerts` returns and clears pending alerts, so each queued alert is received by one consumer.
- May be called from any thread. The queue retains the latest 100 pending alerts and drops the oldest when full.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    mcp::alert("Camera disconnected");
}
```

## mcp::registerInspectionTools

- Calls `mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::ReadOnly)`; see `mcp::setToolLevel` for access and HTTP behavior.
- Deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; use `mcp::setToolLevel` directly.

## mcp::registerControlTools

- Calls `mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::Control)`; see `mcp::setToolLevel` for access and HTTP behavior.
- Deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; use `mcp::setToolLevel` directly.

## mcp::registerDebuggerTools

- Calls `mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::Control)`; see `mcp::setToolLevel` for access and HTTP behavior.
- Deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; use `mcp::setToolLevel` directly.

## mcp::enableDebugger

- Calling this function has no effect; it does not change the tool level or open HTTP.
- Deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.0.0; use `mcp::setToolLevel(mcp::ToolLevel::Control)` to request control access.
- This function is unavailable in Web builds.

## mcp::ToolArg::name

- This string becomes the property name in `mcp::Tool::getSchema`; when `required` is true, it is also added to the schema's required-name array.

## mcp::ToolArg::type

- The string is copied into the schema's `type` field, for example `"string"`, `"integer"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`, `"object"` or `"array"`; `"int"` and `"float"` are not converted.
- The special value `"string|null"` produces `"type": ["string", "null"]`.

## mcp::ToolArg::description

- This string is included in the argument property's `description` field by `mcp::Tool::getSchema`.

## mcp::ToolArg::required

- Defaults to `true`; when true, `mcp::Tool::getSchema` adds the argument name to `required`.
- This flag only describes the schema; it does not check incoming arguments or provide a default value when an argument is omitted.

## mcp::Tool::name

- Clients use this string to identify the tool in listings and calls.
- Registering the same name again replaces the previous tool and logs a Warning.
- When registering through `mcp::tool`, names beginning with `tc_` are reserved for framework tools and are rejected with an Error log.

## mcp::Tool::description

- The tool listing includes this string as `description`, alongside the tool name and input schema.

## mcp::Tool::level

- Defaults to `mcp::ToolLevel::Public`; levels increase in the order `Public`, `ReadOnly`, `Control`.
- A tool above the level returned by `mcp::getToolLevel` is omitted from listings, and calls return a tool error without running its handler.
- A health-only endpoint also hides and rejects user tools at `Public`; see `mcp::setToolLevel` for exposure settings.

## mcp::Tool::args

- This `vector<mcp::ToolArg>` is initially empty and supplies the definitions used by `mcp::Tool::getSchema`.
- Typed `mcp::ToolBuilder::bind` overloads match function parameters to these definitions in their registration order.

## mcp::Tool::handler

- The signature is `json(const json&)`; HTTP tool and resource handlers run synchronously on the main thread, so long processing delays the frame loop.
- Receives the request's `arguments` value without schema validation. A nonempty returned array whose first element contains `type` is used directly as MCP content; other values are serialized as JSON inside a text content item.
- Exceptions derived from `exception` and other exceptions are caught and returned as errors; admission limits can also reject processing, as described in `mcp::AdmissionLimits`.

## mcp::Tool::owner

- This opaque `const void*` defaults to `nullptr`; tool and resource registration replace the supplied value with the framework's current registration owner.
- During hot reload, registrations belonging to the old app generation are removed before that app is deleted; pending deferred tool replies belonging to it are completed with an error.
- Ordinary apps use `nullptr`, which owner cleanup does not remove. This field tags registrations; it does not own or delete the pointed-to object.

## mcp::Tool::getSchema

- Returns a new JSON object with `type` set to `"object"`, a `properties` object, and a `required` array, using the definitions in `args`.
- Each property contains its argument's type and description; required names follow argument order. With no arguments, both collections are empty.
- During MCP request processing with an active request budget, metadata construction uses the reply and working-memory limits in `mcp::AdmissionLimits` and can throw when those limits are exceeded. Direct calls outside an active request budget do not enforce these limits.

## mcp::Resource::uri

- Clients read the resource by matching this string exactly; when resource access is enabled, an unknown URI returns JSON-RPC error `-32602`. Health-only endpoints reject resource reads with JSON-RPC error `-32000`.
- Registering another resource with the same URI replaces the previous registration.

## mcp::Resource::name

- The resource listing includes this string as `name`; resource reads use `uri` to identify the registration.

## mcp::Resource::mimeType

- This string is included as `mimeType` in resource listings and read results; it does not convert the handler's output.
- Defaults to an empty string. Listings represent an empty value as JSON `null`, while read results retain the empty string.

## mcp::Resource::description

- The resource listing includes this string as `description`; its default is an empty string.

## mcp::Resource::handler

- The signature is `string()`; the returned string is placed in the read result's `text` field, including when the string contains base64 data.
- For the shared main-thread execution rules, see `mcp::Tool::handler`.
- An exception derived from `exception` returns JSON-RPC error `-32000` with a resource-read error message.

## mcp::Resource::owner

- The default is `nullptr`; registration tagging and hot-reload cleanup follow the shared rules in `mcp::Tool::owner`.

## SaveResult

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Contains a `SaveError` in `error` and a human-readable `message`. A default-constructed result has `error == SaveError::None` and an empty message; `ok()` tests only the error value.
- Explicit Boolean conversion supports conditions such as `if (saveTextFile(path, text))`; Boolean assignments and function arguments require `.ok()` or an explicit cast.
- Small-file saves check writing and closing before atomically replacing the destination with the temporary file, and check that replacement succeeds. Append writers and recorders write in place.
- Stream opening reports whether opening succeeded, recorder frame submission reports backend acceptance, and `stop()` or `close()` reports finalization or the first retained recording failure.
- `saveScreenshot()` still returns a `bool` indicating queue acceptance. Web screenshot output is handed to the browser, so completion of the browser's disk write is not observable.

## SaveResult::error

- This `SaveError` field defaults to `SaveError::None`, which indicates success.
- `ok()` and explicit boolean conversion determine success solely from this field; see `SaveResult`.

## SaveResult::message

- This `string` field defaults to an empty string and may also be empty on failure.
- The message does not determine success; `ok()` checks only `error`.

## SaveResult::ok

- Returns `true` exactly when `error == SaveError::None`, regardless of `message`.
- Explicit boolean conversion uses the same test; see `SaveResult` for conversion rules.
- For recorder submissions, success means backend acceptance. Check `close()` or `stop()` for finalization or an earlier recording failure.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    SaveResult result = saveTextFile("settings.txt", "ready");
    if (!result.ok()) logError("Save") << result.message;
}
```

## SaveResult::success

- This static function takes no arguments and returns a `SaveResult` with `error` set to `SaveError::None` and an empty `message`, so `ok()` returns `true`.

## SaveResult::fail

- Call the static function as `SaveResult::fail(error, message)` with a `SaveError` and an optional `string` message, which defaults to empty.
- Stores the supplied error and message without validation. Passing `SaveError::None` produces a result whose `ok()` returns `true`.

## SaveError

- This scoped enum contains `None`, `AccessDenied`, `NoSpace`, `WriteFailed`, and `Unknown`; `None` has value `0` and means success.
- Shared file-writing helpers map permission errors and read-only filesystems to `AccessDenied`, lack of disk space to `NoSpace`, and other reported write failures to `WriteFailed`. Refusing a write inside the app bundle also returns `AccessDenied`.
- Replacement failures use the underlying error classification; a destination that has become a non-regular file is reported as `WriteFailed`. `Unknown` is used when an atomic writer throws an exception.

## getWidth

- Returns an integer width in the active target's drawing coordinate units: attachment pixels inside an FBO, or logical pixels for a window unless `pixelPerfect` is enabled.
- For a window in logical mode, divides the target's framebuffer width by that window's DPI scale and truncates the fractional part.
- `getHeight()` follows the same rules for height. Window-specific getters continue to report the window inside an FBO, and object member getters continue to report that object's dimensions.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    drawCircle(getWidth() * 0.5f, getHeight() * 0.5f, 40);
}
```

## getHeight

- Returns an integer height in the active target's drawing coordinate units; see `getWidth` for FBO, DPI, pixel-perfect, and window-getter behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    drawCircle(100, getHeight() * 0.5f, 40);
}
```

## getSize

- Returns `Vec2(float(getWidth()), float(getHeight()))`, with width in `x` and height in `y`; the dimensions are truncated to integers before conversion to floating point.
- The size follows the active drawing target, including an active Fbo; see `getWidth` for coordinate units, DPI scaling, and `pixelPerfect` behavior.

```cpp
void tcApp::draw() {
    Vec2 size = tc::getSize();
    drawCircle(size.x * 0.5f, size.y * 0.5f, 30.0f);
}
```

## getViewMatrix

- Returns a `Mat4` by value; modifying the returned matrix does not change the camera.
- `Fbo::begin` switches to the Fbo's camera, and `Fbo::end` restores the previous drawing target and camera. `EasyCam::end` restores the camera saved by its matching `EasyCam::begin`.
- CameraContexts stored by Nodes remain immutable snapshots from drawing time; these scope changes do not modify existing snapshots. See `Node::getCameraContext`.

## getProjectionMatrix

- Returns a `Mat4` by value; modifying the returned matrix does not change the camera.
- The matrix uses the active backend's clip-space convention: normalized device coordinate Z ranges from -1 to 1 for OpenGL/OpenGL ES, and from 0 to 1 for Metal, D3D11 and WebGPU.
- Camera restoration and Node snapshot behavior are described in `getViewMatrix`.

## Image::loadAsync

- OOM recovery is supported in Release builds, or with iterator debugging off (`_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL=0` on MSVC). With iterator debugging enabled, even an empty `std::string` or container, including a move on return, can allocate a proxy; persistent allocation failure can terminate in a `noexcept` operation. Diagnostic text and logging are best effort under OOM.
- Asynchronous Image, SoundBuffer and Font loads share 4 active preparations. Local-file requests wait in a growable queue without pending/live-request admission caps; successful local results are kept even above the shared 1 GiB retained-byte budget, with at most one Notice per app run on the first overage (an undelivered Notice is omitted at shutdown). Local loads still fail for file, decode, representation or allocation errors. Anything passed as a file path is local, including UNC/network-share paths; URLs and buffers received from the network are network/external. Paths from untrusted sources (drops, clipboard, network messages) are treated as local; validate them in the app before loading. Bound (security): URL/network-buffer loads keep 64 pending requests, 68 live-request credits and 1 GiB of retained decoded results awaiting main-thread application. Whole external requests/results that cannot fit report `TooLarge` once through `onLoad`; the first admission loss logs a Warning and later losses are counted internally. Request and byte credits include local loads and remain held until application or cancellation; external admission can therefore reject while local loads exceed these budgets. Credits are returned on application, cancellation, destruction and app exit/hot reload. Generic app-authored jobs are unaffected. Decoder working memory is governed separately.
- On Web, CMake propagates exception support to framework and application C++ code for document/font loaders and reflection. Resource preparation and application also retain exception-enabled out-of-line host definitions. If a custom build disables exception support in application TUs, allocation failure inside inline header helpers remains outside the recovery guarantee.
- Bound (gpu): images above the GPU maximum texture size on either axis are rejected before decoding (`TooLarge`). Without a recorded GPU limit (headless or before window creation), the limit is 16384 pixels per axis. Bound (security): encoded files or memory inputs larger than 64 MiB are not loaded. Allocation failure reports an Error and rejects the whole image.
- `loadAsync(path, mipmaps = false)` returns without a result; retain an `onLoad` listener to receive the `LoadResult`. Path resolution, formats and load errors follow `Image::load`.
- On native platforms, a worker decodes into private CPU pixels. A later main-thread frame applies the result, uploads the Immutable texture, optionally builds mipmaps and sends `onLoad`; notification never occurs inside `loadAsync()`.
- The committed image remains readable until application. A surviving failure clears it, as with synchronous loading. Headless loading retains CPU pixels without allocating a texture.
- Use all Image operations, access, moves and destruction on the main thread. GPU resource rules are described in `Texture`.
- Every new request cancels the previous one, even with identical arguments. `load()`, `loadFromMemory()`, `allocate()`, `clear()`, `setColor()`, `crop()`, `resize()`, `halve()` and all mirror methods also cancel pending delivery, including invalid or unchanged editing requests.
- Moves cancel pending requests on both involved handles while transferring committed data; listeners remain attached to their original handles. Destruction discards pending results and events.
- Cancellation does not wait, send an event or emit a cancellation diagnostic. A running decoder may already have logged an ordinary error; replaced decodes finish privately and can temporarily overlap.
- Completion work is taken once at the start of each frame or headless pass. Work queued during delivery waits for another pass. `isLoading()` becomes false after application and before the single `onLoad` event; a listener may start another load, move the image or delete it.
- Completions require an active `runApp()` or `runHeadlessApp()` loop. A bare `main()` without an app run does not deliver completion events. App exit waits for native decodes still running; results from an ended run or hot reload are discarded.
- On Web, VFS reading and CPU decoding are deferred to a main-loop pass and may stall that frame; application follows in a subsequent pass. This entry point does not wait through Asyncify.

```cpp
// tcApp.h: Image image; EventListener listener;
void tcApp::setup() {
    listener = image.onLoad.listen([](LoadResult& result) {
        if (!result) logError("Image") << result.message;
    });
    image.loadAsync("photo.png");
}
void tcApp::draw() { image.draw(0, 0); }
```

## Image::onLoad

- An `Event<LoadResult>` sent once on the main thread after a surviving asynchronous result has been applied. Both success and failure are reported; synchronous loading and cancellation do not send this event.
- `isLoading()` is false before notification. Retain the `EventListener` returned by `onLoad.listen()` to keep the callback registered.
- See `Image::loadAsync` for application timing, cancellation and listener lifetime during moves or destruction.

## Image::isLoading

- Returns true while the current request belongs to an active app run and is decoding or awaiting main-thread application.
- Returns false after cancellation or application, before `onLoad`, and when the associated app run has ended. This does not indicate whether committed pixels are allocated; use `isAllocated()` for that state.

## SoundBuffer::loadAsync

- Asynchronous Image, SoundBuffer and Font loads share 4 active preparations. Local-file requests wait in a growable queue without pending/live-request admission caps; successful local results are kept even above the shared 1 GiB retained-byte budget, with at most one Notice per app run on the first overage (an undelivered Notice is omitted at shutdown). Local loads still fail for file, decode, representation or allocation errors. Anything passed as a file path is local, including UNC/network-share paths; URLs and buffers received from the network are network/external. Paths from untrusted sources (drops, clipboard, network messages) are treated as local; validate them in the app before loading. Bound (security): URL/network-buffer loads keep 64 pending requests, 68 live-request credits and 1 GiB of retained decoded results awaiting main-thread application. Whole external requests/results that cannot fit report `TooLarge` once through `onLoad`; the first admission loss logs a Warning and later losses are counted internally. Request and byte credits include local loads and remain held until application or cancellation; external admission can therefore reject while local loads exceed these budgets. Credits are returned on application, cancellation, destruction and app exit/hot reload. Generic app-authored jobs are unaffected. Decoder working memory is governed separately.
- On Web, CMake propagates exception support to framework and application C++ code for document/font loaders and reflection. Resource preparation and application also retain exception-enabled out-of-line host definitions. If a custom build disables exception support in application TUs, allocation failure inside inline header helpers remains outside the recovery guarantee.
- `loadAsync(path)` returns no result directly and uses the same path resolution, format selection, errors, and decoder logs as `SoundBuffer::load`. Native builds prepare private PCM and metadata on a worker; existing committed data remains readable until the result is applied.
- Results are applied on the main thread in a later frame, never during this call. Each frame or headless loop pass takes one batch of pending completions; work queued during that pass waits for another pass. After application, `isLoading()` becomes `false` before one `onLoad` event delivers the `LoadResult`.
- A successful replacement of PCM and metadata holds the audio mixer lock, including when the buffer is playing. On any failure, previous PCM and audio metadata are preserved and no partial sound is published; the recorded path is cleared as with synchronous loads.
- A new request, even for the same path, cancels pending delivery. Synchronous loading, waveform generation, `applyADSR`, `mixFrom`, and `clip` also cancel it. Cancellation does not wait, emit an event, or log a diagnostic; decoding already underway may finish privately, retain its ordinary logs, and temporarily overlap a replacement.
- Serialize handle operations, access, copying, moving, and destruction on the main thread. Direct sample access and copy/move operations still require synchronization with audio playback.
- Copy construction copies committed data into an idle buffer with no listeners and leaves the source request running. Assignment between different buffers cancels the destination request and retains its listeners; move construction and move assignment also cancel the source request and transfer committed data while listeners remain with their original handles.
- Destruction discards pending delivery. A completion listener may start another load, move the buffer, or destroy it; retain the returned `EventListener` to keep the subscription active.
- Completion delivery requires an active `runApp` or `runHeadlessApp` run; a standalone `main()` without either receives no completion event. Results from an ended run or an earlier hot reload are discarded, and native app exit waits for decodes still running.
- On Web, WAV/MP3/FLAC/OGG file reading and CPU decoding are deferred to a main-loop pass and may stall that frame; application waits for a subsequent pass. AAC/M4A use asynchronous browser decoding and poll for completion before application is queued. This entry point does not wait through Asyncify.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    static SoundBuffer buffer;
    static auto listener = buffer.onLoad.listen([](LoadResult& result) {
        if (!result) logError("Audio") << result.message;
    });
    buffer.loadAsync("click.wav");
}
```

## SoundBuffer::onLoad

- This `Event<LoadResult>` fires once on the main thread after an uncancelled result is applied and `isLoading()` becomes `false`; cancellation emits no event.
- Retain the `EventListener` returned by `onLoad.listen(...)`. See `SoundBuffer::loadAsync` for completion timing, threading, and lifetime rules.

## SoundBuffer::isLoading

- Returns `true` while the current request is preparing data or awaiting application during an active app run; it becomes `false` before `onLoad`, after cancellation, or when the app run ends.
- See `SoundBuffer::loadAsync` for threading and completion rules.

## Font::loadAsync

- Asynchronous Image, SoundBuffer and Font loads share 4 active preparations. Local-file requests wait in a growable queue without pending/live-request admission caps; successful local results are kept even above the shared 1 GiB retained-byte budget, with at most one Notice per app run on the first overage (an undelivered Notice is omitted at shutdown). Local loads still fail for file, decode, representation or allocation errors. Anything passed as a file path is local, including UNC/network-share paths; URLs and buffers received from the network are network/external. Paths from untrusted sources (drops, clipboard, network messages) are treated as local; validate them in the app before loading. Bound (security): URL/network-buffer loads keep 64 pending requests, 68 live-request credits and 1 GiB of retained decoded results awaiting main-thread application. Whole external requests/results that cannot fit report `TooLarge` once through `onLoad`; the first admission loss logs a Warning and later losses are counted internally. Request and byte credits include local loads and remain held until application or cancellation; external admission can therefore reject while local loads exceed these budgets. Credits are returned on application, cancellation, destruction and app exit/hot reload. Generic app-authored jobs are unaffected. Decoder working memory is governed separately.
- On Web, CMake propagates exception support to framework and application C++ code for document/font loaders and reflection. Resource preparation and application also retain exception-enabled out-of-line host definitions. If a custom build disables exception support in application TUs, allocation failure inside inline header helpers remains outside the recovery guarantee.
- Call `loadAsync(nameOrPath, size, faceIndex = 0)` with a file path, system font name, or Web URL. Size is in logical pixels; path precedence and collection-face selection follow `Font::load`.
- Returns no result directly. Success, failure, and cache hits are applied on the main thread in a later frame, never during this call; `isLoading()` becomes `false` before the single `onLoad` notification.
- On native platforms, a worker prepares owned font bytes and CPU metrics. Shared-cache access and GPU work remain on the main thread, glyph rasterization stays lazy, and the request captures the current DPI, oversampling, and mipmap options.
- Serialize all operations on each `Font`, including access, copying, moving, and destruction, on the main thread. Previously committed data remains readable until the new result is applied.
- Failure normally clears the committed atlas. A URL request on a native platform reports `UnsupportedFormat` and keeps the old atlas, while still applying the requested size and captured DPI.
- A new asynchronous request, even with identical arguments, synchronous `load`, `clearAtlas`, `setOversampling`, or `setMipmaps` cancels pending delivery. The two atlas-option setters cancel even when their value is unchanged; destruction also discards pending delivery.
- Cancellation does not wait and emits no completion event or cancellation diagnostic. A running decoder may already have logged ordinary messages and can finish privately while a replacement load runs; application exit waits for native decoders still running.
- Completions are processed from one batch taken before each frame or headless pass. Work queued during that processing waits for another pass. Delivery requires `runApp` or `runHeadlessApp`; a bare `main()` has no completion delivery, and results from an ended or hot-reloaded app run are discarded.
- Copy construction shares committed data, starts idle with empty listeners, and leaves the source request running. Copy assignment cancels only the destination request and preserves its listeners.
- Moving cancels pending requests on both handles and transfers committed data; listeners remain with their original handles. Listener lifetime and callbacks that restart, move, or destroy the font are described in `Font::onLoad`.
- On Web, CPU preparation is deferred to a main-loop pass and can stall that pass, including without pthreads; application follows in a subsequent pass. This entry point does not wait through Asyncify, and URL fetching uses a 30-second timeout.

```cpp
// tcApp members: Font font; EventListener fontLoadListener;
void tcApp::setup() {
    fontLoadListener = font.onLoad.listen([](LoadResult& result) {
        if (!result) logError("Font") << result.message;
    });
    font.loadAsync(TC_FONT_SANS, 24);
}
```

## Font::onLoad

- This `Event<LoadResult>` fires once on the main thread after the surviving asynchronous result is applied, for either success or failure. `isLoading()` is already `false`; cancellation produces no event.
- Retain the `EventListener` returned by `onLoad.listen(...)` for as long as notifications are needed, and keep the font alive until completion.
- A listener may start another load, move the font, or destroy the emitting font. Delivery timing, thread rules, and copy/move behavior follow `Font::loadAsync`.

## Font::isLoading

- Returns `true` while the current request is preparing or awaiting main-thread application, provided its app run is still active.
- Returns `false` before `onLoad` fires, after cancellation, and after the app run ends. Threading and delivery rules follow `Font::loadAsync`.

## ScreenshotSaveEventArgs

- `path` identifies the destination, and `result` is a `SaveResult` describing success or failure; check it with `if (e.result)`.
- On native platforms, `path` is the resolved absolute output path after extension normalization; if path resolution throws, it retains the requested path. On Web, it contains only the download filename.
- `onScreenshotSave()` delivers the result on the main thread in a later frame, including rejected requests. Delivery requires `runApp` or `runHeadlessApp` and is suppressed after the requesting app run ends.
- On Web, success means that the download click was submitted; the browser's actual disk-save completion cannot be observed.

## ScreenshotSaveEventArgs::path

- On native platforms, this `fs::path` is the absolute, lexically normalized destination fixed when the request is submitted. Relative paths are resolved against the data directory, and unsupported or missing extensions cause `.png` to be appended.
- If native path resolution throws an exception, the failure event contains the original requested path instead.
- On Web, this contains only the download filename, with directories removed. An empty filename receives a timestamp-based PNG name; extensions other than PNG or JPG/JPEG cause `.png` to be appended.

## ScreenshotSaveEventArgs::result

- This `SaveResult` reports success or failure, including rejected requests and capture failures. Use `result.ok()` or `if (result)` to check success, and inspect `result.error` and `result.message` on failure.
- Native success confirms encoding, checked writing, closing and replacement of the destination file.
- Web success means that a download click was submitted. Browser download policy and actual disk completion cannot be observed.

## saveScreenshotAsync

- Call `saveScreenshotAsync(path)` on the main thread to capture the requesting window at its next presentation. The function returns `void`; receive the result through `onScreenshotSave()`.
- The destination is fixed at submission. Path and extension rules are described in `ScreenshotSaveEventArgs::path`.
- On native platforms, encoding and writing run on a worker, but GPU readback still runs on the main thread and may stall the capture frame.
- Each window permits at most four pending jobs, including capture requests, writes and results awaiting notification. Further requests receive `SaveError::WriteFailed` with the message `Screenshot queue is full`.
- Hidden secondary windows wait for their own next presentation without blocking captures in other windows. Requests for the main window also request a redraw.
- Native writes across all windows run one at a time in capture-completion order. A slow write delays later writes; serialize other saves to the same destination yourself.
- Closing the window before capture, calling without a render window, or supplying an empty native path produces a deferred failure. Headless calls have no render window.
- On Web, the canvas is captured and submitted as a PNG or JPEG download. The meaning of success is described in `ScreenshotSaveEventArgs::result`.
- Completion timing, application lifetime and listener retention are described in `onScreenshotSave`.

```cpp
void tcApp::setup() {
    saveScreenshotAsync("screenshot.png");
}
```

## onScreenshotSave

- Returns the host-owned `Event<ScreenshotSaveEventArgs>&`. Register with `onScreenshotSave().listen(...)` and retain the returned `EventListener` as a member; destroying it disconnects the listener.
